Checkpoint 857 extends coalesced destination damage through guest
`BltBitMapRastPort` and `BltMaskBitMapRastPort`. The unmasked full-row copy
changes only destination x=0..11. With a `0xAA,0xAA` one-bit mask, the masked
variant changes only even x positions 0..10 admitted by that projection. Both
preserve the active coalesced ClipRect, flags, mask/source data as applicable,
and caller DamageList pointer/Region bytes; successful `EndUpdate` restores
the stable head and clears Refresh. G211 applies destination scroll `(1,1)` to
the unmasked path: the screen-space damage row remains `(0..11,0)`, and a
checkerboard proves the copied source coordinates advance to `(1..12,1)`. G212
applies the same scroll to the masked path; a checkerboard source and a mask
with only source/mask bit `(1,1)` set produce exactly destination pixel
`(0,0)`, preserving all 32 mask bytes and the caller Region state.
G213 uses source origin `(2,0)` and destination origin `(4,0)` under the same
projection; destination clipping keeps x=4..11 and preserves the copy delta,
so the third-bit source pattern changes only destination x=4,7,10.
G214 clips source origin `(-2,0)` and then applies damage x=0..11, yielding
only x=6,9 from the every-third-bit source. G215 clips destination origin
`(-2,0)`, advances source selection to x=2, and writes only x=0,3,6,9.
G216 mirrors these leading-origin checks on Y: paired source/destination y=-2
clips to source row zero, while destination y=-2 alone advances source reads
to row two; the projected screen-space damage admits output only on row zero.
G217 clips a positive source-X tail and damage x=11..12 down to destination
x=11 only. G218 clips source rows 14..15 against damage row zero, exposing only
the row-zero pattern x=1,4,7,10.
G219 applies source origin x=2 and destination origin x=4 to the masked path;
source/mask x=9 maps to damage-edge destination x=11, which is the sole pixel
changed.
G220 starts masked source x at -2; clipping advances source/mask x=3 together
to destination x=9, the only changed pixel.
The boot-layer class passes 193/193 after
these additions. No production graphics source changed; this is CopperStart-

## Refresh flag ownership — native V40 correction (checkpoint 858)

Layers `EndUpdate` restores the stable clipping topology, clears Updating,
and completes owned damage when requested. It does not clear Refresh.
The configured native-ROM nonempty-damage differential proves that Refresh
remains set after both partial and complete EndUpdate. The public
[Intuition EndRefresh contract](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/intuition.library/EndRefresh.html)
assigns refresh-flag clearing to Intuition after calling Layers. Portable
Layers must preserve the caller's current Refresh value, including a value
the caller explicitly cleared. Earlier checkpoint statements and test
expectations that attributed this clear to EndUpdate are superseded.

## Layer BeginUpdate failure-state contract

Keep preflight rejection and post-lock projection failure distinct. Invalid or
malformed layer/DamageList state rejected before update acquisition leaves the
public ClipRect head, Layer flags, DamageList pointer, and Region bytes
untouched. If a valid projection fails after BeginUpdate acquires the layer
lock (including temporary-allocation failure), preserve the published ClipRect
head and free every provisional projection allocation, then expose the
abortable update state: SaveClipRects references the unchanged head, Updating
is set, and the lock remains owned by the caller. The caller must finish with
EndUpdate(FALSE); this clears the transaction, releases the lock, and retains
pending damage for retry. Tests and future changes must not conflate these two
failure classes or require unchanged Layer flags for the post-lock case.
Temporary damage ClipRects may coalesce only when both their bitmap and
obscuring-layer targets match, and their exact union is itself rectangular.
G199-G201 cover the positive case and the two independent target-mismatch
cases. G202 covers a bridge candidate coalescing two already-built nodes.
G203 verifies that a later allocation failure correctly frees the merged
temporary node after that coalescing has happened. G204 verifies full vertical
edge adjacency merges, while corner-only and partial-edge L-shaped contact do
not. G205 carries a coalesced projection into RectFill and validates actual
pixels. G206 carries it into ClipBlit and validates the destination endpoint.
G207 projects damage independently at both ClipBlit endpoints; G208 extends
that projection through independent nonzero X/Y scroll transforms. G209 and
G210 verify the coalesced destination boundary through unmasked and masked
bitmap-to-RastPort blits, respectively.

This document records the architectural rationale and contracts; the goals
file is the separately selectable work ledger, and the execution plan records
evidence for each completed unit.

Status: foundation design for a staged implementation.

## Objective

Provide a Kickstart 3.1/V40-compatible replacement for `graphics.library` in small, independently verifiable units. The first units are RastPort text, drawing primitives, and `View`/`ViewPort` lifecycle. The implementation must be usable from the CopperStart host emulator and remain suitable for a future native 68k Kickstart ROM built with CopperSharp68k.

CyberGraphX is deliberately outside this component. Its patches may consume the base library later, but the base implementation must not reference or depend on CyberGraphX. Intuition remains responsible for screen ownership (`OpenScreen`/`CloseScreen`); this project implements the graphics-side `View`, `ViewPort`, display database, and synchronization contracts that Intuition consumes. The synthetic host handoff may claim only its own screen: `CloseScreen` blanks an active synthetic view through the same `LoadView(NULL)` frame boundary, retires compatibility copper wrappers, clears the guest LOF/SHF CPR links, and drops compatibility-owned backing handles so a later `OpenScreen` can rebuild its guest geometry. Foreign screens remain available to native Intuition or a provider.

That ownership rule also applies to active-view publication. If a foreign
`View` has been loaded while the synthetic screen is still allocated,
`CloseScreen` must release only the synthetic screen's copper/backing state;
it must not clear the foreign `GfxBase->ActiView` pointer or host current-view
selection. This keeps screen teardown composable with a native or provider
display handoff.

The ownership test is the guest `View` address, not merely its `ViewPort`
address. A provider may temporarily reuse the screen-owned embedded
`ViewPort`; that shared structure does not authorize the compatibility bridge
to call `LoadView(NULL)` for the provider's active `View`.

The embedded `ViewPort.Next` link is an ownership boundary as well. A
non-null or unreadable tail is left for the native/provider display owner to
detach before synthetic screen teardown clears copper links.

The `ViewPort.RasInfo` head is part of the same source-storage boundary. A
replaced or unreadable head keeps `CloseScreen` unclaimed until the owner that
installed it restores or detaches the link.

The compatibility RasInfo chain has an exact public cardinality at each
`MakeVPort`/`MrgCop` boundary: a single-playfield ViewPort terminates at its
first `RasInfo`, while `DUALPF` supplies exactly one companion whose `Next` is
NULL. A readable extra tail is still invalid: `MakeVPort` returns
`MVP_NO_DISPLAY` and `MrgCop` returns its failure status before copper
allocation/publication rather than silently claiming a third playfield.
RTG/provider paths remain separate ownership boundaries.

`LoadView` applies the same cardinality rule when a present `RasInfo` head is
used for standard-planar display publication. A null head remains legal while
screen assembly is incomplete, but a readable third node is rejected before
the active View or host display stream is replaced.

RTG/provider `LoadView` handoff is status-aware at every adapter boundary.
When a provider exposes only `TryLoadView`, a declined request preserves the
guest D0/cycle state and remains tail-chainable to the native vector; an
accepted request publishes the classic void-vector success (`D0 = 0`). The
legacy void callback remains supported as an always-claiming compatibility
path. ROM-overlay, normal LVO, and direct CopperScreen entry points use the
same helper so provider ownership does not depend on how the call arrived.

The synthetic `View` LOF/SHF CPR links are validated before `CloseScreen`
clears them. Mapped foreign CPR envelopes block teardown; unmapped stale
values retain the compatibility cleanup path.

The synthetic Intuition rethink path uses the same provider boundary as the
graphics-library lifecycle vectors: a nonzero `ViewPort.ExtendedModes` byte is
not projected by the OCS/ECS compatibility builder. Rethink leaves the current
CPR/DspIns links and active stream intact, allowing a monitor or CyberGraphX
owner to rebuild the extended viewport independently.

`CloseScreen` reconciles the guest `GfxBase->ActiView` field with the host
current-view cache before blanking. A direct native/provider publication is
therefore authoritative even when it bypasses the host `LoadView` gateway.

The synthetic `View.ViewPort` link must still identify the Screen's embedded
`ViewPort`; a repointed or unreadable link leaves the View and Screen available
to the owner that changed it.

The public Screen `RastPort.BitMap` and each compatibility `RasInfo.BitMap`
link must retain the storage published by the synthetic session. Repointed
bitmap links block teardown so foreign raster storage is never detached.

OpenScreen request state is staged transactionally as well. If the guest
Screen envelope or its planar backing cannot be allocated, the failed request
must return to the reset-scoped defaults (while retaining the shared default
font), so a subsequent unrelated OpenScreen call cannot inherit geometry,
flags, palette, or font choices from an operation that never published a
Screen.

The same rule applies to malformed legacy `NewScreen` requests: odd,
over-depth, or unreadable caller-owned fields are declined without leaving
their partially decoded geometry in the compatibility session. A later
untagged request starts from the profile defaults and may be staged afresh.

A non-null legacy `NewScreen` pointer whose required prefix is itself
unreadable is also a provider/native handoff, not an implicit null request.
The compatibility path must decline before display publication; only a
separate null request may select the profile-default synthetic screen.

## Compatibility authority

The compatibility target is the documented Kickstart 3.1/V40 graphics.library surface:

1. NDK 3.1 `graphics_lib.fd`, graphics autodocs, and graphics include files define LVOs, register conventions, structure layouts, and documented return/failure behavior.
2. The local Commodore Amiga Hardware Reference Manual defines custom-chip, copper, blitter, display, palette, sprite, and beam side effects.
3. Existing ROM fixtures and focused hardware conformance tests are the differential oracle where the documentation leaves behavior implicit.

The complete V40 vector inventory is tracked in the companion execution document. Every vector is assigned to exactly one implementation goal; completion cannot leave an unclassified LVO.

The implementation covers API semantics for OCS, ECS, and AGA-visible modes. The current emulator intentionally rejects executable AGA chipset profiles, so AGA hardware activation is a later dependency gate rather than an undocumented claim of conformance. OCS/ECS PAL and NTSC profiles must never share PAL geometry or timing assumptions silently.

## Layered architecture

The dependency direction is:

```text
68k LVO adapter (CopperStart or future native ROM)
        -> typed graphics.library core
        -> guest memory and capability boundaries
        -> host bus/scheduler/custom chips or native Amiga hardware
```

### Portable core

The portable core lives under `CopperMod.Amiga.Emulator/CopperStart/Graphics/Portable`. It owns guest-visible algorithms and fixed-width structure/layout constants. It receives integer guest addresses and values; host object references are never written into guest structures.

The first contracts are:

- `GraphicsLvo`: V40 vector constants and the full manifest identity.
- `GraphicsLayouts`: explicit offsets and sizes for `RastPort`, `BitMap`, `TextFont`, `View`, `ViewPort`, `RasInfo`, and copper-list structures.
- `IGraphicsMemory`: guarded big-endian byte/word/long access over guest addresses.
- `IGraphicsAllocatorBackend`: allocation/free operations with explicit chip/public memory class.
- `IGraphicsBlitterBackend`: ownership, submission, and wait boundaries.
- `IGraphicsDisplayBackend`: view publication, beam/frame waits, and display-side effects.
- `IGraphicsFontBackend` and `IGraphicsFontLifecycleBackend`: decoded guest glyph/metric access plus explicit font-list ownership and extension allocation boundaries.
- `GraphicsLibraryCore`: the typed entry point that will receive function-specific semantic methods as goals land.

Portable code uses fixed-width primitives, caller-owned buffers, deterministic integer arithmetic, and documented status/results. Timing-sensitive work never advances time by itself; it calls the scheduler-aware backend. If the CopperSharp68k compiler subset rejects a managed facade, a native adapter supplies an equivalent binding without changing the portable algorithm or guest layout.

### Host adapter

The existing `GraphicsServices`, `CopperStartGraphicsContext`, and `AmigaBoot` code remain the host integration layer during migration. A host gateway decodes 68k registers, invokes the typed core, and maps results back to registers. Existing behavior is preserved until the corresponding goal has passed its tests.

The host adapter may use `HostGuestMemory`, scheduler callbacks, custom-register services, and host allocations. Those dependencies are forbidden in the portable directory and are not part of the native ROM ABI.

### Native path

The future native path supplies resident/library initialization, `GfxBase`, vector stubs, memory access, and custom-chip bindings using the same documented guest layouts. The current image builder is exercised by headless AccurateM68000 fixtures that follow both a fixed-base and HUNK-loader-relocated `JMP.L` vector stub into mapped native code; that proves the shared negative-vector envelope and relocation records are executable without claiming host/native semantic parity. Native compilation and CopperSharp68k differential execution remain separate gates; they do not force CopperStart to expose host implementation details.

The shared layout contract now includes the native `GfxBase->ActiView` and `GfxBase->ChipRevBits0` offsets alongside the View, ViewPort, RastPort, BitMap, and font structures. CopperStart host publication and future CopperSharp68k/native code should consume these constants rather than reconstructing host-only field offsets.

The native image builder keeps the historical compact `0xF0` positive image as
its default for CopperScreen compatibility, but accepts an explicit positive
image size for a native build. Supplying the full `0x220` `GfxBase` envelope
initializes the embedded `MonitorList` with valid empty Exec sentinels while
leaving `current_monitor`, `default_monitor`, semaphore, display-database, and
active-view-semaphore pointers zero until their owning native/provider
subsystems publish them. This makes the image-size choice explicit at the
CopperSharp68k boundary instead of silently widening every host shim.

The relocatable HUNK builder exposes the same size choice and carries the
native envelope through its AUTOINIT resident. When the full image is selected,
the HUNK relocation table also covers the nonzero `MonitorList` head and
tail-predecessor self-pointers, so loader mapping preserves the Exec list
sentinels. Compact HUNK output keeps the historical relocation footprint.

Native takeover also rebases the portable core's guest-library ownership
registries. Extended nodes created after takeover point back to the discovered
native `GfxBase`, monitor opens splice that base's `MonitorList`, and active-view
publication targets the native `ActiView` field. Reversible overlay teardown
restores the compatibility base together with the font-list binding, so a
host/native transition cannot leave mixed ownership pointers.

### Current foundation implementation

Decoded guest `TextFont` lookups now support both proportional `CharLoc` tables and fixed-cell fonts with no `tf_CharLoc`; both use the final glyph-table entry as the documented default glyph for characters outside `tf_LoChar..tf_HiChar`, and an absent `tf_CharSpace` falls back to the nominal cell width. The portable metric and rendering paths therefore agree on fallback-cell width. `OpenFont` now selects the highest-positive Kickstart `WeighTAMatch`-style score: designed requests accept candidates marked `FPF_DESIGNED` or `FPF_DISKFONT`, while a non-disk constructed candidate is rejected; `REVPATH` is a hard incompatibility, size uses the documented asymmetric penalty, and intrinsic underline/bold/italic mismatches use the ROM bit-clearing weights. Resident-list matching compares the requested name to the stored `TextFont` node name exactly; path stripping remains a compatibility-only Topaz default check and is not used to turn an `OpenDiskFont` path into an `OpenFont` hit. Removed fonts and zero-weight candidates are not opened; the compatibility default still requires a Topaz name while using its guest `TextFont` attributes. Tagged `OpenFont` requests now validate the bounded guest suffix and compare `TA_DeviceDPI` aspect ratios against candidate `TextFontExtension` tag lists, so equivalent raw DPI pairs retain an exact score while a mismatch receives a positive ranking penalty. This keeps the ROM/DISK source rule and guest tag ABI in the portable matcher; native exact weight calibration and broader malformed/failure coverage remain later gates ([OpenFont](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/OpenFont), [WeighTAMatch](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html), [TA_DeviceDPI](https://d0.se/include/graphics/text.h)).

The font decoder now requires a readable common strike envelope before a `TextFont` can become selectable: `tf_CharData` must point at readable guest storage, while `tf_Modulo`, the character range, and the optional table pointers retain their structural checks even when a proportional `tf_CharLoc` table is non-null. This prevents a plainly unmapped strike pointer from passing `AddFont`/`OpenFont` and only failing at its first glyph dereference, while leaving table widths and full per-row rendering validation to the text preflight; native and host paths therefore share the same fail-closed admission rule.

`OpenFont` applies that same strike-envelope check while scanning the selected guest `TextFonts` list. This covers resident/native nodes that were published outside the portable `AddFont` path and were later corrupted by another owner: they remain visible to list traversal, but cannot win matching or increment their accessor word unless their header and strike storage are still usable.

`ExtendFont` now publishes the guest `FSF_TAGGED` style bit only after its system-owned `TextFontExtension` is fully initialized, stores the prior `tf_Extension` in `tfe_OrigReplyPort`, and restores that pointer and the prior style bits on `StripFont`. A pre-existing extension is treated as foreign ownership: the portable backend reports success but neither detaches nor frees it, matching the ownership boundary needed for diskfont/library-provided extensions. The extension match word/back pointer remain guest-visible for future tag-weighting work ([graphics/text.i](https://d0.se/include/graphics/text.i)).

The portable `WeighTAMatch` size term now sign-extends both `ta_YSize` UWORDs
through the guest WORD contract before taking the absolute difference. This
preserves the native edge behavior for high-bit sizes (for example, `$FFFF`
and `$0001` are two signed units apart) instead of letting an unsigned host
subtraction turn the same request into an immediate zero-weight mismatch.
The source rule, REVPATH rejection, style-bit clearing, and asymmetric
penalties remain unchanged ([AROS `weightamatch.c`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/weightamatch.c)).

The V40 `WeighTAMatch` slot is now routed at the documented `-804` LVO through a pure guest-memory matcher. It preserves the Kickstart positive metric, designed/disk source rule, hard `REVPATH` mismatch, asymmetric size penalty, and intrinsic style bit-clearing. When `FSF_TAGGED` is set, the matcher reads the extended `TTextAttr` pointer, validates bounded `TAG_MORE`/`TAG_SKIP` chains, and compares `TA_DeviceDPI` by aspect ratio; malformed chains fail closed and equivalent raw DPI magnitudes remain equal. The portable path reserves a dedicated mismatch ranking bit while native exact-ROM calibration remains a later gate ([WeighTAMatch autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html), [TA_DeviceDPI](https://d0.se/include/graphics/text.h)).

Font removal now follows the documented lifecycle boundary: `RemFont` withdraws a font from future matching but retains it as a closeable removed node while accessors are outstanding; the final `CloseFont` releases that removed-state tracking, after which `AddFont` may publish the node again. This keeps guest `FPF_REMOVED` visibility and accessor ownership independent of the active lookup list ([RemFont autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html)).

Decoded metric operations now reject null guest string pointers for non-empty `TextLength`, `TextExtent`, and `TextFit` calls instead of reading address zero as a character stream; zero-length `TextExtent`/`TextFit` register calls preserve the empty-string result without dereferencing A0. `AskFont` also preflights its complete 8-byte `TextAttr` destination before writing any field, so malformed guest output buffers cannot expose a partial font attribute update. Planar pixel addressing keeps `(row * BytesPerRow) + byteOffset` in a wide intermediate and checks the final 32-bit guest address, preserving the `BitMap` modulo contract without host integer wraparound.

Fixed-cell metric envelopes now carry the guest font's `CharSpace`/`CharKern`
presence through `GraphicsFontMetrics`. When neither table is present and the
font is not proportional, `TextLength`, `TextExtent`, and `TextFit` use the
nominal per-character movement cell rather than allowing an individual strike
bitmap to expand the public horizontal extent. Proportional fonts and fixed
fonts with either table retain their per-glyph kerning/strike bounds. The text
renderer applies the same distinction to glyph placement, underline coverage,
destination preflight, and the published cursor, so a provider kerning value
cannot expand a fixed-cell advance when `CharKern` is absent. The same guard
applies to `FontExtent`; the strike still draws at its actual width, while
only the public movement cell is fixed.

Metric providers now preserve the guest movement-field width at the portable
boundary: a `tf_CharSpace`-backed advance must fit a signed WORD, while a font
without that table may use the unsigned `tf_XSize` cell (or its negative
`FPF_REVPATH` form). Host-only advances outside those envelopes are rejected
by `TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` before a result is
published. This keeps the CopperSharp68k-facing metric contract independent
of the provider's host integer representation ([AROS
`TextLength`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textlength.c), [AROS
`TextExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c)).

Planar region operations apply that check to the inclusive byte-span end: a touched row may end at guest address `0xFFFFFFFF`, but no row may wrap into address zero. Region preflight and the transaction snapshot use the same rule so a malformed span is rejected before any selected plane is published.

The V36 chunky pixel-array writers stage all logical source bytes before touching the destination planes. This preserves temporary-RastPort conversion semantics when a caller's byte array overlaps planar storage, while retaining the guarded guest-array and destination transactions used by the host/native boundary.

Their guest-array preflight also validates the full padded `RASSIZE` envelope for every row. The logical byte count may be smaller than the reserved stride, but the complete stride must remain addressable so a native conversion path cannot cross an unmapped padding boundary.

The V36 pixel-line/array result is the number of pixels actually read or
plotted after the destination RastPort clips the requested rectangle. Reads
still consume the complete padded source envelope and publish deterministic
zero bytes for out-of-raster samples; writes skip those samples. Malformed
guest storage still fails before any destination mutation. This follows the
autodoc result wording for `WritePixelArray8` ([d0 autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelArray8)).

The host register boundary carries an explicit success bit for signed metric results. `Text`, `TextLength`, and `TextExtent` consume their documented signed WORD count from the low register field; `TextFit` consumes UWORD `strLen`/width/height fields and a signed WORD direction. Negative signed counts are rejected before guest traversal, while unrelated high-word residue is ignored. `TextLength` publishes its classic sign-extended WORD result, so it may legitimately return `-1` for a valid condensed/reverse-path advance; malformed font or string storage still declines. `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` likewise leave D0 and cycles untouched when their complete guest input/output envelopes cannot be validated, without turning valid zero-width or zero-fit results into provider fallbacks.


For an empty `TextExtent` query, the shared guest structure keeps the font's vertical envelope (`MinY=-tf_Baseline`, `MaxY=tf_YSize-tf_Baseline-1`). Fixed-cell fonts remain horizontally empty (`Width=0`, `MinX=0`, `MaxX=-1`), while proportional/kerning fonts retain the classic zero-width movement cell (`MinX=0`, `MaxX=0`) before algorithmic bold/italic expansion. This preserves the native distinction between a fixed-cell empty rectangle and a proportional metric cell ([AROS `TextExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c)).

`FontExtent` now scans only the font's declared `LoChar..HiChar` range, reports the maximum single-glyph movement (`tf_CharSpace + tf_CharKern`) under the normal-font direction rule (left-moving totals do not make a normal width negative) or the `FPF_REVPATH` rule (right-moving totals do not make a reverse width positive), and fails closed on a movement outside the 32-bit result contract. Proportional and fixed-cell fonts derive that width from their glyph advances instead of seeding the result with the nominal `tf_XSize` cell width. Its rectangle includes each candidate glyph's signed `CharKern` offset and bitmap width, so a glyph that moves outside the nominal cell still contributes to `te_Extent` even when its movement is ignored for `te_Width` ([FontExtent autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html)).

`InitRastPort` establishes the documented pen, draw-mode, line-pattern, and pen-size defaults. When the host/native boundary has a validated `GfxBase->DefaultFont`, it also publishes that guest font pointer and its cached height, width, and baseline; `TxSpacing` remains the zeroed caller-owned word because the subsequent classic `SetFont` operation does not overwrite it. CopperStart prefers the rebound guest `TextFonts`/`DefaultFont` list for this selection and uses the compatibility callback only for a host-shim session without that list; a malformed guest default therefore declines before the clear rather than exposing a fontless success. Callers without a font provider retain the pure zeroed-font construction path. `SetFont` treats a null guest font pointer as a request for the active `GfxBase->DefaultFont`, then treats that selected pointer, the `AlgoStyle` reset, and the cached RastPort metrics as one update: it preflights those exact fields before publishing any field. Caller-owned `TxSpacing` remains outside the access envelope, so a truncated RastPort or unavailable default cannot expose a new font with stale or missing metrics.

For a mapped native overlay, the compatibility callback is not a substitute for
the guest default-font list. If no rebound `TextFonts`/`DefaultFont` owner is
present, `InitRastPort` remains unclaimed so the resident Kickstart vector can
select its own `GfxBase->DefaultFont`; only the host-shim path may use the
compatibility callback.

`ClearScreen` treats its text-line prefix and the rows below it as one guest operation. Both clipped destination spans are probed before the first write, so a malformed later plane or row cannot publish a partially cleared screen. `ClearEOL` remains a single clipped span with the same preflight discipline.

The native display database now treats ECS SuperHires as a first-class OCS/ECS mode boundary: PAL and NTSC progressive/interlaced records use the documented composite `SUPER_KEY`/`SUPERLACE_KEY` values (`HIRES|SUPER`), plus the ECS-compatible `SUPERDPF`/`SUPERDPF2` dual-playfield variants, 1280-pixel nominal width, two-plane/four-colour depth, `DIPF_IS_ECS`, and standard-sprite support without attached-sprite mode. Ordinary OCS/ECS planar records publish the documented `DIPF_IS_SPRITES_ATT` capability for attached sprite pairs; a focused PAL/NTSC matrix keeps that flag separate from the SuperHires exception ([graphics/displayinfo.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/displayinfo.h)). The same ModeID-backed records flow through `FindDisplayInfo`, `BestModeIDA`, `CoerceMode`, `GetDisplayInfoData`, and the CopperStart register adapter. Double-scan, extended-monitor, and RTG records remain separate provider gates.

The `DTAG_DISP` payload keeps the SuperHires exception coherent at both levels of the public record: its property mask retains `DIPF_IS_SPRITES` but clears `DIPF_IS_SPRITES_ATT`, and `NumStdSprites` remains eight. Standard PAL/NTSC records publish the same eight standard sprites; only attached-sprite selection is rejected for ECS SuperHires. This prevents a caller from treating the capability mask and the numeric sprite count as contradictory mode metadata.

The same payload publishes native colour precision rather than deriving palette
metadata from plane count: ordinary OCS/ECS lores/hires records use 4/4/4 RGB
bits and `PaletteRange == 4096`, progressive ECS SuperHires uses 2/2/2 RGB bits
and `PaletteRange == 64`, and interlaced SuperHires uses the full 4/4/4 RGB
precision and 4096-entry range. `BestModeIDA` applies the `BIDTAG_RedBits`,
`BIDTAG_BlueBits`, and `BIDTAG_GreenBits` minimums to those published record
values, so a default four-bit request cannot silently choose progressive
SuperHires. This keeps `DisplayInfo` internally consistent for callers that
size palette tables from the component fields. Its
`SpriteResolution` point likewise reflects the ECS hardware contract: 140 ns
(`4` ticks) for lores/hires standard sprites and 70 ns (`2` ticks) for
SuperHires positioning ([ECS hardware docs](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/AmigaDevDocs/hard_c.html)).

The display property vocabulary is kept complete at this boundary: all V39/V40 `DIPF_*` values are named in the portable database, and `SPECIAL_FLAGS` is built from the documented feature constants. This keeps future monitor and BestMode slices aligned with the public Kickstart header without claiming CyberGraphX or extended-monitor records.

The display-query ownership boundary is equally explicit. `ModeNotAvailable`
claims canonical default/PAL/NTSC OCS/ECS keys and the four V40 scan-doubled
query keys, but leaves arbitrary keys under those monitor parts unclaimed for
the future native monitor or CyberGraphX provider. A recognized monitor family
alone is not sufficient evidence that the portable database owns a mode.

Portable `MonitorSpec` objects also initialize the embedded `DisplayInfoDataBase` with the standard empty Exec-list sentinels and a valid public `SignalSemaphore` prefix (empty wait queue, zero owner/nesting/count, and node type 15). The list is intentionally empty until a native monitor provider publishes records, but both the list and its lock envelope remain structurally walkable through the guest ABI.

The resident `MonitorSpec` initializer preflights word alignment and the complete `MonitorSpecSize` guest envelope before clearing or publishing any field. It stages the entire public prefix and commits it only after every field has succeeded, restoring the original bytes if a late guest write is rejected. A high allocator result therefore cannot wrap its tail into low guest memory; failed initialization rolls the public allocation back to the same graphics-instance owner without leaving a half-built node for allocator reuse or native list walks.

When a full native `GfxBase` is mapped, the optional `MonitorList` splice is
part of the same publication transaction. If a later list-link write is
rejected, the list links and the complete resident `MonitorSpec` envelope are
restored before the allocation is released, so native CopperSharp68k callers
never observe a partially published monitor node.

The native `GfxBase->DisplayInfoDataBase` field is an `APTR` to the private
display-database object, not an embedded Exec `List`. The host bridge now
publishes a small, self-describing private sidecar (magic, version, byte size,
record count, and the native ModeID table) only after validating the full
native `GfxBase` envelope. The sidecar is an explicit CopperScreen/
CopperSharp68k handoff object; it does not claim to reproduce undocumented ROM
database internals, and the public ModeID/query methods remain the portable
owner. A non-zero pointer supplied by Kickstart or a display provider is
preserved byte-for-byte. Sidecar initialization writes the APTR last and
rolls back both the allocation and pointer on any guest-memory failure, so the
host bridge must never use that pointer field as scratch list storage.

Before that optional monitor-list splice, the bridge validates the native
Exec `List` type and pad bytes as zero. A foreign or partially initialized
list therefore declines transactionally, preserving the provider's links and
the newly allocated `MonitorSpec` envelope for native fallback.

Monitor specs are resident monitor-list nodes rather than per-open handles:
`OpenMonitor` shares one object per native PAL/NTSC family, `CloseMonitor`
decrements `ms_OpenCount`, and the object remains addressable at zero so
`DTAG_MNTR` and a later open observe the same guest pointer. Allocation is
therefore retained for the graphics-instance lifetime; provider/native
semaphore and callback ownership is still explicit.

The display-database tag parser treats `TAG_MORE` with a null continuation as a clean end-of-list, while non-null chains remain bounded by the same cycle and malformed-pointer guards used by the other guest tag APIs.

`BestModeIDA` preserves the distinction between an omitted `BIDTAG_MonitorID`
and an explicit `DEFAULT_MONITOR_ID` value of zero.  An omitted monitor tag is
free to match any native PAL/NTSC family; an explicit zero constrains scoring,
viewport/source compatibility, and the result to the zero-monitor-part
default family.  This keeps the portable selector aligned with the native
ModeID namespace instead of treating a valid default monitor as a wildcard.

`GetDisplayInfoData` snapshots the requested clipped chunk before publication and restores it on a late guest write failure. Display and monitor records therefore obey the same all-or-nothing guest-memory boundary as the View and RastPort structures they describe.

The portable `DTAG_DISP` payload now uses the complete Kickstart `DisplayInfo`
layout: a 0x38-byte chunk with a five-double-longword local payload, public
resolution/sprite/palette fields, the V39 RGB-bit fields, and zeroed
padding/reserved terminators. Its `QueryHeader.Length` publishes the
five-double-longword local payload size, excluding the 16-byte header. A
caller may still request a shorter clipped copy, but the guest header
describes the full native structure so a CopperSharp68k consumer can safely
use the same offsets and trailing terminators.

`DTAG_VEC` is deliberately a separate ownership boundary.  The V39/V40
`graphics/displayinfo.h` header labels it internal-use-only for monitor-driver
`VecInfo` records; the portable public database therefore declines that tag
instead of returning an empty chunk.  A resident monitor or a future
CopperSharp68k/native provider can publish its private vector record without
being masked by the standard `DTAG_DISP`/`DTAG_DIMS`/`DTAG_MNTR`/`DTAG_NAME`
overlay.  Unknown public tags retain the documented zero-result behavior.

`GetRGB32` applies the same rule to ColorMap output: all source entries and the complete RGB32 destination table are preflighted, then a late write restores the caller's original bytes.

`LoadRGB4` and `LoadRGB32` use the corresponding input-side transaction boundary.  The source table and all guest ColorMap entries are decoded first; high/low nibble words are then published together, with rollback if a later word write fails.  Display/native palette callbacks run only after the guest commit, and the RGB32 loader preserves the Kickstart interleaved triplet-record and zero-count terminator format ([LoadRGB32 autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node02FB.html)).

Direct `SetRGB4CM`/`SetRGB32CM` and the viewport setters use the same two-word ColorMap transaction, so a failed low-word write cannot leave a new high-word value behind or trigger a host palette callback.

At the host register boundary, `GetRGB4` preserves its ULONG 12-bit palette result in D0 and declines the `0xFFFFFFFF` invalid-entry sentinel without claiming the call.  This keeps the portable ColorMap overlay and a future CopperSharp68k vector table on the same observable ABI.

`VideoControl` uses the same bounded guest-tag discipline: all `TAG_MORE`/`TAG_SKIP` branches are decoded before any ColorMap or private sidecar mutation.  This preserves the prior state when a later continuation is malformed and treats a null `TAG_MORE` as the end of the list.

Classic `VTAG_*_GET` items follow the Kickstart in-place ABI: the TagItem is rewritten to its corresponding SET/CLR tag and `ti_Data` becomes the queried scalar or pointer value.  Only the V40 `VC_*_Query` items use an external four-byte destination, which is range-preflighted before setters execute.  All guest writes are staged through a transaction, so an unsupported later tag, failed extended-node association, late commit failure, or rejected continuation restores ColorMap bytes, rewritten TagItems, query destinations, allocation-owned sidecars, and the extended-node registry together.

`VTAG_IMMEDIATE` is the explicit portable/provider seam: its output word is
validated and word-aligned with the other external query destinations, then
written only after
the complete tag transaction commits.  The portable owner clears the word for
pure read-only/immediate batches and sets it when a setter cannot patch an
already-published copper list, telling the caller to perform the normal
`MakeVPort`/`MrgCop` remake.  `VTAG_BATCH_ITEMS_ADD` now appends a bounded,
alignment-checked guest command list to the portable `ColorMap` batch head;
an enabled list is replayed transactionally at the next `MakeVPort` before
host copper publication.  Pointer-bearing batch setters and `ADD` remain
declined by the mapped native overlay so CopperSharp68k or a provider can
retain ownership of caller-owned list mutation.  In-place copper patching
remains native/provider-owned, so a future CopperSharp68k ROM and the
CopperScreen host path can share the same guest transaction boundary without
claiming CyberGraphX behavior.

`VTAG_NEXTBUF_CM` is handled as a bounded command-buffer splice: the portable
collector validates and walks the next guest `TagItem` stream before applying
any state, while a null continuation terminates cleanly. This keeps the
classic multi-buffer VideoControl ABI shared by direct CopperStart dispatch,
the mapped native overlay, and a future CopperSharp68k implementation.

Region boolean operations now treat the guest `Region` header as one publication unit.  `PublishRegion` and `ClearRegion` restore the original bounds and linked-rectangle pointer if allocation or a late header write fails, so callers never observe a half-replaced region.

The same allocator boundary covers provisional addresses: `NewRegion` and
transactional rectangle-node publication release a nonzero out address even
when the allocator returns a false status.  This prevents a failed region
operation from leaking public memory before the native/provider fallback can
claim the call.

The guest `RegionRectangle` nodes retain the classic relative-coordinate
contract: `Region.Bounds` is the absolute origin and each node stores its
rectangle relative to that origin.  The portable boolean engine translates
nodes to absolute coordinates only while evaluating the operation, then
re-encodes the published list relative to the new bounds.  This keeps the
linked guest layout consumable by native layer code while preserving the
transactional allocation and header rollback boundary.

`AndRectRegion` uses the native no-growth contract: it clips the existing
linked nodes in place, removes nodes that no longer intersect, and never asks
the allocator for a replacement list.  The complete header/node snapshot is
still restored if a guarded guest write fails, so allocation exhaustion cannot
turn a valid intersection into a provider fallback.

Region rectangle vectors distinguish an unreadable guest rectangle from an
"evil" rectangle whose minimum exceeds its maximum.  `OrRectRegion`,
`XorRectRegion`, and `ClearRectRegion` treat the latter as a successful no-op;
`AndRectRegion` clears the destination region.  This follows the native
`IS_RECT_EVIL` branches while keeping malformed guest pointers available for
native/provider ownership.

The portable status returned by `AndRectRegion` is adapter-only.  Its public
68k vector is void, so the register boundary clears D0 after a successful
guarded operation instead of exposing the internal success flag.

`ChangeVPBitMap` applies the same rule to screen-buffer association: if the guarded `RasInfo.BitMap` long write fails after a partial prefix, the previous bitmap pointer is restored before the display boundary is notified. A replacement that advertises `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` must also pass the strict display-surface envelope—word-aligned plane pointers and readable complete row spans—before that association changes; geometry-only headers remain accepted while a viewport is being assembled.

The displayable-swap rule is shared by direct CopperStart dispatch and the mapped ROM overlay. A malformed displayable plane envelope remains available to the original native/provider vector with D0, CPU cycles, the old `RasInfo.BitMap`, and the rebuild callback untouched; repairing the plane envelope then follows the normal standard-planar association path.

Bitmap attribute queries keep a status bit beside their classic value result. A readable standard `BitMap` returns zero for an unknown selector, while an unreadable envelope declines at the register boundary; only an explicitly RTG-owned bitmap crosses to the provider callback. `FreeBitMap` follows the same ownership split, so a foreign or malformed standard bitmap is never freed by the host compatibility path.

The RastPort state setters use the same transaction rule.  Pen/draw-mode changes restore their line-pattern phase, `SetABPenDrMd` restores all three fields, `SetOutlinePen` restores both the pen and flags word, and `Move` restores both cursor coordinates after any later write failure.

`TextFit` keeps the Kickstart reverse-string ABI: direction `-1` treats the supplied string pointer as the final character and subtracts offsets, while direction `+1` walks forward. `Text` now preserves the documented cursor contract at both planar RastPort boundaries (the cursor is truncated to the drawable interval `[0,width]` instead of wrapping a signed word when rendering runs past the bitmap), reports malformed in-range plane writes, and preflights every destination row/plane plus the final cursor store before publishing any glyph pixels. This prevents a later malformed row from leaving a partially rendered string while retaining zero-write-mask no-op behavior. The direction contract follows the graphics.library autodoc ([TextFit](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)). Direct/core calls with a nonzero `RastPort.Layer` remain provider-owned; the validated Layers projection now supplies its explicit visibility predicate to text and drawing primitives so hidden clip fragments are skipped during both destination preflight and publication. The predicate restores the selected layer-domain origin before matching public clip-fragment coordinates, so scrolled layers retain the same visibility envelope. Layer damage/backing-store and full provider fallback semantics remain outside this portable slice.

The same text transaction now guards all intermediate 32-bit coordinates. Cursor advances, signed kerning, italic shifts, underline spans, and bold smears are checked before conversion back to guest pixel coordinates; an oversized decoded advance or long stream fails atomically and restores `CurrentX` rather than wrapping into an unrelated raster location. This keeps the portable renderer deterministic for malformed font providers while preserving the shared guest layout for a future CopperSharp68k implementation.

After low-word gateway normalization, text requests validate the complete
guest character span before entering font decoding. Forward strings may end
at `0xffffffff`, and reverse `TextFit` requests may end at address zero, but
neither direction may wrap the 32-bit guest address space. The gateway's
signed WORD/UWORD fields bound the guest request; the portable core may still
use widened host counts for guarded arithmetic and direct host tests. This
admission check is shared by `TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and
`Text`; malformed oversized requests therefore leave the metric result and
native/provider ownership untouched without changing the established spacing
or reverse-string semantics.

All metric vectors preflight the complete 12-byte guest `TextExtent` result before writing width, height, and rectangle fields. A malformed output pointer therefore fails without a half-published extent, preserving the same guest-memory ownership rule used by the RastPort setters.

`TextFit` now rejects a spacing pattern that stalls or reverses the effective inter-glyph path. The check is performed per boundary, so proportional glyph advances cannot pass the first character and then silently change direction; the documented result is an empty `TextExtent` and zero fitted characters ([TextFit autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html)).

The alternate `TextFit` form also short-circuits a box whose height is less
than `tf_YSize` before decoding the string. It publishes the empty extent as
a successful zero-fit, so malformed glyph storage cannot turn a geometrically
impossible request into a claimed failure. For a non-empty request, the
alternate width/height and an explicit `TextExtent` are both active: the
rendering-box dimensions bound the candidate envelope, while the explicit
extent additionally requires an origin-relative rectangle containing x=0 and
the candidate bounds ([TextFit](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).

`TextFit` treats each candidate glyph envelope as speculative. If a later
character exceeds the constraining box, its kerning, strike, and movement
bounds are discarded before the accepted prefix is published; the returned
`TextExtent` therefore describes exactly the characters counted in the result,
not the rejected candidate that stopped the scan.

For pixel primitives, the clipped `SetBitmapPixel` helper remains internal to drawing operations, while the public `WritePixel` vector performs an explicit bitmap-bound check and returns `-1` for an outside coordinate, matching the documented result ([WritePixel](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixel)). The helper snapshots every selected planar byte before publication and restores earlier planes if a later byte write fails, so a guarded multi-plane update cannot expose partial colour state.

The shared planar write helper treats a zero `RastPort.Mask` as a successful no-op for `WritePixel`, `Draw`, `RectFill`, and the other non-layered primitives. It still reports failure when a selected in-range plane cannot be addressed, so masking off all planes does not hide malformed memory while preserving the expected write-mask contract.

Before writing a selected multi-plane pixel, the helper probes and snapshots every selected plane. A malformed later plane fails before publication, and a later byte-write failure restores earlier planes, keeping planar colour updates atomic at the portable/native boundary.

`Draw` extends the same boundary across its complete patterned line: it snapshots each touched selected-plane byte and the original RastPort line state, restoring pixels, flags, pattern phase, and cursor if a later pixel or state write fails.

`Text` applies the same transaction boundary across the complete rendered string: it snapshots each touched selected-plane byte and restores those bytes plus the original `CurrentX`, `Flags`, and line-pattern phase if a later glyph, style pass, or final cursor write fails. A successful text operation finishes through the same fresh-position state as `Move`, publishing `FRST_DOT` and `linpatcnt=15` together with the clipped next-character `CurrentX`; this keeps a subsequent connected line from inheriting text's stale pattern phase ([TextLength autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html), [AROS Text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c), [AROS Move](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/move.c)). A negative kerning offset before the first glyph is used for strike placement but omitted from the published cursor advance, matching `TextLength`/`TextExtent` and the documented classic contract.

`PolyDraw` extends the line transaction across the complete point chain: it snapshots all touched selected-plane bytes and the original cursor, pattern phase, and flags, restoring them if a later connected `Draw` fails.

`SetFont` snapshots the existing guest font pointer, soft-style byte, and
cached metric words, restoring the complete mutated font/cache state if a
later write fails.  The classic vector clears the prior `AlgoStyle` effect
when selecting a new font, while leaving caller-owned `TxSpacing` untouched
([SetFont autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0479.html)).

The native SetFont body admits the exact fields it publishes rather than
borrowing the host overlay's conservative whole-object writability policy.
Its A1 envelope ends with the `TextBaseline` WORD at RP+3E/+3F, so the last
valid even base is `0xFFFFFFC0`. The guard runs before explicit/default Font
resolution; an invalid default-font call therefore retains original A0=0 for
native/provider tail chaining. This remains compatible with the host overlay's
separate 100-byte probe and with a future CopperSharp68k resident layout.

The native `TextLength` body similarly admits its operation-wide exact read
envelope before selecting a metric arm. The widest RastPort field is the
signed `TxSpacing` WORD at RP+40/+41, so `0xFFFFFFBE` is the last valid even
base and `0xFFFFFFC0` is the first wrapping base. The D1 pre-read guard runs
before the body's D7/A5 scratch captures; malformed calls therefore preserve
their original D0/A0/A1 and callee-saved registers while tail-chaining. Fixed
selected-font and NULL-Font cached-width forms share this boundary without
requiring the unused remainder of the 100-byte RastPort.

Admitted `TextLength` calls now enter one public frame that also snapshots
original D0. This extra value is necessary because proportional default-slot
and forward-walk logic legitimately reuse D7/A5. Saved A6 temporarily carries
original A0, allowing the common decline epilogue to restore the complete
native/provider call even after table selection or source walking; the common
success epilogue retains D0's signed metric result while restoring D2-D7 and
A2-A6. Pre-admission declines remain outside the frame and tail-chain directly.

Native `TextExtent` now applies the same exact RastPort admission before its
D7/A3 captures. Its widest A1 read is the signed `TxSpacing` WORD at +40/+41,
so `0xFFFFFFBE` is the last valid even base and `0xFFFFFFC0` is the first
wrapping base. Fixed and bounded proportional arms share the guard while the
12-byte A2 result preflight remains an independent output transaction.
Admitted calls enter one outer native frame that preserves original D0,
D2-D7, A0, and A2-A6. Fixed, forward-proportional, and reverse-proportional
successes converge on a result-preserving epilogue; all post-admission
declines converge on a complete original-call restore before provider tail
chaining. The reverse arm's temporary A2 stack slot nests above that frame and
is removed before either common epilogue, so early and late fallback depths
remain identical. Pre-admission A1 declines stay outside the frame.

`TextFit` retained a separately staged boundary. Its native arms read RP.Font,
RP.AlgoStyle, and the signed RP.TxSpacing WORD through +40/+41. The exact A1
guard therefore admits `0xFFFFFFBE` and rejects `0xFFFFFFC0` before any body
read or the first A6 source capture. D1 is the live direction input, so the
guard brackets only its own validation with a temporary D1 stack save and
restores that value on both admitted and declined paths. This keeps exact
admission independent of the later public frame.

The completed `TextFit` public frame accounts for every fixed, proportional,
no-fit, and post-scratch exit without changing ownership. It saves original D1
separately from D0/D2-D7/A0/A2-A6 after admission. D0-D3/A0-A3 remain complete
provider-call provenance on decline, D2-D7/A2-A6 are restored on success, and
only the fitted-count D0 plus the atomic 12-byte result escapes a native
success. The reverse proportional arm's private A2 result-pointer slot and the
multi-glyph arm's private D7 slot remain nested above the outer frame and are
removed before either common epilogue.

Native `FontExtent` now has its independently staged metric admission. Its A0
guard covers the complete 0x34-byte `TextFont` prefix through the `CharKern`
LONG at +0x30..+0x33. Its A1 guard covers the complete 12-byte packed result:
`0xFFFFFFF4` is the last even exact-end base and `0xFFFFFFF6` is the first
wrapping base. All six malformed A0/A1 exits branch to the owner before D7
captures original D0, so pre-admission tail chains retain D0, A0, A1,
callee-saved registers, and result bytes.

The post-admission `FontExtent` public frame is now complete without widening
fixed/proportional/reverse ownership. It saves original D0/D2-D7/A0/A2-A6
immediately after admission, initializes D2 before the byte-sized Flags/LoChar
loads so caller bits 8..15 cannot affect the declared-range compare, and
converges all four native success returns on a D0-preserving restore. Both
fixed and proportional fallback funnels restore the complete original call
before tail chaining; the six pre-admission exits stay outside the frame and A1
remains the stable result pointer throughout. The proportional-forward loop
also retains the declared glyph count in framed D7 before D5 becomes baseline
scratch, removing a latent count/baseline alias that happened to be masked by
the earlier three-glyph/baseline-two probe.

`AskFont` now has the same independently staged native admission and public
frame. Its exact A0 TextAttr, A1 RastPort.Font, and selected TextFont-prefix
checks use volatile D1 only, so malformed public calls branch directly to the
owner before any callee-saved scratch or output byte escapes. Admitted calls
then preserve D2-D7/A2-A6 around the four-field publication; A0, A1, and D1
remain publicly volatile and the successful void result remains D0=0.

`OpenFont` begins with separately tested request, GfxBase-field, and selected-
font boundaries. Its A0 TextAttr is exactly eight bytes, so FFFFFFF8 is a valid
final even base and FFFFFFFA is the first wrapping base. The DefaultFont LONG at
GfxBase+0x9A..0x9D admits A6 through FFFFFF62 and rejects FFFFFF64. The selected
font then requires the complete 0x34-byte TextFont prefix, admitting FFFFFFCC
and rejecting FFFFFFCE. All three guards use volatile D1 and finish before
original D0 is copied into D7 or a request field is loaded into D2. The admitted
match and accessor publication then run inside a D2-D7/A2-A6 public frame:
success retains the selected-font result in D0, while every late decline
restores original D0 and the callee-saved set before owner handoff. A0, A1, and
D1 remain publicly volatile.

`CloseFont` keeps NULL as a read-free successful no-op. For a non-NULL A1, the
DefaultFont LONG at A6+0x9A..0x9D now uses volatile D1 admission through
A6=FFFFFF62 and completes before original D0 or any callee-saved register is
reused. The selected default's complete 0x34-byte TextFont prefix uses the same
volatile admission phase, with FFFFFFCC as the exact-end pointer and FFFFFFCE
as the first wrapping pointer. Pointer identity, zero-accessor handling, and
accessor decrement for admitted non-NULL calls now run inside a complete
D2-D7/A2-A6 frame. Resident success and late owner decline both restore that
frame, while NULL stays on its separate read-free, unframed success exit.

Native `WeighTAMatch` admission is separately staged from ranking. Its narrow
exact-match owner accepts only A2=NULL and two complete eight-byte TextAttrs at
A0/A1. Those three checks now complete through volatile D1 before the existing
D7 result provenance or D2-D6 ranking scratch is touched; FFFFFFF8 is the final
even exact-end TextAttr and FFFFFFFA first wraps. Every rejected input branches
directly to the owner with the original call intact. The admitted exact match
and all YSize/tag/style/flags late declines now run inside a complete
D2-D7/A2-A6 frame; success retains 32767 and late declines recover original D0
before restoring. This does not widen the native ranking subset.

Native `StripFont` remains intentionally narrow: A0=NULL is a read-free
successful no-op and every non-NULL extension pointer stays with the portable/

borrowing D4/D7 or inspecting guest memory. This closes public preservation
without claiming extension teardown.

`CloseMonitor` now completes its first monitor-lifecycle boundary. NULL A0
succeeds before any scratch or A6 access. Non-NULL calls validate the complete
DefaultMonitor LONG at A6+0x18E..0x191 through volatile D1, admitting FFFFFE6E
as the final even base and rejecting FFFFFE70 before D7/D5/D6 scratch. All
malformed A6 paths tail-chain directly with the original call intact.

The selected DefaultMonitor pointer now has its independent admission too. Its
complete 0xA0-byte `MonitorSpec` envelope admits FFFFFF60 as the final even
exact-end base and rejects FFFFFF62 before D7 or decrement scratch. The field
value stays in volatile D1 during admission; caller A0 is reloaded only after
that guard for resident identity. Malformed selected pointers therefore retain

The admitted CloseMonitor identity/count public frame is complete. It saves
D2-D7/A2-A6 only after both A6 and selected-pointer admission, restores on the
resident decrement, and restores original D0 before zero-count or late foreign-

The adjacent OpenMonitor body is staged the same way. Its narrow resident-
default owner first requires A1=NULL and D0=FFFFFFFF, then validates the exact
DefaultMonitor LONG at A6+0x18E..0x191. Those request and A6 checks now complete
through volatile D1 before D7 retains original D0. Named/other-ID and malformed
A6 calls therefore tail-chain with the original call intact.

The selected OpenMonitor DefaultMonitor pointer now has its independent
admission. The complete 0xA0-byte `MonitorSpec` admits FFFFFF60 and rejects

display ID and D0 receive the selected pointer. Malformed selected pointers

The admitted OpenMonitor increment/saturation public frame is complete. It saves
D2-D7/A2-A6 only after complete request/A6/default admission, restores while
retaining the selected D0 result after a successful count increment, and

CyberGraphX/provider monitors keep their external ownership.

`NextDisplayInfo` now follows that D0-only contract. The native database walk
keeps original-cursor provenance in volatile D1 rather than callee-saved D7;
fixed/HUNK negative-vector and AUTOINIT evidence freezes zero, immediate,
invalid, private-handle, and foreign results, with no enumeration, code-size,

The shared `FindDisplayInfo`/`ModeNotAvailable` immediate database body now has
the same public-register shape. D1 retains the original ModeID for both foreign

freezes ordinary, valid-ECS, no-ECS, invalid, and foreign results.

The separate `ModeNotAvailable` A6 capability-field envelope is now narrower
than a complete GfxBase: only recognized SuperHires records read the one-byte
`ChipRevBits0` field. That path validates NULL, even library-base alignment,
and the precise non-wrapping byte endpoint before the read, using volatile D0
while D1 retains the ModeID. Invalid, ordinary, and foreign ModeIDs never
acquire an A6 dependency merely because both public vectors share one emitted
constructor. Fixed/HUNK direct-native and AUTOINIT evidence covers the first
even base, last aligned base, exact 32-bit endpoint, first wrap, and final
addresses; a malformed base restores D0 and reaches the existing owner seam.

`GetDisplayInfoData` now separates destination admission from its later
handle/mode and public-frame work. Supported tag and minimum-size
classification runs while the requested size remains staged on the caller
stack. Complete long/word record writers require A1 to be non-NULL, even, and
no greater than the exact maximum base for the tag-selected 0x38/0x58/0x60
chunk; `FFFFFFC8`, `FFFFFFA8`, and `FFFFFFA0` therefore admit an exact
`$FFFFFFFF` final byte, while the following bases decline. The separately
documented one- through sixteen-byte `DTAG_NAME` byte writer accepts odd A1 and
uses dynamic inclusive-end carry admission. Unsupported, undersized non-name,
NULL, or wrapping requests unwind the staged value and return without touching
D2-D7/A2-A6 or the destination. Separate pre-pop and post-pop decline stubs
prevent a later handle mismatch from consuming the caller return address.

`GetDisplayInfoData` now also keeps that size staged through authoritative mode
selection. A non-NULL A0 selects the handle regardless of D2, with the private
`FFFFFFFE` compatibility handle normalized to public mode zero in volatile D0;
NULL A0 selects D2. Canonical membership and the resident-default-only
`DTAG_MNTR` rule complete before the size enters D7. Each of the 66 matched
record arms pops the size exactly once; foreign exhaustion restores original
D0 before the fallback RTS. No D2/D6 scratch is borrowed during admission.

The independent capability A6 gate now applies only after canonical mode
membership. Bit 13 of the supported tag separates `DTAG_DISP`/`DTAG_DIMS`
from read-free `DTAG_NAME`/`DTAG_MNTR`; the two capability tags then make a
membership-only pass across the canonical IDs before inspecting A6. Foreign
provider modes therefore reach the existing dispatch/fallback without an A6
read. A canonical capability request stacks its selected mode, rejects NULL,
odd, or bases greater than `FFFFFF13`, restores the selected mode on success,
and locally unwinds both it and the staged requested size on failure. This
admits the last aligned base `FFFFFF12` through the byte at `FFFFFFFE` while
rejecting the first even wrapping base `FFFFFF14`, all before D7. Default
`DTAG_MNTR` now owns its separate distant-field gate: after the default-only
mode check it validates a non-NULL even A6 through `FFFFFE6E`, reads the exact
`DefaultMonitor` LONG at `A6+0x18E..0x191`, and rejects a zero resident before
D7. The exact pointer is retained in volatile A0 and published later without an
A6 reread, avoiding a post-admission time-of-check/time-of-use split. Every
non-default monitor and non-monitor tag branches over this guard.

The admitted `GetDisplayInfoData` public frame is now complete across all four
native tags. Canonical membership remains the ownership boundary: foreign modes
continue to the existing unframed fallback, `DTAG_NAME` reaches the frame without
an A6 read, and the other admitted paths reach it only after their capability or
resident-monitor checks. `MOVEM.L D2-D7/A2-A6,-(A7)` creates a 44-byte public
frame beneath the already-staged requested size; the body loads that size from
`44(A7)` rather than borrowing a caller register before admission. Every one of
the 66 emitted records has a local result epilogue that restores the frame,
discards the staged size with the address-register `ADDQ.L` form (which leaves
CCR unchanged), and returns the record byte count in D0. This avoids distant
signed-word return branches and guarantees one restore for `DTAG_DISP`,
`DTAG_DIMS`, `DTAG_NAME`, and resident-default `DTAG_MNTR` alike.

NULL-handle/`INVALID_ID` zero-query ownership is now complete. A 68000-safe
`CMPA.L #0,A0` plus `CMPI.L #INVALID_ID,D2` prelude returns D0=0 before the
stack, tag, size, A1, or A6 is touched. Either nonmatch reaches the old entry, so
a canonical, private-default, or provider handle remains authoritative even
when D2 is invalid. The exact precedence over `DTAG_VEC` follows the portable
database's local compatibility contract; the public autodoc does not specify
that ordering, and no configured Kickstart ROM differential currently proves
it. The native-overlay length probe retains its separately documented provider
precedence.

Ordinary NULL-destination and zero-size no-write query ownership is now complete.
After the sentinel, `CMPA.L #0,A1` and `TST.L D0` select only empty candidates.
Exact `DTAG_VEC` reaches an explicit provider branch before staging. Every other
candidate saves original D0, resolves authoritative A0/private-default/D2 in
volatile D0, and passes the same 66 canonical ModeIDs used by publication. A
canonical match discards the saved value and returns `MOVEQ #0,D0`; exhaustion
restores D0 and reaches a `BRA.W`-linked local RTS clone. Thus foreign/provider
ownership precedes the empty result, while canonical no-write forms touch no A1,
capability byte, or lazy resident monitor. Nonempty supported calls branch over
this lane into the prior destination/tag/public-frame body unchanged.

Terminal provenance is part of the fixed/HUNK direct/AUTOINIT regression: the
instruction before terminal RTS is `BRA.W` for provider takeover and `MOVEQ` for
owned zero, so a coincidental zero return cannot conceal the old local stack-pop
decline. The clean red was 32 failures/16 controls over 48 routes. Independent
applied review found the emitted lane ABI-, stack-, and branch-safe, then added
four passing private-default and conflicting-handle routes and widened A1 no-
access checks to the maximum 0x60-byte chunk. Final functional gates are 374
focused, 4,278 NativeGraphics, 339 support and 1,797 scaffold; every audited
subset has zero non-passing rows. The linked delta is +732 bytes/+74 branches,
for `1,440,704 / 71,472 / 3,428 / 7 / 3,346`. This is a local compatibility
ordering pending a configured Kickstart 3.1 ROM differential, not a CyberGraphX
claim. The separate overlay length probe keeps its `DTAG_VEC`-first contract.

Nonempty unsupported non-`DTAG_VEC` ownership now uses that same authoritative
lane. The ordinary entry first recognizes exact `DTAG_VEC` and links it directly
to the completed provider terminal without staging D0. The final failed public-
tag comparison enters `emptyModeResolutionOffset` after the ordinary path's one
D0 save. Canonical membership therefore reaches the existing owned-zero
epilogue, while exhaustion restores original D0 and reaches the explicit
provider branch. The tag and mode passes remain orthogonal, with only one emitted
66-mode table shared by empty and unsupported queries.

The fixed/HUNK direct/AUTOINIT regression froze 16 canonical failures and 16
provider/publication controls before implementation. Its protected odd A1 and
invalid A6 prove that the new zero/provider decisions are data-read/write-free;
terminal opcode checks distinguish owned `MOVEQ #0` from provider `BRA.W`.
Independent review confirmed ordering, balanced stacks, preserved public
registers, signed-word-safe branches, and the exact +10-byte/+1-branch delta.
Final functional gates are 406 focused, 4,310 NativeGraphics, 339 support and
1,797 scaffold, with every audited subset at zero non-passing. The resulting

The first supported short-buffer slice is now complete for an exact eight-byte
`DTAG_NAME` identity prefix. Tag classification separates exactly eight from the

admits `FFFFFFF8` while rejecting `FFFFFFFA`. It then reuses authoritative mode

staged size, and returns eight. Foreign membership exhaustion branches directly
past this arm to the unframed provider dispatch.

The clean red froze 20 failures/12 controls across 32 fixed/HUNK direct/AUTOINIT
routes. Independent review confirmed the 68000 opcodes, precedence, inclusive

every audited subset at zero non-passing. The resulting fingerprint is
`1,440,808 / 71,482 / 3,428 / 7 / 3,346`.

The common QueryHeader prefix is now complete for every requested length 1..16.
Native pre-admission borrows volatile D1 for `size-1`, adds that to A1 in D0,
branches on unsigned carry immediately, and restores the known `DTAG_NAME`
constant on both exits. This byte-granular path removes the exact-eight arm's

reverse pushes construct a 16-byte scratch header as structure ID, resolved

advances over the destination; `SUBQ.W #1,D7` plus `DBRA` copies exactly 1..16
bytes without changing public A1. The scratch discard, requested-size reload,
MOVEM restore, staged-size discard, and RTS balance an exact 68-byte maximum
active stack window. D1 remains the public tag, D0 returns the requested count,
and admitted foreign modes bypass the frame and scratch.

The initial fixed/HUNK direct/AUTOINIT red froze 40 failures/20 controls across
60 routes. Review expansion covered every length, D1, zero/55 controls, the

NativeGraphics, 339 support and 1,797 scaffold, with every audited subset at

The coherent partial-name interval 17..55 is now complete. For requested size
N, the native arm reproduces the normal zero-filled 56-byte NameInfo, including

The emitted layout deliberately avoids a 56-byte writable scratch. After the

Valid foreign modes skip the frame/table path and retain provider provenance.

The one- through sixteen-byte `DTAG_DISP` QueryHeader slice is now complete. Its
published bytes are exactly `DTAG_DISP`, resolved ModeID, `TAG_SKIP=3`, and

The aligned 16-byte QueryHeader scratch is now tag-aware: it pushes public D1 as

The exact `DTAG_DISP` requested-size-17 slice is now complete.
DisplayInfo stores `NotAvailable` as a big-endian UWORD at offset `0x10`; its

`1,443,896 / 71,493 / 3,428 / 7 / 3,346`, exactly -6 bytes with every structural

The exact `DTAG_DISP` requested-size-18 slice is now complete. Offset `0x11`
is the low byte of big-endian `NotAvailable`: ordinary canonical modes publish

A separate full-record audit found a pre-existing default-monitor-family
classification defect outside the partial-prefix units: the 21 nonzero default-family modes omit
`DIPF_IS_PAL` in full native `DTAG_DISP`, use NTSC dimensions, and receive NTSC
names even though the portable database treats that family as PAL/default.
Keep the full-DISP, DIMS, and NAME corrections as separately tested bounded
units; do not fold them implicitly into a partial-prefix slice.

`TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` snapshot the complete 12-byte `TextExtent` result before writing and restore it after any late word failure, preserving atomic metric publication.

`SetRast` snapshots every selected plane's complete row envelope and restores the full raster if a later pixel write fails, preserving the unconditional pen-write contract without exposing partial rows.

`BltPattern` and `RectFill` snapshot the clipped selected-plane byte region before patterned writes and restore it on a later pixel failure, preserving atomic rectangle publication.

When `BltPattern` has no `AreaPtrn`, its external mask follows the classic
template path: `INVERSVID` inverts the mask's selected cells before JAM1,
JAM2, or COMPLEMENT applies the pen/minterm, while `COMPLEMENT|JAM2` keeps
the native whole-region-invert shortcut and leaves the supplied mask as the
stencil.  The portable path records that distinction explicitly so a future
CopperSharp68k implementation can share the same one-bit source contract.

`ClearScreen` snapshots the selected plane storage across both its text-prefix and remaining-row fills, restoring the complete raster if the lower span fails after the prefix has published.

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` snapshot the clipped destination byte region after source capture and restore it if a later moved or vacated pixel write fails, preserving the original overlap image.

`Flood` treats the connected-region walk as one guest operation: after complete destination and pattern preflight it snapshots the selected planar storage and restores the raster if a later pixel, pattern, or temporary-raster access fails.  This keeps failure ownership compatible with a native 68k implementation while preserving the existing caller-owned/allocator-owned `TmpRas` lifetime boundary. Direct nonzero-layer and RTG calls remain provider-owned; the validated Layers projection supplies its visibility predicate so hidden destination fragments are omitted from Flood preflight, snapshot, and publication while source connectivity remains readable through the projected layer bitmap.

`DrawEllipse` snapshots its bounded midpoint outline envelope before publishing pixels. `AreaEnd` extends that transaction across scanline fill, optional outline, and collector reset, restoring the shape bounds and leaving the recorded area retryable if a late planar write fails. Direct nonzero-layer and RTG AreaEnd calls remain provider-owned; the validated Layers projection supplies its visibility predicate through fill and outline publication so hidden clip fragments are omitted from destination preflight and rollback storage. `BltClear` snapshots its complete byte/row span, while `BltBitMap` snapshots clipped participating destination planes after its overlap-safe source capture; both restore on late writes so the host portable path has the same all-or-nothing memory boundary expected of a native Kickstart vector.

`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` snapshots its clipped destination planes after capturing source, destination, and mask state, and `BltTemplate` snapshots its clipped destination after decoding the complete template.  A late masked/template plane write therefore restores the original guest raster. Direct nonzero-layer and RTG calls remain provider-owned; the validated Layers projection supplies a visibility predicate to `BltTemplate`, so hidden clip fragments are omitted from destination preflight, snapshot, and publication.

The V36 pixel-array conversions apply the same rule at both sides of the ABI: `ReadPixelArray8` snapshots logical guest output bytes, while `WritePixelArray8` and `WriteChunkyPixels` snapshot the clipped planar destination after complete source/plane preflight.  Late array or plane faults restore the prior bytes without changing the layer/RTG provider boundary.

`BitMapScale` snapshots its clipped destination planes and the existing `BitScaleArgs` destination extent words before committing the derived scale.  A late extent or planar write failure restores both guest geometry and pixels, keeping the utility operation atomic for native-compatible callers.

User-copper `CMove` and `CWait` snapshot the six-byte pseudo-instruction before writing its three words, restoring the original instruction if a later word write fails.  The guest list remains retryable and hardware copper allocation/merge stays behind the CopperStart/native boundary.

`CBump` snapshots the current `CopList` before publishing its next pointer and count, and snapshots both current and owner copper-list envelopes during full-block rollover.  A late count or owner-link failure restores the prior guest links and frees any speculative successor block; an existing-block relink is guarded by the same owner snapshot.  This keeps the portable intermediate-list ABI retryable while allocation and hardware merge remain explicit backend concerns.

`FreeCopList` snapshots the owner `UCopList` before clearing its two public links and delays registry/allocation retirement until both writes succeed.  `UCopperListInit` snapshots the caller envelope before allocating and publishing the first block, restoring it and releasing the internal block on any late failure.  Both lifecycle operations therefore preserve the guest owner boundary for native/provider retry.

The guest `GfxBase.TextFonts` Exec list applies the same transaction rule.  `AddFont` and `RemFont` snapshot the list header, font link/flag bytes, and neighboring node links before publishing; a late link or removed-flag failure restores every touched node and leaves the font available for a retry.

`GraphicsGuestFontListBackend.Initialize` and `SetDefaultFont` snapshot the guest `TextFonts`/`DefaultFont` image envelope as well.  A failed initialization or late default-font long write therefore restores the original image bytes rather than exposing a half-built native-compatible list.

`GraphicsMemoryFontBackend.TryAdd` publishes the font accessor word before the guest list insertion and restores it if the list backend declines.  The host registration sidecar and guest `TextFonts` node therefore cross the provider boundary together.

`AllocDBufInfo` snapshots its allocator-owned guest envelope before clearing and publishing message lengths.  If either Exec message word fails late, the original DBufInfo bytes are restored before the allocator release, preserving the View/Screen double-buffer owner boundary.

`AskFont` snapshots the complete guest `TextAttr` result after range preflight and restores it on a late output-byte failure, keeping font attribute queries consistent with the transactional text metric outputs.
