Owned `TextFontExtension` publication is transactional across `tf_Extension` and `tf_Style`.  `ExtendFont` and `StripFont` restore both fields on a late write failure, retain the owned allocation for retry, and leave foreign extensions untouched.

`CloseFont` applies the same rule to the accessor word: a partial decrement is restored before the vector declines, so an already-open or removed font remains closeable and retryable.

`AllocBitMap` snapshots the public `BitMap` envelope immediately after allocation and restores it before freeing on any later geometry, plane, pointer, or displayable-flag failure.  The returned standard-planar object is therefore either fully published or absent.

The allocator boundary also rejects any returned header, interleaved block, plane, or raster range whose inclusive 32-bit guest span wraps past `0xffffffff`.  The rejection happens before clear/pointer publication, and every provisional allocation is released; this keeps a high chip address from aliasing low guest memory in either the CopperSharp68k layout or the host portable path.

If an allocator reports a failed contiguous interleaved request but leaves a nonzero provisional address, that address is released before the public bitmap header is rolled back.  On ECS/AGA the portable boundary does not publish a separate-plane replacement: `BMF_INTERLEAVED` is a required contiguous-storage form, so the call returns NULL.  OCS keeps the documented rule that the flag is ignored and allocates ordinary per-plane storage.  This preserves the display-safe row contract and prevents a false-status allocator from leaking chip storage across the compatibility/provider split.
`AllocRaster` applies the same rule to its single chip span: a false allocator status never leaves a provisional raster range live, while successful allocations still pass through the word-alignment and inclusive guest-span gates before entering the instance-owned registry.

`AllocDBufInfo` applies the same rule to screen double-buffer envelopes: a
false public allocation status with a nonzero provisional address releases the
complete `DBufInfo` span before any message fields or ownership registry entry
are published. A failed allocation therefore remains retryable for both the
CopperSharp68k guest path and the CopperScreen host adapter.

`ExtendFont` follows the same ownership boundary for its public extension
allocation. If a backend returns a nonzero provisional address with a false
status, the complete extension-plus-cloned-tag span is released before
returning failure; no `tf_Extension` or `FSF_TAGGED` publication is exposed,
so CopperSharp68k and CopperScreen adapters can retry without leaking public
memory.

`MoveSprite` snapshots the public `SimpleSprite` envelope and any attached POS/CTL words before publishing coordinates and regenerated hardware words.  `ChangeSprite` restores the original image pointer if a late long-word byte fails.  The optional sprite backend is called only after the complete guest transition succeeds, leaving sprite state retryable for native or provider-owned display projection.

`ChangeExtSpriteA` applies the same all-or-nothing rule to the complete public `ExtSprite` envelope.  A late field failure restores the prior image, geometry, allocation number, width, and flags before the hardware-facing boundary is considered claimed.

Extended-sprite creation also treats a false public allocation status with a
nonzero provisional `ExtSprite` address as an owned span. `AllocSpriteDataA`
releases that envelope before returning failure, before any chip image or
registry state is published, preserving retryable ownership for both native
68k and host adapters.

`GetGBuffers` applies the same false-status rule to each Bob/VSprite buffer:
a nonzero provisional save, border, mask, shadow, or double-buffer address is
released before the allocation enters the owned `BufferSet`. Guest pointers
and the registry therefore remain unchanged when a buffer provider declines.

`AddVSprite` and `RemVSprite` now snapshot all four reciprocal GELS links before insertion or removal.  A late link-byte failure restores the original list topology and detached-node state, so the guest list remains valid for a retry before sorting or display projection.

`InitGels` snapshots both sentinel `VSprite` envelopes, the caller-owned `GelsInfo`, and the optional collision-vector word before clearing or publishing defaults.  A late initialization failure restores the complete GELS owner boundary, including preserved caller bounds and collision state.

`SortGList` snapshots every reciprocal link it will rewrite before applying the stable signed Y/X order.  A late link failure restores the prior ordering, so sorting cannot expose a partially reordered GELS list to a native or display provider.

`InitMasks` now snapshots the complete border and collision-mask spans before publishing computed words.  A late destination failure restores both caller-owned mask buffers, keeping the true-VSprite/Bob collision state retryable.

`SetCollision` now snapshots the selected collision routine entry and restores it if the guarded long write fails late, preserving the prior callback-vector table for native/provider retry.

`AddBob` now treats Bob flags, VSprite flags, and the VSprite-to-Bob owner pointer as one guest publication.  A late owner-pointer failure restores all three fields before GELS insertion or display projection is attempted.

`RemIBob` snapshots the reciprocal VSprite links and Bob owner fields before unlinking.  If the final Bob-flag or owner-pointer publication fails, the guest list and ownership association are restored; the background restore remains the committed raster side effect of the removal operation.

`InitVPort` now has the same split boundary as the other structure initializers: the portable/register path clears the guest `ViewPort` and publishes the documented `SpritePriorities=0x24` default, while `GraphicsServices` invokes the host display-projection callback only after the complete guest range validates. This preserves the void A0-only ABI and keeps host projection out of the portable/native-compatible layer ([InitVPort autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/InitVPort)).

`InitView` follows the same failure-ownership rule: a valid guest View is cleared and claimed as a void operation, while a malformed or truncated envelope is left unclaimed with D0/cycles preserved so a native ROM or provider can retain ownership. The shared layout publishes the standard OCS/ECS origin (`DyOffset=$002C`, `DxOffset=$0081`) after the clear, matching the local default DIWSTRT baseline and the documented half-inch default placement; the values remain explicit shared constants so a future profile-aware native backend can replace them without changing the guest layout.

`GfxAssociate` treats a View/ViewPort extended-node transition as one guest operation. It publishes the new node link first, clears the previous node only when that write succeeds, and restores the new link on a late failure; the in-memory association registry is updated only after both guest writes complete. A failed association therefore leaves `GfxLookUp`, the old node, and the new node mutually consistent for a native/provider retry.

`InitBitMap` uses the same guarded envelope boundary. It snapshots only the
eight-byte writable geometry/header prefix, publishes the requested geometry,
leaves all caller-owned `Planes[]` links untouched, and restores the original
bytes if any header write is rejected. Native CopperSharp68k and host
CopperScreen paths can therefore share the guest layout without exposing a
partially initialized bitmap.

All seven portable structure initializers (`RastPort`, `View`, `ViewPort`,
`RasInfo`, `BitMap`, `AreaInfo`, and `TmpRas`) snapshot the writable
caller-owned envelope before clearing or publishing defaults. `InitBitMap`
intentionally limits that envelope to its eight-byte header and leaves
`Planes[]` storage to the caller; the other constructors apply the same
descriptor-specific boundary. If a guarded write fails after preflight, the
initializer restores the original bytes and declines, so a provider never
observes a partially initialized guest structure.

`SetRPAttrsA` and `GetRPAttrsA` use the same failure-ownership rule for V39 tag lists: the bounded `TAG_MORE`/`TAG_SKIP` chain is collected first, all touched RastPort fields or result destinations are journaled, and a late setter/output failure restores earlier pen, line-pattern, font-cache, soft-style, outline, mask, or result writes. Unknown/private tags remain ignored, while malformed chains remain available to native or provider ownership.

`GetRPAttrsA` also treats each result destination as a complete guest
envelope. A four-byte scalar result or the eight-byte `RPTAG_DrawBounds`
rectangle must fit entirely below `0xFFFF_FFFF` and start on a word boundary;
wrapped or odd output pointers are declined before any result is published,
preserving the CopperSharp68k/native boundary even when a host memory adapter
models 32-bit address wrapping.

The source RastPort fields obey that boundary too. `RPTAG_Font` and the
layer-owner read used by `RPTAG_DrawBounds` go through checked long-word
addressing, so a high RastPort whose field offset wraps cannot satisfy the
query from a low alias. Pure and register-level calls preserve their result
buffers and D0 for native/provider fallback.

RastPort scalar state vectors now use the same checked guest-address envelope as the structure and drawing paths. `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, `SetABPenDrMd`, `SetWriteMask`, `SetMaxPen`, the scalar getters, `SetOutlinePen`, and `Move` reject a non-null high pointer whose field or line-pattern phase would wrap at the 32-bit boundary. This prevents a malformed RastPort from aliasing low guest memory while preserving the register adapter's native/provider fallback state.

The SetWriteMask seam preserves the public ABI independently of the compact
guest field layout: its portable and host-facing entry points take a ULONG,
then store only the low eight bits in `rp_Mask`. High register bits therefore
cannot alter adjacent RastPort state, while direct, tag-list, and register
paths share the same byte-accurate result ([SetWriteMask autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetWriteMask), [RastPort layout](https://d0.se/include/graphics/rastport.h)).
The mapped native-overlay differential fixture also exercises a high-bit input
through the captured jump-table vector, proving that direct and future native
entry paths publish the same byte and return state.

The remaining portable RastPort consumers now use the same checked field
helpers rather than constructing `rastPort + offset` directly. Initialization,
`Draw`, `PolyDraw`, `RectFill`, `BltPattern`, `DrawEllipse`, `ScrollRaster`,
`SetRast`, `AreaEnd`, `Flood`, `ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `EraseRect`, and
their rollback/preflight paths therefore reject a wrapped field before reading
or publishing it. `RPTAG_WriteMask` and the tag-list journal share that
envelope, keeping the entire text/drawing slice aligned for both
CopperSharp68k guest memory and the CopperScreen host adapter.

Decoded-font text now applies the RastPort's signed `TxSpacing` after every character, including the final character, consistently in `Text`, `TextLength`, `TextExtent`, and `TextFit`, while preserving the leading negative-kerning exclusion used by the native advance result. `TextExtent` and `TextFit` retain the complete movement cell in their horizontal bounds, so proportional glyph ink and trailing spacing cannot produce different fit decisions. `Text` also preflights every character and every bit-packed glyph row before drawing, so a malformed final character cannot leave a partially rendered string in the planar destination ([RastPort `TxSpacing`](https://d0.se/include/graphics/rastport.h), [TextLength description](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html), [TextExtent description](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextExtent.html)).

Text metric reads now validate their own guest envelopes in the portable core, not only at the CopperStart gateway. RastPort font/cache fields and `TextFit` constraint extents reject high pointers whose 32-bit field addresses would wrap, so a pure CopperSharp68k-compatible call cannot alias low memory simply by bypassing the host adapter.

At the register boundary, `TextLength` treats a null `RastPort.Font` as the
legacy cached fixed-metric state, but a non-null pointer must decode through
the selected guest font backend. An undecodable foreign font is left for
native Kickstart or a provider rather than being silently reinterpreted as
cached width/spacing state. A zero-count request still validates a non-null
selected `TextFont` but does not consume the cached `TxWidth` word; only the
legacy null-font path uses that cache for an empty query. This keeps a valid
decoded-font no-op independent of stale RastPort cache bytes while preserving
the compatibility path's fixed-cell behavior.

The `TextExtent` result envelope is likewise treated as a native 68k
structure: `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` require an even guest
address before reading or publishing their 16-bit fields. Odd result pointers
remain untouched and unclaimed for the native/provider boundary rather than
being byte-processed by a host implementation.

Decoded `TextFont` pointers used by `SetFont`, text rendering, metrics, and
soft-style queries carry the same even-address requirement. The host backend
is not allowed to make an odd foreign font look portable simply because it can
return synthetic metrics; native 68000 ownership remains available for that
address-error case.

RastPort bases used by the text/font-state vectors carry that same native
word-alignment rule. `SetFont`, `AskSoftStyle`, `SetSoftStyle`,
`TextLength`, `TextExtent`, and `TextFit` reject an odd RastPort before reading
cached fields, even when the host byte-memory model could otherwise decode
them. The zero-count `Text` no-op remains unconditional, while non-empty text
continues to rely on the planar bitmap envelope; this keeps CopperSharp68k and
CopperScreen ownership aligned without claiming a host-only odd-address
interpretation.

The shared drawing-state accessors now enforce that same rule for the
non-text RastPort vectors. `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, `GetAPen`,
`GetBPen`, `GetDrMd`, `SetABPenDrMd`, `SetWriteMask`, `SetMaxPen`,
`GetMaxPen`, `GetOutlinePen`, `SetOutlinePen`, and `Move` reject an odd base
before consuming or publishing byte/word state. Area and primitive paths that
reuse those helpers inherit the boundary, so a host byte-addressable odd
object remains available to native 68000 or provider ownership.

The same rule applies to `GfxNew`: every public extended node is allocated only
when the returned guest span is word-aligned and stays inside the 32-bit
address space. A rejected allocator result is freed before any node bytes or
registry association are published, leaving malformed ownership to native
Kickstart or the selected provider.

All graphics/Intuition `TagItem` walkers use the matching envelope rule:
initial lists and `TAG_MORE` continuations must be even-aligned before a
longword is read. This keeps `BestModeIDA`, `OpenScreenTagList`, RastPort
attributes, sprite tags, and best-pen tags compatible with a native 68000
address-error boundary while leaving malformed or foreign chains available to
their original owner.

`GfxAssociate` applies the same alignment gate to the public View/ViewPort
pointer used as the association key; malformed odd keys never enter the
registry and cannot be returned by `GfxLookUp`.

Algorithmic text styling follows the classic baseline geometry: italic shear is derived from the font baseline countdown rather than the decoded strike height, and underline is one run-wide line covering the complete consumed text cell (including inter-character spacing) when the font has a usable row below the baseline. Bold smear uses the decoded `tf_BoldSmear` width exactly, including a valid zero-smear value. These rules keep the portable planar renderer aligned with a future CopperSharp68k glyph provider without introducing CyberGraphX color-font behavior.

`Text` now honors `FPF_REVPATH` at the rendering boundary as well as in its metrics: a negative-advance glyph cell is anchored immediately to the left of the pen, and algorithmic underlines follow that same consumed cell. The normal left-to-right strike bit order is preserved so a native/CopperSharp68k font provider can share the decoded glyph contract without a second bitmap representation.
Underline range admission also reuses the algorithmic style envelope: bold smear and italic padding are included in the run-wide line just as they are in `TextExtent`, so combined styles do not leave an un-underlined styled edge. The pure renderer and its destination preflight share this expanded range before publishing pixels or `CurrentX`.

Soft-style state follows the byte-sized Kickstart contract independently of
which transforms the portable renderer currently knows how to draw:
`AskSoftStyle` returns the complement of the intrinsic `TextFont.tf_Style`
byte, and `SetSoftStyle` ignores enabled bits that are intrinsic, updates the
remaining bits in `RastPort.AlgoStyle`, and returns the resulting algorithmic
byte combined with the intrinsic style.  Underline, bold, and italic are the
portable transforms; extended and future bits remain provider/native-defined
so their state is preserved without inventing a host rendering policy.

The style-query read set is intentionally narrower than the rendering read
set. `AskSoftStyle`/`SetSoftStyle` need only the `TextFont.tf_Style` byte plus
the RastPort algorithmic-style byte; they must not demand strike rows,
`CharLoc`, or metric fields that are irrelevant to the resident vectors. A
future CopperSharp68k implementation can therefore query a partially mapped
resident font without accidentally making the portable glyph renderer claim
that same font.

The native 68k admission mirrors those exact read/write sets before its first
RastPort access. `AskSoftStyle` validates only the `RP.Font` LONG and therefore
admits even bases through `0xFFFFFFC8`. `SetSoftStyle` also reads and writes
`RP.AlgoStyle`, so its last valid even base is `0xFFFFFFC6`. NULL, odd, and
wrapping bases tail-chain with the complete original arguments and public
register frames intact. The host query keeps admission separate from its ULONG
value because `0xFFFFFFFF` is a valid complement result, not a failure sentinel.
These are base-library rules; CyberGraphX retains its independent provider
patches.

`AskFont` follows the same separation: its resident read set is the font node
name pointer, `tf_YSize`, `tf_Style`, and `tf_Flags`, followed by a complete
eight-byte `TextAttr` output transaction. It must not reuse the lifecycle
validator’s nonzero-strike rule, because querying a readable zero-height font
is distinct from selecting or rendering that font.

The renderer also rejects provider glyph advances outside the signed guest `CharSpace` word before entering its cell traversal. This keeps malformed host/native font data fail-closed and preserves the all-or-nothing destination preflight guarantee.

`ScrollRasterBF` no longer aliases `ScrollRaster`: the normal vector fills newly exposed pixels from `BPen`, while the BF variant clears them through the non-layered `EraseRect` behavior. Layered calls remain explicitly owned by the layer provider, where the real backfill hook can run ([ScrollRasterBF backfill contract](https://www.build.alb42.de/fpcbin/docu/amigaos4/intuition/scrollwindowraster.html)).

Positive area patterns remain source masks in `COMPLEMENT` mode: only pattern 1 bits toggle the destination, and `COMPLEMENT|INVERSVID` selects the zero bits. This keeps `RectFill`, `AreaEnd`, and patterned flood behavior aligned with the documented draw-mode/minterm contract instead of complementing every pixel in the rectangle.

`BltPattern` keeps its typed helper wide enough for checked guest addressing,
but the register adapter consumes the documented D4 WORD mask byte count.
Upper-half register residue cannot change the guest stride or force a valid
stencil into native/provider fallback; malformed or unreadable masks still
decline before any destination write.

The clear/erase writer uses the same clipped destination rectangle for
preflight, snapshot, and publication. Signed-WORD bounds far outside a planar
bitmap therefore remain harmless no-ops outside the drawable area without
forcing the host path to walk every off-screen coordinate.

`BltBitMapRastPort` carries the destination RastPort's write mask into the
minterm operation, so a masked destination plane is preserved. The separate
`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` path intentionally keeps its documented behavior of
ignoring `RastPort.Mask` while applying its one-bit source stencil.

`ClipBlit` uses the same destination-mask rule for its non-layered
RastPort-to-RastPort form. The portable path reads `RastPort.Mask` before the
bitmap transaction and declines layered ports first, preserving the provider
boundary while keeping masked destination planes unchanged.

All RastPort fields consumed by the portable blit family (`Layer`, `BitMap`,
`Mask`, and template destination state) pass through a checked 32-bit address
envelope. This is important for the future native 68k layout: a malformed
high pointer must remain available to native/provider ownership instead of
wrapping into an unrelated low-memory field.

The active `LoadView` fingerprint extends through each linked `RasInfo` and
the display-relevant standard-planar `BitMap` fields (geometry, depth, and
the guest `Planes[]` links). It hashes those plane-pointer fields rather than
pixel bytes at the linked storage: a valid one-row/two-byte display raster
must not require a four-byte read merely to decide whether the view changed,
and changing pixel contents alone is not a display-topology change. The three
public `View` longwords are themselves read through a checked 32-bit envelope,
so a high `View *` cannot wrap its LOF/SHF fields into low memory. A caller may
reuse the same `View *` while changing the nested scanout envelope; that
change is therefore visible to the native-compatible publication boundary
without making unchanged loads rebuild copper state.

CPR wrapper and raw copper-list candidates follow the same rule: the wrapper's
`cpr_Start` field and each scanned instruction word must be addressable without
32-bit wrap before the host queues a custom-chip publication. This keeps a
malformed high list from aliasing an unrelated low-memory copper stream.

Negative `AreaPtSz` multicolor patterns retain the native two-mode split:
JAM1 treats the decoded planes as a nonzero stencil and writes `APen`, while
JAM2 writes the decoded color. `INVERSVID` complements the source planes
before this decision, and `COMPLEMENT|JAM2` remains the whole-region invert
operation.

An explicitly attached `TmpRas` is now sized per operation. `AreaEnd` requires the 16-pixel-word-aligned byte envelope of the largest decoded polygon or ellipse bounding rectangle and consumes that buffer as the one-bit areafill mask, while `Flood` retains full destination-raster capacity because its connected region can span the entire bitmap and consumes the buffer as its visited bitmap. Flood connectivity is independent of AreaPt pattern emission: suppressed stencil cells still enqueue their neighbors, so patterned fills do not stop at a zero bit. `AreaEnd` also treats its outline decision as part of the atomic guest operation and fails closed if the RastPort flags word cannot be read, without resetting the recorded area stream. When the real graphics-library core sees an unset `RastPort.TmpRas`, both `AreaEnd` and `Flood` now allocate temporary guest Chip raster storage through the allocator boundary, clear it before the operation, and release it on success or failure; explicitly attached descriptors remain caller-owned and strict. The direct portable helpers retain host-workspace compatibility overloads for transitional callers, while the core/native-compatible path is guest-backed ([InitTmpRas reference](https://erikarn.github.io/amiga/docs/Amiga_ROM_Kernel_Reference_Manual_v1.3.pdf), [Graphics Primitives](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Graphics_Primitives)).

`ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` follow the Kickstart contract that clearing uses pen zero, except when the RastPort's base draw mode is `JAM2` (mode 1), where `BPen` supplies the clear colour. `COMPLEMENT` is not a clear-background selector; `INVERSVID` remains an orthogonal flag. The portable helper therefore inspects the base-mode bits and keeps the host/native boundary free of a second clear policy ([ClearEOL/ClearScreen autodocs](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/ClearEOL.html), [ClearScreen](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/ClearScreen.html)).

`SetRast` is an unconditional planar initialization operation: it preflights the complete bitmap, then writes the requested pen through the current plane mask and does not apply the RastPort's active `DrawMode` (so `COMPLEMENT` cannot toggle the existing raster instead of setting it). `RectFill`, `BltPattern`, and the other pattern-aware primitives continue to apply the draw mode separately; `RectFill`/`BltPattern` now preflight every selected destination plane in the clipped region before publishing any pixels, so a malformed late row cannot leave a partial rectangle. RastPort setters that update multiple guest fields (`SetOutlinePen` and `Move`) preflight the complete destination span, preserving atomic state when a truncated guest structure cannot accept the full update ([SetRast autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html)).

`ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, and non-layered `EraseRect` share the same complete clipped-fill preflight, so a malformed later destination row fails without partially clearing earlier rows. Their existing `JAM2`/background-pen and text-geometry rules remain unchanged.

The classic compatibility implementation also reaches the clear fill through `SetAPen` twice (temporary clear pen, then the original `FgPen`), and `SetAPen` restarts `linpatcnt` at 15. The portable `ClearEOL`/`ClearScreen` path publishes that same phase boundary after all selected-plane writes; it snapshots and restores the phase and bitmap if the final phase store fails, while leaving `FRST_DOT` and the caller's pens untouched. This is implementation evidence from the classic-compatible AROS path rather than an additional autodoc promise ([AROS ClearEOL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/cleareol.c), [AROS ClearScreen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/clearscreen.c), [AROS SetAPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c)).

The same classic `SetAPen` boundary surrounds non-layered `EraseRect`: the compatibility path temporarily selects `BgPen`, fills, then restores `FgPen`, so the portable standard-planar vector publishes a fresh `linpatcnt=15` after its clipped fill and restores both raster bytes and phase on a failed final store. Layered `EraseRect` remains an explicit provider/native operation and does not enter this portable state transaction ([AROS EraseRect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/eraserect.c)).

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` publish the same fresh phase after a real standard-planar move and vacated-area fill: AROS uses `SetABPenDrMd`/`RectFill` for the normal path and `EraseRect` for backfill, so both variants select the RastPort's `BPen` for vacated cells. The portable scroll transaction preflights and snapshots `linpatcnt` alongside the clipped destination, restoring both if the final phase store fails; clipped/no-op normal scrolls retain their unchanged-raster boundary ([AROS ScrollRaster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollraster.c), [AROS ScrollRasterBF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollrasterbf.c)).
An explicit zero-displacement guard applies the same rule to both vectors: after validating the guest source/destination storage, a valid `dx=dy=0` request returns without writing pixels or changing `linpatcnt`. This keeps a true no-op separate from a real move and from a fully vacated `ScrollRasterBF` clear.

`ScrollRaster` now preflights its clipped destination after taking the complete source snapshot and before publishing moved or vacated pixels. This keeps the logical-coordinate snapshot rule intact while preventing a malformed destination row from exposing a partial scroll.

`DrawEllipse` uses the same atomic destination rule: midpoint points are collected, every outline point must remain inside a non-layered bitmap, all selected planes are probed, and only then are the outline writes published. This preserves the Kickstart non-layered no-software-clipping contract while keeping the portable memory boundary fail closed; layered clipping remains provider-owned.

`BltClear` now probes its complete byte/row span before applying the requested zero or fill-word pattern, preventing a malformed late byte from exposing a partial clear.

Line state keeps the classic `RastPort.Flags` first-dot bits guest-visible. `Move()` starts a fresh segment by setting `FRST_DOT`; a line with that bit set draws its starting pixel and consumes the bit, while a subsequent connected line preserves the shared endpoint in `COMPLEMENT` mode instead of toggling it twice. `linpatcnt` is the current line-pattern preshift (`SetDrPt()` publishes 15 for the first pattern bit), and the phase advances by the line's major-axis distance rather than by the number of emitted samples. The phase still advances for a skipped shared start, so pattern continuity is independent of endpoint suppression. `ONE_DOT` is the blitter line-mode `ONEDOT`/`SING` rule: at most one emitted sample is published for each horizontal raster row, while the Bresenham traversal and line-pattern phase continue through suppressed samples. The flag remains persistent across `Draw` calls; layer clipping remains provider-owned ([`rastport.h` line flags](https://d0.se/include/graphics/rastport.h), [blitter `ONEDOT` definition](https://d0.se/include/hardware/blit.h), [line-mode reference](https://www.winnicki.net/amiga/memmap/LineMode.html)).

`ScrollRaster` keeps its source snapshot in the caller's logical rectangle coordinates before clipping to the destination bitmap.  A rectangle that starts or ends outside the RastPort therefore vacates pixels according to the true source bounds instead of treating the clipped edge as a new origin; `ScrollRasterBF` retains the separate non-layered `EraseRect`-style clear policy.

Non-layered rectangle and full-raster clears validate touched planar storage by contiguous row-byte spans before publishing pixels.  This preserves the complete failure boundary for wide guest bitmaps while avoiding repeated per-pixel probes of the same planar byte; the later fill still uses the shared pixel helper for draw-mode and plane-mask semantics.  Layer clipping, damage, and backing-store selection remain provider-owned.

`Draw` now preflights the complete Bresenham/pattern traversal and the RastPort fields it updates after the raster pass before publishing any pixels. `PolyDraw` first snapshots its complete guest coordinate stream and then preflights every connected line destination before moving or drawing, so malformed point storage or a later unreadable plane cannot expose a partial chain. A malformed later destination row therefore fails atomically, while clipped points and zero write-mask no-ops retain the shared planar primitive semantics.

The register adapter now keeps the 68k ABI separate from portable helper status: RastPort setters (`SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, `SetABPenDrMd`, `SetWriteMask`, and `SetFont`), `Move`, `Draw`, area construction/fill, rectangle/ellipse/scroll/clear/erase primitives, `PolyDraw`, `Text`, and `LoadView` are void vectors and leave D0 cleared after invoking the portable operation. Pen/mode setters preflight both their target byte and the associated line-pattern phase, so a truncated guest RastPort cannot publish a partial state update. Status-bearing vectors such as `SetOutlinePen`, `Flood`, `ReadPixel`, and `WritePixel` retain their documented D0 results. This lets the portable layer fail closed internally without exposing a host-only status convention to native callers ([SetAPen autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetAPen), [SetDrMd autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetDrMd), [Draw autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Draw), [RectFill autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/RectFill), [Text autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Text), [LoadView autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/LoadView)).

The first portable slice now contains the V40 manifest, guest layout constants, explicit memory/allocation/blitter/display/font contracts, RastPort state initialization and pen/mode/write-mask/outline/MaxPen attributes plus V39 `SetRPAttrsA`/`GetRPAttrsA` tag-list routing, planar pixel/line/rectangle/PolyDraw operations, guarded min-depth planar `BltBitMap` and non-layered `ClipBlit` with overlap snapshots and minterms, `BltClear` byte-count/rows/fill-word modes, `BltBitMapRastPort`, masked planar `BltMaskBitMapRastPort`, clipped bit-offset `BltTemplate` with complete template/destination preflight before mutation, `BltPattern`, area-pattern-aware `RectFill`/`AreaEnd`/seed-color `Flood`, validated `InitTmpRas`, operation-specific capacity checks for explicitly attached temporary rasters in AreaEnd/Flood, explicit-backend `OwnBlitter`/`DisownBlitter`/`WaitBlit` ownership calls, guarded V40 `QBlit`/`QBSBlit` node validation with an optional scheduler queue sidecar, clear-line/screen and non-layered erase behavior, integer midpoint `DrawEllipse` with non-layered no-software-clipping validation, non-layered seed/outline `Flood`, guarded `AreaInfo` initialization that preflights caller-owned coordinate/flag storage plus 5-byte-per-vector `AreaMove`/`AreaDraw` recording with coordinate/flag-table preflight, two-vector `AreaEllipse` center/radius recording, and non-layered integer scanline `AreaEnd` filling with shape-bound/no-clipping/pattern preflight plus complete-destination Flood preflight before mutation, allocator-backed guest-compatible `Region`/`RegionRectangle` lifecycle and rectangle/region boolean operations, snapshot-based non-layered `ScrollRaster`/`ScrollRasterBF`, guarded `InitBitMap` geometry initialization that preserves caller-owned plane links, portable standard-planar `AllocBitMap`/`FreeBitMap` with clear/interleaved allocation, strict ECS/AGA failure for unavailable contiguous interleaved storage plus OCS ignore semantics, rollback, overflow-safe teardown, and readable standard-friend stride negotiation with malformed/foreign friend rejection, native bitmap readers requiring even byte-per-row strides and word-aligned display planes before publication, chip-memory `AllocRaster`/`FreeRaster` sizing through the allocator boundary, pure V39 `GetBitMapAttr` geometry/flags queries, allocator-backed `AttachPalExtra`/ColorMap palette-sharing envelope publication, pure RasInfo viewport bitmap association with depth/row-layout validation, guest `TextAttr`/`TextFont`/`TextFontExtension` layouts, portable `AskFont`/`OpenFont`/`CloseFont`/`AddFont`/`RemFont`/`ExtendFont`/`StripFont` lifecycle operations with accessor tracking, cached and guest-`TextFont` text metrics (`TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent`) with signed-spacing and 32-bit overflow guards, bit-packed proportional glyph rendering with `tf_CharSpace`/`tf_CharKern`, documented `INVERSVID` text-cell and line-pattern behavior, explicit-extent precedence in `TextFit`, soft-style state queries/updates, algorithmic underline/bold/italic rendering, and View/ViewPort/RasInfo initialization with documented InitVPort SpritePriorities default plus bounded multi-viewport `LoadView` validation, validated `ScrollVPort`, profile-aware native PAL/NTSC `GetVPModeID` mapping for the canonical lores/hires/interlace, HAM, extra-halfbrite, dual-playfield, and PF2-priority keys (runtime sprite/genlock controls are stripped before key matching), six-plane display records and DIPF property chunks, first-slice public `AllocDBufInfo`/`FreeDBufInfo` guest envelopes, DBufInfo-aware planar `ChangeVPBitMap` association with an explicit display-rebuild boundary, and scheduler-aware `LoadView`/`WaitTOF`/`VBeamPos`/`WaitBOVP` publication through an explicit host display adapter. Layered drawing, text, pixel, area, and RastPort blit vectors now fail closed at the portable register adapter so layers.library or a future provider retains clipping/damage/backing-store ownership; this does not claim layer clipping semantics. Structure clears preflight the full guest range, invalid view/viewport/RasInfo chains are rejected before display callbacks, and invalid `InitVPort` pointers no longer invoke host display projection callbacks. Portable validation now precedes the host copper-construction boundary for `MakeVPort`/`MrgCop`; actual copper instruction allocation and merge remain backend-owned. Pure-memory RastPort/View/BitMap operations plus decoded-font text, metric, attribute, lifecycle, allocation, planar blit, pattern/mask, template, scroll, area-recording/fill, flood, region, temporary-raster setup, mode-ID, double-buffer envelope, bitmap-switch, copper-gateway, blitter-gateway, and display-gateway vectors are now covered by focused tests; CyberGraphX-owned RTG bitmap allocation/free/attribute/blit paths remain owned by its separate patches. Guest-compatible host-shim `GfxBase.TextFonts`/`DefaultFont` publication now mirrors font-node links and `FPF_REMOVED` state; exact ROM/disk font weighting, external extension ownership, full font fallback, temporary-raster consumption, remaining area/flood edge cases, advanced blit clipping, queued blitter ownership/timing, circles/ellipses beyond the recorded AreaInfo item, layer clipping/damage, synchronized safe/display message signaling, copper instruction parity, friend/displayable policy, bitmap copy/sync helpers, full display mode database, and ROM-overlay eligibility remain later goal gates.

Host/provider classifiers validate arithmetic before inspecting linked guest fields. A high `ViewPort`, `View`, or `RastPort` address therefore cannot wrap into low memory and be misclassified as an RTG/layer object, preserving the native ownership boundary even when the host bus happens to map the wrapped address.

The bitmap allocator now treats `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` as a capability result: it retains the bit only when every allocated chip plane is word-aligned and, when the optional `IGraphicsDisplayMemory` sidecar is present, each complete plane span belongs to the provider's native display-DMA address class. An odd or non-DMA allocation remains usable as a standard planar bitmap and is published as non-displayable. This keeps `GetBitMapAttr(BMA_FLAGS)` honest before the stricter `LoadView`/displayable-swap readers inspect the surface; bitmap copy/sync helpers remain open.

`BltClear` now accepts the documented V36 combination of rows/bytes-per-row mode and fill-word mode. The packed `byteCount` continues to select row geometry, while the upper `Flags` word is repeated into every row; odd `memBlock` addresses are rejected at the native word-aligned blitter boundary, and complete destination preflight remains shared with byte-count and rows-only clears.

The layer-ROM slice now has its own `IGraphicsLayerBackend` seam. Portable and host-gateway tests cover guest-vector ABI behavior, nested `LockLayerRom` depth, immediate `AttemptLockLayerRom` failure while held, release via `UnlockLayerRom`, zero-pointer rejection, and callback forwarding for lock ownership plus `SyncSBitMap`/`CopySBitMap`. CopperStart can inject all three lock callbacks for a layers/native owner; without them, the default backend tracks ownership without interpreting the private `Layer`/`ClipRect` layout. Layered `RPTAG_DrawBounds` queries now have an optional `IGraphicsLayerRasterBackend.TryGetDrawBounds` hand-off, while the portable path still owns only non-layered bitmap bounds. Synchronization is claimed only by an explicit provider, while clipping, damage, and actual SuperBitMap/ClipRect copying remain later layers/native work.

`AttachPalExtra` now owns a guest-compatible V39 palette-sharing envelope: it validates the associated `ViewPort`, derives the sharable span from the first RasInfo bitmap depth when that guest chain is present (limiting sub-8-plane viewports to 2^depth entries), allocates/clears the `PaletteExtra`, WORD reference-count, and WORD linked allocation-list blocks through the public allocator, publishes `ColorMap.PalExtra`, supports same-viewport idempotence, rejects conflicting reattachment, and releases all three blocks from `FreeColorMap`. Its leading 0x2E-byte `SignalSemaphore` is initialized with `NT_SIGNALSEM`, an empty guest `MinList`, and zero owner/nesting/queue state, matching the public `PaletteExtra` layout while leaving task scheduling to the Exec/native boundary. Portable pen, ColorMap, and VideoControl entry points serialize each allocation on a host lock corresponding to that semaphore, so sidecar reference counts and guest palette bytes cannot interleave across host calls. Pen obtain/release operations now mirror the classic free/shared linked-list invariants, WORD reference counts, and exclusive entries into that envelope. `pe_SharableColors` is treated as the highest sharable pen index, so a value of N exposes entries 0..N inclusive; non-sharable entries remain available to exclusive `ObtainPen` requests but are excluded from shared nearest-color selection and from the synchronized free/shared counts. `ObtainPen` and `ObtainBestPenA` now fail closed when the `ColorMap` has no attached `PaletteExtra`, matching the documented Kickstart contract that pen acquisition is unavailable without the palette-sharing envelope ([ObtainPen autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/ObtainPen.html)). `ObtainBestPenA` now parses the documented `OBP_Precision`/`OBP_FailIfBad` tag pair, considers only sharable entries, increments shared references without rewriting an occupied palette entry, allocates a free entry when the nearest color is outside the requested tolerance, and fails or returns the nearest shared entry according to `OBP_FailIfBad`. The named precision presets retain their documented 8-bit RGB values, while the arithmetic accepts any non-negative precision value and squares it in a checked 64-bit intermediate, matching the reference implementation's tolerance expression ([AROS ObtainBestPenA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c), [ObtainBestPenA autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node0306.html)); exact ROM color-distance calibration and scheduler-visible semaphore behavior remain later parity gates.

The G14 foundation slice now adds allocator-backed guest ColorMap storage with separate high/low nibble tables, RGB4/RGB32 set/load/get behavior, shared/exclusive pen reference tracking, nearest-color lookup, and a guarded VideoControl subset. `VTAG_VIEWPORTEXTRA_SET/GET` updates the native `ViewPortExtra` association through the GfxNew-owned registry, `VTAG_NORMAL_DISP_SET/GET` and `VTAG_COERCE_DISP_SET/GET` store/query the portable ModeID-backed display handles, and private `VTAG_VPMODEID_SET/GET/CLR` controls the native mode-query override. Classic GET tags now publish their SET/CLR snapshot in-place, while only the V40 query tags retain external output buffers. The layout-backed V39 state family now also covers chroma/bitplane key flags, user-copper clipping, batch-mode/list publication, border sprites, sprite-resolution/default resolution, playfield/sprite color-base words, chroma-plane selection, and full-palette mode through the documented ColorMap fields; `VTAG_CHROMA_PEN_SET/GET/CLR` and PF-to-sprite-priority SET/GET use allocation-owned private sidecars because the public ColorMap has no fields for them. Immediate copper application, native palette publication, and custom-chip copper timing remain explicit provider/native gates. The portable path now owns bounded `VTAG_BATCH_ITEMS_ADD` guest-list append and transactional replay at `MakeVPort`, while the mapped native overlay declines pointer-bearing batch setters/`ADD` for provider ownership. Foreign extended-node types and display handles are rejected so a later CyberGraphX patch can claim its own path. `ObtainBestPenA` now has pure and register-level coverage for tag parsing, sharable-pen filtering, tolerance selection, free-pen allocation, shared reference release, and `PaletteExtra` count/byte publication. Palette projection remains an explicit host/native boundary; CyberGraphX continues to own RTG palette behavior. ROM error-metric/free-entry scaling, the `PaletteExtra` semaphore protocol and exact allocation-list meaning, and scheduler-visible OCS/ECS/AGA palette publication remain later gates. The public precision values and tag IDs follow `graphics/view.h` ([Classic M68k graphics/view.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/view.h)); the documented contract still requires a tolerance-aware nearest-color search and `OBP_FailIfBad` failure behavior ([ObtainBestPenA autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ObtainBestPenA)).

The G19 foundation slice now adds the V36 byte-per-pen pixel-line and pixel-array gateways, V40 `WriteChunkyPixels`, pure `ScalerDiv`, and pure planar `BitMapScale`. Guest arrays retain the documented 16-pixel row stride (or explicit V40 source stride), scaled rectangles derive and write `BitScaleArgs` destination extents from the documented factors, reads/writes are clipped to the planar raster with deterministic failure checks, and the A0/A1/A2 register contract is kept separate from the pure memory conversion. Pixel-array operations preflight the complete guest array and every touched planar source/destination plane before mutation, so truncated arrays and malformed later planes cannot expose partial updates. When a non-null temporary RastPort is supplied, its layer, one-row padded BitMap geometry, depth, plane links, alignment, and complete temporary row envelopes are validated before the conversion claims the vector; the host-only null-temporary form remains supported as a transitional direct-conversion path. `BitMapScale` now derives extents with the documented nearest-integer `ScalerDiv` rule, samples each axis with the centered native DDA schedule, snapshots every source sample, probes its selected destination planes, and rejects aliased planar storage even when source and destination use distinct `BitMap` headers before publishing derived extents or pixels. Layered RastPorts and CyberGraphX/RTG endpoints remain explicit fallback boundaries; remaining bitmap utility parity is a later gate ([ScalerDiv](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ScalerDiv), [AROS bitmapscale.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c)).

The pixel-array row helper also widens the 16-pixel padding calculation before
rounding. A requested rectangle whose width would round beyond the 32-bit
guest address contract is declined before `CanAddressArray` or any planar
read/write, rather than relying on an intermediate `ULONG` wrap to reject it.
This keeps the portable failure boundary deterministic for both CopperStart
and a future CopperSharp68k-native array adapter.

`FreeBitMap` ownership is kept at the portable graphics-library instance boundary: only a structure returned by that instance's `AllocBitMap` is eligible for teardown, and successful release removes the ownership token so a foreign instance or a second release cannot free arbitrary guest/RTG storage. A failed structural validation retains the token for a later retry; provider-owned bitmap paths remain separate.

The native overlay admits this standard-planar bitmap lifecycle only after the
same ownership check: a mapped `AllocBitMap` publishes a host-allocated guest
envelope and planes, while malformed friends, failed allocations, and foreign
or repeated `FreeBitMap` calls decline without consuming D0/cycles, allowing
the captured Kickstart vector to retain the call.

`BMF_MINPLANES` now follows the V39 contract at the guest-memory boundary: the bitmap envelope is allocated only through the requested depth's plane-pointer span, while all portable readers and teardown derive that compact structure size from the published flag/depth. Full eight-plane `BitMap` storage remains the default; RTG-specific minimum-plane/provider behavior is still outside this OCS/ECS path.

`InitBitMap` is deliberately narrower than bitmap allocation and consumption.
The resident initializer writes `BytesPerRow`, `Rows`, `Flags`, `Depth`, and
the padding word, but does not inspect or clear `Planes[]`. The portable
constructor therefore snapshots only the eight-byte header, publishes those
fields atomically, and leaves plane-link readability and display ownership to
the bitmap consumers. This preserves the CopperSharp68k field layout for
sparse or provider-backed plane tables ([AROS `InitBitMap`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initbitmap.c)).

`SetFont` keeps the same split between guest state and provider ownership. A
NULL font is first resolved through the font backend's default-font boundary,
then the selected font's metrics and the RastPort cache are published as one
transaction. A backend with no default owner declines without touching the
RastPort, leaving the call available to a native GfxBase or provider. The
register adapter may resolve the guest `GfxBase->DefaultFont` itself, but the
pure core follows the same contract ([AROS `SetFont`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setfont.c)).

`SetRPAttrsA` preserves that boundary for `RPTAG_Font=0`: the pure tag walker
passes zero into `SetFont` so the backend can resolve the current default,
while the mapped adapter may supply its already-resolved guest default. The
two paths therefore share the same cache transaction and no-default fallback,
without moving font-list ownership into the tag parser ([AROS `SetRPAttrsA`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setrpattrsa.c)).

`DisposeRegion` follows the same ownership boundary for `NewRegion` results. Boolean operations may continue to edit a valid guest region, but only the graphics-library instance that allocated the region can reclaim its rectangle chain and Region envelope; layer-installed or provider-owned regions remain outside this portable registry.

The G18 foundation slice now adds a deterministic native default/PAL/NTSC ModeID registry for lores, hires, interlace, and hires-interlace combinations plus guest-compatible `DTAG_DISP`, `DTAG_DIMS`, `DTAG_MNTR`, and `DTAG_NAME` data chunks. The zero monitor part (`DEFAULT_MONITOR_ID`) is enumerated before explicit PAL and NTSC records and uses the portable PAL geometry fallback when no active profile is supplied; CopperScreen/native display adapters now resolve that default timing through the active machine profile without changing guest IDs. `FindDisplayInfo`, `NextDisplayInfo`, `ModeNotAvailable`, `GetDisplayInfoData`, and guarded `BestModeIDA` tag-list selection share the same registry and documented availability/header contracts; `GetDisplayInfoData` gives a non-null handle precedence over its optional ID argument, while a null handle can query the real default-mode ID `0`. `DTAG_DISP` reports the 140/70/35 ns horizontal mode resolution, `DTAG_DIMS` reports the 362/724/1448-pixel PAL/NTSC/SuperHires hardware envelope, and `DTAG_MNTR` reports physical PAL/NTSC rows, 280 ns color-clock width, legal view range, minimum active row, and monitor compatibility rather than nominal viewport height. When a matching `OpenMonitor` object is owned by this graphics instance, the `MonitorInfo.Mspc` field points at it; zero-monitor-part records resolve to that same resident active-profile `MonitorSpec`, and the pointer remains stable after close while `ms_OpenCount` is zero. `BIDTAG_ViewPort` supplies validated viewport geometry/depth, uses a native ColorMap/`ViewPort.Modes` association when no explicit host provider exists, and keeps strict explicit-provider monitor association, with `BIDTAG_SourceID` precedence. Handles are represented as ModeIDs at this portable boundary. `BestModeIDA` rejects out-of-range UWORD/UBYTE fields, conflicting property masks, and source/viewport monitor mismatches before scoring native records, preserving the classic source/monitor compatibility boundary for a later monitor provider. `OpenMonitor`/`CloseMonitor` now allocate one resident documented guest `MonitorSpec` prefix per native PAL/NTSC family and change only its open count, while unknown monitor requests remain an explicit fallback boundary. `CoerceMode` now derives a native mode from validated viewport dimensions/bitmap depth, honors canonical viewport HAM/dual-playfield/interlace feature keys, rejects unsupported native keys, and applies `PRESERVE_COLORS`/`AVOID_FLICKER` filtering; `GetVPModeID` now falls back to validated native `ViewPort`/`ColorMap` state when no explicit host mode provider is available, mapping `vp_Modes` through the active PAL/NTSC profile; full native monitor timing/property database parity remains a separate display-database gate.

The display-database handle distinction is now explicit: `FindDisplayInfo`
returns the private nonzero handle for the valid zero default ModeID, while
`NextDisplayInfo` returns public ModeID keys and therefore yields zero first.

The portable G18 timing boundary now uses one immutable PAL/NTSC monitor
envelope for both `DTAG_MNTR` and resident `MonitorSpec` publication.  Rows,
color-clock width, Denise legal columns, minimum active row, PAL `BEAMCON0`,
and the legal view rectangle are consequently shared by the guest query and
the future CopperSharp68k/native monitor owner instead of being duplicated in
two host paths.  The pure regression compares both monitor families field by
field; provider-owned monitor records remain a separate seam.

The earlier G18 wording that limited `MonitorInfo.Mspc` to an already-open
monitor is superseded: a native `DTAG_MNTR` query now lazily creates the same
resident PAL/NTSC node through the monitor registry, with a zero public
`ms_OpenCount` until an explicit `OpenMonitor` acquires it. This keeps the
display-record pointer stable without claiming foreign monitor families.
The same display boundary now carries ECS display-register capability separately from PAL/NTSC timing. ECS SuperHires records stay queryable so `DisplayInfo.NotAvailable` can explain why an OCS machine cannot use them, while `BestModeIDA` and `CoerceMode` refuse to select those records when the active chipset lacks ECS display support. The portable default remains capability-enabled for host-independent tests, and the A500 host path publishes `DI_AVAIL_NO_CHIPS` through both `ModeNotAvailable` and `DTAG_DISP`.

The screen lifecycle mirrors that capability boundary: an OCS
`OpenScreenTagList` request carrying an ECS SuperHires display ID is left for a
native/provider implementation, while an ECS request clamps explicit
`SA_Depth` to SuperHires' two-plane hardware envelope before allocating the
guest bitmap.

`SA_DisplayID` is treated as an optional tag: when absent, the legacy
`NewScreen.ViewModes` remains authoritative; when present, `DEFAULT_MONITOR_ID`
(`0`) is a valid native ID and every other unknown ID remains available to a
native monitor or provider path without synthetic state or error-code writes.
The corresponding Intuition overscan query also leaves an OCS rectangle
untouched for an unavailable SuperHires ModeID.

`SA_BitMap` is an ownership-bearing request rather than a geometry hint.  A
validated standard-planar `BitMap` is borrowed by the portable screen path:
the screen RastPort/RasInfo chain points at the caller's header and planes,
while the embedded Screen bitmap receives only a compatibility header copy.
Close and rollback never free or rewrite that caller-owned storage.  Malformed
headers, unsupported bitmap families, and CyberGraphX/RTG storage remain
unclaimed so native Intuition or the provider patch can install them.

The same handoff applies to the `SA_PubName`/`SA_PubSig`/`SA_PubTask` family:
public-screen list membership and visitor-notification task ownership are
Intuition responsibilities, so the private synthetic screen session declines
those requests instead of publishing an unlinked screen.

The private synthetic screen session also declines a second legacy
`OpenScreen` or tagged `OpenScreenTagList` while its Screen is live. Reusing
the existing guest pointer would make a replacement caller appear to own the
original Screen and could mutate the active ViewPort geometry beneath a
display that is already published. The decline leaves the live Screen,
`GfxBase->ActiView`, and any caller-owned `SA_ErrorCode` destination untouched;
`CloseScreen` remains the explicit teardown boundary before a fresh synthetic
screen can be staged. Native Intuition retains ownership of true multi-screen
and public-screen list semantics.

`ScreenToFront` follows the same ownership split. For the one private
synthetic Screen, the Intuition bridge re-enters the scheduler-aware
`LoadView` handoff for that Screen's View, restoring `GfxBase->ActiView` and
the queued compatibility copper stream after a blank or temporary foreign
publication. A screen not owned by this session still goes through the
provider viewport-selection seam and is not interpreted as a standard-planar
screen by the compatibility path.

When `OpenScreenTagList` receives a non-null legacy `NewScreen`, its public
prefix is validated even if the tag list supplies every geometry field.  An
unreadable prefix is not treated as `NULL`; the call remains available to the
native/provider implementation with no synthetic screen or success code.

The G15 lifecycle slice now also provides allocator-backed `ViewExtra` and `ViewPortExtra` guest structures through `GfxNew`/`GfxFree`. `GfxAssociate` replaces and cleans previous pointer associations, `GfxLookUp` is registry-backed, and freeing a node removes its association before returning memory to the explicit allocator; unsupported extended-node types remain outside the native boundary. `MakeVPort` follows the public temporary-node lifecycle: when no caller-owned `ViewPortExtra` is associated it allocates one, publishes `VPXF_FREE_ME`, and rolls it back on failed copper construction; DUALPF construction requires the second RasInfo node before allocation or copper publication; replacing a temporary association with a caller-owned node reclaims the displaced allocation and clears the free-me marker; successful `FreeVPortCopLists` reclaims a still-associated temporary or any registry-owned ViewPortExtra carrying the documented free-me marker.

The native overlay now admits only the independently proven portion of that
extended-node lifecycle: mapped `GfxNew` allocates and initializes a node in
the active graphics instance, while mapped `GfxFree` requires that ownership
token before releasing it. Foreign, repeated, and unsupported calls retain
the captured Kickstart vector and their original D0/cycle state. Arbitrary
guest-pointer association keys are now safe because the registry uses them
only as opaque keys: mapped `GfxAssociate` requires an instance-owned node,
and mapped `GfxLookUp` reads only the registry. A foreign node still remains
resident/provider-owned.

`CalcIVG` is deliberately split at the display/copper boundary. The portable core validates the guest `View`/`ViewPort` envelopes, while an optional CopperStart/native provider counts the scan lines consumed by the actual merged copper stream. When no provider is installed, the register adapter leaves the vector unclaimed so a higher-level dispatcher can chain to Kickstart or a later native implementation; the current host gateway then retains its existing compatibility fallback. The portable path never returns an invented timing value. This follows the documented meaning of `CalcIVG` as the number of viewport resolution scan lines needed to execute all viewport copper instructions ([MorphOS graphics reference](https://morphos-team.net/sdk/graphics.html)).

`SetChipRev` follows the same explicit capability boundary. Its D0 request and D0 result are routed through an optional CopperStart/native provider; the provider enables only bits available on the configured Agnus/Denise/Alice/Lisa profile, treats `SETCHIPREV_BEST` as “all available,” and keeps the result monotonic for the lifetime of the graphics instance. The host shim publishes the resulting byte at the native `GfxBase->ChipRevBits0` offset, while a ROM implementation retains ownership of its own full `GfxBase` image. The OCS/ECS host path is covered by production guest-vector tests; AGA capability mapping is represented in the boundary but remains gated by the emulator's current AGA execution support. This matches the documented `SetChipRev` contract ([SetChipRev autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetChipRev)) and the `GfxBase` capability flags/layout ([gfxbase.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/gfxbase.h)).

The G16 copper lifecycle slice now includes the guest-side `FreeVPortCopLists` teardown contract: after validating the complete `ViewPort` range, DspIns, SprIns, ClrIns, and UCopIns are cleared, then the viewport owner is offered to an optional native teardown boundary. The four-link clear is snapshot/rollback atomic, so a guarded write failure restores the original guest ownership record and no native callback is invoked; the register adapter can therefore leave D0/cycles untouched for provider fallback. CopperStart's compatibility builder uses that callback to reclaim its tracked wrapper/raw allocations and to retire replaced viewport lists. `MakeVPort` returns the documented `MVP_NO_VPE` or `MVP_NO_DISPLAY` status when its validated guest prerequisites are unavailable, including a missing DUALPF second RasInfo and CopperStart's undisplayable-viewport result, and propagates `MVP_*` results from status-aware native builders, while successful calls retain `MVP_OK`. When no caller-owned `ViewPortExtra` is associated, `MakeVPort` creates a temporary public node marked `VPXF_FREE_ME`, rolls it back if copper construction fails, and leaves caller-owned nodes untouched; a caller association displacing that temporary node reclaims it, while a transferred temporary node clears the marker; successful `FreeVPortCopLists` reclaims any still-associated registry node carrying the marker. `MrgCop` preserves `MCOP_NOP` for empty Views and propagates `MCOP_OK`/`MCOP_NO_MEM` from status-aware native backends. The host compatibility projection now preflights and walks every linked `ViewPort.Next` node with a bounded cycle guard, builds each node's DspIns state, keeps the first node's CPR wrapper active, and reuses the same full-chain rebuild during display rethink/palette refresh; malformed chains leave the existing View CPR links untouched. General intermediate/hardware copper storage remains owned by the explicit CopperStart/native backend until profile-specific allocation and full multi-viewport merge semantics are implemented.

The host-facing G16 follow-up makes the rebuild transaction explicit: a later viewport projection failure restores the prior View CPR links, every affected DspIns pointer, and the compatibility ownership registry before returning `MCOP_NO_MEM`. Replacement `MakeVPort` wrappers are allocated before the prior wrapper is retired; if program memory is exhausted after a raw chip copper list was built, that raw list is released and the prior View/CPR/DspIns publication remains retryable with `MVP_NO_DISPLAY`. The rebuilt CPR registry now returns wrapper addresses (rather than raw starts), so rollback and teardown release each wrapper/raw pair exactly once. For ordinary linked ViewPorts, the first active raw list is extended in place with a bounded vertical wait and the later viewport streams; if the fixed compatibility buffer cannot hold the complete merge, the transaction returns `MCOP_NO_MEM` and releases every speculative wrapper. The host `MrgCop` register path now distinguishes `MCOP_NOP`, `MCOP_OK`, and `MCOP_NO_MEM`; display rethink skips publication after a failed non-empty chain rebuild, preserving the already active copper stream. This follows the documented merge-result contract ([MrgCop autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/MrgCop)) while remaining a compatibility projection boundary, not a claim of exact Kickstart instruction ordering or custom-chip merge timing.
The G16 copper lifecycle slice now includes the guest-side `FreeVPortCopLists` teardown contract: after validating the complete `ViewPort` range, DspIns, SprIns, ClrIns, and UCopIns are cleared, then the viewport owner is offered to an optional native teardown boundary. The four-link clear is snapshot/rollback atomic, so a guarded write failure restores the original guest ownership record and no native callback is invoked; the register adapter can therefore leave D0/cycles untouched for provider fallback. CopperStart's compatibility builder uses that callback to reclaim its tracked wrapper/raw allocations and to retire replaced viewport lists. `MakeVPort` returns the documented `MVP_NO_VPE` or `MVP_NO_DISPLAY` status when its validated guest prerequisites are unavailable, including a missing DUALPF second RasInfo and CopperStart's undisplayable-viewport result, and propagates `MVP_*` results from status-aware native builders, while successful calls retain `MVP_OK`. When no caller-owned `ViewPortExtra` is associated, `MakeVPort` creates a temporary public node marked `VPXF_FREE_ME`, rolls it back if copper construction fails, and leaves caller-owned nodes untouched; a caller association displacing that temporary node reclaims it, while a transferred temporary node clears the marker; successful `FreeVPortCopLists` reclaims any still-associated registry node carrying the marker. A single-viewport `MakeVPort` rebuild now preserves an already-published multi-viewport `View.ViewPort` head and LOF/SHF CPR links when the selected viewport is not the head, replacing only that node's `DspIns`; `MrgCop` remains responsible for publishing a new complete chain. `MrgCop` preserves `MCOP_NOP` for empty Views and propagates `MCOP_OK`/`MCOP_NO_MEM` from status-aware native backends. The host compatibility projection now preflights and walks every linked `ViewPort.Next` node with a bounded cycle guard, builds each node's DspIns state, keeps the first node's CPR wrapper active, and reuses the same full-chain rebuild during display rethink/palette refresh; malformed chains leave the existing View CPR links untouched. General intermediate/hardware copper storage remains owned by the explicit CopperStart/native backend until profile-specific allocation and full multi-viewport merge semantics are implemented.

The compatibility copper projection now translates the canonical OCS/ECS ViewPort mode feature bits into the corresponding BPLCON0 controls: HAM, dual-playfield, and ECS superhires are retained when MakeVPort rebuilds a display list, while Hires and Interlace continue to map directly. This keeps the shared guest `ViewPort.Modes` layout usable by both CopperSharp68k and CopperScreen without treating mode IDs as raw hardware register values.

The CopperStart synthetic Intuition screen handoff now preserves the single-playfield HAM, Extra-Halfbrite, SuperHires, and Interlace mode bits when it creates the guest `ViewPort`, allows the SuperHires raster width and profile-aware interlace height, and publishes all six requested OCS/ECS planes for HAM/EHB (including when the NewScreen depth is left at zero). Synthetic dual-playfield screens additionally publish a second `RasInfo` node that shares the standard-planar bitmap, allowing graphics.library's existing two-node ViewPort/copper projection to run without inventing a distinct host surface; distinct playfield bitmap ownership remains a graphics/provider boundary.

The same compatibility projection now consumes the complete dual-playfield `RasInfo` pair. Distinct playfield bitmaps contribute their bounded, word-aligned plane pointers in alternating hardware order and publish the combined BPLCON0 depth for each legal 1+1, 2+1, 2+2, 3+2, or 3+3 distribution; their palette banks are emitted as `COLOR0..COLOR7` for playfield A and `COLOR8..COLOR15` for playfield B, bounded by each playfield's declared depth. The shared-bitmap construction used by the host screen shim retains its existing total-depth layout instead of duplicating planes. Missing, malformed, or over-depth second playfields fail closed before copper allocation/publication, while CyberGraphX-owned RTG surfaces remain outside this path.

The dual-playfield priority mode is projected independently through BPLCON2: the canonical `PlayfieldBitAssignment` mode bit emits PF2-first priority, while every non-DPF or ordinary DPF viewport explicitly emits zero so a rebuilt copper stream cannot inherit a prior priority selection. This keeps the mode-ID contract separate from raw custom-register values for both CopperSharp68k and CopperScreen.

RasInfo horizontal scrolling is split at the same boundary: the coarse word portion advances each playfield's bitplane pointers, while the residual 0..15 pixel delay is emitted as PF1/PF2 fine-scroll fields in BPLCON1. Negative guest offsets use floor division so the pointer and fine delay remain a coherent hardware pair; shared dual-playfield backing mirrors the fine delay into both fields.

Distinct dual-playfield bitmaps also retain independent row strides: BPL1MOD is derived from playfield A's `BytesPerRow` and BPL2MOD from playfield B's, while the shared-bitmap compatibility path intentionally emits the same modulo to both registers.

The display-height projection is bounded by both distinct rasters. A second playfield with fewer available rows (after its `RyOffset`) shortens the generated DIW stop before copper publication, matching the first-playfield envelope rule and preventing the compatibility list from fetching beyond either declared raster.

The CopperStart provider now follows the Kickstart 3.1 `CalcIVG` arithmetic:
each compatibility `DspIns` stream retains its generated display-instruction
prefix count separately from appended `UCopIns`, and the host callback applies
the selected monitor color-clock divisor, rounding, OCS/ECS floor, and lace or
scan-double scaling. Unbuilt, foreign, malformed, and provider-owned streams
still fall through to the native/provider owner.

The host compatibility builder also has a bounded user-copper bridge: a `ViewPort.UCopIns` pointer is walked through validated `UCopList`/`CopList` chains, and only the classic MOVE/WAIT pseudo-instructions are translated into the generated hardware stream. Cycles, unreadable envelopes, unsupported opcodes, inconsistent counts, and fixed-list capacity overflow fail closed before replacing the existing View/CPR links. Exact Kickstart instruction placement, WAIT timing, and multi-list merge ordering remain native CopperSharp68k/CopperScreen parity gates; CyberGraphX does not claim this OCS/ECS path.

Synthetic `OpenScreen` also derives a zero-height request from the active video profile rather than the PAL host default: standard height is `256` for PAL and `200` for NTSC, with Interlace doubling the selected default before the profile maximum is applied. Explicit heights continue to be clamped to the same profile-aware envelope.

The standard Intuition bridge also exposes `OpenScreenTagList` as a separate OCS/ECS handoff. Explicit `SA_Width`, `SA_Height`, `SA_Depth`, native PAL/NTSC or zero-monitor-part default `SA_DisplayID`, signed `SA_Left`/`SA_Top`, `SA_Title`, bounded `SA_DClip` fallback geometry, profile-aware `SA_Overscan` defaults, legacy/default `DetailPen`/`BlockPen`, `SA_Pens`, explicit `SA_DetailPen`/`SA_BlockPen`, initial `SA_Colors`, `SA_Colors32` interleaved RGB triplets, `SA_Interleaved`, and the classic title/behind/quiet/autoscroll booleans override the legacy `NewScreen`/`ExtNewScreen` request. The V39 `SA_SharePens` boolean is also projected to the guest `PENSHARED` screen flag, while actual palette ownership remains outside this graphics-side handoff. Default-monitor mode keys resolve against the active PAL/NTSC machine profile for screen geometry and overscan queries. Owned screens publish the classic `CUSTOMSCREEN` type nibble and standard-planar bitmap classification; accepted standard opens initialize the optional `SA_ErrorCode` word to zero. The standard Intuition `ShowTitle` vector toggles the published `Screen.SHOWTITLE` bit, `GetScreenData` copies bounded prefixes for owned custom and standard-screen queries while projecting the requested Workbench/Public type, and `QueryOverscan` publishes profile-aware native PAL/NTSC rectangles; foreign screens and non-native display IDs remain available to native/provider ownership. The guest `Screen.DefaultTitle` and current `Screen.Title` pointers are published for legacy/tagged opens and `SetWindowTitles`; `STDSCREENWIDTH`/`STDSCREENHEIGHT` retain profile defaults. RGB32 values are reduced to the four-bit-per-gun values consumed by OCS/ECS COLOR moves; RTG display IDs and custom bitmap selection remain in the CyberGraphX/native scanout boundary. This keeps the guest Screen/ViewPort envelope shared by CopperSharp68k and CopperScreen without allowing the host compatibility path to claim RTG scanout.

`OpenScreenTagList` decodes both the explicit and `ExtNewScreen` extension chains before mutating the synthetic screen request. A missing `TAG_DONE`, a wrapped/unmapped item, a cycle, or bounded tag-walk exhaustion returns a null screen without applying a decoded prefix; a null list and a null `TAG_MORE` continuation are treated as empty valid lists. The register callback retains the classic D0 screen-pointer result, so a later native Intuition or CyberGraphX provider can claim malformed or non-native requests without observing half-applied geometry.

The same checked-address discipline covers the AreaInfo collector used by the drawing primitives: the `rp_AreaInfo` link, AreaInfo envelope, and vector/flag table advances are validated before `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, or `AreaEllipse` can publish state. This keeps CopperSharp68k guest layout and CopperScreen host memory behavior aligned at the failure boundary.

The AreaInfo flag table is now deliberately guest-native rather than a
portable-private encoding: `MOVE=0`, `DRAW=1`, `CLOSEDRAW=2`, and `ELLIPSE=3`.
Starting a new polygon or appending an ellipse closes a preceding DRAW item in
the same way as Kickstart—either by adding the first vertex with CLOSEDRAW or
by retagging an already matching final vertex—before publishing the new item.
This keeps the stream directly consumable by a future native 68k graphics
implementation while retaining the host decoder as a separate path.

Scroll operations retain the native distinction between a completely
vacated source and a partially shifted source. `ScrollRaster` leaves a region
unchanged when either absolute displacement reaches the logical width or
height; `ScrollRasterBF` uses the same move boundary but clears that fully
vacated region through the EraseRect-style `BPen` path. The portable host path
keeps the source snapshot and rollback boundary around both cases.

The same host projection now consumes a valid guest `ViewPort.ColorMap`/`ColorTable` for OCS/ECS COLOR moves, masking each stored RGB4 high-nibble word to the 12-bit hardware register. Synthetic display palettes retain their explicit host precedence, while malformed or foreign color-map storage stays on the existing compatibility fallback boundary until native palette ownership is available.

The standard-planar copper builder also proves the complete displayed plane envelope after applying each `RasInfo.RxOffset`/`RyOffset`. A nonzero plane pointer that cannot cover `BytesPerRow × displayedRows` is rejected before allocation or CPR publication, so `MakeVPort` reports `MVP_NO_DISPLAY` instead of emitting DMA addresses into unmapped memory. This is an OCS/ECS host projection guard; CyberGraphX remains responsible for RTG surface validation.

The host projection applies the same rule to the linked structure itself. `ViewPort.RasInfo`, `RasInfo.BitMap`, the complete BitMap plane table, and both dual-playfield RasInfo nodes are read through checked 32-bit field envelopes before any nested pointer is added. RasInfo source offsets are widened before conversion to a DMA displacement, and the resulting plane span must remain inside the 32-bit guest address space before the chipset address adapter is consulted. A high structure whose `BitMap` field would wrap into a low-memory alias therefore fails before allocating or replacing a copper wrapper; an existing `DspIns`/View CPR publication remains intact. This keeps the guest layout directly consumable by CopperSharp68k while giving CopperScreen a transactional host boundary, and leaves RTG/CyberGraphX surface ownership separate.

The same projection boundary covers optional palette and user-copper links. `ViewPort.ColorMap`, `ColorMap.ColorTable`, `UCopList`, `CopList`, and `CopIns` fields are read through checked field helpers, and the complete instruction block is admitted only when its byte envelope fits in the guest address space. A malformed present ColorMap falls back to the compatibility palette without reading a wrapped low alias; a malformed user-copper wrapper rejects the new build before replacing the prior DspIns/CPR state. These links remain guest-layout compatible for CopperSharp68k while CopperScreen receives no partially decoded or partially published stream.

The final `MakeVPort` publication step preflights the exact `View.ViewPort`, LOF/SHF CPR, and `ViewPort.DspIns` fields it will write. A host-only builder call with a wrapped `View` or `ViewPort` pointer therefore declines before allocating or retargeting any guest link; the field envelope is treated as one publication boundary even though CopperScreen stores the generated raw list separately.

Scheduler-facing viewport reads and synthetic-screen teardown use the same field helpers. Beam waits, active-viewport detection, mode lookup, and close-time DspIns/CPR clearing no longer rely on an unchecked addition followed by a wrapped bus probe, keeping a malformed host pointer from turning a wait or teardown into a low-memory mutation.

After portable `SetRGB4`/`LoadRGB4` commits a registered guest ColorMap, an active standard-planar ViewPort requests the same guarded copper rebuild used by display rethink. The active-chain check is bounded and RTG scanout is excluded, so palette changes for inactive or provider-owned ViewPorts do not mutate the current hardware stream.

The G16 copper lifecycle slice now also provides the guest-compatible `UCopperListInit`/`CINIT` allocation contract.
