A caller-owned `UCopList` is validated, its internal public `CopList` and six-byte `CopIns` buffer are allocated and cleared, and `FirstCopList`/`CopList`/`CopPtr`/`MaxCount` are published at the documented 68k offsets. Intermediate `CMove`, `CWait`, `CBump`, and macro-equivalent `CEND` now write guarded pseudo-instructions using the classic A1/D0/D1 ABI; a full block lazily rolls to a successor block with allocator rollback, and registry-owned `FreeCopList` clears owner links before releasing every block. `FreeCprList` now validates the exact public 12-byte `cprlist` envelope and forwards the pointer through an optional native resource-owner callback; private hardware deallocation, copper merge/publication, and profile-specific parity remain separate follow-on units. CyberGraphX does not claim this OCS/ECS path.

The G17 double-buffer lifecycle slice now tracks `AllocDBufInfo` ownership per graphics-library instance and asks an explicit display-capability boundary whether the selected mode supports double buffering. The native CopperStart `ScrollVPort`/`ChangeVPBitMap` boundary now requests a causal copper rebuild for the active planar view, publishes the previous bitmap to the host scheduler, and queues the DBufInfo safe and display messages at successive profile-owned frame boundaries through the existing Exec reply service. Untimed gateway calls anchor that schedule to the live CPU cycle; timed calls preserve their explicit cycle. Both timed and untimed `WaitBOVP` paths now reach an explicit host vertical-blank boundary, so the host adapter cannot silently turn the public wait into a no-op. Palette vectors now use the same optional timed boundary: portable ColorMap storage is committed first, then `LoadRGB4`/`LoadRGB32`/`SetRGB4`/`SetRGB32` callbacks receive the guest call cycle instead of being rebased to cycle zero; a present but malformed or foreign viewport ColorMap fails closed before any host palette publication. `LoadView` publishes or clears the guest-compatible `GfxBase->ActiView` pointer on the host shim, validates every linked `RasInfo` envelope, and rejects a present malformed standard-planar `RasInfo.BitMap` before publishing the view. That envelope requires nonzero row geometry, every declared plane link, and a readable `BytesPerRow × Rows` storage range for each declared plane; null bitmap links remain legal while a screen is assembled, and `LoadView(NULL)` clears the active publication without mutating guest View memory. `ScrollVPort` deliberately keeps bitmap-envelope validation provider-owned because its display boundary may still be assembling the scanout surface. RTG scanout remains owned by CyberGraphX, and the portable `ChangeVPBitMap` gateway now explicitly declines both RTG replacement bitmaps and viewports already attached to RTG memory. The portable host path enforces a live DBufInfo envelope returned by the same graphics-library instance; the native AmigaBoot shim additionally accepts a mapped guest envelope for Kickstart-compatible callers. Successful `FreeDBufInfo` first cancels any pending scheduler replies for the safe/display message pair, then releases storage, preventing a later frame boundary from touching a stale message port. `FreeDBufInfo(NULL)` is a claimed no-op; nonzero foreign and duplicate frees are rejected before touching the allocator. Synthetic VBlank counters, queued copper publication, title redraw waits, and the no-input `WaitPort` compatibility wait all sample the active bus beam clock, so NTSC/ECS field geometry cannot be silently replaced by the PAL frame constant. The safe/display message split follows the documented `DBufInfo` ownership and message contract ([AllocDBufInfo autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocDBufInfo); [RKRM graphics changes and additions](https://developer.amigaos3.net/sites/default/files/downloads/2024-02/RKRM%20changes%20and%20additions-%282021-12-26.pdf)); exact Kickstart timing, frame ownership, and ROM Exec delivery remain separate parity gates.

For interlaced NTSC/ECS publication, the queued copper source retains both the View's `LofCprList` and `ShfCprList` resolutions until the safe frame boundary. Selection is made from the canonical Agnus beam clock's `IsLongFrame` state at that boundary, so a View changed during a long frame publishes its short-frame list on the next alternating boundary. A single resolved CPR source (including the existing ViewPort/DspIns fallback) is copied to both slots, preserving progressive/PAL behavior and the malformed/empty-view ownership rules. This is a field-length publication rule; field parity and full hardware copper merge remain separate parity gates.

An assembling `View` with no viewport or CPR links is a legal intermediate
publication. When it replaces a View whose copper list is still queued for the
next frame, the queue is retired without writing the custom-chip copper pointer;
the already-visible stream remains unchanged until a complete provider-owned
chain is ready. This keeps `GfxBase->ActiView` and hardware ownership from
desynchronizing during screen construction.

The DBufInfo message boundary follows the same profile-owned frame clock. A native AmigaBoot `ChangeVPBitMap` request made during an NTSC long or short frame queues `SafeMessage` at the next Agnus frame start and `DispMessage` at the following start; message delivery remains behind the existing Exec reply service and never substitutes the PAL frame constant. Focused host coverage exercises this ordering on the alternating NTSC/ECS profile in addition to the PAL lifecycle case.

If one host scheduler quantum crosses both queued frame boundaries, the pending
messages are drained by due cycle (stable insertion order for equal cycles), so
the earlier `SafeMessage` remains ahead of the later `DispMessage` in the guest
reply port. This keeps catch-up behavior observationally equivalent to stopping
at each intermediate frame boundary.

The mapped-guest DBufInfo path keeps the same 68k envelope rule as the
instance-owned allocator path: the complete public structure must be readable
and word-aligned before `ChangeVPBitMap` can publish a swap. An odd address is
not rescued by a byte-readable span, so the portable gateway preserves D0,
cycles, the current `RasInfo.BitMap`, and the display-rebuild callback for
native/provider ownership.

Both direct and timed host entries complete this guest envelope validation
before querying a status-aware presentation adapter. Capability discovery is
therefore not observable for malformed native requests; only a valid viewport
reaches the provider's acceptance boundary.

Timed native viewport rebuilds carry the guest call cycle through the explicit CopperStart host seam. `ScrollVPort` and `ChangeVPBitMap` may be invoked through a direct host gateway without updating the emulator CPU state first; the host must therefore queue the rebuilt copper stream from the supplied cycle, not from a stale host-side sample. Guest `DspIns` links may be rebuilt immediately, but custom-chip copper registers remain frame-boundary-owned. Untimed CopperScreen/native callbacks remain available when the host itself owns the current-cycle source.

Synthetic `CloseScreen` teardown now clears the complete public `ViewPort` copper-link quartet (`DspIns`, `SprIns`, `ClrIns`, and `UCopIns`) after retiring compatibility-owned wrappers. This keeps the guest viewport reusable and aligns the host screen hand-off with the portable `FreeVPortCopLists` envelope contract while leaving foreign screens unclaimed.

The same teardown boundary validates the embedded `ViewPort.ColorMap` pointer
against the compatibility-owned palette before releasing it. A native/provider
owner may reuse the screen's viewport while replacing that link; until it
restores or detaches the foreign map, `CloseScreen` preserves the active view
and returns failure instead of freeing the old map or clearing provider-owned
state.

The embedded `Screen.BitMap` is checked with the same identity rule: its
published geometry, flags, depth, and declared plane pointers must still match
the compatibility backing header before teardown. This prevents a provider
that repoints a screen plane from being mistaken for the private bitmap owner;
the request remains retryable after the original guest link is restored.

`ChangeVPBitMap` keeps the same display geometry contract at the swap boundary:
the replacement must match the attached bitmap's stride, depth, and non-zero
row count before `RasInfo.BitMap` is published. A zero-row current header is
treated as an assembling viewport with no established height, so the first
concrete replacement may establish that field; once the current header has a
row envelope, a mismatch is declined transactionally and the prior association
remains visible. This keeps geometry-only assembly useful without allowing a
live viewport to swap to a bitmap with a different display height.

The host-facing `ChangeVPBitMap` paths also run the bounded viewport envelope
before publishing the swap. This keeps malformed or cyclic secondary
`RasInfo` nodes and nonzero `ViewPort.ExtendedModes` on the native monitor or
provider path, while the pure two-argument association helper remains
available for screen assembly before presentation ownership is established.

The host `LoadView` bridge now has a status-aware callback in addition to its legacy void action. Copper publication is resolved before `_currentViewAddress` and the guest-compatible `GfxBase->ActiView` pointer are committed; a non-empty view whose CPR source cannot be resolved is therefore a no-op at the host boundary and leaves the previously active hardware stream intact. `LoadView(NULL)` replaces any queued mid-frame copper request with a blanking request at the next safe frame boundary, and the queue is clamped beyond the finalized presentation horizon before custom-register writes are scheduled. Empty assembly views and CyberGraphX-owned front viewports retain their explicit ownership paths.

The synthetic Intuition `RethinkDisplay` bridge follows that same final handoff: after a successful linked-`ViewPort` rebuild and CPR resolution it publishes `GfxBase->ActiView`, while a failed rebuild leaves the prior guest pointer and hardware stream untouched. This keeps the host screen path aligned with the native `MrgCop`/`LoadView` sequence without moving CyberGraphX or layers ownership into the portable graphics core.

Screen font selection keeps the public `Screen.RastPort` and `Window.RPort`
boundaries distinct. `SA_SysFont=1` may select a screen-preference font for the
screen while retaining `GfxBase->DefaultFont` for a window; the compatibility
provider currently supplies the same reset-scoped Topaz font for both, but the
state boundary is preserved so a future CopperSharp68k/native preference
source can diverge without changing the guest structures.

The G20 foundation slice now adds per-library simple-sprite ownership for the eight hardware sprite slots plus guarded guest state for `MoveSprite` and `ChangeSprite`. `GetSprite` and `FreeSprite` preserve the V36 `SimpleSprite` offsets and failure write-back contract; movement writes the documented x/y words and regenerates the standard OCS/ECS `SPRxPOS`/`SPRxCTL` words when the caller supplies a valid `PosCtlData` envelope, adding viewport Dx/Dy offsets, converting hires/interlace coordinates, preserving `SPRITE_ATTACHED`, and preflighting malformed position data before changing guest coordinates; image changes rebind the validated sprite-image pointer, while an optional `IGraphicsSpriteBackend` receives the committed transitions for host/native DMA publication. Extended-sprite conversion accepts the documented 16/32/64-pixel hardware widths, -2..2 X/Y replication factors, transparent right-padding for narrow source bitmaps, and attached 3rd/4th-plane data with V39-compatible attach markers. `GetExtSpriteA` and `ChangeExtSpriteA` now expose typed provider callbacks for `GSTAG_SOFTSPRITE` and `GSTAG_SCANDOUBLED`; portable OCS/ECS requests remain local, while provider decline is transparent in native-overlay mode. Exact scheduler ownership, profile-specific active-View offsets, and display DMA remain explicit host/native gates.

`AllocSpriteDataA` also accepts the legacy `SPRITEA_OldDataFormat` source
shape without widening the public 68k structures: the packed two-plane words
are read four bytes into the caller-supplied address, the required
`SPRITEA_OutputHeight` bounds the source rows, the requested 1..16-pixel width
is masked before conversion, and a fixed 16-pixel `ExtSprite` envelope is
published through the same allocator/registry transaction as standard planar
bitmaps. Attached and wide legacy requests, missing height, and truncated
guest rows remain explicit declines. This follows the classic tag contract
([`graphics/sprite.h`](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node060B.html)) and the reference conversion structure in
[`AROS AllocSpriteDataA`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c).

The G12 queue slice now claims the public `QBlit` and `QBSBlit` vectors without executing guest function pointers in the host process. It validates the packed 68k `struct bltnode` prefix (`n`, function, status, blit size, beam sync, cleanup), rejects unreadable or callback-less nodes before submission, and forwards the node to the existing blitter boundary. Hosts that need to preserve the QBS class and signed VBEAM value implement the optional `IGraphicsQueuedBlitterBackend`; older adapters retain the address-only `Submit` fallback. The status-aware CopperStart adapter declines `OwnBlitter`, `DisownBlitter`, `WaitBlit`, `QBlit`, and `QBSBlit` when no scheduler/custom-chip owner is supplied, leaving D0 and cycles untouched for native Kickstart or another provider; callback-backed adapters claim the same vectors and preserve queue metadata. This keeps queue ownership, callback execution, FIFO fairness, cleanup signaling, and custom-chip timing in the scheduler/native boundary, matching the V40 QBlit/QBSBlit contract ([`hardware/blit.h`](https://d0.se/include/hardware/blit.h), [QBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/QBlit), [QBSBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/QBSBlit)).

The G20 extended-sprite slice adds the standard V39 planar forms of `AllocSpriteDataA`, `GetExtSpriteA`, `ChangeExtSpriteA`, and ownership-aware `FreeSpriteData`. It converts a guest `BitMap` into an `ExtSprite`/sprite-image envelope for the documented 16-, 32-, and 64-pixel hardware widths, records the matching `es_WordWidth`, parses the documented sprite/query tags, applies bounded -2..2 replication and transparent narrow-source padding, supports the attached 3rd/4th-plane form with V39-compatible 2nd/3rd/5th-word attach markers, and `GetExtSpriteA` now reserves and publishes a transactional even/odd attached pair when `GSTAG_ATTACHED` points at the second `ExtSprite`; a failed pair publication rolls both sprite slots and guest envelopes back. Soft/scan-doubled forms, hardware pos/ctl regeneration, scheduler ownership, and display DMA remain explicit host/native gates; the ABI/tag names follow the classic [`graphics/sprite.h`](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node060B.html) contract.

The G21 foundation slice adds the standard 68k `VSprite`/`GelsInfo` layouts with guarded `InitGels` sentinel linking, `SetCollision` table writes, y/x-sorted `AddVSprite` plus reciprocal `RemVSprite` list ownership, and validated `SortGList` reordering.  `InitMasks` now accepts both true VSprites and Bob-backed envelopes: it reads the caller's planar image, preflights complete image and destination spans, and publishes the one-plane collision mask plus border OR mask without invoking guest callback pointers.  `DoCollision` now walks the sorted chain, checks the collision-mask pixels, applies the documented upper-left `MeMask`/lower-right `HitMask` selection and least-significant routine bit, detects top/bottom/left/right boundary flags, and forwards decoded routine addresses through the explicit backend.  `DrawGList` and `DoCollision` require an `IGraphicsGelsBackend` before any host-visible effect; CopperStart can provide that boundary through all-three projection callback slots on `CopperStartGraphicsContext`, while no guest routine pointer is executed in the host process.  The structure offsets and initialization contracts follow classic [`graphics/rastport.h`](https://d0.se/include/graphics/rastport.h), [`graphics/gels.h`](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node00C3.html), and the `InitGels`/`InitMasks` autodocs ([`InitGels`](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html), [`InitMasks`](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html)).

The G22/G23 animation slice adds the classic 68k `Bob`, `AnimComp`, `AnimOb`, and `DBufPacket` layouts plus the remaining nine public GELS/animation gateway cases.  `AddBob`/`RemIBob` preserve Bob-to-VSprite ownership and transient flags; `GetGBuffers`/`FreeGBuffers` use per-library allocator registries with rollback and foreign-pointer protection; `AddAnimOb` links an AnimOb chain, initializes active-component timers, and adds only the active Bob for each sequence; `Animate` advances signed fixed-point positions, velocity/acceleration, clocks/timers, switches timed `NextSeq` frames while preserving the active `NextComp` chain, and updates active VSprite coordinates in deterministic guest order; and `GetGBuffers`/`InitGMasks` walk every frame in every sequence.  Portable `DrawGList` now restores previously saved Bob backgrounds in reverse list order, captures current `SAVEBOB` backgrounds in forward order around the explicit provider draw boundary, and `RemIBob` restores its saved region before unlinking.  Sequence callbacks, collision callback dispatch, copper projection, and final raster/display publication remain explicit native/display responsibilities, so the same guest-memory core can be hosted by CopperSharp68k or CopperScreen without widening the 68k structures.  The animation ABI follows the classic [`graphics/gels.i`](https://d0.se/include/graphics/gels.i) offsets and the documented [`AddAnimOb`](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html), [`Animate`](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html), [`GetGBuffers`](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html), and [`FreeGBuffers`](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html) contracts.

The animation publication rule is transactional at the guest boundary: `AddAnimOb` snapshots the AnimOb chain and active-component fields before linking; `Animate` snapshots the complete position/velocity/clock word set before advancing, the active component timer/VSprite/Bob fields before final publication, and sequence component/VSprite links before replacement; `GetGBuffers` snapshots every Bob/VSprite buffer pointer before clearing or publishing owned storage, and restores the complete envelope before freeing storage on any late failure; `FreeGBuffers` keeps its registry and allocations live when a late pointer clear fails, allowing a safe retry. `InitGMasks` similarly restores Bob owner links if mask generation fails after ownership publication. These rollback guarantees keep the 68k layouts stable for both CopperSharp68k and CopperScreen adapters while leaving raster side effects explicit and testable.

At the register boundary, `LoadView` claims the documented void call only after the portable View/ViewPort/RasInfo validation succeeds. A malformed or RTG-owned View remains unclaimed with D0, cycles, and the previously published display state untouched, preserving the native Kickstart/CyberGraphX handoff; valid calls still publish through the scheduler-aware display boundary.

The display publication callback is optional at the CopperStart host boundary. A validated `LoadView` therefore remains unclaimed when no host scheduler/display publisher is connected, preserving the classic void-call D0 and cycle state for a native 68k implementation or provider. The AmigaBoot scheduler supplies the callback and keeps the normal cycle-sampled publication path.

`WaitTOF` uses the matching optional frame-wait boundary. Without a scheduler callback the host adapter declines the vector and does not alter D0 or the cycle counter; the production AmigaBoot callback remains the canonical frame synchronization source and derives its next boundary from the active bus beam clock, preserving PAL/NTSC/ECS field geometry rather than assuming PAL frame length.

The same status-aware rule now covers `WaitBOVP`, `ScrollVPort`, and `ChangeVPBitMap`: validation alone does not claim a display-side operation. The host must expose a vertical-blank or rebuild callback (or a DBufInfo message scheduler for a non-null double-buffer swap) before the adapter commits the operation; otherwise guest registers, cycles, and bitmap association remain available to native/provider code.

`VBeamPos` follows the same explicit display ownership rule: CopperStart samples the configured scheduler beam callback at the guest call's cycle, but a host with no canonical beam source declines the vector rather than claiming a fabricated zero. This keeps the classic D0/cycle state available to a native 68k ROM or provider boundary.

The host compatibility dispatcher keeps that split when the portable adapter declines: only a positively classified RTG View may reach the CyberGraphX/native `LoadView` callback. A malformed standard View cannot be converted into a synthetic host publication by the legacy fallback.

The direct portable `LoadView` path also checks every linked viewport's
`ColorMap` association. Null maps are legal while a screen is assembled, and
maps allocated by the active graphics instance remain native-owned only after
the complete public ColorMap envelope has been byte-probed. A foreign,
truncated, or otherwise unreadable map declines before active-view publication.
An explicit status-aware display backend is the provider handoff and may
consume that association without the portable registry claiming it.

The same boundary applies to palette void vectors: malformed or foreign ColorMap/viewport state leaves `SetRGB4CM`, `SetRGB32CM`, `GetRGB32`, `LoadRGB4`, `LoadRGB32`, `SetRGB4`, and `SetRGB32` available to native/provider implementations without changing D0 or cycles.

For the two legacy host palette callbacks, `GraphicsServices` applies the same rule explicitly: only a positively classified RTG viewport is forwarded after a portable decline. A malformed standard viewport cannot be turned into a host palette update by the compatibility fallback.

The `ChangeVPBitMap` compatibility callback follows the same discriminator for both the replacement bitmap and the viewport's current bitmap. This preserves the native/provider handoff for malformed standard swaps without interrupting CyberGraphX ownership of RTG surfaces.

The same provider discriminator covers the remaining host blit fallbacks: layered/RTG `BltBitMap`, `ClipBlit`, and `BltBitMapRastPort` calls are forwarded only after ownership is positively identified; malformed standard endpoints cannot be turned into compatibility success by the host dispatcher.

The portable blit register adapter keeps the classic function contracts distinct from its internal status convention. `BltClear`, `ClipBlit`, `BltMaskBitMapRastPort`, `BltPattern`, and `BltTemplate` are void vectors: a guarded portable failure declines the call without changing D0, while success publishes the normal void result. `BltBitMapRastPort` is the BOOL exception and publishes TRUE (1) only after a successful planar operation. This prevents an address-error or truncated standard endpoint from becoming a synthetic `-1` success path and leaves native Kickstart, layers.library, or CyberGraphX provider ownership explicit.

## ABI and patch policy

- Guest addresses are 32-bit values and all multi-byte memory access is big-endian.
- Structure offsets are constants, not host-runtime field layouts.
- Register argument/result rules come from the V40 FD and are tested at the gateway boundary.
- A function is migrated in three stages: portable semantic core, host adapter and focused tests, then optional ROM overlay registration.
- CopperStart may temporarily retain its current compatibility dispatch while goals are incomplete.
- ROM mode uses an explicit `RomSafeOverlayLvos` allow-list. Unsupported vectors retain original Kickstart ROM bytes and behavior.
- No unimplemented vector receives a fake success result as a permanent policy. The broad fallback is removed when the V40 inventory is complete.

## Timing and hardware boundaries

Pure structure manipulation, clipping, text measurement, and CPU planar operations may use a zero-cycle guest-memory abstraction. Blitter ownership, copper construction/publication, palette writes, `LoadView`, `WaitTOF`, beam queries, display DMA, and other custom-chip effects must use the scheduler's canonical integer timebase and normal bus side effects. No floating-point timing, arbitrary delays, cropping, or title-specific exceptions are permitted.

The strongest current timing baseline is A500 PAL OCS. Every display or timing test records the applicable chipset, video standard, CPU profile, and chip-RAM configuration; NTSC, ECS, and later AGA tests are separate cases.

AreaEnd's attached temporary raster is now an actual guest one-bit areafill mask: the portable path clears it, stages the decoded geometry, then applies area-pattern and draw-mode rules from that mask. This is separate from Flood's full-raster visited bitmap; both remain caller-owned when explicitly attached and allocator-owned only for the duration of an unset-TmpRas core call.

`InitArea` and `InitTmpRas` use the same atomic descriptor rule as `InitBitMap`: after complete descriptor-range and checked-address arithmetic preflight, a rejected descriptor write restores the original public envelope. Both constructors publish caller-owned pointer/count or pointer/size pairs without dereferencing the backing storage; `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, `AreaEnd`, `Flood`, and `Text` retain operation-specific capacity/readability checks when they consume those descriptors. The guest layout remains directly usable from CopperSharp68k while host CopperScreen can retain its own allocator/provider boundary.

Explicit `TmpRas` consumers apply the same word-aligned, complete-structure
envelope before clearing or using caller scratch. An odd or wrapped descriptor
therefore cannot alias low guest memory or partially mutate an `AreaEnd`/`Flood`
destination; unset descriptors retain the allocator-backed core path.

Area construction now extends that atomic boundary beyond the initial descriptor: `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, and `AreaEllipse` snapshot the affected 5-byte vector/flag records and the pointer/count/first-point metadata before publication, restoring both when a late guest write fails. `AreaEnd` applies the same rollback rule to its collector reset, so a failed reset leaves the recorded area retryable instead of exposing a partially consumed stream.

The collector also treats the `RastPort->AreaInfo` link and all vector/flag pointer advances as checked 32-bit guest addresses. A high RastPort or a table positioned at the end of the guest address space cannot wrap into a low alias during `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, or `AreaEllipse`; the portable path declines before any collector bytes change so CopperSharp68k/native ownership remains available.

`SetMaxPen` has a field-free `maxpen == 0` no-op. The portable path returns
before probing the RastPort mask byte, matching the resident implementation
and leaving NULL, odd, truncated, or provider-owned objects untouched. A
nonzero request retains the valid-object mask boundary.

An `AreaEnd` call against an already-empty collector is a valid completed boundary and returns success without touching bitmap or `TmpRas` state. This keeps repeated `AreaEnd` calls compatible with the native collector lifecycle while non-empty malformed streams still fail closed before reset.

Planar bitmap-copy vectors also enforce the 68k word-addressed `BitMap` envelope: an odd header pointer is rejected before its word fields or plane links are read, leaving the call for CopperSharp68k/native or CyberGraphX provider ownership rather than allowing a host-only odd-address interpretation.

The same envelope applies to V36 pixel-array conversions when callers supply a temporary RastPort: its linked BitMap must be word-aligned before the helper claims the workspace, while the host-only null-temporary path remains available for transitional CopperScreen callers.

The reset boundary is covered independently: a forced late `AreaInfo` field rejection after the fill has published pixels restores the destination snapshot and leaves the vector/count/first-point state unchanged, so the caller can repair the descriptor and retry `AreaEnd`.

`AreaCircle` remains a macro-level compatibility helper rather than a new library vector: the portable/core path expands it to `AreaEllipse` with equal positive radii, preserving the classic two-vector `AreaInfo` representation and its rollback semantics. CopperSharp68k can map the same helper to an inline macro while CopperScreen keeps the host dispatch local.

`GetVPModeID` also has an explicit screen-assembly state: a valid ViewPort with a null `ColorMap` may still resolve its native OCS/ECS mode from `vp_Modes`. A non-null foreign or malformed ColorMap remains a provider boundary instead of being silently reinterpreted as a standard display.

The same query is valid before Intuition links the first `RasInfo`: mode
identity is a property of the viewport geometry/mode word (or its ColorMap),
not of the later bitmap association. `GetVPModeID` therefore accepts an
otherwise complete, unlinked viewport during screen assembly, while a
nonzero RasInfo chain is still fully probed for cycles and truncation. The
stricter chain requirement remains in `ScrollVPort`, `AllocDBufInfo`,
`ChangeVPBitMap`, and `LoadView`, where the bitmap/display association is
actually consumed. Nonzero `ViewPort.ExtendedModes` continues to belong to a
native monitor/provider path.

At the register boundary, the structure constructors claim only successful portable operations. A malformed or failed `InitRastPort`, `InitBitMap`, `InitArea`, or `InitTmpRas` leaves D0 and the cycle counter unchanged, allowing the native ROM or a separate provider to handle the call rather than observing a fabricated success. When a compatibility font is selected, a late cached-metric write failure is not retried as a no-font success.

The host `GraphicsServices` dispatcher follows the same text ownership rule: its legacy Text/SetFont helpers remain callable for explicit boot/CyberGraphX patch integration, but they are not fallback claims after the portable register adapter declines. This keeps malformed RastPort/font streams outside the host compatibility path.

The synthetic `OpenScreenTagList` bridge now keeps a validated `SA_ErrorCode`
destination pending until the accepted OCS/ECS screen session finishes staging.
Program-memory exhaustion reports `OSERR_NOMEM` (3), while a failed standard
planar backing allocation reports `OSERR_NOCHIPMEM` (4); successful opens still
publish zero. Unknown display IDs, custom bitmaps, public-screen requests, and
malformed tag/legacy structures remain provider/native declines and leave the
caller's error word untouched. This preserves the documented Intuition error
ABI without allowing the host compatibility path to claim CyberGraphX or
public-screen ownership ([OpenScreen autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenScreen), [screens.h](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node0602.html)).

For an accepted native OCS/ECS mode, an explicit `SA_Depth` above the six-plane
hardware envelope now returns `OSERR_TOODEEP` (7) before any Screen/View or
bitmap state is staged. The tested ECS SuperHires compatibility rule remains
the exception: its native two-plane cap is retained rather than reclassified as
an error. This keeps the error code meaningful while preserving the existing
provider boundary for unsupported monitor IDs and RTG/custom-bitmap requests.

The legacy `OpenScreen(NewScreen *)` entry now applies the same six-plane
admission rule before staging its synthetic Screen. It has no `SA_ErrorCode`
destination, so an over-depth native request returns NULL; the rejection is
request-scoped and a repaired `NewScreen` can be retried successfully. Extended
monitor/RTG requests remain intercepted by their provider before this standard
OCS/ECS path claims them.

## Scope boundaries

Included: RastPort text and metrics, drawing primitives, planar bitmap operations, blitter-facing graphics operations, colors and pens, View/ViewPort lifecycle, copper lists, display modes, synchronization, sprites, GELS, regions, bitmap utilities, and the remaining documented V40 vectors.

Excluded: CyberGraphX implementation, Intuition screen allocation/ownership, a new AGA chipset implementation, and unrelated bus or CPU refactors. Integration tests may exercise Intuition consumers without moving their ownership into graphics.library.

The native overlay admits the guest-only `VideoControl` subset at the same
ownership boundary: scalar ColorMap flags and classic in-place GET snapshots
may commit for an instance-owned map, while `VC_*_Query` buffers are the only
external getter destinations. `VTAG_ATTACH_CM_SET`,
`VTAG_VIEWPORTEXTRA_SET`, and batch-list attachment setters remain on the
resident/provider vector. Foreign maps and malformed tag chains preserve the
captured Kickstart jump and the original D0/cycle state.

The V40 `BitMapScale` overlay follows the same ownership rule for mutating
planar storage: mapped calls are claimed only when both source and destination
BitMaps were allocated by the active graphics instance. The scaler retains its
transactional extent/pixel rollback, while foreign/native/RTG endpoints and
malformed `BitScaleArgs` remain available to the resident or CyberGraphX path.

The V36 `ReadPixelLine8`/`WritePixelLine8`/`ReadPixelArray8`/`WritePixelArray8`
family and V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` are also safe for the native overlay when
the A0 RastPort is a validated non-layered standard planar port. These
operations touch only guest planar bytes and caller buffers; layered, RTG,
and malformed RastPorts remain provider/native-owned, with the mapped gateway
preserving D0 and cycles on decline.

The simple-sprite pool has the same bounded native split: mapped `GetSprite`
claims only a readable/writable `SimpleSprite` envelope and an instance-owned
pool, while mapped `FreeSprite` claims only a valid slot in that pool. Invalid
guest envelopes, out-of-range slots, and foreign/provider state preserve the
captured resident vector with the original D0/cycle state. `MoveSprite`,
`ChangeSprite`, extended-sprite conversion, and display-DMA publication remain
outside this guest-only overlay until their provider/native timing contracts
are independently proven.

The extended-sprite lifecycle follows the same rule. Mapped `AllocSpriteDataA`
claims only a validated standard planar source and supported tag conversion;
`GetExtSpriteA` claims a validated `ExtSprite` envelope and bounded tag
request, requiring an independently writable, non-overlapping second envelope
for `GSTAG_ATTACHED`, and reserving only the instance's simple-sprite slot
pool. Mapped `ChangeExtSpriteA` publishes only a validated guest-envelope
replacement; and
`FreeSpriteData` claims only an allocation recorded by that instance's registry.
Unsupported tag forms, malformed envelopes, allocator failure, and foreign
allocations preserve the resident vector and original register state. Hardware
sprite/DMA publication remains a separate native/provider gate.

GELS/VSprite maintenance is likewise guest-only at the native boundary:
`InitGels`, `SetCollision`, `InitMasks`, `AddVSprite`, `RemVSprite`, and
`SortGList` are admitted only after their complete sentinel, mask, or
reciprocal-list envelopes validate. They publish no host callback or DMA
effect; malformed structures preserve the resident jump and register state.
`DrawGList`, `DoCollision`, Bob/animation traversal, and callback dispatch stay
provider/native-owned.

Animation state and buffer maintenance use the same split. Mapped
`AddAnimOb`, `Animate`, and `InitGMasks` publish only guest links, timers,
fixed-point positions, and masks after complete validation. `GetGBuffers` claims
only a successful allocator-backed guest buffer set, and `FreeGBuffers` claims
only the matching instance registry entry before clearing guest pointers and
releasing storage. Draw/collision callbacks and display/DBuf projection remain
provider/native-owned.

Simple-sprite movement and Bob unlinking use an explicit provider discriminator:
mapped `MoveSprite`/`ChangeSprite` are admitted only when no sprite backend is
attached, and mapped `RemIBob` is admitted only when no GELS backend is
attached. `AddBob` has no callback side effect and is guest-only. A configured
sprite/GELS backend therefore receives the original vector with D0/cycles
untouched instead of a synthetic compatibility success.

The standard-planar `BltBitMap` path now has the same mapped proof for two
validated guest bitmap envelopes. Its minterm transaction snapshots source
and destination pixels before writing, so overlap and late-write failure do
not expose partial planar state; malformed or provider-owned endpoints remain
available to the resident/provider vector.

`ClipBlit` extends that proof to two validated non-layered RastPorts. Its
destination mask and minterm semantics remain pure guest planar operations;
layered, RTG, and malformed ports are declined before any write and remain
available to the layer/CyberGraphX/native provider boundary.

The bitmap-to-RastPort variants `BltBitMapRastPort` and
`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` use the same mapped admission rule. Their distinct
TRUE/void return ABIs are preserved, and the mask plane is read only after the
bitmap/RastPort envelopes pass validation.

`BltClear` is admitted as a guest-buffer-only void vector. Its complete
row/byte envelope is probed before mutation, and native-overlay decline keeps
the original D0/cycles available to the resident implementation.

The row form keeps the same word-oriented contract as scalar byte-count mode:
the low 16 bits of `byteCount` (bytes per row) must be even. An odd row span
is rejected before probing or mutation, so every subsequent row remains on a
word boundary for both zero-fill and V36 fill-word operations.

Guest-template `BltTemplate` and external-mask `BltPattern` use the same
non-layered RastPort boundary for direct/core calls. Their source/mask spans
and every selected destination plane are preflighted before the void operation
publishes pixels; RTG and malformed inputs remain provider/native-owned. A
validated Layers call supplies the exact ClipRect visibility predicate to the
template path, preserving the same provider-owned clipping boundary while
skipping hidden destination fragments during preflight and publication.

Bulk palette loads use the corresponding viewport ownership boundary. Mapped
`LoadRGB4`/`LoadRGB32` calls may stage and publish only through a viewport that
resolves to an instance-owned `ColorMap`; a readable but unassociated or
foreign viewport does not authorize palette mutation or callback publication.

Per-pen `SetRGB4`/`SetRGB32` uses the same native-overlay boundary. A mapped
setter is claimed only when the viewport's readable `ColorMap` is owned by the
active graphics instance; the guest ColorTable update preserves its reserved
high nibble and the original call cycle. Foreign, unassociated, RTG, and
malformed viewport chains remain transparent so resident Kickstart or a
provider can apply its own palette semantics.

## Completion criteria

G14 update: portable `ObtainBestPenA` now searches already-shared entries (leaving unallocated ColorMap slots to the allocation fallback), applies checked free-entry-scaled tolerance, and chooses a fresh pen or shares the nearest occupied entry with pure and register-level regression coverage. A newly claimed pen now publishes its viewport RGB4 callback only after guest ColorMap/PaletteExtra state commits; shared references and `PEN_NO_SETCOLOR` remain side-effect free. PaletteExtra free/shared WORD chains now preserve the native head-removal, shared-head insertion, and free-head reinsertion order, including non-sharable exclusive entries staying outside the published lists. The remaining G14 parity gates are ROM error-metric calibration, native sidecar/list corruption behavior, Exec task ownership/contention, native palette publication beyond the callback seam, and scheduler-visible OCS/ECS/AGA timing; CyberGraphX/RTG palette ownership remains outside this implementation.

G14 precision update: `ObtainBestPenA` now uses the public `PRECISION_EXACT=-1`, `PRECISION_IMAGE=0`, `PRECISION_ICON=16`, and `PRECISION_GUI=32` values as the native squared-error precision term. The acceptance test is integral and overflow-guarded: `bestDistance * pe_NFree <= precision² * pe_SharableColors`, where `pe_SharableColors` is the highest sharable index. Exact precision rejects every non-zero distance; with no free sharable entries, non-exact modes retain the nearest shared pen as the native free-entry relaxation requires. ROM-specific color-distance calibration and scheduler-visible semaphore behavior remain explicit parity gates.

G14 color-table update: `SetRGB4CM` and `SetRGB32CM` now preserve the classic high `ColorTable` nibble while replacing RGB data, and RGB4 writes clear the low-color table as native graphics.library does. This keeps reserved genlock/alpha state stable across portable palette edits and is covered by the pure ColorMap layout regression.

The same reserved-nibble rule now applies to staged `LoadRGB4` and `LoadRGB32` table commits, so bulk palette loads cannot erase legacy high-nibble state while updating the RGB planes.

Pen acquisition now consumes the guest-compatible `pe_FirstFree` head for any-entry requests and walks `pe_FirstShared` for duplicate-color reuse. This preserves the native LIFO allocation policy and shared-list tie order instead of silently preferring the lowest numeric pen.

`FindColor(..., maxPen=-1)` now applies the attached `PaletteExtra` sharable span, while every other ULONG limit—including high-bit values such as `0xFFFFFFFE`—clamps to the requested full ColorMap range. Only the all-ones value is the native sharable-pen sentinel, so sprite/pointer entries beyond the planar depth remain discoverable for ordinary large limits ([FindColor source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/findcolor.c), [FindColor autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/FindColor)).

### G14 legacy ColorMap low-nibble boundary (2026-08-14)

The native `color_distance` helper treats `COLORMAP_TYPE_V1_2` (`Type == 0`)
as a high-nibble-only map: it ignores `LowColorBits` even when a readable
extension table happens to follow the public structure. V36/V39 maps continue
to assemble the complete 8-bit RGB value from `ColorTable` and
`LowColorBits`. `TryReadColor8` now reads the guest `Type` field and applies
that distinction before `FindColor` and `ObtainBestPenA` compare colors. A
two-entry high/low conflict proves that V36/V39 selects the exact 8-bit entry,
while V1.2 preserves the first high-nibble tie; pure, register, and ROM-overlay
paths cover the result and D0/cycle boundary. This follows the native helper's
layout and metric ([AROS `color_support.c`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/color_support.c),
[AROS `FindColor`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/findcolor.c)).

The same optional-table rule now covers `SetRGB4CM`, `SetRGB32CM`,
`LoadRGB4`, `LoadRGB32`, and `GetRGB32`: V1.2 updates publish only the
high-nibble `ColorTable` and preserve any extension storage, while reads expand
the high nibbles with zero low nibbles. V36/V39 retain the complete two-table
transaction and rollback behavior. Direct and register tests cover read/set
results, and the mapped overlay covers a V1.2 `SetRGB32CM` without changing
the low table.

The View activation sidecar now mirrors the native `LoadView` lifecycle: once
a View pointer and its validated View/ViewPort chain are active, loading that
unchanged guest state again succeeds without re-running the display/copper
publication callback. A different pointer, `NULL` for a blank display, or a
caller edit to the active CPR/ViewPort links remains an explicit host
transition; status-aware publication failure does not advance the sidecar, so
the previous View can be retried without losing the active state.
The sidecar also distinguishes the first `LoadView(NULL)` from later blank
requests, ensuring an initially unknown display state receives one explicit
blanking publication.

The active-View shortcut is only allowed when a status-aware display adapter
reports a connected publication owner. An adapter with no host/native callback
still declines the request, including a blank-view request, so native or
provider code retains ownership instead of receiving a synthetic success.

Synthetic `CloseScreen` uses the same transaction boundary in reverse: it
first requests `LoadView(NULL)` and only then retires the screen's compatibility
copper wrappers, guest CPR links, and backing allocations. A provider-declined
blanking handoff therefore leaves the active `View`/`ActiView` and screen
envelope intact for retry, instead of tearing down state while the old display
stream is still published.

When `MrgCop` rebuilds the currently active View, the CopperStart host now
queues the rebuilt CPR source at the call's scheduler cycle so the new merged
stream is visible immediately. Merges for inactive Views remain guest-side
preparation; `LoadView` performs their later presentation hand-off.

`VP_HIDE` is handled as a display-time control during that rebuild. Hidden
ViewPorts are still structurally validated, but contribute no copper list; if
the complete chain is hidden, `MrgCop` returns `MCOP_NOP` and preserves the
previous CPR links.

If the chain head is hidden but a later node is visible, the host rebuild uses
that first visible node as a temporary CPR-construction head, then restores the
original guest `ViewPort` chain head before publication. This keeps the public
chain layout native-compatible while ensuring the merged CPR starts at the
first visible viewport.

Monitor selection uses the same capability boundary as mode selection: an
explicit `OpenMonitor(displayId)` request for an ECS-only mode is rejected on
OCS hardware, while a named native PAL/NTSC monitor remains openable. This
keeps MonitorSpec ownership from claiming a mode the active chipset cannot
present.

Area-pattern drawing keeps the source-mask and draw-mode phases separate:
JAM1 writes only set pattern bits, JAM2 writes both foreground/background
phases, `COMPLEMENT|JAM2` is a whole-region invert, and inverse-video solid
fills select no pixels for JAM1 or the background pen for JAM2. The same rules
are shared by `RectFill`, `BltPattern`, and the area-pattern portions of
`AreaEnd`/`Flood`.

The library is complete only when the V40 manifest has no unassigned vectors, guest structures and register ABIs match the compatibility authority, host and native adapters preserve the same observable semantics, timing-sensitive operations pass profile-specific conformance tests, CyberGraphX remains decoupled, and ROM overlays contain only individually proven vectors. API-complete and hardware-conformant status are reported separately while the AGA execution backend is still pending.

`BltTemplate` keeps the same word-aligned boundary as the classic blitter:
the portable path requires an even source modulo and declines odd row strides
before touching the template or destination. This is the shared guest-memory
rule for CopperScreen and the future CopperSharp68k implementation; the
provider/native path remains free to handle any hardware-specific extension.

Its draw-mode path also keeps the template and destination phases separate:
`INVERSVID` inverts the single-plane stencil, while `JAM2` writes the
foreground pen for selected bits and the background pen for zero bits. The
complete clipped destination is probed before either phase is published.

For `BltPattern` with a null area pattern, a supplied mask is the template
stencil itself. The portable path therefore reduces JAM2 to JAM1 for that
masked call, preserving inverse-video and preventing background deposition in
the zero phase of the external mask.

Mask validation is proportional to the clipped destination width rather than
the declared row stride: each row checks only the touched prefix while the
full 32-bit stride envelope is still overflow-validated. This preserves the
guest ABI for large `ULONG` byte counts without turning a valid call into an
unbounded host loop.

The patterned write pass is also rollback-atomic if a late stencil or
area-pattern read fails after earlier pixels were deposited. The destination
snapshot is restored before the portable vector declines, preserving the
native/provider retry boundary.

The V36/V40 chunky-to-planar write family shares the destination RastPort
write mask with ordinary pixel operations. `WritePixelLine8`,
`WritePixelArray8`, and `WriteChunkyPixels` therefore leave unselected planes
untouched, while retaining the documented array stride and requested-count
contract ([WritePixelArray8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelArray8.html), [WriteChunkyPixels autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/WriteChunkyPixels.html)).

Native ROM boundary status: `GraphicsServices.InstallKickstartRomOverlay` now provides a reversible, base-addressed overlay seam. It is armed after native takeover either when the resident is already present in Exec's library list or when native `OpenLibrary("graphics.library")` returns a mapped base. The discovered native base is also used for guest-compatible `GfxBase->ActiView` and `ChipRevBits0` publication, while host-shim sessions retain the historical fixed base. `GraphicsLibraryImageLayout` is the shared big-endian writer for the library prefix, empty TextFonts list sentinels, and public GfxBase fields; `NativeGraphicsLibraryImageBuilder` emits a complete 176-slot jump table and AUTOINIT resident/function-array fixture only from explicit caller-supplied 68k entry addresses; `NativeGraphicsLibraryHunkBuilder` emits the corresponding relocatable vector/positive-image and resident segments with HUNK_RELOC32 records. Its allow-list currently contains bounded guest-memory constructors, RastPort state including `AskSoftStyle`, `SetSoftStyle`, and the pure pen/mode/mask/outline/MaxPen subset of `SetRPAttrsA`/`GetRPAttrsA`, standard-planar `Text`, `Move`, `Draw`, `PolyDraw`, `RectFill`, `SetRast`, `ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `EraseRect`, `DrawEllipse`, `ScrollRaster`, `ScrollRasterBF`, `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, `AreaEnd`, `Flood`, and validated standard-chain `LoadView`, fixed-metric text measurement (`TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `FontExtent`, and fixed-cell `TextFit`), the pure `GetBitMapAttr` query, arithmetic-only `ScalerDiv`, scheduler/display seams (`WaitTOF`, `VBeamPos`, `WaitBOVP`, `ScrollVPort`, `ChangeVPBitMap`, `AllocDBufInfo`, and `FreeDBufInfo`), status-aware copper construction/teardown (`MakeVPort`, `MrgCop`, `FreeVPortCopLists`, and `FreeCprList`), and user-copper list construction/emission/teardown (`UCopperListInit`, `CMove`, `CWait`, `CBump`, and `FreeCopList`) (`InitRastPort`, `InitVPort`, `InitView`, `InitBitMap`, `InitArea`, `InitTmpRas`, `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, `SetABPenDrMd`, `SetWriteMask`, `SetMaxPen`, `Move`, `Draw`, `PolyDraw`, `RectFill`, `SetRast`, `ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `EraseRect`, `DrawEllipse`, `ScrollRaster`, `ScrollRasterBF`, `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, `AreaEnd`, `Flood`, `LoadView`, `GetAPen`, `GetBPen`, `GetDrMd`, `GetOutlinePen`, `SetOutlinePen`, `AskSoftStyle`, `SetSoftStyle`, `SetRPAttrsA`, `GetRPAttrsA`, `Text`, `TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `FontExtent`, `TextFit`, `GetBitMapAttr`, and `ScalerDiv`). Font and draw-bounds tag handling, hardware copper merge/timing, display, blitter, layer, and RTG paths remain native-owned. A failed or unmapped install leaves the ROM jump table untouched; this is an integration seam, not a claim of full native parity.

Mapped guest overlays retain the same address-class contract as the native
68k path: the newest region is visible, and a read-only ROM/image overlay
masks older writable storage. The scheduler therefore cannot approve a
continuation stack merely because an underlying mapping is writable; the
preflight and the eventual mapped write agree on the visible overlay.

The ROM-overlay structure-initializer seam now has a direct-vs-mapped proof for
both `InitView` and `InitVPort`. The fixture compares the complete cleared
guest envelopes, the standard `View` origin and `ViewPort` sprite-priority
defaults, void D0/cycle preservation, and the post-initialization host
projection callback. This keeps the public screen/view construction layout
identical through CopperStart dispatch and the mapped native jump table while
leaving malformed envelopes unclaimed.

The same overlay proof now covers `FontExtent` alongside `TextLength`,
`TextExtent`, and `TextFit`. A guest proportional strike with explicit
`CharLoc`, `CharSpace`, and `CharKern` tables produces identical movement and
bounding fields through direct and mapped dispatch, including the void D0 and
cycle boundary. This keeps the remaining ROM-safe text metric entry point on
the shared guest layout without claiming font ownership or provider rendering.
The reversible ROM overlay snapshots each replaced slot's original `JMP.L`
target before installing the host gateway. A declined portable call now
tail-chains to that native target, while a positively classified provider call
stays at the provider boundary.

The `SetRPAttrsA`/`GetRPAttrsA` overlay subset also admits validated guest
`RPTAG_Font`, the pure `RPTAG_SoftStyle` query/update tag, and
`RPTAG_DrawBounds` for a validated non-layered RastPort. The SoftStyle query
uses a boolean success path so the valid `0xffffffff` result for a font with
no intrinsic style is not mistaken for the signed helper's legacy failure
sentinel; layered or malformed DrawBounds state still declines to the
layers/native provider.

Scheduler-backed `WaitTOF` uses the same seam: the portable adapter claims it
only when the host supplies a frame-boundary callback, preserving the cycle
and void D0 contract through direct and mapped calls; an unbound host leaves
the original Kickstart vector available.

`VBeamPos` follows the same rule with the canonical cycle-sampled beam
callback: mapped and direct calls return the same UWORD position without
advancing the CPU cycle, while an unbound host remains native-owned.

`WaitBOVP` now uses the validated viewport/RasInfo chain and the explicit
vertical-blank callback. Valid mapped and direct calls preserve the callback's
cycle boundary and void D0 result; malformed or unbound calls remain available
to native Kickstart.

`ScrollVPort` uses the same validated-chain boundary for display rebuilds:
the callback is observable through both direct and mapped paths without
advancing the CPU cycle, while malformed or unbound scrolls remain native-owned.

`ChangeVPBitMap` now preserves that ownership split for screen buffers: a
validated standard-planar replacement updates `RasInfo.BitMap` before the
explicit rebuild callback, while malformed or unbound swaps leave the old
association untouched for native Kickstart.

The public double-buffer envelope follows the same seam: successful
`AllocDBufInfo`/`FreeDBufInfo` calls preserve guest allocator ownership and D0
through direct and mapped paths, while unsupported allocation or foreign/stale
ownership remains native-owned.

`AllocDBufInfo` completes its bounded `ViewPort`/`RasInfo` validation before
asking a display adapter whether double buffering is supported. Malformed
native requests therefore cannot make provider capability probes observable or
allocate a compatibility envelope; only a valid viewport reaches the explicit
display-capability boundary.

`ChangeVPBitMap` uses the same ordering across its complete input envelope:
the viewport/RasInfo chain, DBufInfo ownership, replacement bitmap, and
currently attached bitmap layout are all preflighted before a presentation
adapter is asked to accept the swap. This keeps malformed bitmap storage
unclaimed for CopperSharp68k/native or CyberGraphX ownership while valid
standard-planar swaps still publish the guest association before the explicit
rebuild/message boundary.

The copper-construction vectors use the same explicit boundary: validated
`MakeVPort`/`MrgCop` calls reach status-aware CopperStart callbacks through both
direct and mapped paths, while RTG-owned calls remain on the captured native
provider vector. This is a construction seam, not a claim of complete copper
instruction or timing parity.

Copper teardown uses the matching small-unit seam. `FreeVPortCopLists` clears
the four guest copper-link fields atomically after validating the complete
`ViewPort` envelope, then offers the viewport to the explicit native resource
owner. `FreeCprList` validates the public 12-byte `cprlist` envelope before
offering it to that owner. A result-bearing owner may decline a valid envelope
when its private wrapper/raw allocation is foreign or already released; the
legacy void callback remains an explicit compatibility-owner path. Both vectors are admitted to the reversible native
overlay only after direct-vs-mapped tests compare guest state, owner callbacks,
D0, and cycles; RTG-owned viewport teardown and malformed envelopes tail-chain
to the captured Kickstart vector. Hardware deallocation and full copper timing
remain separate follow-on gates.

The user-copper allocation seam is now similarly bounded. `UCopperListInit`
publishes a caller-owned `UCopList` envelope plus allocator-owned `CopList` and
six-byte `CopIns` storage; `CMove`, `CWait`, and `CBump` write guarded pseudo-
instructions and advance the current block, while `FreeCopList` clears the
caller links before releasing every registry-owned block. The native overlay
admits these vectors only with direct-vs-mapped parity for guest bytes,
allocator publication/release, D0, and cycles. An unavailable allocator or
unknown list leaves the vector transparent and tail-chains to Kickstart;
`CEND` stays the documented macro sequence, and hardware copper merge/timing
remains a separate gate.

`CalcIVG` and `SetChipRev` use the same lifecycle boundary. `CalcIVG` claims
only a validated standard View/ViewPort chain and forwards the scan-line count
to an explicit display backend; `SetChipRev` claims only when a chipset
capability provider is present and returns that provider's supported bits.
Their direct and mapped paths preserve D0/cycles, while RTG or unbound calls
remain transparent and tail-chain to Kickstart. This exposes the host/native
capability seam without pretending to implement profile-specific chipset or
copper timing in the portable layer.

Native display queries use an explicit monitor-family gate. `FindDisplayInfo`
and `NextDisplayInfo` claim only known OCS/ECS mode records and enumeration
sentinels; `ModeNotAvailable` additionally claims recognized PAL/NTSC/default
monitor feature keys so unsupported chipset combinations can report
`DI_AVAIL_NO_CHIPS`. Unknown monitor IDs are left transparent and tail-chain to
the original Kickstart/native provider vector, keeping CyberGraphX records out
of the portable database.

`GetDisplayInfoData` follows the same ownership boundary. Native ModeID
handles and the four portable data tags claim only after the database has
resolved a complete clipped chunk; the host and mapped-ROM paths publish the
same bytes, returned length, and register state. Unknown tags and zero-sized
buffers are valid empty queries, while a non-empty recognized chunk with an
unreadable or unwritable guest span declines to the captured provider vector.
This keeps display records atomic and prevents a malformed RTG/native handle
from being swallowed by the portable implementation.

The adjacent monitor lifecycle uses the same reversible boundary. Native
PAL/NTSC `OpenMonitor` requests allocate or share one guest-compatible
`MonitorSpec`, while `CloseMonitor` decrements the public open count and frees
the record only on the final close. Unknown monitor names or IDs, foreign
specifications, and allocator failures remain transparent to the original
Kickstart/provider vector; no CyberGraphX monitor object is claimed here.

Mode selection follows the same rule. `BestModeIDA` claims only a bounded,
well-formed native tag list, and `CoerceMode` claims only a validated
standard-planar ViewPort/RasInfo/BitMap chain with a native PAL/NTSC monitor
family. Invalid lists, unsupported feature combinations, and RTG-owned
ViewPorts remain provider-owned, preserving the CopperSharp68k-compatible
register ABI without fabricating a host mode.

`GetVPModeID` is the read-only screen-assembly counterpart: it maps validated
standard-planar `ViewPort.Modes`/ColorMap state through the active PAL/NTSC
profile, but leaves an RTG-owned ViewPort transparent so CyberGraphX or the
native monitor provider can answer it.

The pure `WeighTAMatch` vector is likewise safe to expose through the native
overlay: it reads the bounded guest `TextAttr` prefixes and optional tagged-DPI
lists, returns the signed match weight in D0, and performs no host-font or
surface publication. Malformed font attributes remain a zero-weight result at
the portable ABI, while future provider-specific font selection can still
replace the vector independently.

`AskFont` shares that bounded native boundary. It reads the current guest
`TextFont`, preflights the complete 8-byte destination `TextAttr`, and publishes
name, size, style, and flags atomically; a late guest write failure restores the
original bytes. Invalid RastPort, TextFont, or destination envelopes decline
through the captured Kickstart vector, keeping native/provider font ownership
separate from the portable overlay.

`SetFont` is the corresponding guest-state publication path. It decodes the
selected guest `TextFont`, preflights the contiguous RastPort font/cache span,
and atomically updates the font pointer plus cached style and text metrics. A
truncated or unreadable cache span leaves the prior bytes untouched and keeps
the native/provider vector as the owner of the malformed request.

The guest `TextFonts` list follows the selected library instance as well. When
the native overlay discovers a mapped `GfxBase`, the memory-only list backend
rebinds to that base before lifecycle writes are admitted, without clearing
resident nodes already published there. `AddFont`/`RemFont` validation then
operates against that native list header, and overlay disposal restores the
host compatibility base for subsequent shim calls. This keeps native resident
ownership separate from the compatibility list while preserving a reversible
CopperStart boundary.

The overlay claims those two lifecycle vectors only when that explicit guest
list backend is attached. Without it, the mapped slots remain transparent and
tail-chain to native Kickstart or a provider rather than mutating a private
host registry that cannot observe resident fonts.

`OpenFont` uses the same list reader before scoring candidates, so resident
native fonts and host-added fonts share the documented `WeighTAMatch` ordering.
`CloseFont` records only fonts opened through this portable boundary; it can
decrement their guest accessor word while leaving untracked native residents
available to the native implementation.

`ExtendFont`/`StripFont` are admitted under the same guest-list ownership gate.
The overlay refuses to allocate or detach a `TextFontExtension` without a
rebound, structurally valid `TextFonts` list. Extension tag streams are
bounded and cloned into guest memory before publication; teardown restores the
original extension/style and frees only allocations tracked by the portable
backend. This keeps host allocation and extension ownership out of the
native-only path while still allowing a CopperSharp68k-compatible guest
implementation to share the layout and rollback contract.

Allocator-backed Regions use an equivalent native boundary. The portable core
records every Region envelope it allocates, and the overlay admits boolean,
clear, and dispose operations only for those owned envelopes. Rectangle-node
reclamation therefore cannot consume storage belonging to native Kickstart or
another provider; foreign Regions tail-chain without changing D0 or cycles.

`AllocRaster`/`FreeRaster` use an explicit span registry as well. The guest
address is paired with the requested width and height, and only an exact
instance-owned pair can be freed through the native overlay. This preserves
the classic `RASSIZE` byte calculation while preventing a malformed or foreign
free from reaching the host allocator.

ColorMap allocation and pure RGB table vectors follow the same rule. The
native overlay can create a host-owned `ColorMap`, update its RGB4/RGB32 high
and low words, read them back, and free the complete registered allocation;
foreign/native maps remain transparent so their palette storage and ownership
stay with Kickstart or a provider.

The same native boundary now covers palette sharing: `AttachPalExtra`, pen
obtain/release, and `FindColor` may operate only on a ColorMap allocated by
this graphics instance. Their guest free/shared lists, reference counts, and
nearest-color results remain portable; foreign maps or malformed attachments
leave the captured native vector available with D0 and cycles unchanged.

AreaEnd preserves the native per-shape transaction boundary. Each recorded
polygon or ellipse gets its own temporary mask and pattern/draw-mode pass;
overlapping shapes therefore remain observable as separate operations (for
example, `COMPLEMENT` toggles a shared pixel once per shape instead of once
for the union). This mirrors the Kickstart-compatible AreaEnd sequence in
which each item is filled before the next vector item is consumed
([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).
AreaEnd also preserves the per-shape outline ordering: when `AREAOUTLINE` is
enabled, the outline for each polygon or ellipse is emitted immediately after
that shape's fill and before the next shape is processed. This keeps a later
shape's fill able to cover an earlier outline exactly as in the native
AreaEnd sequence ([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).
Area outlines also use one-pixel shared-vertex ownership. A recorded
`CLOSEDRAW` endpoint is not followed by an additional zero-length segment,
and open polygons close without toggling their first vertex twice under
`COMPLEMENT`. This follows the native `Draw`/`PolyDraw` shared-vertex rule
([AROS Draw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c), [AROS PolyDraw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c)).
Area polygon outlines now run through the same `Move`/`Draw` state machine as
`PolyDraw`: `LinePtrn`, `linpatcnt`, `INVERSVID`, `ONE_DOT`, and connected
segment phase continuity are guest-visible during the outline pass. Each
shape restarts the native 15-bit line phase when its outline pen is installed,
restores the caller's pen after the shape, and restores the saved cursor and
flags after the complete AreaEnd transaction. This keeps the portable path
aligned with the future CopperSharp68k implementation while leaving ellipse
outline rasterization in the shared planar DrawEllipse primitive
([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c), [AROS Draw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c), [AROS PolyDraw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c)).
The portable `Move`, `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, and `SetDrMd` operations now restart
`linpatcnt` at 15, the documented first bit of a fresh line pattern. `Move`
publishes that phase together with the cursor and `FRST_DOT` flag, restoring
all four fields on a failed guest write; the same phase is used by the AreaEnd
outline pen transaction
([SetAPen autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node0475.html), [gfxmacros.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/gfxmacros.h), [AROS Move](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/move.c)).
`TextFit` treats a non-null constraining `TextExtent` as a complete rendering
contract: its `te_Width` and `te_Height` limits are checked together with the
relative rectangle, while the alternate bit-width/bit-height arguments are
ignored. This preserves the documented distinction between the explicit
extent and the fallback dimensions, and keeps the zero-character result
atomic when any part of the constraint rejects the first glyph
([TextFit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit), [AROS textfit.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textfit.c)).
The register adapter consumes the documented low fields: signed WORD counts
for `Text`, `TextLength`, and `TextExtent`, plus UWORD `strLen`/width/height
and signed WORD `strDirection` for `TextFit`. Layer providers receive the
same narrowed count/direction values, so CopperScreen and a future
CopperSharp68k provider see identical guest intent; widened host arithmetic
remains an internal implementation detail
([Text](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/Text.html), [TextLength](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextLength.html), [TextExtent](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextExtent.html), [TextFit](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).
An explicit `TextFit` constraint must include the current pen origin on the
X axis (`MinX <= 0 <= MaxX`). A rectangle wholly to the positive or negative
side therefore produces the documented empty fit even when a rendered glyph
envelope would otherwise lie inside it; the guest and native implementations
share this Kickstart constraint rule ([TextFit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).
Connected `Draw` ownership is keyed only by `FRST_DOT`, not by the numeric
line-pattern phase. A segment can consume exactly one 16-bit pattern period
and leave `linpatcnt=0`; the next connected `COMPLEMENT` line still renders
the shared start sample and applies the native one-dot undo when that sample
emits ([AROS draw.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c)).
`PolyDraw` follows the same connected sequence: it calls `Draw` for every
coordinate pair, including the first, so the first line runs from the
RastPort's existing current pen to the first array entry. It does not insert
an implicit `Move`; the first pair therefore consumes the caller's
`FRST_DOT`, line-pattern phase, and draw-mode state ([AROS polydraw.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c), [PolyDraw autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/PolyDraw)).
The `PolyDraw` register adapter likewise preserves the original ROM's count
ABI: although the public prototype names a `LONG`, only the low 16 bits are
consumed as a `UWORD`. Counts above `0x7FFF` therefore remain real point
streams rather than becoming signed negative no-ops, while a zero low word is
the only early-success case ([AROS polydraw.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c)).
`TextFit` keeps the documented `0..32767` range for its alternate rendering
box width and height on every non-empty request. The guest ABI still carries
ULONG values, so an out-of-range input is declined without narrowing. When an
explicit `TextExtent` is provided, it adds origin-relative rectangle bounds;
it does not disable the alternate rendering-box envelope ([TextFit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).
The register adapter consumes the classic WORD/UWORD fields for
`Text`/`TextLength`/`TextExtent` and `TextFit`: signed WORD counts, UWORD
`strLen`/width/height, and signed WORD `strDirection`. `TextLength` publishes
its classic signed 16-bit WORD result, while the published `TextExtent`
retains UWORD width/height fields and signed WORD rectangle coordinates
([Text](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/Text.html), [TextLength](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextLength.html), [TextExtent](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextExtent.html), [TextFit](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).
Portable metric publication validates those field widths before the final
12-byte write: a UWORD width/height is not narrowed from a wider accumulator,
and a signed rectangle coordinate is not wrapped past `WORD` range. A negative
REVPATH width remains valid through its two's-complement UWORD encoding; an
unrepresentable envelope is declined for native/provider handling.
For `TextFit`, the alternate-dimension range check is skipped when `strLen` is
zero: the documented empty request returns an empty extent without treating
unused D2/D3 values as a rendering constraint ([TextFit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit)).
An empty request likewise does not dereference an optional constraining
`TextExtent`; only the validated result structure is required at the portable
boundary. The CopperStart register gateway mirrors this rule and does not
preflight an unused A3 for `strLen == 0`, preserving the native/provider
ownership boundary for malformed optional input; non-empty requests still
preflight a supplied A3 before the portable vector claims the call.
The same zero-count short-circuit avoids reading `TxSpacing` and `AlgoStyle`:
those fields cannot affect an empty result, and a truncated optional RastPort
word must not turn a valid no-op into a provider fallback.
Soft-style register inputs retain the same long-word boundary: `SetSoftStyle`
receives complete D0/D1 values, applies the intrinsic-font and enable-mask
operation in the portable core, then publishes only the guest RastPort's
byte-sized `AlgoStyle` field and returns the resulting style byte. High input
bits cannot turn a valid low-byte style request into a truncated or empty
operation ([SetSoftStyle autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetSoftStyle), [AROS setsoftstyle.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setsoftstyle.c)).
Text JAM2 follows the template-blit envelope rather than limiting BPen writes
to decoded glyph columns. The portable path now paints the measured
`TextExtent` rectangle, including inter-character spacing and font rows with
no glyph strike; `INVERSVID` selects APen for untouched template-zero cells.
`JAM2|COMPLEMENT` applies the complement minterm once to that same complete
rectangle and skips the source phases, so spacing and empty rows are toggled
without a second hit. The full envelope is destination-preflighted and uses
the existing planar clipping/rollback path before the guest cursor is
published ([AROS Text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c),
[AROS TextExtent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c),
[WritePixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixel)).

The timed CopperStart display adapter shares the same publication owner as the
portable lifecycle core even when a host supplies only the status-aware
`TryLoadView` callback. Its void `PublishView(view, cycle)` overload now
constructs the normal 68k state and invokes that callback as a best-effort
fallback; callers that need failure ownership continue through
`TryPublishView`. This preserves a single guest/native View publication layout
for host execution and a future CopperSharp68k vector table without widening
the public `GraphicsServices` surface.

Font lifecycle admission now adds one bounded proportional-font guard: when a
`TextFont` has a `CharLoc` table, both the first and final strike rows implied
by `tf_YSize`/`tf_Modulo` must be readable before the node is added or selected
from a resident guest list. Fixed-cell resident nodes deliberately keep their
classic opaque modulo publication and are validated when their actual glyph
rows are used. This closes a malformed final-row hole without changing the
native resident-list ownership contract.

The proportional admission guard also validates the complete declared
`CharLoc`, `CharSpace`, and `CharKern` spans, including the extra default-glyph
entry used for out-of-range bytes. This keeps malformed table pointers from
entering the selectable font list while leaving per-glyph packed-row checks in
the text/metric preflight and preserving fixed-cell native-list behavior.
Layered `RectFill` now has an explicit provider claim boundary alongside
layered `Draw` and `Text`. The graphics core continues to own only the
non-layered planar implementation; a host/layers provider receives the four
signed rectangle coordinates and remains responsible for `ClipRect`
traversal, backing-store synchronization, and damage publication. A provider
that does not implement this optional method leaves the vector unclaimed for
native layers code, preserving the CopperSharp68k/native ownership split
([RectFill autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/RectFill)).
Layered `DrawEllipse` uses the same explicit claim seam. Its center and radii
remain signed WORDs at the CopperStart boundary, while the provider owns
ClipRect traversal, backing-store selection, and damage publication. The
portable midpoint ellipse remains available only for an ordinary planar
RastPort; a provider that declines the optional operation leaves the native
layers vector untouched ([RectFill autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/RectFill),
[DrawEllipse autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/DrawEllipse)).
Layered `SetRast` now has an optional provider claim carrying the complete
UBYTE pen argument. The provider owns the layer's clipped drawing area,
backing-store synchronization, and damage publication; the portable core
continues to fill only ordinary planar RastPorts. Declining the optional claim
keeps the void vector available to native layers code without fabricating a
success ([SetRast autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/SetRast)).
Layer-owned pixel access now follows the same split: `ReadPixel` returns the
