provider's signed result (including the classic `-1` outside/error value),
while `WritePixel` claims only after the provider accepts the write. The
portable planar pixel paths remain restricted to non-layered RastPorts, so a
declined layer call preserves D0/cycles for native layers or CopperSharp68k
ownership ([ReadPixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixel),
[WritePixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixel)).
Layered `ScrollRaster`, `ScrollRasterBF`, `ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, and
`EraseRect` now use the same optional provider claim boundary. The provider
receives the signed displacement or rectangle ABI and owns ClipRect traversal,
backing-store selection, damage publication, and BF-specific backfill. The
portable planar clear/scroll implementations remain restricted to ordinary
RastPorts; a missing or declining provider leaves D0/cycles untouched for the
native layers path ([ScrollRaster autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ScrollRaster),
[EraseRect autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/EraseRect)).
Layered `PolyDraw`, `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, `AreaEnd`, and
`Flood` now use the same explicit provider boundary. Point-stream counts retain
the low-16-bit guest ABI, area vectors pass their signed WORD geometry, and
`Flood` preserves the provider's BOOL result. The provider owns collector state,
pattern/ClipRect traversal, damage, and backing-store writes; the portable area
and flood implementations remain restricted to ordinary planar RastPorts.
Absent or declining providers leave these vectors available to native layers
ownership ([PolyDraw autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/PolyDraw),
[AreaEnd autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/AreaEnd),
[Flood autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Flood)).

Font-list teardown keeps the same guest-transaction rule as structure and
RastPort updates. When `RemFont` removes the final node, the empty-list
sentinel write is included in the rollback boundary; a late byte rejection
restores the GfxBase links, the detached font links, and `FPF_REMOVED` so a
native 68k or provider implementation can retry from an intact list.
Layer-aware `ClipBlit`, `BltBitMapRastPort`, `BltMaskBitMapRastPort`,
`BltPattern`, and `BltTemplate` now have typed optional claims as well. The
provider receives both RastPort endpoints where applicable, the exact signed
WORD geometry, the byte minterm, and the mask/template pointers; BOOL results
are returned only for `BltBitMapRastPort`, while the remaining vectors retain
their void D0 ABI. RTG endpoints are checked before the layer claim so
CyberGraphX remains a separate owner. A declined or absent layer provider
leaves the call for native/layers fallback ([ClipBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ClipBlit),
[BltBitMapRastPort autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/BltBitMapRastPort),
[BltPattern autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/BltPattern),
[BltTemplate autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/BltTemplate)).
Layered V36 pixel-line/array vectors and the V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` vector
now have the same typed provider seam. `ReadPixelLine8`, `WritePixelLine8`,
`ReadPixelArray8`, and `WritePixelArray8` preserve their UWORD coordinate
inputs, A1 temporary RastPort, A2 byte-array pointer, and provider count in
D0. `WriteChunkyPixels` preserves its signed LONG rectangle, A2 source array,
and D4 bytes-per-row ABI while keeping its void success result. RTG RastPorts
are excluded before the layer claim, and a declined provider leaves the
original vector available to CyberGraphX/native layers code
([ReadPixelLine8 autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixelLine8),
[ReadPixelArray8 autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixelArray8),
[WritePixelArray8 autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelArray8),
[WriteChunkyPixels autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WriteChunkyPixels)).

Standard-planar `ReadPixel` and `WritePixel` now have an independent
direct-vs-mapped ROM-overlay proof. The proof covers multi-plane colour
combination, APen/JAM1 writes, the signed `-1` outside-RastPort result, and
unchanged guest plane bytes after a rejected coordinate. This keeps the
native-overlay claim limited to the same validated planar path while the
layer-provider branch retains clipping and backing-store ownership
([ReadPixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixel),
[WritePixel autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixel)).

Variable-width text now treats signed movement as part of the rendered
envelope in both directions. `TextExtent` and `TextFit` record the intermediate
`CharSpace` advance and the final `TxSpacing` position, so negative spacing
updates `MinX` instead of being lost when only the right edge is expanded. The
alternate `TextFit` width is compared with that complete envelope, and JAM2
background plus underline coverage reuse the same range. This keeps the
portable `Text` path, metric vectors, and the guest `TextExtent` layout aligned
for a future CopperSharp68k glyph provider.

Fixed-cell text now uses the same signed movement envelope as proportional text
without giving up its nominal-cell contract. Negative `TxSpacing` and
`FPF_REVPATH` advances therefore publish the leftward cell in `TextExtent` and
`TextFit`, so fit decisions, JAM2 background, and underline coverage follow the
same side of the pen as the renderer. Strike widths remain excluded from the
fixed-cell metric rectangle unless the font explicitly supplies proportional,
`CharSpace`, or `CharKern` metrics.

`GetBitMapAttr(BMA_FLAGS)` follows the public V39 query contract rather than
echoing allocator request state. It returns only `BMF_DISPLAYABLE`,
`BMF_INTERLEAVED`, and `BMF_STANDARD`; `BMF_CLEAR` and `BMF_MINPLANES` remain
construction-time inputs and are not exposed through the guest attribute
result. The same filtering is used by the pure core and CopperStart register
adapter, while foreign/RTG bitmap ownership remains a separate provider path.

`FreeBitMap` now treats a registered bitmap header as untrusted guest state at
teardown. Before releasing any allocation it validates the complete standard
planar envelope, probes every declared plane raster, and verifies the exact
contiguous sequence for `BMF_INTERLEAVED`. A corrupted plane pointer therefore
leaves the ownership token and allocator state intact so native/provider code
can handle the malformed object; valid allocations retain the existing
instance-scoped release behavior.

`BltBitMap` now honors the classic `TempA` boundary for overlapping planar
spans. A non-null workspace must be word-aligned and readable for one source
row; overlap detection compares byte envelopes across every participating
source/destination plane pair, including shifted and cross-plane aliases. A
null workspace obtains one source-stride scan line from the explicit Chip
allocator boundary and releases it on success or failure; allocator-provided
storage is not re-probed through the host map. A workspace on a non-overlapping
copy is not touched. This keeps overlap safety, allocation rollback, and the
public participating-plane result aligned with the native contract while
leaving malformed caller scratch available to the native/provider path
([BltBitMap autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/BltBitMap)).

The synthetic Intuition screen handoff now keeps title rendering inside the
screen-attribute contract. `SA_Quiet` suppresses the host title renderer while
still publishing `Screen.Title` and `Screen.Flags` for guest callers and native
handoff. `SA_ShowTitle` remains a guest-visible ordering flag; because the
synthetic host has one backing surface and no backdrop stack, clearing it does
not erase the title pixels. Updating a visible title clears and redraws only the
title-bar rows; it no longer clears application pixels in the rest of the
backing store. This matches the documented screen flags and keeps backing-store
ownership separate from the display/provider path
([SA_Quiet and SA_ShowTitle](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Intuition_Screens)).

The synthetic `SetWindowTitles` bridge also checks the caller-owned `Window *`:
foreign non-null windows do not rewrite or allocate the compatibility screen.
The host shim retains a null-window screen-title-only path, while native
Intuition remains responsible for foreign window ownership and title-bar
composition ([SetWindowTitles](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node03F8.html)).

An explicit NULL/empty screen-title request now clears only the synthetic
title-bar rows after publishing the null `Screen.Title` pointer; the
NoTitleChange sentinel continues to preserve the existing title, and pixels
outside the bar remain untouched ([SetWindowTitles](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0598.html)).
Null-window title calls before `OpenScreen` are declined without allocating
compatibility Screen/View state; the host shim accepts that form only for an
already-open synthetic screen.

The synthetic `Screen` prefix now follows the canonical Kickstart 3.1 word
layout: `Title` at `0x16`, `DefaultTitle` at `0x1A`, and the caller-visible
`Font` (`TextAttr *`) at `0x28`, while the embedded `ViewPort`, `RastPort`, and
`BitMap` remain at `0x2C`, `0x54`, and `0xB8`. Legacy `NewScreen.Font` and
`SA_Font` are validated and carried through without replacing caller-owned
objects. When omitted, the compatibility path publishes a reset-scoped
`TextAttr` mirroring the synthetic `TextFont`; malformed font pointers remain
available to native Intuition or another provider. This keeps the public ABI
ready for a CopperSharp68k guest implementation while leaving CyberGraphX
mode and custom-bitmap ownership in its separate patch boundary.

The screen-font selector follows Intuition's documented precedence: an
`SA_SysFont` tag overrides both `NewScreen.Font` and `SA_Font`. The portable
compatibility provider accepts selectors `0` and `1` and maps both to its
reset-scoped default `TextAttr` because no separate preferences-font registry
is installed; unsupported selector values remain available to native Intuition
or a provider patch ([OpenScreenTagList](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenScreenTagList),
[Intuition Screens](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Intuition_Screens)).

After `Screen.Font` is selected, the compatibility path opens the matching
resident guest `TextFont` and publishes that pointer in the embedded
`Screen.RastPort`; the shared window `RPort` inherits that same pointer. A
reset-scoped fixed-cell Topaz envelope supplies the same strike data used by
the portable text routines, so the default path follows
the ordinary OpenFont/CloseFont accessor lifecycle; the RastPort cache words
are copied from the selected TextFont metrics. Caller-owned `TextAttr` storage
is never rewritten or freed; an unmatched but readable request falls back to
the compatibility default, while malformed/native-only font policy remains
outside this host provider.

Focused host coverage also registers a second fixed-cell guest font through the
graphics font list, opens a screen with its `TextAttr`, and verifies that both
the Screen and Window RastPorts select that resident object and release its
accessor on teardown.

Synthetic `OpenScreen` now treats the public `Screen` envelope and its backing
bitmap as one lifecycle transaction. If standard-planar or provider-owned
bitmap setup cannot complete, the staged bitmap/RasInfo links are rolled back,
the compatibility Screen handle is retired, and the Intuition bridge returns
NULL. This prevents a native-style caller from observing a mapped Screen with
no valid `BitMap` or `ViewPort.RasInfo`; the reset-scoped allocator may retain
the raw bytes, but no compatibility state can mistake them for a live display.

The synthetic `OpenScreen` bridge also translates compatibility program-memory
exhaustion into the native allocation result. The boot coordinator continues
to throw for mandatory startup allocations, but a guest screen envelope is a
recoverable public request: when its 0x160-byte `Screen` prefix cannot be
staged, no host exception crosses the Intuition ABI and no compatibility
ownership is published. This keeps CopperSharp68k callers on the classic
NULL-open path while leaving the underlying reset-scoped allocator policy
unchanged.

`ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` now use the same visibility boundary for
preflight, rollback snapshots, and publication. Layered clears therefore do
not touch hidden bitmap rows, while ordinary planar `ClearScreen` retains its
complete-plane transaction; CyberGraphX ownership remains outside this path.

The same translation covers later screen-session envelopes. RasInfo, BitMap,
RastPort, Window, and View allocation failures clear the staged bitmap and
all compatibility handles before returning NULL; when the optional RTG
surface exists, its provider registration is released through the separate
CyberGraphX boundary. No retry can inherit a stale Screen/View link.

Text cell rendering now follows the template-based Kickstart contract across
the complete font-height cell, not only the decoded glyph strike. Empty font
rows therefore participate in `JAM1|INVERSVID` foreground-background inversion
and `COMPLEMENT|INVERSVID` background complementation, while normal JAM2
background coverage remains a single full-cell pass. Underline geometry is
planned and rasterized only when the RastPort's algorithmic underline bit is
set; an unstyled text call cannot accidentally toggle the final font row
([Intuition text drawing modes](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Intuition_Text),
[Text autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/Text.html)).

The screen/view bridge also keeps malformed legacy geometry request-scoped:
when `OpenScreenTagList` receives an over-depth `NewScreen`, unrelated tags no
longer make the synthetic path clamp and publish a different screen. The
request declines before allocation and reports `OSERR_TOODEEP` through
`SA_ErrorCode`; an explicit `SA_Depth` remains the only tag-level override.
This preserves the CopperSharp68k/native-provider boundary for invalid legacy
screen envelopes while retaining the standard-planar host path for valid
requests.

Fixed-cell text keeps the public metric envelope and the rendered strike
envelope distinct. When a non-proportional `TextFont` has a `CharLoc` strike
narrower than its nominal `tf_XSize`, the portable renderer centers that strike
using integer half-padding inside the signed movement cell. The surrounding
source-zero columns stay mapped to their original cell positions, so
`JAM`/`INVERSVID`, complement, bold smear, and all-or-nothing destination
preflight still cover the complete template cell. Proportional fonts retain
their per-glyph origin; reverse-path fixed cells apply the same rule from the
decreasing-X cell origin. This follows the Kickstart split between nominal
`tf_XSize` advance and `tf_CharLoc` bit-width while keeping the guest layout
usable by both CopperSharp68k-native and CopperScreen-host implementations
([Graphics Library and Text](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Graphics_Library_and_Text), [TextFont](https://d0.se/include/graphics/text.h)).

AreaEnd now treats the attached `TmpRas` as a per-shape mask workspace. The
destination rollback envelope still spans the union of all recorded polygons
and ellipses, but the required scratch capacity is the largest individual
shape after 16-pixel word rounding. Each shape receives a local mask origin
and is cleared/applied before the next shape, preserving sequential
`BltPattern` and `COMPLEMENT` behavior without rejecting separated ellipses
that fit the caller's largest-shape raster. The managed fallback follows the
same local bounds, keeping the guest `TmpRas` descriptor and the
CopperSharp68k-compatible AreaInfo stream independent of host allocation
policy ([AROS AreaEnd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/areaend.c)).

The synthetic Intuition bridge also separates the Screen's private
Window-shaped presentation backing from a guest-owned `OpenWindow` claim.
`CloseScreen` returns `FALSE` while that public window is open, preserving the
active View and Screen links; `CloseWindow` retires only the claim, after which
the normal close path can blank and release the synthetic View. This keeps the
host path's reusable RastPort storage compatible with the Kickstart 3.1
screen/window lifecycle while leaving foreign and CyberGraphX-owned objects to
their own providers ([CloseScreen autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/CloseScreen)).

The same lifecycle repair covers an `OpenWindow` request that arrives before
the compatibility `Screen` exists. Once `OpenScreen` finishes staging, the
private backing Window receives its canonical `WScreen` link and becomes the
public `Screen.FirstWindow`; `CloseWindow` detaches that link while retaining
only the reset-scoped host storage. This keeps the guest prefix coherent for
CopperSharp68k callers without making the host presentation object a second
window owner.

When that host bridge reuses the backing object for repeated compatibility
`OpenWindow` calls, it keeps a separate open-claim count. `CloseScreen` remains
refused until every matching `CloseWindow` retires its claim, and only the
final close detaches `Screen.FirstWindow`. A generic host-object allocation
sentinel is never promoted to an open guest Window, so allocation failure
cannot leave the Screen permanently uncloseable.

The guest `NewWindow` and public `Window` prefixes now live beside the
Screen/View/BitMap/RastPort layout constants in one shared portable contract.
The synthetic host bridge aliases those offsets instead of carrying a second
set of literals, so a future CopperSharp68k implementation and the
CopperScreen-host path can share the same word-aligned structure boundary.

Screen teardown also validates the public `Screen.FirstWindow` chain before
blanking or releasing the synthetic View. The reset-scoped presentation
Window remains an allowed private link, while a foreign/native Window keeps
`CloseScreen` on the documented refusal path until its owner removes the
link. Host-only allocation sentinels are never published as guest Window
pointers.

The public Window ownership check includes the `Window.NextWindow` link. A
synthetic backing Window with a non-empty tail keeps `CloseScreen` on the
refusal path, and `CloseWindow` promotes a readable tail instead of dropping
the remaining guest chain. The shared layout contract exposes this link at
offset `0x00` for both CopperSharp68k-native and host implementations.

The optional full-GfxBase bridge also carries `LoadView`'s active-view
pointer. A mapped `GfxBase->ActiView` field is writability-probed and
committed before the scheduler/display handoff, so the owner observes the same
guest pointer that it is about to queue; a status-aware decline restores the
previous pointer. `LoadView(NULL)` clears it, while compact host images skip
the sidecar. This keeps CopperSharp68k/native guest state aligned with the
portable View lifecycle without moving display scheduling into the portable
core.

The idempotent `LoadView` path also repairs that mapped sidecar when a native
caller has edited it between otherwise identical requests. The repair is
guarded and does not rebuild or requeue the display stream; timed requests use
the same rule. Compact images with no mapped public field continue to omit the
optional bridge.

`AllocBitMap` applies the same ownership split to its `Friend_BitMap`: a
CyberGraphX-owned friend is declined before any standard-planar structure or
plane allocation, so the host provider can create its own surface and a native
overlay can tail-chain the original call. A readable standard friend remains
eligible for the portable wider-stride path.

The queued blitter bridge keeps its packed `bltnode` layout native-friendly by
requiring even guest structure and callback addresses before a node reaches the
scheduler. This preserves the 68000 address-error boundary while leaving queue
ordering, completion, and beam timing to CopperStart/custom-chip ownership.

`AllocRaster` applies the same word-boundary rule to the chip base returned by
the allocator. A permissive host allocator's odd result is released
immediately, keeping the raster usable by future native planar code only when
its first 16-bit word is addressable.

Palette ownership is now serialized at the portable `ColorMap` boundary. The
registered `PaletteExtra` lock covers map reads as well as `SetRGB*CM`, bulk
`LoadRGB4`/`LoadRGB32` staging and rollback, viewport setters, and the optional
host palette callback. This keeps CopperSharp68k-compatible guest state and
CopperScreen publication atomic for one map without claiming Exec task or
CyberGraphX ownership; an unmapped viewport still follows its existing provider
path.

PaletteExtra sidecars also have a native/provider corruption boundary. The
portable shadow records the last successfully published sharable span and
pen-list state, then validates the guest ref-count/allocation pointers, full
spans, viewport back-pointer, list heads/counts, list links, and reference
words before a pen-sharing operation. A deliberate narrowing of the private
sharable-index field is normalized into new derived lists; any other mismatch
is left to resident or provider ownership. This keeps the future
CopperSharp68k-native guest envelope authoritative without allowing a damaged
private list to become a host-side allocation or palette mutation.

The layers boundary follows the same ownership rule. CopperStart owns the
guest Layers library node, its Exec list link, and its open count; the
graphics provider consumes the exact layer/clip endpoints after Layers has
validated topology. Synthetic Exec close calls re-enter the library vector so
the host path observes the same `OpenCount` lifecycle as a native 68k call.
DeleteLayer keeps the classic dummy/layer register contract, with a narrowly
guarded compatibility fallback for callers that omit the dummy. No
CyberGraphX surface is admitted to this path.

Compatibility Exec `AddLibrary` and `RemLibrary` are likewise guest-list
operations: the synthetic gateway mutates the active Exec library list so
`FindName` observes the same publication as a native call. Allocation helpers
remain separate memory services and are not used as a substitute for list
ownership.

Validated layer text follows the same split boundary. The endpoint supplied by
layers is authoritative for clip traversal; the portable font/glyph renderer
receives a point-visibility predicate for exact inclusive clip bounds, while
smart/save bitmaps remain with the layer/provider owner. CyberGraphX is not
admitted to this path.

Validated layer Draw follows the same boundary. The portable Bresenham and
line-pattern state machine receives the endpoint clip predicate, while
transactional writes and public RastPort line state remain in the shared
graphics implementation. A layer carrying a provider-owned save bitmap is
declined instead of being redirected through the display bitmap.

Validated layer RectFill uses the portable area-pattern and draw-mode path with
the same endpoint predicate. Its complement/JAM behavior and transaction
boundary stay aligned with standard planar RastPorts; CyberGraphX and
provider-owned save bitmaps remain outside this implementation.

Validated layer SetRast uses the portable full-plane transaction with the same
endpoint predicate. It preflights every selected plane before publishing any
visible pixel, preserving the unconditional pen contract without allowing a
malformed secondary plane to produce a partial update.

Validated layer EraseRect uses the portable background-pen transaction with the
same endpoint predicate. Foreground-pen restoration and line-pattern phase
publication remain part of the shared transaction; provider-owned save bitmaps
and malformed fragments are declined at the layer boundary.

Validated layer `ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` use the portable text geometry and
clear-pen rules with the same endpoint predicate. `ClearScreen` keeps its
two-span preflight/rollback transaction, while smart/save bitmaps and other
provider-owned fragments remain outside the portable claim.

Validated layer `ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` use the portable scroll
transaction with the same endpoint predicate. Source samples are snapshotted
in logical coordinates, destination writes and BF backfill are clipped at the
validated endpoint, and the provider-owned bitmap path remains an explicit
decline.

Validated layer `DrawEllipse` uses the portable midpoint outline transaction
with the same endpoint predicate. Draw mode, write-mask handling, destination
preflight, and rollback remain shared with standard planar RastPorts; a
provider-owned save bitmap is declined instead of being redirected through the
display bitmap.

Validated layer `PolyDraw` uses the portable connected-line transaction with
the same endpoint predicate. Line-pattern phase, `FRST_DOT`, draw mode, cursor
publication, and rollback stay in the shared planar implementation, while
provider-owned save bitmaps remain an explicit decline path.

Validated layer `BltPattern` uses the portable area-pattern and draw-mode
transaction through a layer-local projected bitmap. The exact validated
ClipRect fragments control publication and preserve readable source samples;
write-mask handling, preflight, rollback, and the void D0 ABI remain shared
with the standard planar path. Non-planar provider surfaces stay behind their
explicit provider boundary.

Validated layer `Flood` uses the portable connected-region transaction through
the same projected bitmap. Seed-color matching, area-pattern behavior,
temporary-raster traversal, rollback, and result publication remain shared;
the exact validated ClipRect fragments gate visible writes while the public
layer clip pointer is not rediscovered.

Validated layer `BltTemplate` uses the portable clipped template transaction
through the projected bitmap. Template decoding, selected-plane preflight,
draw-mode publication, rollback, and the void D0 ABI remain shared with the
standard planar path; malformed source spans remain available to native or
provider ownership.

### G15/G18/G25 native-overlay `OpenMonitor` publication admission

`OpenMonitor` creates a resident `MonitorSpec` and, for a full native
CopperSharp68k-shaped `GfxBase`, links that node into the public
`MonitorList`. A mapped native overlay must not allocate a compatibility
node and only discover a read-only/provider-owned list during the later link
write. The portable core now recognizes the complete native base by its
mapped envelope and valid MonitorList sentinels; the overlay then preflights that
whole envelope through the host writability predicate before entering
`OpenMonitor`. Compact compatibility images do not satisfy the native-base
predicate and retain their existing monitor path. A declined full-base call
tail-chains with D0, cycles, and PC unchanged, without allocator activity;
direct compatibility dispatch and successful writable native-list publication
remain unchanged.

Validated layer `AreaEnd` uses the portable scanline area transaction through
the projected bitmap. Recorded polygon fill, temporary-raster ownership,
destination preflight, collector reset, rollback, and void-vector publication
remain shared with the standard planar path, with exact ClipRect fragments
controlling visible writes.

Validated layer `BltBitMapRastPort` consumes the source directly from the
guest BitMap argument and the destination through the exact Layers-supplied
ClipRect head. The portable planar minterm, write-mask, destination
preflight, overlap ordering, and transactional undo journal remain shared
with ordinary RastPorts; a poisoned-public-head regression proves that
clipped writes cannot escape the admitted endpoint. Masked all-planar and
CyberGraphX endpoints remain explicit provider boundaries.

Validated layer `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` now handles standard planar
destinations through the same projected layer-local bitmap and portable
mask-plane/minterm transaction. Exact ClipRect fragments gate the writes, the
destination journal rolls back the complete operation on a late fault, and
the void D0 ABI is cleared only after success. RTG endpoints continue through
the CyberGraphX-aware provider path.

The portable masked-blit transaction also consumes the destination
RastPort's `rp_Mask`. Its intersection with the participating bitmap depth
controls both undo-journal coverage and plane publication, so masked source
pixels cannot alter destination planes excluded by the caller's write mask.
The projected layer path reuses this same rule without widening the
CyberGraphX/provider boundary.

That effective mask also bounds admission and pixel staging. Source and
destination planes excluded by `rp_Mask` are not probed by the portable
transaction, so malformed storage in an unselected plane cannot reject a
valid selected-plane copy; this keeps the native/provider handoff boundary
aligned with the guest write mask.

The `Text` register boundary now preserves the same empty-string contract as
the portable core: a zero character count is a successful void no-op before
the text pointer, RastPort, font, layer, or RTG ownership fields are read.
Non-empty calls still take the guarded decoded-font/provider path, so this
exception does not broaden ownership of malformed or foreign text rendering.

The scheduler-aware CopperStart Layers gateway applies that boundary before it
resolves a layer endpoint or enters the portable layer raster engine. This
keeps a zero-count call independent of layer topology and text storage while
leaving every non-empty layered call on the validated endpoint/provider path.

The synthetic standard-planar screen path now carries an explicit PAL/NTSC
monitor part from `SA_DisplayID` through screen geometry selection. This keeps
`OpenScreenTagList` consistent with `QueryOverscan`: named PAL and NTSC modes
use their own standard raster height even when the host machine's active video
profile differs, while a zero monitor-part mode continues to follow the
machine-selected default. RTG and custom-bitmap display IDs remain outside
this compatibility owner.

The host lifecycle now decodes that monitor part through one helper shared by
`OpenScreenTagList` and `QueryOverscan`. A named PAL query on an NTSC host (and
the inverse) therefore receives the same width/height envelope as an open
screen request; default-monitor IDs still use the active chipset profile.

Validated layer `SetRast` now applies the exact supplied visibility predicate
to both its preflight and transactional snapshot. Hidden bitmap rows may stay
outside the host mapping without rejecting a clipped operation, while all
visible selected-plane writes retain the standard rollback contract. The
non-layered path continues to validate and snapshot the complete planar
allocation, and no CyberGraphX surface is admitted by this change.

The focused planar overlay and layer raster/boot checks remain green after
this boundary change (3 and 49 tests respectively); the graphics scaffold is
green at 743 tests. The direct Amiga test-project run is 3,945 passed, 39
failed, and 12 skipped, with failures confined to the unrelated
CIA/Denise/DMA/event-journal/JIT baseline.

The same visibility contract now reaches clipped `BltPattern`/`RectFill` and
`DrawEllipse` snapshots. Their rollback journals include only visible
selected-plane bytes when a validated layer predicate is present, while the
ordinary planar path keeps its byte-span snapshot. The combined graphics and
layer checks pass 794 tests after this extension; CyberGraphX ownership is
unchanged.

The clear-vector extension adds two hidden-fragment regressions: the focused
clear slice passes 6 tests, the combined graphics/layer slice passes 796, and
the direct Amiga test-project run is 3,950 passed, 38 failed, and 12 skipped
(4,000 total). Remaining failures are outside the graphics replacement in the
chipset/CIA/event-journal/JIT families.

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` now use the validated visibility predicate
for destination admission alongside their destination journal and write loops.
Source staging remains logical and readable without the clip predicate, so
overlap and source-coordinate behavior stay native-compatible; CyberGraphX
ownership remains unchanged. The focused scroll slice passes 7 tests, the
combined graphics/layer slice passes 797, and the direct Amiga test-project run
is 3,949 passed, 40 failed, and 12 skipped (4,001 total), with remaining
failures confined to unrelated chipset/CIA/event-journal/JIT families.

`FontExtent` now treats the decoded TextFont range as a complete contract:
failure to decode any glyph between `LoChar` and `HiChar` is a malformed font
boundary, not a sparse optional entry. The vector therefore leaves its guest
`TextExtent` result untouched and remains available to native/provider
ownership. The focused graphics scaffold passes 749 tests after this
regression, the combined graphics/layer slice passes 798, and the direct
Amiga test-project run is 3,953 passed, 37 failed, and 12 skipped (4,002
total). Remaining failures are confined to the existing CIA/Denise/DMA/event-
journal/JIT baseline; CyberGraphX ownership is unchanged.

`OpenScreenTagList` treats optional screen-tag payloads as atomic caller-owned
structures. Before staging any legacy `NewScreen` fields, the compatibility
bridge validates present nonzero `SA_DClip` and `SA_Pens` records and fully
decodes `SA_Colors`/`SA_Colors32` through their terminators. An unreadable,
cyclic, or unterminated payload declines to native/provider ownership without
publishing a synthetic screen, writing `SA_ErrorCode`, or mutating the
synthetic palette. Valid color records are staged as host tuples and published
only after the rest of the screen request is accepted. This keeps the
standard-planar lifecycle separate from CyberGraphX while making malformed
payload behavior deterministic for a future CopperSharp68k ROM path.

The focused malformed-payload theories pass 6 cases, the complete
`OpenScreenTagList` lifecycle slice passes 38 tests, and the combined
graphics/layer slice remains green at 798 tests after this boundary change.

Screen title pointers use the same ownership boundary as other caller-owned
screen payloads. `NewScreen.DefaultTitle` and the effective tagged `SA_Title`
are validated through the bounded 80-byte prefix consumed by the host title
renderer before legacy geometry or synthetic screen state is published. A
malformed legacy title remains available to native Intuition/provider code,
while an explicit readable `SA_Title` can override that legacy pointer. A
malformed effective title leaves `SA_ErrorCode`, palette state, and screen
allocation untouched; the native CopperSharp68k path can therefore share the
same guest-pointer admission rule without claiming public-screen/title-bar
ownership.

The focused title lifecycle regressions pass 3 cases, the full
`AmigaBootMemoryTests` class passes 221 tests, and the combined graphics/layer
slice remains green at 798 tests.

The screen-tag ABI is now keyed to the Kickstart `intuition/screens.h` values,
including the boolean `SA_ShowTitle`/`SA_Behind`/`SA_Quiet`/`SA_AutoScroll`
range and `SA_Pens`. The compatibility host accepts the earlier shim's five
legacy spellings only through an explicit boundary normalization, so the
CopperSharp68k guest layout and the host implementation share the canonical
numbers. This is intentionally a compatibility bridge, not a second public
tag namespace.

The synthetic owner also has an explicit recognized-tag handoff. It accepts
`SA_FullPalette`, `SA_ColorMapEntries`, and `SA_VideoControl` through the
graphics-owned ColorMap transaction. It declines attachment and
drag/exclusive tags, `SA_BackFill`, `SA_LikeWorkbench`, `SA_Reserved`,
`SA_MinimizeISG`, and the obsolete monitor-name tag before staging `NewScreen`
fields. A tagged `SA_Type` that requests `PUBLICSCREEN` (or another
non-custom type) is likewise left to native Intuition/public-screen ownership.
Unknown tags remain ignorable for forward compatibility. The decline preserves
the caller's `SA_ErrorCode`, palette, and reset-scoped screen state, matching
the existing custom-bitmap, RTG display-ID, and malformed-payload boundaries.

Canonical/alias and unowned-attribute lifecycle coverage now passes 14 new
cases; `AmigaBootMemoryTests` passes 235 tests, the focused OpenScreen slice
passes 71, and the combined graphics/layer slice passes 798.

The same ownership rule now covers the legacy `NewScreen` entry point:
`PUBLICSCREEN` and `CUSTOMBITMAP` type bits decline before the compatibility
allocator can stage geometry or bitmap state. A tagged open can explicitly
replace a legacy public type with a custom `SA_Type`, but no tag can make a
caller-owned bitmap storage request private. The ordinary and tagged paths
therefore converge on one native/provider boundary while retaining the shared
Screen/ViewPort/RastPort layout needed by CopperSharp68k and CopperScreen.
The two added lifecycle theories pass; the `AmigaBootMemoryTests` class now
passes 237 tests and the focused OpenScreen slice 73.

The overlapping legacy screen-tag bridge is also null-safe. A null value on
canonical V39/V40 `SA_VideoControl`, child-screen, or Workbench-pointer tags is
not rewritten as a legacy boolean; it remains an explicit provider-owned
request. Only the old TRUE spelling is normalized, preserving compatibility
with the existing shim without stealing null pointer ownership from native
Intuition or CyberGraphX. Four null-pointer lifecycle cases pass and the full
`AmigaBootMemoryTests` class now passes 241 tests.

`ViewPort.ExtendedModes` is a provider escape hatch rather than an OCS/ECS
mode selector. The portable implementation therefore declines every nonzero
value before deriving a mode ID, scrolling a viewport, or publishing a view.
This prevents an extended/AGA or monitor-specific viewport from being silently
reinterpreted as a standard planar mode and leaves the handoff available to a
future CopperSharp68k/native or CyberGraphX provider. The focused regression
passes and the combined graphics/layer slice now passes 799 tests.

The display database likewise names the canonical foreign monitor families
(VGA, A2024, prototype, Euro72, Euro36, Super72, DBLNTSC, and DBLPAL) without
claiming their records. FindDisplayInfo, ModeNotAvailable, and OpenMonitor
therefore leave those monitor parts to a native monitor or CyberGraphX provider;
the portable owner still exposes only the PAL/NTSC/default OCS/ECS records.
The ownership regression passes alongside the 751-test graphics scaffold.

The bounded ScrollRasterBF implementation also closes the clipped-source
backfill hole. When a displacement leaves no source coordinate inside the
logical rectangle after bitmap clipping, the portable path erases the complete
visible destination through the existing transactional EraseRect operation.
This keeps oversized and off-screen-origin scrolls consistent with the
provider-safe OCS/ECS raster contract while preserving pixels outside the
requested rectangle. The combined graphics/layer verification now passes 801
tests. The fresh full Amiga test-project run passes 3,983 tests and has no
graphics/layer failures; its 39 failures remain confined to the established
CIA, Denise/DMA, event-journal, and JIT baseline.

The display database now resolves `DTAG_MNTR` to a resident PAL/NTSC
`MonitorSpec` even before an explicit `OpenMonitor` call. The registry creates
that node lazily with an already-zero open count, so an existing monitor's
public open count is preserved and the node remains available after
`CloseMonitor` returns it to zero. Foreign monitor families still belong to
their native/provider patch. Pure and mapped gateway fixtures cover the
pre-open pointer, count reuse, post-close persistence, and query parity; the
public structure contract is defined by
[`graphics/displayinfo.h`](https://d0.se/include/graphics/displayinfo.h).

Lazy `DTAG_MNTR` publication uses a count-zero resident constructor rather
than a synthetic `OpenMonitor`/`CloseMonitor` pair. This keeps the query
contract atomic across guest-memory write failures: a failed close cannot
leak a caller-open reference, while a later explicit open still reuses the
same resident address and increments its public count. The zero-count
unmatched-close boundary is covered in the pure display-database fixture.

The lifecycle proof also injects a failure specifically at the
`ms_OpenCount` word used by `CloseMonitor`. `DTAG_MNTR` must still publish its
resident pointer with count zero and no allocator leak, proving that lazy
display queries do not depend on a second close-side guest write.

`SetMaxPen` now follows the classic RastPort contract: a nonzero maximum
publishes the contiguous write mask through the highest requested pen bit,
even when an earlier `SetWriteMask` or `SetMaxPen` call left a narrower mask;
`maxpen == 0` is a no-op. The register and `SetRPAttrsA` paths share this
behavior, and the direct/native-overlay parity fixture observes the resulting
`RPTAG_MaxPen` value through `GetRPAttrsA`. This keeps the guest state
compatible with the documented Kickstart optimization while retaining the
CopperSharp68k-friendly RastPort layout.

An `AreaInfo` initialized with zero maximum vectors is now a valid empty
collector. Its coordinate and flag table pointers are still validated as a
coherent guest envelope, but no vector can be appended: `AreaMove`,
`AreaDraw`, and `AreaEllipse` return failure without mutation, while `AreaEnd`
closes successfully as an empty no-op. This preserves the classic
five-bytes-per-vector storage contract for positive capacities without
turning an intentionally empty collector into a native/provider-only case.

`InitBitMap` now follows the extensible classic `BitMap` envelope instead of
requiring all eight public plane links. It snapshots and writes only through
the declared depth (`BitMapPlanes + depth * 4`), so compact one- and two-plane
structures are valid while caller-owned plane pointers remain untouched. The
same atomic rollback and malformed-span checks remain in force for the
declared portion, and full eight-plane maps continue to work without a
separate layout. This keeps the guest structure suitable for both
CopperSharp68k and CopperScreen memory projections.

All portable bitmap consumers use the same declared-depth envelope. Direct
blits, `BitMapScale`, sprite extraction, animation-buffer setup, and viewport
color sharing first read the fixed geometry/depth header and then probe only
`BitMapPlanes + depth * 4`; they never require the unused five-to-eight-plane
tail. The shared geometry/query reader keeps the full-envelope fast path for
ordinary standard maps and falls back to the compact span when a standard
marked header ends after its declared plane table. This preserves the native
`BMF_MINPLANES` representation while keeping the provider handoff explicit for
odd, wrapped, or truncated declared spans.

The screen lifecycle keeps `SA_ErrorCode` ownership consistent across both
forms of `OpenScreenTagList`: an explicit tag list takes precedence over the
`ExtNewScreen` chain, and an extension-only destination is retained through
accepted screen staging and completion. This prevents a legacy extended open
from publishing a screen while silently losing the caller's success/error
word, while malformed or provider-owned requests still leave that destination
untouched for native Intuition or a separate provider.

A nonzero error destination is admitted only when its 68k word alignment and
complete four-byte guest range are readable. An odd, wrapped, or unmapped
`SA_ErrorCode` therefore declines the synthetic owner before any Screen,
palette, or legacy request state is published; the native/provider path keeps
ownership of malformed output buffers.

Short `DTAG_NAME` display-database copies now reserve their final byte for a
guest C-string terminator whenever the caller's buffer ends inside the
`NameInfo.Name[32]` payload. Header-only probes remain intact, and full chunks
retain the fixed 32-byte name envelope. This keeps display-mode consumers from
observing an unterminated screen name while preserving the existing
CopperSharp68k-compatible QueryHeader layout. The native 17..55 implementation
reads the zero-filled name/reserved tail from a fixed-stride PC-relative table;
only the common 16-byte header is writable stack scratch, so HUNK relocation and
future ROM placement require no absolute pointer fixup.

`GetVPModeID` keeps the same status-aware ownership boundary as the other
screen/view vectors. A validated standard-planar `ViewPort` may publish its
profile-aware native ModeID, including `INVALID_ID` for a readable but
unsupported native state. A malformed or provider-owned viewport declines
without changing D0 or the CPU cycle, leaving Kickstart or the monitor/RTG
provider available to handle the request. The value-only core helper remains
available for host callers that intentionally consume `INVALID_ID`.

`BestModeIDA` now makes the same distinction for mode selection. A
well-formed native tag list that has no matching OCS/ECS record claims the
vector and publishes `INVALID_ID`, as required by the V39 result contract;
cyclic/unreadable lists, malformed viewport/source records, and foreign
monitor requests remain unclaimed for Kickstart or a provider. This keeps the
CopperStart status boundary useful to a future native 68k overlay without
inventing a host-only error code.

`CoerceMode` follows the same rule for a validated standard viewport. A
native geometry/depth request with no compatible PAL/NTSC record claims the
call and returns `INVALID_ID`; malformed or foreign-monitor requests remain
transparent to the resident/provider path. The portable result value and the
register-overlay ownership decision are therefore consistent for both mode
selection vectors.

The direct CopperScreen host entry and the reversible native-overlay gateway
are verified against the same no-match cases. A valid native depth-eight
request reaches both paths, publishes `INVALID_ID`, and preserves the caller's
cycle state; malformed tag/viewport envelopes still decline before either
entry point mutates the guest registers. This keeps the result/ownership
contract suitable for a future CopperSharp68k implementation without adding
CyberGraphX behavior to the base library.

The current verification slice is 35/35 for display and mode-selection
queries, 813/813 for the combined portable graphics/layer scaffold, and
244/244 for the AmigaBoot screen-memory lifecycle class. The emulator project
builds with zero warnings or errors; formal G6/G7 throughput gates were not
run because this unit changes no scheduler or custom-chip timing.

Standard screen dimensions are represented at both ABI boundaries. A tag-list
`SA_Width`/`SA_Height` value of `$FFFFFFFF` and a legacy `NewScreen` UWORD
value of `$FFFF` are the public `STDSCREENWIDTH`/`STDSCREENHEIGHT` sentinels,
not large literal rasters. The synthetic OCS/ECS path resolves them from the
active display clip, applying the selected monitor family, hires/superhires,
interlace, and the existing `SA_DClip` over `SA_Overscan` precedence. When no
legacy `NewScreen` exists, a standard dimension also defaults its edge to the
display clip; when one exists, its left/top coordinates remain caller-owned.
This keeps the Screen, ViewPort, and BitMap projections consistent for a
future CopperSharp68k ROM while leaving RTG/CyberGraphX ownership untouched.

When a legacy `NewScreen` is present, its `LeftEdge` and `TopEdge` remain the
position source even if its width/height fields use the standard sentinels and
the tag list supplies a custom `SA_DClip`. The clip still determines the
sentinel dimensions; only the no-NewScreen case derives an edge from the
display clip. This keeps the classic NewScreen-present position contract
separate from the tag-list-only defaulting rule.

G09 interleaved-layout closeout: the public `BitMap.BytesPerRow` now follows
the Kickstart 3.x interleaved convention and carries the complete row stride
across all declared planes. The portable/native-compatible readers derive a
physical per-plane stride before probing, drawing, blitting, scaling, or
tearing down storage; non-interleaved maps retain their ordinary per-plane
meaning. `AllocBitMap` publishes the aggregate stride only while
`BMF_INTERLEAVED` is present; on ECS/AGA an unavailable contiguous request
fails instead of being rewritten to separate planes, while OCS ignores the
flag and publishes ordinary per-plane storage. `GetBitMapAttr(BMA_WIDTH)`
reports the pixel width from the per-plane stride. This keeps the guest header,
plane pointers, allocator spans, and CopperScreen host projection coherent for
both native 68k and portable paths ([AllocBitMap autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocBitMap.html),
[GetBitMapAttr autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/GetBitMapAttr.html)).

G09 OCS/ECS capability closeout: the active display-chipset capability now
gates `BMF_INTERLEAVED` at both allocation and synthetic screen publication.
On OCS, Kickstart ignores the request, clears the flag, and exposes ordinary
separate-plane storage with per-plane `BytesPerRow`; ECS/AGA keeps the
aggregate interleaved stride. This follows the `AllocBitMap` OCS contract
while keeping the capability decision outside the guest `BitMap` layout, so a
future CopperSharp68k ROM and the CopperScreen host can share the same
structure offsets without importing CyberGraphX policy.

G09 synthetic ECS row-layout closeout: an ECS/AGA `OpenScreenTagList` request
with `SA_Interleaved` now publishes one contiguous row-interleaved backing
store. The public `BitMap.BytesPerRow` is the aggregate stride, each plane
pointer begins at its physical per-plane offset within the row, and host pixel
addressing advances by the aggregate stride for later rows. OCS continues to
publish separate-plane storage and the ordinary per-plane header value. The
screen lifecycle therefore exposes the same layout that `AllocBitMap`, native
68k callers, and the CopperScreen host renderer consume, without adding
CyberGraphX policy.

G12 blitter status boundary: the CopperStart context now accepts optional
status-returning callbacks for `OwnBlitter`, `DisownBlitter`, `WaitBlit`, and
`QBlit`/`QBSBlit`. These callbacks take precedence over the legacy `Action`
callbacks and can decline ownership or queue submission without changing D0,
cycles, or guest node memory. The graphics core still validates the packed
guest `bltnode`; a timed `IGraphicsTimedBlitterBackend` sidecar now carries the
guest call cycle into an explicit `GraphicsBlitterFifoBackend`. The backend
keeps V39+ ordinary and beam-synchronized requests in one bounded FIFO,
preserves strict submission order, gates a QBS head until its signed beam
predicate is ready, and retains beam metadata, ownership, in-flight
completion, and WaitBlit completion cycles. It never invokes guest
function or cleanup pointers itself: `CopperStartGraphicsBlitterScheduler`
dequeues a ready node through its dedicated 68k continuation gateway, enters
the function and optional cleanup callback with A0=`$DFF000` (custom-chip
register base) and A1=`bltnode`, repeats while D0 is nonzero, waits for custom
chip idle, and enters the optional cleanup callback before calling
`CompleteInFlight`. AmigaBoot supplies that scheduler to its host-device
boundaries, including blitter/beam wake candidates, and re-registers the
continuation after bus reset. Malformed or guest-mutated nodes fail closed.
This keeps callback execution and bus arbitration out of the portable host
process while exposing a deterministic CopperSharp68k-compatible handoff. A
host-backed regression now drives the real Agnus blitter registers through the
callback's A0 base and proves that the queued node remains in flight until the
custom-chip engine clears BBUSY; exact ROM callback instruction timing and
profile-specific arbitration remain native/provider gates. The base
`IGraphicsBlitterBackend` ABI and CyberGraphX boundary remain unchanged.

G09 raster ABI boundary: `AllocRaster` and `FreeRaster` do not share the same
register-width contract. `AllocRaster` receives ULONG width/height values,
but Kickstart's `FreeRaster` entry consumes UWORD width/height in D0/D1. The
portable adapter now truncates only the FreeRaster inputs before ownership and
teardown checks, preserving the guest chip-raster layout while keeping the
host/native overlay path from rejecting a valid allocation because stale high
register words were present ([FreeRaster autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/FreeRaster.html)).

G14 palette index boundary: the classic `SetRGB4CM` and `SetRGB4` entries
declare their pen number as a signed 16-bit `SHORT`. CopperStart therefore
decodes only D0's low word at the register boundary, while retaining the
portable ColorMap range check and rejecting `$FFFF` as a negative index. This
keeps direct CopperScreen and future CopperSharp68k dispatch aligned when
callers leave unrelated high register bits set
([SetRGB4CM autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/SetRGB4CM.html),
[SetRGB4 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/SetRGB4.html)).


G15 screen/ViewPort ownership rule: `SA_VideoControl` is admitted only after
its guest TagItem list is structurally readable. The synthetic screen session
allocates and owns a portable ColorMap for the screen depth, links it through
the public ViewPort and ColorMap fields, and invokes the same graphics service
used by the standalone `VideoControl` LVO. Completion is transactional: the
Screen is not returned, and `SA_ErrorCode` is not modified, if ColorMap
allocation or VideoControl semantics fail. A successful open writes the
deferred zero status after all display objects and VideoControl writes commit;
CloseScreen frees the owned map through the graphics service. This keeps the
guest layout and rollback boundary suitable for a future CopperSharp68k ROM
while leaving RTG/CyberGraphX ownership to its provider.

G15 ColorMap sizing rule: `SA_ColorMapEntries` is a bounded allocation
request, not a hint to silently fall back to the native depth. Values from 1
through 256 select the guest ColorMap size and force the Screen's ViewPort to
publish that map; zero or larger values decline to the native/provider path
before staging. If both `SA_ColorMapEntries` and `SA_VideoControl` are present,
the requested count is applied before the VideoControl transaction. The map
remains instance-owned and is released through `graphics.library` on
CloseScreen, preserving the common guest layout for CopperSharp68k and
CopperScreen. Without the tag, the screen uses Kickstart's default
`max(32, 1<<depth)` entry count.

`SA_FullPalette` is now accepted as the standard preference-selection tag.
Its presence requests the full depth-derived ColorMap (with an explicit
`SA_ColorMapEntries` count taking precedence), and the map follows the same
transactional Screen/BitMap/RasInfo ownership and CloseScreen teardown rules.
The host shim deliberately leaves actual preference color values at the
OCS/ECS palette boundary rather than fabricating a CyberGraphX/RTG palette.

G20 extended-sprite failure state: when a structurally valid automatic
`GetExtSpriteA` request cannot reserve a hardware slot, the portable manager
publishes `0xffff` into the ExtSprite's `SimpleSprite.num` field before
returning `-1`, matching the simple-sprite allocation convention. Explicit
number requests and already-reserved attached pairs preserve their existing
guest numbers, so a failed pair request cannot partially rewrite a caller's
state. Malformed or foreign envelopes remain an untouched native/provider
handoff. `GSTAG_SOFTSPRITE` and `GSTAG_SCANDOUBLED` are admitted only through
the typed `IGraphicsSpriteBackend` provider seam; the portable core does not
invent scheduler, scan-doubling, or software-sprite state.

`TextFit` path admission includes character kerning in each signed cursor
step. A kerning-induced stall or direction reversal is returned as an empty
fit, matching the cursor movement already used by `TextExtent` and `Text` and
leaving any provider/native fallback boundary explicit.

`BitMapScale` uses the requested source/destination scale factors as the
centered DDA phase inputs. The rounded destination width/height remain the
published extents, but are not substituted for the factors when selecting
source pixels; this preserves Kickstart's 1:2, 2:1, and other non-integral
sampling schedules while keeping planar and RTG/CyberGraphX ownership
separate.

The interleaved planar path now keeps the same ABI distinction during every
mutating operation. `BMF_INTERLEAVED` means `BitMap.BytesPerRow` is the
aggregate row-to-row stride, while each `Planes[n]` link starts at that
plane's byte slice in the first row; `AllocBitMap` publishes and frees one
contiguous block using that layout. Raster pixel addressing, blitter probes,
transaction snapshots, display-DMA envelope checks, and `BitMapScale` all
advance rows by the aggregate stride and touch only the per-plane byte width.
Malformed links or wrapped row envelopes decline before publication. OCS
ignores the interleaved request and uses ordinary per-plane storage; ECS/AGA
returns NULL when the required contiguous block is unavailable rather than
rewriting the header to a different storage form. The direct/register
regression exercises a two-plane scale across a later row, while the native
overlay retains its ownership/tail-chain boundary.

`AllocBitMap` keeps the chipset-specific width gate at the portable/native
boundary. ECS/AGA rejects requests wider than 32760 pixels, as documented by
Kickstart V39+, while OCS intentionally leaves that safety check to callers.
The guard is selected from the display capability supplied to the graphics
core; it is not encoded into the shared bitmap geometry helper, so a future
CopperSharp68k or provider implementation can apply its own hardware policy.

V36 pixel-array ABI boundary: `ReadPixelLine8`, `WritePixelLine8`,
`ReadPixelArray8`, and `WritePixelArray8` take UWORD coordinates and counts at
the Kickstart register boundary. The portable planar core therefore keeps
non-negative `int` dimensions, while CopperStart decodes only each argument's
low word as unsigned before dispatch. Layered and RTG/provider callbacks retain
their explicit provider contracts, so this ABI correction does not import
CyberGraphX policy into the native planar path
([ReadPixelLine8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixelLine8.html),
[WritePixelLine8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelLine8.html),
[WritePixelArray8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelArray8.html)).

V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` ABI boundary: `bytesperrow` is a signed LONG, not an
unsigned host stride. The portable core and both CopperStart layer/native
bridges therefore preserve the complete 32-bit signed register value and
reject non-positive strides before probing the source array or publishing any
planar writes. This keeps negative or high-bit malformed requests available
to the native/provider owner while retaining the documented LONG coordinate
semantics and the separate CyberGraphX boundary
([WriteChunkyPixels autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WriteChunkyPixels)).

Pixel-array ownership is now enforced at the pure/core boundary as well as at
the CopperStart register adapter. `ReadPixelLine8`, `WritePixelLine8`,
`ReadPixelArray8`, `WritePixelArray8`, and `WriteChunkyPixels` reject a
nonzero `RastPort.Layer` before reading caller arrays or touching planar
storage. The explicit LayersRaster provider remains the only path that can
claim a layered request, so direct CopperSharp68k-compatible helpers cannot
silently bypass layers.library clipping, damage, or backing-store policy.

SetRast write-mask rule: the whole-raster copy operation ignores the active
draw mode, but it still applies `RastPort.Mask` to protect unselected
bitplanes. The portable planar path already carries that mask through its
transactional preflight/write loop; a focused two-plane regression now locks
the behavior to the classic write-mask contract without expanding the
CyberGraphX/provider boundary
([Graphics Primitives — RastPort Write Mask](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Graphics_Primitives)).

`SetOutlinePen` consumes the classic ULONG pen argument through the portable
core, tag-list setter, CopperStart register adapter, and direct host path. Only
the low byte is committed to the guest `RastPort.AOlPen` field, while
`AREAOUTLINE` and the previous byte-sized result retain their existing
semantics. This preserves the public 68k ABI without widening the
CopperSharp68k guest layout; malformed RastPorts remain available to native or
provider ownership ([AROS `SetOutlinePen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setoutlinepen.c)).

The same boundary applies to `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, and
`SetABPenDrMd`: each consumes full ULONG register values, then commits only the
documented low byte to `FgPen`, `BgPen`, or `DrawMode`. Minterm recomputation,
line-pattern restart, and the existing all-or-nothing guest transaction are
unchanged. This keeps high-bit input available to the native/provider owner
until the portable call claims it while retaining the classic RastPort layout
([AROS `SetAPen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c),
[AROS `SetBPen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setbpen.c),
[AROS `SetDrMd`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setdrmd.c),
[AROS `SetABPenDrMd`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setabpendrmd.c)).

`SetRast` follows the same ULONG-input rule. The full pen value reaches the
standard-planar core and any validated layer provider, while only its low byte
selects the planar color bits. The existing write-mask, copy-mode, visibility,
and rollback semantics remain unchanged; the public void D0 ABI and
CopperSharp68k guest layout are preserved ([AROS `SetRast`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setrast.c)).

Layered line ownership is enforced at both host and pure-core boundaries:
`Draw` and `PolyDraw` now read `RastPort.Layer` and decline a nonzero layer
unless an explicit provider visibility predicate is supplied. CopperStart
already routes mapped layered vectors to layers/native callbacks; the core
guard prevents a direct CopperSharp68k-compatible caller from bypassing that
clipping, damage, and backing-store boundary. A focused regression proves
that both calls preserve the cursor and destination when no provider exists.
Standard-planar clipping and line-pattern phase behavior are unchanged.

The same direct-core ownership guard now covers `ReadPixel`, `WritePixel`,
and `SetRast`: a nonzero `RastPort.Layer` is rejected unless the operation
has an explicit provider visibility predicate. This keeps pure standard-planar
helpers from bypassing layers/native clipping or damage tracking while the
CopperStart adapter continues to route layered vectors to the provider. The
regression also proves that these calls leave the backing planes untouched.

Area construction/fill and seed `Flood` now use the same guard for direct
portable calls: a layered RastPort is rejected before collector, temporary
raster, or destination state is touched. Layered callers continue through the
explicit layer backend, keeping clipping, damage, and backing-store policy out
of the standard-planar implementation.

`Text` now enforces the same rule for direct rasterized text: a layered
RastPort is rejected unless a visibility predicate explicitly represents the
provider's logical surface. The host adapter still routes layered text to its
layer backend, while standard-planar text retains its existing glyph,
draw-mode, cursor, and rollback semantics.

Validated layer execution has an explicit `allowLayered` collector path for
`AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, `AreaEnd`, and `Flood`. It is used only
inside the already-admitted LayersRaster provider, whose endpoint validation
and logical-memory projection supply the missing clipping/damage authority;
ordinary `GraphicsLibraryCore` calls retain the fail-closed layer guard.
G19 native `BitMapScale` alignment closeout: the portable scaler now rejects
odd non-null source or destination plane pointers before publishing either
destination extent word. Source row addressing also keeps the guest
`WORD * WORD` stride product wide until the final 32-bit address check, so a
large valid bitmap cannot wrap into a low alias on the host path. Null source
planes remain legal for the classic source form; destination planes remain
strictly required.

G10 large-stride blit closeout: the portable `BltBitMap` pixel readers and
writers now keep the guest row-base calculation wide for large `BytesPerRow`
and late rows reached through the signed-WORD blit coordinates. The final
plane-address addition still enforces the 32-bit guest envelope, so a valid
high-row copy cannot wrap into an unrelated low address while malformed spans
remain unclaimed. The sparse high-address regression exercises source staging,
minterm publication, and the destination write at row 65533 without requiring
a contiguous host allocation.

G19 endpoint-range closeout: the V36 pixel-array helpers now reject endpoint
spans wider than the 32-bit guest coordinate contract before narrowing their
width/height to unsigned values. This prevents a full signed-int span from
becoming a zero-sized success after truncation, and keeps the maximum UWORD
register rectangle on the bounded staging/failure path without publishing
partial planar or array state.

G10 native blit alignment closeout: standard planar `BltBitMap` validation
now rejects odd ordinary source-plane and destination-plane pointers before
TempA selection, source staging, or destination mutation. The classic source
constants (null and `$FFFFFFFF`) remain legal special planes, while every
ordinary planar stream keeps the 68000 word-address rule. Shifted-overlap
coverage uses two even bases and still proves TempA overlap handling without
encoding a non-native odd plane address.

G09 native header-alignment closeout: `AllocBitMap` now requires the returned
public `BitMap` header to be word-aligned before probing, clearing, or writing
any guest fields. A byte-addressable host allocator may still return an odd
provisional address, but a native 68000 cannot legally consume the header's
WORD/LONG members there; the bridge releases that provisional public span and
leaves the vector available to the native/provider owner. Odd chip-plane bases
remain usable as non-displayable standard storage when the header itself is
aligned, preserving the separate `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` capability result.

### Private RastPort pen-enable state

The portable layout reserves the private `RPF_NO_PENS` bit in the guest
`RastPort.Flags` word at `0x4000` (bit 14). The public `graphics/rastport.h`
header does not expose this bit, but the classic setter implementations use it
to represent disabled pens. `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, and
`SetABPenDrMd` therefore clear the bit whenever they successfully publish a
new pen/mode state, while preserving all unrelated flag bits. The update is
transactional with minterm regeneration and line-pattern restart: a failure in
the late Flags-word write restores the source byte, derived minterms, pattern
phase, and both flag bytes. `SetRPAttrsA` snapshots the same private bytes so a
later tag failure cannot leak the cleared state. This keeps the guest layout
usable by a future CopperSharp68k implementation while matching the portable
host path; CyberGraphX/provider color ownership remains outside this bit.

The bit definition and setter behavior are source-backed by the AROS graphics
support header and classic setter sources ([`gfxfuncsupport.h`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h), [`SetAPen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c), [`SetBPen`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setbpen.c), [`SetABPenDrMd`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setabpendrmd.c)).

G17 viewport-aware bitmap-swap handoff closeout (2026-08-12): the
`ChangeVPBitMap` display adapter now prefers the explicit viewport-aware
rebuild callback for both untimed and timed calls, falling back to the generic
display rebuild only when a host does not expose the narrower seam. Capability
reporting includes both callback families, and the timed path preserves the
caller cycle when routing the request. This keeps per-viewport presentation
ownership available to CopperScreen/native hosts and avoids collapsing a
multi-viewport swap into an unrelated global rethink; DBufInfo message timing
and CyberGraphX bitmap ownership remain separate boundaries.

G06/G07 zero-mask ellipse closeout (2026-08-12): non-layered `DrawEllipse`
now returns success without probing outline points when `RastPort.Mask` is
zero, matching the shared planar primitive no-op contract. Real writes still
retain the Kickstart no-clipping boundary and complete preflight/rollback;
layered ownership still requires the explicit provider visibility seam.

G08 zero-mask AreaEnd closeout (2026-08-12): a non-empty area stream now
retains its collector transaction but completes successfully when
`RastPort.Mask` selects no planes. The portable path validates the recorded
vectors, resets the AreaInfo collector, and skips shape-bound, pattern, and
temporary-raster destination probes that cannot affect a write. This keeps an
out-of-raster area shape a masked no-op while nonzero-mask AreaEnd retains its
strict non-layered bounds and rollback contract; layer damage and provider
ownership remain separate.

G07 `INVERSVID|JAM1` RectFill closeout (2026-08-12): when no external stencil
or AreaPtrn is present, inverse video turns the implicit all-one source into
all zeroes. With JAM1 (including `COMPLEMENT|INVERSVID`) no destination cells
are selected, so the portable path now returns success without probing planar
storage. JAM2, explicit stencils, and non-empty area patterns retain their
normal pattern and destination preflight behavior ([AROS `RectFill`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/rectfill.c)).

G08 `INVERSVID|JAM1` AreaEnd closeout (2026-08-12): the same null-pattern
empty-source rule now applies to recorded polygon and ellipse fills. After
validating and decoding the AreaInfo stream, the portable path resets the
collector and skips temporary-raster, pattern, and destination probes when no
fill cell can be selected. JAM2 and explicit patterns retain the ordinary
shape-bound and rollback path; layer damage/provider ownership remains
separate.

G07 SetRast zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-12): `SetRast` now
returns immediately after validating the RastPort/BitMap envelope when
`RastPort.Mask` is zero. The successful no-op no longer walks every logical
pixel of a maximum-size guest raster, while nonzero masks retain complete
plane preflight, snapshot, and rollback semantics.

G07 ScrollRaster zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-12): both
`ScrollRaster` variants now return successfully after validating the
RastPort/BitMap envelope when no destination planes are selected. The portable
path no longer stages the potentially enormous source rectangle or reads
source planes that cannot be committed; nonzero-mask scrolling retains its
source snapshot, vacated-area, and rollback semantics.

G07 clear-vector zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-12): the shared
`FillRectangle` writer now treats an empty `RastPort.Mask` as a successful
destination no-op after the caller has validated the public envelope. This
keeps `ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` line-pattern publication and rollback
semantics intact while preventing a maximum-size guest bitmap from entering a
multi-billion-pixel host walk; nonzero-mask clear writes retain their clipped
preflight, snapshot, and restore path.

G06/G19 pixel-array zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): the V36
`WritePixelLine8`/`WritePixelArray8` and V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` writers now
complete as zero-count successes after validating the RastPort, bitmap, and
request geometry when no destination planes are selected. They do not stage
the caller's padded byte array, validate a temporary RastPort, or walk the
destination plane span; nonzero-mask requests retain complete source,
destination, and rollback preflight. The CopperStart gateway applies the same
mask-aware destination probe boundary so malformed/unmapped plane storage does
not steal an otherwise bounded masked no-op from native/provider ownership.

G19 `ReadPixelArray8` aliasing closeout (2026-08-13): the portable reader now
stages every logical planar sample before publishing any chunky output byte.
This keeps a caller-owned array that overlaps a source plane deterministic
instead of allowing an early output write to change later source bits. Direct
and CopperStart regressions cover the same clipped count and byte result;
temporary-RastPort validation and the CyberGraphX/provider boundary remain
unchanged.

G04/G06 text zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): `Text` now keeps
decoding the guest character stream and publishing its cursor/line state, but
skips glyph-cell, background, underline, and destination traversal when
`RastPort.Mask` selects no planes. This preserves text advancement while
preventing a valid maximum-size glyph from becoming a multi-billion-cell host
walk; nonzero-mask text retains complete glyph-strike and destination
preflight with its transactional raster/state rollback.

G11 `BltTemplate` zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): after
validating the aligned template pointer, RastPort/BitMap envelope, and
destination mask, the portable template vector now returns a successful void
no-op when no destination planes are selected. It avoids allocating or
decoding a potentially enormous clipped template while preserving the full
source/destination preflight and rollback path for nonzero masks; the
CopperStart adapter keeps the same D0/cycle boundary.

G11 `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` zero-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): the
portable masked planar blit now defers probing the external stencil until
after clipping and the destination `RastPort.Mask` plane-selection gate. A
valid zero-mask call therefore succeeds without requiring an otherwise
unmapped or huge stencil rectangle, while nonzero effective masks retain
stencil, source, destination, and rollback preflight. Direct and CopperStart
register coverage preserves the documented void/D0 boundary.

G08 zero-mask `Flood` boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): after validating the
mode, layer, bitmap, mask, and in-raster seed envelope, `Flood` now returns a
bounded BOOL success when no destination plane is selected. It skips
optional `TmpRas`/area-pattern inspection, full-raster destination probing,
connected-region staging, and temporary Chip allocation; nonzero-mask flood
retains its complete source, pattern, temporary-raster, snapshot, and
rollback path.

G07/G11 zero-mask `BltPattern` boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): the
rectangular pattern path now returns a bounded void success after validating
the public rectangle and RastPort/BitMap envelope when no destination plane is
selected. External stencils and area-pattern storage are not probed in that
case; selected-plane pattern operations retain stencil, pattern, destination,
and rollback preflight.

G06 zero-mask `Draw`/`PolyDraw` boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): connected
line primitives now preserve their guest cursor, `FRST_DOT`, and line-pattern
phase transitions without walking every Bresenham sample when `RastPort.Mask`
selects no planes. `PolyDraw` still consumes and validates the complete point
stream, while each segment's state-only commit remains transactional; selected
plane paths retain full traversal, visibility, destination preflight, and
rollback.

G11 `BltClear` span-guard closeout (2026-08-13): the portable clear vector
 now rejects an arithmetically valid but larger-than-`Int32` transactional span
 before probing any guest bytes. This preserves the native/provider fallback
 boundary for maximal row-mode requests and leaves ordinary word-clears'
 complete preflight and rollback unchanged.

G06 `SetRast` span-guard closeout (2026-08-13): complete planar SetRast
staging is now bounded by the host transactional limit. A valid maximum
UWORD bitmap whose selected plane exceeds `Int32.MaxValue` is rejected before
the byte preflight or List-backed undo journal; clipped layer/provider paths
continue to stage only visible fragments, and zero-mask SetRast remains a
successful bounded no-op.

G08 temporary-raster probe closeout (2026-08-13): shared contiguous/row-span
consumer validators fail closed for multi-gigabyte guest spans before any host
byte walk. `InitTmpRas` itself only snapshots and publishes its descriptor, so
even a multi-gigabyte or currently unmapped backing span is not probed until an
AreaEnd/Flood/Text consumer needs it. Normal guest scratch buffers continue
through the same guarded consumer validation and descriptor rollback
transaction.

G05/G07 region-preflight closeout (2026-08-13): planar region probing and
undo-snapshot helpers now apply a common host-work bound to both selected
plane bytes and visibility-aware pixel walks. A maximum eight-plane
`ClearScreen` request therefore declines before the remaining full-width
bitmap span can monopolize the host, while ordinary clipped/layer-visible
regions continue through their existing provider and rollback paths.

G07 `SetRast` pixel-walk closeout (2026-08-13): complete non-layered fills now
bound the logical pixel count as well as each selected plane's byte span before
the per-pixel write loop. A bitmap can fit the per-plane `Int32` staging bound
while still containing more than two billion samples; that case now declines
without probing or mutating guest plane storage. Direct and CopperStart
coverage preserve the native/provider D0 and cycle boundary, while zero-mask
and visibility-aware paths remain explicitly separate.

G04 text-work closeout (2026-08-13): nonzero-mask `Text` now applies a shared
portable work budget before nested glyph-cell rendering. The budget covers
decoded strike bytes, character-cell rows/columns, bold smear, JAM2 background
envelopes, and underline spans; the guest stream and font metadata are still
validated before any raster mutation. Maximal valid glyph declarations now
decline before a multi-billion host walk, while zero-mask text retains its
cursor/line-state-only semantics and CopperStart preserves the native void/D0
fallback boundary.

G03/G04 text-metric count closeout (2026-08-13): `TextLength`, `TextExtent`,
and the non-empty `TextFit` path now reject character counts above the
portable `Int32.MaxValue` work contract before decoding or walking the guest
