stream. `TextFit` keeps its established alternate-height no-fit shortcut
authoritative, so a valid zero-fit query still publishes an empty extent
without inspecting malformed text. Direct and CopperStart metric vectors
preserve the native/provider fallback boundary and leave guest extents
unchanged on bounded decline.

G05/G07 region pixel-walk closeout (2026-08-13): shared planar region
preflight and snapshot helpers now bound logical touched pixels as well as
selected byte spans for ordinary non-layered operations. A maximum
`ClearScreen` whose plane bytes fit the transactional limit but whose
65536-by-65535 publication would exceed it now declines before probing or
mutating guest storage; visibility-aware layer paths retain the same bound and
zero-mask no-op paths remain successful.

G05/G07 visibility-snapshot closeout (2026-08-13): the direct
visibility-aware `SetRast` snapshot path now applies the same logical pixel
budget before invoking a provider predicate. This closes the alternate path
that bypasses clipped-region preflight while keeping explicit layer ownership,
zero-mask success, and native/provider fallback unchanged.

The shared guards treat a write mask that selects only planes above the
declared bitmap depth as an effective zero mask, preserving the bounded
successful no-op contract for both ordinary and visibility-aware callers.

G15/G17 CyberGraphX RasInfo-chain ownership closeout (2026-08-13): the
portable host classifier now scans the bounded linked `RasInfo` chain of a
viewport, rather than inspecting only its first node, before claiming OCS/ECS
display lifecycle vectors. A provider-owned bitmap in a secondary
dual-playfield/interleaved node therefore keeps `ChangeVPBitMap`, viewport
timing, copper, and mode-query paths on the CyberGraphX/provider boundary;
malformed or cyclic chains remain unclaimed for native/provider handling.
Focused classifier coverage proves secondary-node detection alongside the
existing wrapped-address rejection; full provider display-DMA parity remains
outside this graphics.library replacement.

G04/G06/G07/G08/G11 effective-mask boundedness closeout (2026-08-13): a
RastPort write mask is now intersected with the linked BitMap's declared
plane depth before text, lines, fills, area/flood, ellipse, scroll, template,
and complete-raster operations choose their work path. Masks containing only
bits above `bm_Depth` therefore publish the same bounded successful no-op as
an explicit zero mask, without staging glyph cells or walking destination
pixels. Direct and CopperStart regressions cover maximal `SetRast` and Text
requests with an unavailable declared plane; selected-plane behavior is
unchanged.
### G06 effective-mask pixel-write boundary (2026-08-13)

The shared per-pixel writer now normalizes `RastPort.Mask` against the linked
`BitMap` depth itself. This keeps direct `WritePixel` calls on the same
effective-zero-mask contract as the higher-level line, fill, text, and
complete-raster paths: mask bits above `bm_Depth` select no storage and must
complete without probing or mutating a declared plane. Direct and
CopperStart register coverage preserve the pixel byte, D0, and cycles.

### G04 zero-mask text stream bound (2026-08-13)

`Text` now bounds the character decode/cursor-advance pass itself, not only
the nonzero-mask glyph and destination work. A zero or above-depth effective
mask still has the classic cursor-only behavior for ordinary counts, but an
oversized ULONG character stream declines before asking the font backend for a
glyph. This keeps the portable host path finite while preserving the native
provider fallback boundary and leaving the RastPort cursor unchanged on the
bounded decline.

### G07/G11 patterned-rectangle pixel-walk bound (2026-08-13)

`BltPattern`/`RectFill` now bound a maximal signed-word request when the linked
bitmap envelope is also above the portable pixel budget, before the stencil,
area-pattern, visibility, and destination preflight loops. Small bitmaps keep
the classic clipping behavior for extreme coordinates; the later transactional
byte snapshot and clipped-pixel guard still protect the remaining staging and
provider-visible paths. The inverse-video/JAM1 null-pattern no-op remains a
successful bounded shortcut.

### G06/G19 effective-mask chunky-writer boundary (2026-08-13)

The V36 `WritePixelLine8` and `WritePixelArray8` paths, together with the
V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` path, now intersect `RastPort.Mask` with the linked
`BitMap` depth before staging the guest chunky source or probing planar
destination rows. A mask containing only bits above `bm_Depth` cannot publish
a planar byte, so it is claimed as the same zero-count successful no-op as an
explicit zero mask. The direct core and CopperStart register paths are both
covered with maximal signed-word geometry, an unreadable source envelope, and
an unavailable plane; selected-plane conversion and clipped-count behavior
remain unchanged. This is a portable OCS/ECS boundedness rule and does not
claim CyberGraphX/RTG surfaces.

### G10 V36 constant source planes (2026-08-13)

The portable `BltBitMap` path accepts the Kickstart V36 source-plane
sentinels: a zero source plane is an all-zero source and `$FFFFFFFF` is an
all-one source. These values are source-only constants; destination planes
remain ordinary, aligned guest storage. The operation preserves the classic
participating-plane count while avoiding a bogus guest-memory probe, with a
focused regression covering direct portable execution.

### G09 `ScalerDiv` word-return ABI (2026-08-13)

The V36 `ScalerDiv` helper keeps its widened product and remainder arithmetic
through the division/rounding step, then returns the result through its public
`UWORD` ABI. It therefore exposes the low word when a valid 14-bit-factor
product exceeds `$FFFF`; the portable implementation must not saturate such a
value at `UWORD_MAX`. Focused direct and CopperStart coverage pins the
overflowing `0x3FFF * 0x3FFF / 1` case to the native low-word result while
retaining zero-factor/denominator rejection and ordinary nearest-integer
extent behavior.

### G11 `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` mask ownership (2026-08-13)

The classic masked bitmap-to-RastPort vector has two independent masks: the
external one-bit `bltMask` gates pixels, while the destination `RastPort.Mask`
field is explicitly ignored. The portable OCS/ECS path therefore validates and
publishes every plane common to the source and destination, even when the
RastPort mask is zero or selects only a subset. This keeps the CopperSharp68k
ABI aligned with Kickstart and leaves layered RastPorts and CyberGraphX/RTG
surfaces to their existing provider boundaries. Direct and CopperStart tests
cover both the ignored RastPort mask and the required external mask envelope.

### G09/G15 NULL structure-initializer boundary (2026-08-13)

The portable structure initializers now reject a zero guest base before any
range probe or clear for `RastPort`, `View`, `ViewPort`, `RasInfo`, `BitMap`,
`AreaInfo`, and `TmpRas`. A host memory adapter may expose address zero as a
byte-addressable location, but the native 68000 ABI still treats it as the
NULL pointer; accepting it would let the compatibility path clear low memory
and steal a malformed call from Kickstart or a provider. Direct core tests and
the CopperStart register adapter verify that the guest bytes, D0, and cycles
remain unchanged on every rejected initializer. Successful construction keeps
the existing word-alignment, full-envelope, default-origin, sprite-priority,
and transactional rollback rules. No CyberGraphX or display-DMA ownership is
introduced by this guard.

### G09/G19 `GetBitMapAttr(BMA_FLAGS)` displayability capability (2026-08-13)

`BMA_FLAGS` now treats `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` as a derived capability rather than
blindly echoing a stale guest request bit. When the header advertises that
flag, the portable query re-reads every declared plane pointer and applies the
same word-aligned stride/plane-start predicate used by `AllocBitMap`; a null,
odd, or unreadable plane link clears only `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` while preserving
the public `BMF_STANDARD`/`BMF_INTERLEAVED` classification. This matches the
Kickstart contract that displayability is reported only when the bitmap meets
the native alignment restrictions ([GetBitMapAttr autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/GetBitMapAttr)). Direct and CopperStart
coverage pin both the misaligned fail-closed result and the aligned result.
The rule remains limited to native planar OCS/ECS storage; CyberGraphX/RTG
providers keep their own bitmap-attribute semantics.

### G09 display-DMA address-class capability (2026-08-13)

Word alignment is necessary but not sufficient for a native display surface.
The portable memory contract now has an optional `IGraphicsDisplayMemory`
sidecar with `IsDisplayDmaRange(address, byteCount)`. When present, bitmap
publication and strict display-chain validation require every complete plane
span to belong to that provider-selected address class; `CopperStart` wires
the sidecar to the bus's chip-RAM classifier, which is the native OCS/ECS
display-DMA class. A memory-only CopperSharp68k provider that does not expose
the sidecar retains the existing alignment/mapping rule, while RTG/CyberGraphX
providers remain outside the portable path. No fixed host address range is
encoded in graphics.library, and the sidecar is intentionally orthogonal to
guest `BitMap` offsets and the scheduler/timing boundary.

### G09/G19 native-overlay BMA_FLAGS parity (2026-08-13)

The native-safe ROM overlay differential now exercises the same
`GetBitMapAttr(BMA_FLAGS)` capability rule as the direct portable core. It
proves that an aligned declared plane set publishes `BMF_DISPLAYABLE`, while
making one plane odd clears only that capability in both paths. This keeps the
CopperSharp68k-compatible guest ABI and the CopperScreen host gateway on the
same result without claiming RTG or layered bitmap ownership.

### G16/G17 NULL viewport-copper teardown boundary (2026-08-13)

`FreeVPortCopLists(NULL)` now declines explicitly before probing or clearing
guest memory. This keeps a host memory adapter that happens to map address zero
from turning the null pointer into a real viewport teardown, and leaves the
optional CopperStart/native resource owner untouched. Direct core coverage and
the CopperStart register adapter verify that the four guest copper links, D0,
cycles, and owner callback count remain unchanged. The guard is limited to the
standard OCS/ECS viewport-copper lifecycle; native/provider and CyberGraphX
ownership remain available for other display objects.
### G18 zero-default DisplayInfo handle boundary (2026-08-13)

The valid default-lores ModeID is `0`, which is also the public NULL value for
display-info handles. The portable registry therefore preserves compact
ModeID-backed handles for nonzero records but returns the reserved nonzero
`GraphicsDisplayDatabase.DefaultModeHandle` (`0xFFFFFFFE`) for the default
record. `GetDisplayInfoData` maps that compatibility handle back to the zero
record and keeps a non-null handle authoritative over its optional ID. Direct,
register, and CopperStart ROM-overlay regressions cover this boundary. The
`NextDisplayInfo` iteration returns public ModeID keys (including the valid
zero default-lores key); only `FindDisplayInfo` exposes the private nonzero
handle. The CyberGraphX/provider seam remains unchanged.

Reference contracts: [`NextDisplayInfo` autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html)
and [`graphics/displayinfo.h`](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node00BD.html).

### G12/G26/G27 status-aware blitter overlay boundary (2026-08-13)

The native-safe overlay now includes the three synchronous blitter ownership
vectors: `OwnBlitter`, `DisownBlitter`, and `WaitBlit`. They are claimed only
when the CopperStart context exposes the corresponding status-aware callback;
otherwise `GraphicsServices` restores the original native vector target and
leaves the guest register/cycle state available to Kickstart or another
provider. Direct and mapped jump-table execution share the same portable
register adapter and have differential coverage for D0, cycles, and callback
cardinality. The asynchronous `QBlit`/`QBSBlit` vectors now share the
conditional overlay boundary, while queue execution, completion, and beam
arbitration remain provider-owned. No CyberGraphX surface is introduced by
this overlay slice.

### G12/G26/G27 queued-blitter overlay boundary (2026-08-13)

`QBlit` and `QBSBlit` are now admitted beside the synchronous blitter vectors
when an explicit queue backend accepts the validated guest `bltnode`. The
portable adapter preserves the packed node contract and signed QBS beam-sync
metadata, while a backend refusal restores the original native vector target
without changing D0 or cycles. The overlay never calls a guest function or
cleanup pointer itself; CopperStart/native scheduling owns FIFO order,
completion, cleanup, and custom-chip arbitration. CyberGraphX remains outside
this boundary.

### G24/G26/G27 super-bitmap overlay boundary (2026-08-13)

`SyncSBitMap` and `CopySBitMap` are now admitted to the native-safe overlay
when an explicit Layers/native backend claims the layer address. They retain
the classic void result boundary and tail-chain transparently on provider
decline, preserving D0 and cycles. `LockLayerRom`, `AttemptLockLayerRom`, and
`UnlockLayerRom` now cross the same overlay through the typed Layers gateway:
the gateway's `Completed` or `BlockCurrentTask` result is returned unchanged,
while foreign or provider-less layers tail-chain to the captured native
vector. No CyberGraphX behavior is added here.

### G20/G26/G27 GELS overlay boundary (2026-08-13)

The native-safe overlay admits `DoCollision` and `DrawGList` only after the
typed GELS backend is fully present, including its required Bob-removal
callback. The portable path initializes and validates the guest `GelsInfo`
envelope, then forwards the classic void calls; without that provider it
tail-chains to the captured native vector. Callback execution, sprite/DMA
publication, and collision routine ownership stay in the explicit GELS/native
provider, with CyberGraphX unaffected.

### G24/G26/G27 scheduler-aware layer-lock overlay (2026-08-13)

The final three public overlay omissions are closed without weakening the
layer/native ownership boundary. The mapped jump-table handler checks the
typed `IGraphicsLayerGatewayBackend` before the portable register adapter, so
a live `LockLayerRom` can park the current task and return
`M68kHostGatewayResult.BlockCurrentTask` with its continuation frame intact.
`AttemptLockLayerRom` and `UnlockLayerRom` retain their classic D0/void ABI,
and direct host dispatch is compared with mapped dispatch for all three
vectors. If no Layers gateway or callback bundle claims the layer, the handler
restores the original program counter and leaves D0/cycles untouched for
Kickstart/native handling. This is a CopperStart/layers boundary only; no
CyberGraphX surface or clipping implementation is introduced.

### G05/G17/G26/G27 scheduler-aware Layers raster overlay (2026-08-13)

The native ROM overlay now consults `IGraphicsLayerGatewayBackend` for layered
RastPort vectors before entering the ordinary portable adapter. This keeps the
mapped jump-table path aligned with direct `InvokeGateway` dispatch: a Layers
provider receives the original register frame and can return its scheduler
continuation result, while a foreign or declined endpoint restores the
captured Kickstart target with D0 and cycles unchanged. The focused `Draw`
fixture covers both provider claim and transparent decline. Layer clipping,
damage, and backing-store effects remain exclusively in Layers; no
CyberGraphX behavior is introduced.
Batch-list implementation note (2026-08-13): the portable `VTAG_BATCH_ITEMS_ADD`
path appends a bounded, alignment-checked guest command list and replays the
enabled list transactionally at `MakeVPort` before host copper publication.
`VTAG_BATCH_ITEMS_SET` accepts a null list as the assembling/no-op clear form;
non-null lists and viewport/extended-node attachment pointers must be even and
structurally readable before publication.  Malformed existing or added chains
fail before the batch head is published.  The
mapped native overlay continues to decline pointer-bearing batch setters/`ADD`
for provider/CopperSharp68k ownership; in-place copper patching and native
palette publication remain provider/native gates, and CyberGraphX is separate.

Text metric origin closeout (2026-08-13): `TextExtent` and `TextFit` retain
the current pen origin in their horizontal envelope when positive kerning on
the first proportional glyph moves the strike to the right. The strike may
start at a positive X, but the movement-cell envelope remains anchored at
zero, keeping direct host metrics compatible with the future CopperSharp68k
guest implementation.

### G06 WritePixel minterm selection (2026-08-13)

`WritePixel` now enters the shared planar writer with an explicit one-cell
source decision rather than passing the raw `DrawMode` through as if it were a
pattern stream. The implicit source cell is selected for ordinary writes;
`INVERSVID` flips it, so inverse `JAM1` leaves the destination untouched and
inverse `JAM2` resolves `BPen`. `COMPLEMENT` toggles only when that resolved
cell remains selected, making `COMPLEMENT|INVERSVID` a successful no-op for
the public single-pixel vector. This matches the classic requirement that
`WritePixel` obey the RastPort minterms while keeping plane-mask, malformed
storage, and rollback behavior in the lower-level writer. The rule is shared
by the portable host and the future CopperSharp68k guest path; RTG/CyberGraphX
pixel ownership remains outside this OCS/ECS boundary.

### G02 `WeighTAMatch` name-field boundary (2026-08-13)

The matcher uses only `ta_YSize`, `ta_Style`, and `ta_Flags`, plus the optional
tag suffix required by a tagged request. It does not load or dereference either
`ta_Name` field, as required by the Kickstart autodoc. OpenFont and lifecycle
operations retain the full TextAttr decoder because they need the name for
font-list selection; keeping the two decoders separate lets a future native
68k matcher preserve the same field-access boundary. A faulted unused name
pointer therefore cannot turn a valid metric into a portable failure, and the
CyberGraphX/provider seam is unchanged.

### G15/G26/G27 `NextDisplayInfo` public-key boundary (2026-08-13)

The display iterator now follows the Kickstart contract by returning the
public 32-bit ModeID key rather than the internal `FindDisplayInfo` handle.
The default monitor's lores record is a real zero key and is therefore the
first result after `INVALID_ID`; the private `0xFFFFFFFE` compatibility
handle is accepted only as a defensive input from older host callers. This
keeps `NextDisplayInfo`/`FindDisplayInfo` composable for native 68k callers
without changing the handle mapping or claiming RTG/CyberGraphX records.

`GetDisplayInfoData` now encodes `QueryHeader.Length` in the documented
8-byte double-longword units for the local payload, excluding the 16-byte
header, for `DTAG_DISP`, `DTAG_DIMS`, `DTAG_MNTR`, and `DTAG_NAME`. This keeps
native chunk walking aligned with `graphics/displayinfo.h` while preserving
bounded partial-copy and provider-decline behavior.

### G15/G18 synthetic `ScreenToFront` idempotence (2026-08-13)

The compatibility Intuition bridge now recognizes an already-front synthetic
Screen without re-entering the scheduler-aware `LoadView` publication path.
The decision requires both the host current-View cache and, when the optional
guest graphics sidecar is mapped, agreement with `GfxBase->ActiView`. This
keeps repeated `ScreenToFront` calls from moving a stable display stream to a
new frame boundary while still allowing a native/CopperSharp68k or provider
handoff that replaced the guest active-view pointer to reclaim the Screen
explicitly. The state-aware and cycle-only activation seams share this rule;
caller registers and cycles remain untouched on the no-op. CyberGraphX remains
outside this compatibility ownership boundary.

### G15/G18 boot LoadView topology idempotence (2026-08-13)

The boot-side graphics gateway now stores a bounded FNV-1a fingerprint of the
guest View envelope and its linked ViewPort, RasInfo, and BitMap topology after
each successful display publication. A repeated `LoadView` for the same active
topology repairs only the mapped `GfxBase->ActiView` sidecar and avoids queuing
a second frame-boundary copper handoff. The fingerprint is deliberately
topological: plane links and public geometry invalidate it, while copper bytes
remain owned by the normal resolver and provider/native path. Sparse or
malformed envelopes disable the optimization rather than changing the existing
failure boundary. The synthetic `ScreenToFront` takeover path explicitly clears
the fingerprint when the guest active-view sidecar was replaced, preserving a
native/provider reclaim. Portable direct tests and mapped boot tests cover the
no-requeue and edited-ViewPort branches, with CyberGraphX outside this
standard-planar contract.

### G15/G18 boot `LoadView(NULL)` idempotence (2026-08-13)

The boot-side NULL handoff now consults the same published topology state as
the non-NULL path. If the compatibility stream is already blank and the
mapped `GfxBase->ActiView` field is still zero (or the optional sidecar is not
mapped), the request repairs the sidecar and returns without queueing another
frame-boundary copper load. A foreign nonzero guest sidecar bypasses that
shortcut, so a direct native/provider takeover can still be reclaimed by the
normal blanking path. This keeps the CopperSharp68k-compatible guest contract
aligned with the portable core while leaving CyberGraphX ownership unchanged.

### G15/G18 `CloseScreen` fingerprint teardown (2026-08-13)

Synthetic `CloseScreen` retires the compatibility View envelope and now also
invalidates the boot-side published topology fingerprint. The invalidation is
performed even when a foreign active View remains published, because the
fingerprint belongs to the retired synthetic session and must not make a later
open or native/provider handoff look like the old topology. The existing blanking
and field teardown remain unchanged; mapped close/open coverage asserts that the
fingerprint is cleared.

### G01/G04/G06/G07 NULL RastPort ownership (2026-08-13)

All portable RastPort byte, word, and long field helpers now reject a zero base
before range probing. This matters on host memory models that expose address
zero: a mapped NULL RastPort must remain a native 68000/provider address-error
boundary, not become a compatibility object merely because its bytes are
readable. The shared guard covers text, state, pixels, lines, fills, areas,
templates, and scrolling without changing the nonzero alignment or rollback
rules; direct and ROM-overlay regressions exercise `Draw` and `Text` with A1
equal to zero, alongside the same ownership result for `ReadPixel` and
`WritePixel`.

### G01/G06 setter probe ordering (2026-08-13)

`SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, and `SetDrMd` share a transactional setter that derives
minterms, restarts the line pattern, and publishes the Flags word. Its old
value and line-phase reads now use the even/nonnull RastPort field helpers
before any host memory probe. A host mapping at address zero or an odd guest
base therefore remains available to native 68000/provider ownership even when
the bytes happen to be readable; valid aligned setters retain their existing
rollback and derived-state behavior.

### G01/G06 PolyDraw point-table ownership (2026-08-13)

The non-empty `PolyDraw` path now admits its coordinate stream only when the
guest point-table base is non-null and word-aligned. Each pair is consumed by
native-compatible word reads, so a host byte mapping at address zero or an odd
address must not be reinterpreted as a portable point table. The rejection is
performed before the first coordinate read and therefore preserves the
caller’s D0/cycles, current pen, and planar bytes for native/provider fallback.
The classic low-UWORD zero-count form remains an explicit successful no-op and
does not require either guest endpoint.

### G01/G06 V36 temporary RastPort status ownership (2026-08-13)

The V36 line and rectangle pixel-array vectors accept an optional temporary
`RastPort` as a guest-owned native workspace. The portable bodies continue to
return the classic `-1` for malformed geometry or caller arrays, but their
status adapters now mirror the body’s ordering: they first require positive
geometry, the padded array envelope, and (for writes) a nonzero effective
destination mask. Only then is the temporary structure’s even base, Layer link,
BitMap link, plane span, and one-row workspace envelope validated. A malformed
workspace consequently leaves the host vector unclaimed so resident Kickstart,
CyberGraphX, or another provider can receive the original call. This keeps the
CopperSharp68k/native layout boundary explicit without making host-only null
temporary workspaces mandatory.

### G06 PolyDraw aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`PolyDraw` stages the complete low-UWORD point stream before it mutates the
RastPort. The staged chain is also bounded by the aggregate number of
Bresenham samples that its connected segments would traverse. If that sum
exceeds the portable `Int32.MaxValue` host-work contract, the vector declines
before destination-plane probing, line-pattern publication, or any pixel write.
This guard applies even when `ONE_DOT` suppresses repeated destination rows,
because the line walk still has to consume every major-axis step to preserve
native pattern phase. An effective zero mask retains the bounded cursor/phase
state-only path, and ordinary chains continue through the existing per-plane
transaction and provider visibility boundary. A future CopperSharp68k body can
use the same guest point layout and decline rule without importing host
storage or CyberGraphX policy.

### G08 Flood aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`Flood` is one Kickstart vector even though a portable implementation must
preflight the complete destination, retain a rollback snapshot, and walk the
connected region before it can commit. The core therefore computes the guest
logical-cell count immediately after the effective RastPort mask is known and
requires three bounded passes to fit within the shared `Int32.MaxValue`
portable host-work contract. The guard is intentionally before optional
`TmpRas` lookup, seed/pattern reads, plane probing, scratch allocation, and
snapshot creation, so an oversized but otherwise readable UWORD bitmap cannot
force a multi-billion-entry managed traversal or pending list. Zero-mask
Flood retains its successful state-only no-op; normal small standard-planar
fills, validated layer-provider calls, and any future CopperSharp68k guest body
retain their existing ownership and ABI seams. CyberGraphX/RTG paths remain
outside this rule.

### G19 BitMapScale aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BitMapScale` derives a destination rectangle from the public factor fields,
then samples/probes that rectangle, retains a rollback snapshot, and publishes
the scaled pixels. The portable body now requires three bounded logical passes
to fit within the shared `Int32.MaxValue` host-work contract before allocating
the DDA arrays or byte-per-pixel staging buffer. A near-maximum UWORD rectangle
therefore declines without changing `bsa_DestWidth`, `bsa_DestHeight`, or the
destination planes. Direct and CopperStart register calls retain the void/D0
boundary; the native overlay still admits only instance-owned bitmap endpoints
and tail-chains caller-owned or provider-owned surfaces. CyberGraphX/RTG
ownership remains outside this planar rule.

### G06/G19 Pixel-array aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

The V36 `ReadPixelLine8`, `WritePixelLine8`, `ReadPixelArray8`,
`WritePixelArray8`, and V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` paths now share an explicit
portable work envelope. The admission check accounts for logical pixels and
the complete padded source-array rows before staging, planar preflight,
rollback snapshot, or publication. A request whose array envelope itself
cannot fit the guest/portable contract remains a claimed classic `-1`
failure; a representable envelope whose aggregate conversion work exceeds the
`Int32.MaxValue` host budget declines so native Kickstart, Layers, or the
CyberGraphX patch can own it. This keeps host memory bounded without changing
the guest array layout or the separate RTG provider boundary.

### G08 AreaEnd aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`AreaEnd` decodes a bounded guest vector stream, then processes each polygon
or ellipse through a temporary mask, destination preflight/snapshot, and
fill publication. The portable path now sums the logical-cell envelopes of
the effective shapes and requires four bounded passes to fit the shared
`Int32.MaxValue` host-work contract before acquiring either managed or guest
scratch. Oversized representable shapes decline without resetting the
`AreaInfo` collector or reading destination planes; empty, zero-mask, inverse
JAM1, and malformed paths retain their established semantics. Layers and
CyberGraphX remain explicit provider boundaries.

### G10 BltBitMap aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BltBitMap` and `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` are transactional planar copies: the
portable paths stage source/destination (and, for the masked form, external
mask) pixels, retain a destination rollback snapshot, and then publish the
minterm result. Their signed-WORD rectangles are therefore bounded by
aggregate logical-cell work rather than by an individual `int` array length
check alone. The four-pass `BltBitMap` envelope and five-pass masked envelope
are checked immediately after clipping and before overlap/TempA or external
mask inspection, reusable scratch growth, plane-pointer reads, or destination
validation. An oversized but representable request consequently declines
without allocator or guest-raster side effects; ordinary copies and the
separate layer/CyberGraphX provider paths retain their existing ABI and
ownership boundaries. The guest `BitMap` layout remains unchanged and can be
consumed by a future CopperSharp68k body.

### G11 BltTemplate aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BltTemplate` decodes a guest bit template into a clipped selection buffer,
preflights the destination, retains a rollback snapshot, and then publishes
the selected RastPort pixels. The portable path now requires three bounded
logical passes for that sequence immediately after clipping and before any
template-byte read or `GraphicsBlitScratch` growth. A full signed-WORD
rectangle can therefore remain structurally valid yet decline without host
allocation, source probing, or guest-raster mutation. The zero-effective-mask
success path remains ahead of this guard, and the guest template alignment,
draw-mode, layer, CyberGraphX, and CopperSharp68k layout boundaries are
unchanged.

### G07 ScrollRaster aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` stage a logical source rectangle, probe
the clipped destination, snapshot rollback bytes, and publish the moved or
vacated pixels. The portable path now applies a four-pass aggregate-cell
guard immediately after the displacement no-op boundary and before reading
the source plane or the line-pattern phase. A structurally representable
near-maximum rectangle therefore remains available to the native/provider
owner without forcing a large host source walk; ordinary overlap, clipped
 source coordinates, BPen backfill, and the separate Layers/CyberGraphX seams
remain unchanged.

### G11 `BltClear` aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BltClear` is transactional even in its byte-oriented form: it probes the
complete destination span, retains a rollback snapshot, and then publishes
the fill. The portable admission check now treats those as three host passes
and rejects a guest-valid span that exceeds the shared `Int32.MaxValue`
work envelope before the first destination read or managed snapshot
allocation. The existing word-alignment, rows-mode, fill-word, rollback, and
native/provider handoff rules remain unchanged; CyberGraphX is still outside
this standard blitter boundary.

### G07/G11 `BltPattern` aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BltPattern` evaluates its stencil/area pattern, preflights destination
pixels, retains a selected-plane rollback snapshot, and then publishes the
patterned result. Its full-raster path now accounts for the three logical
passes plus snapshot bytes before reading an external stencil or destination
plane. A guest-valid request covering a large bitmap therefore remains
available to native/provider ownership instead of entering a multi-billion
pixel host walk; zero-mask and `INVERSVID|JAM1` no-op paths retain their
successful semantics, and CyberGraphX/layer clipping remain explicit seams.

### G07 ClearScreen aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`ClearScreen` is a single void vector even though the portable transaction is
split into the current text-line prefix and the remaining rows. The admission
check now sums both clipped logical spans, the four probe/publication passes,
and the selected-plane rollback bytes before reading the line-pattern field or
any plane pointer. A representable bitmap whose two halves would each fit in
isolation but whose complete clear would exceed the portable host-work
contract therefore remains available to native/provider ownership. Zero-mask
clears retain the classic successful line-state update, and standard planar
direct plus ROM-overlay paths preserve the existing all-or-nothing pixels and
provider boundaries.

## G04/G05 `Text` source-pen ownership boundary (2026-08-17)

The planar `Text` renderer now resolves `FgPen` and `BPen` at the first
visible template cell that selects each source. JAM1 all-zero glyphs,
zero-effective-mask cursor-only calls, and hidden/off-raster cells do not
consume unrelated public pen bytes. Inverse-video JAM2 background cells use
the lazily resolved foreground pen; underline uses the same foreground
boundary. COMPLEMENT remains pen-free. ColorTextFont mapping keeps its
existing eager foreground read because the pen participates in its
provider-specific source-color remap.

The destination preflight remains pen-independent and the existing `FailText`
transaction restores the raster and RastPort line state if a required pen
read fails after preflight. The direct and CopperStart regression
`Jam1TextWithAnAllZeroGlyphDoesNotRequireForegroundPenAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
proves the field boundary and void-vector ABI. The source operation is the
classic [`Text` autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Text), with
layer damage/clipping and CyberGraphX/RTG retained as provider boundaries.

## G11 multicolor source ownership across pattern consumers

The negative `AreaPtSz` form is a source-plane table, not a one-bit stencil.
For ordinary JAM2, `BltPattern`, `Flood`, and `AreaEnd` therefore write the
decoded plane value directly and must classify the signed pattern height before
claiming the public `FgPen` or `BPen` bytes. Positive one-bit patterns retain
their scalar foreground/background phases; NULL inverse-video JAM2 retains its
background phase; JAM1 uses the non-zero source as a foreground stencil; and
COMPLEMENT remains an inversion-only path. This ordering keeps malformed or
provider-owned pen fields outside a valid encoded-source operation without
changing the shared RastPort layout.

`FloodMulticolorJam2DepositsEncodedPlanesWithoutReadingPens` covers the pure
and CopperStart register paths, while
`AreaEndMulticolorJam2DepositsEncodedPlanesWithoutReadingPens` covers the
collector/fill boundary and its transactional planar result. Layer clipping,
damage, RTG/CyberGraphX ownership, and native timing remain explicit provider
or later profile goals.

### G04 Text selected-plane aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`Text` already validates the complete character stream and glyph strikes
before touching a destination. Its destination transaction also retains one
rollback byte per selected plane, so the admission check now multiplies the
background, underline, glyph-cell, and bold-smear work by the effective
selected-plane count before the destination preflight begins. A guest-valid
large multi-plane cell therefore remains available to native/provider
ownership instead of growing an unbounded rollback journal; zero-mask cursor
semantics, glyph decoding, and the separate Layers/CyberGraphX boundaries are
unchanged.

### G07 SetRast selected-plane aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`SetRast` initializes the complete planar bitmap transactionally: the
portable path probes the selected planes, retains rollback bytes, and then
publishes the requested pen. Its admission now accounts for the effective
selected-plane count across those passes, including the visibility-aware
provider path. A valid bitmap whose depth makes the complete transaction
exceed the host work envelope declines before plane-pointer reads; zero-mask,
single-plane span, and provider visibility semantics remain unchanged.

### G07 ClearEOL selected-plane aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`ClearEOL` retains an outer rollback snapshot and delegates the actual fill to
the same preflight/snapshot/publication path used by rectangle clears. Its
admission now bounds that combined work by the effective selected-plane count
before reading the line phase or destination planes. A guest-valid deep
bitmap therefore remains available to native/provider ownership instead of
growing nested rollback state; zero-mask and layer-provider semantics remain
unchanged.

### G07 EraseRect combined-transaction ownership (2026-08-13)

`EraseRect` retains an outer selected-plane rollback snapshot while it
temporarily routes through `RectFill`/`BltPattern`, which has its own
preflight, snapshot, and publication work. Its admission now accounts for the
combined depth-multiplied transaction before minterm state or destination
storage is read. A guest-valid large rectangle therefore remains available to
native/provider ownership; inverted/zero-mask and layer-provider semantics
remain unchanged.

### G06/G07 DrawEllipse bounding-transaction ownership (2026-08-13)

`DrawEllipse` preflights the complete midpoint outline before reading selected
planes, but its rollback snapshot covers the full clipped bounding rectangle.
Admission now accounts for that bounding snapshot plus per-plane outline probe
and publication work, including the denser visibility-aware path. A
guest-valid maximum ellipse therefore declines before a multi-billion-cell
host walk or plane read; zero-mask, non-layered outline bounds, and layer
provider ownership remain unchanged.

### G02/G04 InitRastPort default-font ownership (2026-08-13)

`InitRastPort` has two valid construction forms: a pure zero-font default,
or a compatibility/provider-selected `GfxBase->DefaultFont` with decoded
cached metrics. A nonzero callback result is therefore an ownership claim,
not a hint that may be silently discarded. The register adapter now keeps
that result unclaimed when the guest `TextFont` cannot be decoded, matching
the existing `SetFont(NULL)` boundary and preserving D0, cycles, and every
caller-owned RastPort byte for native Kickstart or another font provider.
Successful default-font initialization and late cached-metric write rollback
remain unchanged; CyberGraphX is not involved in this font-state boundary.

### G03 TextFit explicit vertical-constraint ownership (2026-08-13)

`TextFit` has a second no-fit admission boundary when the caller supplies an
explicit `TextExtent`: the box must contain the selected font's complete
vertical envelope before the string is examined. The portable path now
short-circuits that case after validating the font metrics and constraint
structure, publishes the empty extent, and avoids decoding any glyph bytes.
This preserves native/provider ownership for malformed character streams while
retaining the existing horizontal prefix and alternate-width/height rules.
CyberGraphX is outside this text-metric boundary.

### G03 FontExtent default-glyph boundary (2026-08-13)

The guest `TextFont` tables reserve one trailing character entry for bytes
outside `LoChar..HiChar`. `FontExtent` now consumes that entry when the font
backend can decode it, so an out-of-range fallback glyph contributes to the
maximum movement and horizontal envelope just as it does to `Text` and
`TextExtent`. Lightweight host font providers may omit the optional accessor;
their declared-range behavior remains unchanged while the memory-backed guest
provider exposes the classic table slot.
The memory-backed decoder reads that slot by table index, including a full
`0..255` declared range where no byte value can name an out-of-range character.

### G06/G07 RectFill no-pattern field ownership (2026-08-13)

The native no-area-pattern `RectFill` path selects its source from the implicit
all-one cell and consumes `AreaPtrn`, pens, and `DrawMode`; it does not need the
`AreaPtSz` byte. The portable `BltPattern` decoder now reads `AreaPtSz` only
when `AreaPtrn` is non-null. A no-pattern fill can therefore remain claimable
when that trailing RastPort byte is unavailable, while patterned fills still
require and validate the signed pattern-height field. Pure-core and
CopperStart register coverage exercise the same field-level ownership boundary.

### G08 AreaEnd no-pattern field ownership (2026-08-14)

`AreaEnd` now follows the same field-level ownership boundary as
`RectFill`/`BltPattern`: a NULL `AreaPtrn` uses the implicit all-one source
and does not consume `AreaPtSz`. Patterned area fills still require and
validate the signed pattern-height byte. Direct and CopperStart coverage
keep a malformed/provider-owned trailing byte from stealing a valid
no-pattern AreaEnd operation.

### G08 Flood no-pattern field ownership (2026-08-14)

`Flood` now follows the same field-level ownership boundary: a NULL
`AreaPtrn` uses the implicit all-one source and does not consume `AreaPtSz`.
Patterned seed-color floods still require and validate the signed
pattern-height byte. Direct and CopperStart coverage preserve connected-region
mutation and the void/status register ABI when that trailing byte is
provider-owned or unavailable.

### G14 FreeColorMap NULL-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`FreeColorMap(NULL)` is a successful void no-op. The portable core now claims
that form without entering the per-map lock or allocator, while non-null
foreign, stale, and malformed maps remain unclaimed for their native/provider
owner. The reversible native overlay applies the same exception only to the
NULL handle, preserving the foreign-map tail-chain boundary ([AROS
`FreeColorMap`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freecolormap.c)).

### G16 FreeCopList NULL-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`FreeCopList(NULL)` now follows the native empty-list teardown: it succeeds as
a void no-op without requiring a registry-owned intermediate block. Non-null
foreign and stale lists retain the strict registry check, so a provider or
native CopperSharp68k implementation can still reclaim ownership safely.

### G16 FreeCprList NULL-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`FreeCprList(NULL)` now follows the native empty-list teardown: it succeeds as
a void no-op without probing a public `cprlist` envelope or invoking the
optional resource backend. Non-null foreign, stale, and malformed lists retain
the strict validation/provider boundary ([AROS `FreeCprList`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freecprlist.c)).

### G09/G19 FreeBitMap NULL-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`FreeBitMap(NULL)` now follows the native empty teardown: it succeeds as a
void no-op before registry lookup or guest-header probing. Non-null foreign,
stale, and malformed standard bitmaps remain strict, and RTG/provider-owned
forms continue to tail-chain ([AROS `FreeBitMap`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freebitmap.c)).

### G22/G25 GfxFree metadata ownership (2026-08-14)

`GfxFree` now revalidates the guest extended-node `NT_GRAPHICS`,
`SS_GRAPHICS`, and recorded subtype before reading its association or
freeing the registry-owned allocation. A corrupted owned node therefore
remains available to the native/provider owner; direct, register, and
mapped overlay coverage preserves D0, cycles, and allocator state on decline
([AROS `GfxFree`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfree.c)).

### G02/G03 WeighTAMatch zero-size metric input (2026-08-14)

`WeighTAMatch` now scores a structurally readable `TextAttr` whose
`ta_YSize` is zero, matching the native matcher’s field-only metric. The
nonzero height requirement remains in `OpenFont`’s selected `TextFont`
envelope validation, so this change does not make an unusable font drawable.
Direct, register, and mapped overlay coverage preserve the exact score and
the odd-address native/provider handoff ([AROS `WeighTAMatch`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/weightamatch.c)).

### G02/G03 WeighTAMatch signed-penalty width (2026-08-14)

The portable matcher now stores the asymmetric size penalty in the same
signed `WORD` width used by Kickstart before comparing or subtracting it.
This preserves the native wrap for upward size deltas from 256 through 511
(for example, a 256-pixel delta returns the wrapped `-1` metric) instead of
silently converting the temporary to a host-width positive no-match. Pure,
register, and mapped overlay tests cover the wrapped result and cycle/D0 ABI
([AROS `WeighTAMatch`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/weightamatch.c)).

### G02/G03 OpenFont zero-size request (2026-08-14)

`OpenFont` now preserves a readable request with `ta_YSize == 0` through
resident-list matching instead of declining before `WeighTAMatch` scoring.
The selected `TextFont` remains subject to its nonzero strike, glyph-table,
and accessor checks. Direct/register and rebound-list mapped coverage prove
that a valid candidate opens and closes with the classic D0/cycle ABI, while
malformed requests remain available to native/provider ownership.

### G02/G04 CloseFont resident-list ownership (2026-08-14)

`CloseFont` now removes a non-ROM font from a rebound guest `GfxBase->TextFonts`
list when its final accessor closes, matching the native `CloseFont` → `RemFont`
lifecycle. The portable backend distinguishes resident-list ownership from
the private compatibility registry, preserves `TE0F_NOREMFONT`, fails closed on
malformed guest lists, and restores the accessor on failed removal. Direct,
register, and mapped native-overlay tests cover the transition.

### G15/G16/G17 FreeVPortCopLists NULL teardown (2026-08-14)

The native `FreeVPortCopLists` path first resolves the optional
`ViewPortExtra` through `GfxLookUp`; a NULL viewport therefore resolves to no
owner and is a successful void no-op. The portable raster operation and core
wrapper now preserve that boundary before guest-envelope probing, registry
lookup, or provider teardown. Non-NULL malformed, foreign, and stale
viewports remain strict and can tail-chain to the native/provider owner.
Direct, register, and mapped-overlay tests cover the NULL D0/cycle frame and
prove that no display callback or allocator work occurs
([AROS `FreeVPortCopLists`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c),
[AROS `GfxLookUp`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxlookup.c)).

### Display query sentinel ownership

The display database treats `INVALID_ID` as a universal no-record sentinel.
The portable boundary claims that sentinel for the three public query forms:
`FindDisplayInfo(INVALID_ID)` publishes NULL, `ModeNotAvailable(INVALID_ID)`
publishes `DI_AVAIL_NOMONITOR`, and
`GetDisplayInfoData(NULL, ..., INVALID_ID)` returns zero without reading or
writing the caller buffer. This distinction is intentionally narrow: any
other unknown mode remains unclaimed so a native monitor or CyberGraphX patch
can answer it.

### Palette teardown sentinel ownership

`ReleasePen` has one intentionally ownership-free argument: `pen == -1`
(`0xffffffff`). Kickstart treats it as a successful no-op, so the reversible
native overlay claims that form before looking at `ColorMap`, palette-extra
state, or provider identity. This permits callers to use unconditional cleanup
without turning a foreign or absent palette into a portable allocation. Every
other pen value still requires the active instance's ColorMap and palette-state
validation; CyberGraphX remains outside this boundary.

### `SetFont` cached-state transaction

`SetFont` publishes the selected guest `TextFont` and the cached RastPort
metrics as one update. The native soft-style contract is part of that update:
selecting a font clears the previous `AlgoStyle` effect, while `TxSpacing`
remains caller-owned and is not rewritten. The portable implementation
preflights the complete cache envelope, snapshots the old font/style/metrics,
publishes the new font with `AlgoStyle == 0`, and restores every snapshot field
if any guest write fails. This keeps the CopperSharp68k-compatible guest layout
and the CopperScreen host-register/ROM-overlay paths on the same ABI boundary
([SetFont autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0479.html)).

### G02/G04 `RPTAG_Font=0` default-font ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

`SetRPAttrsA` now treats a classic `RPTAG_Font` tag whose data is zero exactly
like `SetFont(NULL)`: the entry path resolves the selected
`GfxBase->DefaultFont`, then publishes the font pointer and cached RastPort
metrics through the same transactional `SetFont` body. The pure portable core
does not read a global default; its optional default argument keeps the
CopperSharp68k-compatible contract explicit. The register adapter resolves the
compatibility provider's default, while a native ROM overlay requires the
rebound guest `TextFonts` backend and reads its selected `GfxBase` default.
Pen-only tag lists therefore do not fabricate or probe a font, and a missing or
undecodable default leaves the call unclaimed for the native/provider owner.
Direct, register, and mapped-overlay tests prove the published pointer,
metrics, D0/cycle frame, and existing rollback behavior
([AROS `setfont.c`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setfont.c)).

### G02/G03 odd font-table pointer ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The guest `TextFont` decoder now requires an even font base and even
non-NULL `CharLoc`, `CharSpace`, and `CharKern` table pointers before exposing
metrics or glyphs. These tables are consumed with native WORD reads; allowing
the host byte adapter to interpret an odd pointer would create a value that a
68000 would reject with an address error. `CharData` remains byte-packed and
may start at either parity. Direct decoder/core tests, register `TextLength`
dispatch, and mapped ROM-overlay ownership tests cover all three table types,
preserve D0/cycles and guest output on decline, and leave malformed fonts to
Kickstart/provider ownership. The graphics scaffold is green at 1001/1001;
exact ROM fault frames, display timing, and CyberGraphX remain separate gates.

### G02/G04 odd TextFontExtension pointer ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

Font lifecycle now requires a non-NULL `TextFont.tf_Extension` pointer to be
even before reading its match word, flags, back pointer, or tagged attributes.
`RemFont`, `StripFont`, `ExtendFont`, and tagged resident matching therefore
decline a byte-readable odd extension envelope instead of synthesizing a
byte-shifted WORD/LONG result. The font remains listed, unremoved, and
retryable; direct and native-overlay register coverage preserves D0/cycles and
the guest pointer on decline. This keeps future CopperSharp68k extension
accesses on the same 68000 address-error boundary while foreign extension
ownership remains outside the portable allocator. The full graphics scaffold
is green at 1002/1002; exact ROM fault frames, display timing, and CyberGraphX
remain separate gates.

### G09/G26/G27 odd `FreeRaster` PLANEPTR closeout (2026-08-14)

`FreeRaster` now enforces the same native word-address boundary as
`AllocRaster`: a nonzero odd `PLANEPTR` is rejected before raster-size
reconstruction, ownership lookup, or the chip-memory allocator is touched.
This prevents a byte-addressable host mapping from releasing a neighboring
allocation while preserving the captured native/provider vector for any
non-standard pointer policy. Pure helper, direct register, and mapped ROM
overlay coverage verify unchanged D0/cycles and allocator counts for an odd
address; the standard even-address free path remains unchanged.

### G15/G26/G27 odd native `GfxBase` sidecar closeout (2026-08-14)

The optional native publication sidecar now requires an even discovered
`graphics.library` base before probing `GfxBase->ActiView` or the full native
`GfxBase` envelope. A byte-readable odd base is still an address-error
envelope for a 68000 LONG field, so `LoadView` declines without a display
handoff or sidecar mutation and a failed odd rebind leaves the existing
portable registry base unchanged. Direct core and native-overlay adapter
coverage preserve D0/cycles and the guest active-view pointer; aligned native
bases retain the existing publication and display-provider ordering.

### G15/G26/G27 odd native ROM-overlay base closeout (2026-08-14)

The reversible CopperStart ROM-overlay installer applies the same rule at its
outer boundary. An odd discovered `graphics.library` base is rejected before
mapped vector probing or host-gateway replacement, so a byte-addressable ROM
image cannot create a half-native overlay whose negative vectors and positive
`GfxBase` disagree about 68000 alignment.

### G15/G17 odd native AmigaBoot sidecar closeout (2026-08-14)

The CopperScreen/AmigaBoot lifecycle bridge now applies the same boundary when
it reconciles `ActiView` or publishes `ChipRevBits0`. Odd discovered native
library bases are never read or written through the host byte adapter; blanking
and `ScreenToFront` remain eligible for native/provider ownership, while an
aligned base retains the existing frame-boundary publication order.

### G15/G17 host View-chain alignment closeout (2026-08-14)

The AmigaBoot display bridge now rejects odd guest WORD/LONG addresses in its
shared lifecycle readers. A byte-readable odd `View` or an even `View` whose
linked `ViewPort` is odd therefore remains available to native/provider
ownership before `ActiView`, copper, or display state can be published. Byte
fields remain readable through their existing byte path; only native WORD/LONG
accesses receive the 68000 alignment guard. Focused boot coverage preserves
the caller D0/cycle frame and the prior active-view sidecar.

### G06 connected COMPLEMENT/JAM2 zero-pattern ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable `Draw` path now treats a connected shared endpoint as owned by the
preceding segment for every `COMPLEMENT` write, including a `JAM2` pattern-zero
sample sourced from `BPen`. The endpoint is toggled back after the normal
sample write, so line-pattern phase no longer changes the visible vertex when
the continued segment begins on a zero bit. Line preflight uses the same
`pattern-one || JAM2` write predicate as publication, preserving transactional
rollback and provider visibility boundaries. A focused planar regression covers
the phase transition; exact ROM line timing, layer damage, and CyberGraphX
remain separate gates.

### G07 zero-mask scroll line-state closeout (2026-08-14)

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` now distinguish pixel selection from the
native scroll state boundary. A real, nonzero displacement with an effective
zero write mask restarts `linpatcnt` at 15 without staging source pixels or
touching destination planes; a zero-displacement request remains a complete
no-op, and the normal full-displacement boundary remains unchanged. A failed
phase publication returns failure before any raster mutation. This preserves
the classic `SetABPenDrMd`/`EraseRect` phase contract while keeping the
portable host work bounded; layer damage and exact ROM timing remain open.
### G04 fixed-cell unsigned advance closeout (2026-08-14)

Decoded fixed-cell fonts now keep the native `tf_XSize` WORD contract through
the complete RastPort text path. When `tf_CharSpace` is absent, a nominal cell
advance may occupy the full `0..65535` range; `FPF_REVPATH` represents the same
cell as a negative movement down to `-65535`. Text rendering, destination
preflight, work-budget accounting, underline coverage, and metric accumulation
therefore share one range rule instead of rejecting valid cells above the
signed-WORD limit. The UWORD `te_Width` publication accepts the same wrapped
16-bit representation for reverse-path results below `-32768`. The public
current-X store remains clipped to the signed RastPort coordinate range, and
malformed provider glyphs remain rejected when an explicit `CharSpace` table
makes the advance a signed WORD.

### G17 all-hidden rethink closeout (2026-08-14)

The host `RethinkDisplay` bridge now has focused coverage for a validated
`ViewPort` chain whose every node carries `VP_HIDE`. The chain is consumed
for ownership validation, but no replacement CPR/DspIns stream is published;
the previously active copper list and `GfxBase->ActiView` remain unchanged so
a later visible viewport can rebuild from the same `View`.

The same bridge now publishes the V39+ `RethinkDisplay()` status split:
malformed viewport reconstruction or failed copper publication returns a
nonzero failure result, while a valid all-hidden chain remains a successful
no-op. This keeps the guest status ABI separate from the preserved display
stream and leaves pre-V39/native-provider ownership available at the vector
boundary.

### G19 layered pixel-array UWORD closeout (2026-08-14)

The typed layer-provider boundary now preserves the V36
`ReadPixelLine8`/`WritePixelLine8`/`ReadPixelArray8`/`WritePixelArray8`
UWORD coordinates and extents instead of narrowing them to signed `short`.
The register adapter masks each D-register to its low word before a layered
claim, and the Layers bridge writes those unsigned values back into the guest
frame unchanged. A high-coordinate forwarding regression proves that
`$FFFE` remains 65534 at the provider boundary; standard planar, RTG, and
CyberGraphX ownership rules are unchanged.

### G02/G15 Screen-font residency closeout (2026-08-14)

Compatibility screen creation uses one reset-scoped default `TextFont`. Its
screen-owned accessor is still opened and closed per screen, but closing the
last accessor must not remove that shared default from the resident font list.
The portable font backend now keeps the configured default resident even when
the synthetic header omits `FPF_ROMFONT`; ordinary non-default non-ROM fonts
still transition to `FPF_REMOVED` on their last close. This keeps the guest
`Screen.RastPort.Font`, `TextFont.tf_Accessors`, and subsequent screen opens
consistent without making CyberGraphX or native font providers depend on host
state.

### G04 ColorTextFont planar composition (2026-08-14)

The memory-backed portable renderer now admits a standard-planar
`ColorTextFont` rather than treating its first source plane as an ordinary
one-bit strike. The shared guest layout exposes the extension fields after
the `TextFont` prefix. The decoder validates each selected source plane's
bit-packed rows, maps source planes to destination planes using
`ctf_PlanePick`/`ctf_PlaneOnOff`, and remaps the designated `ctf_FgColor` to
the RastPort `APen`. Nonzero composed color indices are the source stencil;
JAM2 still fills the complete text-cell envelope with `BPen`, while the
existing text styles, cursor clamp, line-pattern publication, and rollback
journal remain common with ordinary text. The color-table pointer is retained
as guest ABI metadata; palette/RTG mapping is intentionally not synthesized
inside the OCS/ECS planar path. An `IGraphicsFontBackend` without the optional
color-font capability declines before glyph/destination work, preserving the
native/provider handoff and keeping CyberGraphX independent.

### G02/G03 tagged WeighTAMatch request-envelope closeout (2026-08-14)

`WeighTAMatch` now treats `FSF_TAGGED` on the requested `TextAttr` as an
independent guest-envelope promise. The request's `tta_Tags` pointer is read
and its complete bounded `TagItem` chain is validated even when A2 supplies a
zero target-tag pointer. A malformed `TAG_MORE` continuation therefore stays
available to native Kickstart/provider ownership instead of being interpreted
as an ordinary untagged metric call. A2==0 remains a valid target with no
known aspect ratio, and ordinary (non-tagged) requests retain the no-suffix
read rule. This keeps the public matcher boundary aligned with `OpenFont`'s
tagged request admission without synthesizing host font state.

### Validation snapshot (2026-08-14)

The normal emulator/test project-reference graph builds cleanly with zero
warnings/errors, and the portable graphics scaffold passes 1013/1013 tests.
This validates the staged portable contracts and their host seams; native
CopperSharp68k execution, exact Kickstart timing, layer damage, RTG, and
CyberGraphX remain separate goals.

### G15/G18 OpenScreen display-reconstruction atomicity (2026-08-14)

`OpenScreen` and `OpenScreenTagList` now publish a Screen pointer only after
the post-allocation `RethinkDisplay` callback reports success. A failed
reconstruction immediately re-enters the established `CloseScreen` ownership
boundary with the exact new Screen pointer, retiring the synthetic lifecycle
session before the host returns `NULL`. This keeps screen allocation,
viewport linkage, and active-view publication transactional while leaving
foreign/provider Screens untouched.

The optional `FinalizeScreenOpen(success)` context callback extends that
transaction over the `SA_ErrorCode` output. The synthetic builder retains a
request-scoped copy of the error destination after provisional construction;
the Intuition bridge commits zero only after `RethinkDisplay`, or writes the
staged failure code after rolling the new Screen back. Hosts without a synthetic
error destination leave the callback unbound, so CopperScreen/native paths keep
their existing provider boundary.

### G09 layers/bitmap null-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`SyncSBitMap` and `CopySBitMap` are status-bearing layer vectors, but their
private `Layer`/`SuperBitMap` layout is owned by layers.library or a native
provider. The portable core now rejects a null Layer handle before entering
the optional callback-backed host. A rejected register call leaves D0 and the
cycle counter untouched, allowing the resident/provider vector to receive the
malformed request; non-null handles retain the existing explicit provider
claim. No private layer structure is decoded or copied by this graphics
slice.

### G19 BitMapScale source-plane ownership (2026-08-14)

`BitMapScale` now requires every declared source `BitMap` plane link to be
non-null and readable before it claims the portable vector. A missing source
plane is not treated as the constant-zero plane form supported by
`BltBitMap`; it is a malformed standard-planar endpoint and remains available
to the native/provider owner. The rejection occurs before source sampling,
destination probing, extent publication, or destination writes, so direct and
register callers retain their prior geometry, raster bytes, D0, and cycle
state. Destination-plane admission remains unchanged.

### G12 WaitBlit queued-work boundary (2026-08-14)

The timed blitter boundary distinguishes an active hardware operation from a
node that has only been submitted to the asynchronous queues. `WaitBlit` now
returns at the caller's cycle when the FIFO contains queued `QBlit` or
`QBSBlit` work but no node is in flight; it still advances through the custom
chip's predicted completion when the blitter is busy and still declines while
a guest callback or cleanup continuation owns the node. This preserves the
classic synchronous/asynchronous split: `WaitBlit` protects memory from the
current hardware operation without accidentally executing or draining queued
callbacks ([WaitBlit autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html)).
The direct FIFO, timed register adapter, scheduler, and mapped native-overlay
fixtures all compare D0/cycles and retain one queued node after the wait.
The full portable graphics scaffold remains green at 1017/1017; this is
portable/native-overlay evidence, not a claim of exact custom-chip timing.

### G12 V39+ single-FIFO queue ordering (2026-08-14)

The timed queue now models the V39+ rewrite documented by `QBSBlit`: ordinary
and beam-synchronized nodes share one bounded submission FIFO. The scheduler
examines only the head, so a ready QBS request submitted after an ordinary
node cannot reorder it, and a QBS head whose beam has not arrived blocks later
ordinary work. This replaces the earlier pre-V39 two-queue priority model while
keeping the guest `bltnode` layout, signed beam word, capacity, callback
gateway, and explicit native/provider decline boundary unchanged
([QBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/QBlit), [QBSBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/QBSBlit)).
Focused FIFO, scheduler, and native-overlay fixtures cover both ordering
directions and retain the separate `WaitBlit` queued-work rule.

### G17 native ActiView readability boundary (2026-08-14)

`LoadView(NULL)` idempotence must not infer a native display state from an
unreadable optional GfxBase tail. The host bridge therefore keeps the compact
compatibility image's cache-based blank no-op, but requires an explicitly
discovered native base to expose a readable `ActiView` LONG before suppressing
the handoff. If that native field is absent, the request proceeds through the
normal blank/frame-boundary path so resident Kickstart or a provider can own
the unknown state. No native GfxBase bytes are synthesized or cleared by this
boundary.

### G15/G18 `LoadView(NULL)` DMA-preservation closeout (2026-08-14)

The synthetic blanking publication no longer writes the normal display-on
`DMACON` mask when the selected copper list is zero. Existing DMA enables
therefore survive the frame-boundary handoff: sprite DMA remains active, while
a provider/native owner that disabled bitplane DMA does not have it resurrected
by the host bridge. The focused PAL regression compares the pre- and
post-handoff DMA mask, including `DmaconSprite`, and the broader lifecycle gate
remains green. This is the host-side realization of the Kickstart
`LoadView(NULL)` contract; exact Agnus register timing and resident/native
ownership remain separate evidence gates
([LoadView autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/LoadView)).

### G14/G18 `OpenScreenTagList` palette rollback closeout (2026-08-14)

The standard-planar Intuition bridge decodes `SA_Colors` and `SA_Colors32`
before allocating the guest Screen, because the request must be validated
without exposing a half-built public chain. Those palette writes are now
transactional: the pre-request palette and `PaletteLoaded` bit are captured
once, retained through screen allocation and `RethinkDisplay`, and committed
only at the final successful OpenScreen boundary. The common rollback/reset
path restores the snapshot on allocation failure, rejected `VideoControl`, or
failed display reconstruction. This keeps a failed provider-facing request
from changing the reset-scoped compatibility state observed by a later screen
open while leaving successful palette selection intact. RTG/CyberGraphX palette
surfaces remain outside this standard-planar transaction.

The same transaction is regression-covered when `SA_Colors32` has already
staged a valid entry and `CompleteSyntheticScreenOpen` rejects a later
`SA_VideoControl` tag. Construction rollback clears the staged Screen and
restores the pre-request palette before the next open; the caller-owned
`SA_ErrorCode` remains untouched because the failed VideoControl request is
still available to its native/provider owner.

### G15/G18 display-database QueryHeader length closeout

`QueryHeader.Length` is local-data length measured in 8-byte
double-longwords; it excludes the 16-byte query header. The portable display
database now publishes `(chunkBytes - sizeof(QueryHeader)) / 8` for every
public `DTAG_*` record. Direct and mapped native-overlay fixtures compare the
corrected header and payload, while unknown tags and `DTAG_VEC` retain their
existing native/provider ownership boundary.

### G20 sprite-image display-DMA admission closeout

The portable `AllocSpriteDataA` path has two deliberately different storage
classes. The public `ExtSprite` envelope is allocated as `Public`, while the
converted OCS/ECS image stream is allocated as `Chip`. When the active guest
memory adapter implements `IGraphicsDisplayMemory`, the image allocation must
also satisfy `IsDisplayDmaRange(image, imageBytes)`. `imageBytes` is the full
hardware image span: the eight-byte POS/CTL prefix plus `4 * height *
wordWidth` bytes of row data. This keeps a host allocator that returns a
mapped but non-DMA chip address from advertising a sprite that the custom-chip
fetcher cannot consume. The check is optional for a memory-only
CopperSharp68k layout, where address-class knowledge is unavailable, and it
never applies to the public envelope or CyberGraphX/provider-owned software
sprites. A failed admission frees the image and envelope before any guest
publication; successful conversion retains the existing registry ownership
used by `FreeSpriteData`.

### G03/G04 `SetFont` state ownership closeout

`SetFont` selects the guest `TextFont`, refreshes `TxWidth`, `TxHeight`, and
`TxBaseline`, and clears the prior `RastPort.AlgoStyle` effect. `TxSpacing`
remains caller-owned and is not rewritten. The contiguous cache envelope is
preflighted, and a late write restores the original font, style, and metric
words atomically. Direct guest memory, the CopperStart register adapter, and
the reversible native overlay use the same field-level contract.

### G20 simple-sprite `ChangeSprite` DMA admission

The simple-sprite image pointer is a hardware-facing handoff. When the active
memory adapter implements `IGraphicsDisplayMemory`, the portable path queries
the full image span (`8 + 4 * height` bytes) before changing
`SimpleSprite.PosCtlData`; the POS/CTL prefix is part of the admitted range.
The check is optional for a memory-only CopperSharp68k layout, so a native
provider can still own address-class policy when no host classification is
available. A declined range performs no guest publication and no sprite
backend callback, while the register gateway preserves D0 and the cycle frame
for a native/provider implementation to claim.

### G20 extended-sprite `ChangeExtSpriteA` DMA admission

The standard hardware `ChangeExtSpriteA` form reads the new ExtSprite's
`PosCtlData`, height, and word width, then applies `IsDisplayDmaRange` to the
complete image span (`8 + 4 * height * wordWidth`) before copying any fields
into the old public envelope. This extends the simple-sprite handoff rule to
wide hardware sprites without affecting `GSTAG_SOFTSPRITE` or
`GSTAG_SCANDOUBLED`, which remain explicit provider forms. Native-overlay
decline keeps the register frame available for the provider.

### G07 ClearEOL/ClearScreen guest-font geometry

`ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` are text-aware vectors: their first cleared row
starts at `cp_y - TxBaseline`, but the row height comes from the selected
`TextFont.tf_YSize`, not from the cached `TxHeight` word. The portable helper
therefore reads the even guest `Font` pointer and its Y-size when that header is
available; a zero/unreadable synthetic header falls back to `TxHeight` so a
host-only font provider is not forced to materialize a guest `TextFont`.
`TxBaseline` remains the RastPort-owned baseline offset, and the existing
JAM2/BPen and provider-layer boundaries are unchanged. This layout-neutral
split keeps direct CopperSharp68k calls and mapped CopperStart calls aligned.

### G07 ClearEOL/ClearScreen combined-mode BPen selection

The clear helpers derive their temporary fill pen from the JAM2 bit, matching
the native `bgfill_pen()` contract: any mode with JAM2 set uses `BgPen`; modes
without it use pen zero. They then call the normal `RectFill` path while that
pen is selected, preserving `COMPLEMENT` and `INVERSVID` minterm behavior
instead of collapsing the clear into a raw color store. Direct guest-memory
and mapped host paths therefore share one transaction and line-state rollback
boundary, while layer/provider damage and resident timing remain with their
owners.

### G08 Flood mode-specific field ownership

`Flood` has two source-selection modes. Outline mode (`mode==0`) needs the
`RastPort.OutlinePen`; seed-color mode (`mode==1`) reads the seed pixel and
must not require that unrelated field. The portable path keeps the
`OutlinePen` read inside the outline branch so a valid seed-color request can
remain claimable when only the optional outline byte is unavailable. This is
an ABI/ownership rule, not a layer or CyberGraphX behavior change.

### G07 RectFill mode-specific BPen ownership

The no-pattern `RectFill` fast path has an all-one source. JAM1 writes only
the foreground pen, ordinary JAM2 still writes only that all-one source, and
COMPLEMENT|JAM2 inverts without consulting either pen. Only inverse-video
JAM2 selects BPen for the null pattern; a real non-complement JAM2 pattern
can also select BPen on source-zero cells. The portable `BltPattern` adapter
therefore probes `BgPen` only for those cases, leaving unrelated malformed
state available to native/provider ownership.

### G04 Text mode-specific BPen ownership

The planar text path follows the same field-level ownership rule as the
classic template operation. `BgPen` is consumed only when JAM2 is selected,
because only that mode paints source-zero glyph/background cells. JAM1,
COMPLEMENT, and JAM1|INVERSVID do not require the byte and must remain
claimable when it is unreadable. The direct and mapped gateways share this
predicate; color-font composition, layer damage, and resident timing stay
outside the portable boundary.

### G07 BltPattern COMPLEMENT|JAM2 source ownership

`BltPattern` treats `COMPLEMENT|JAM2` as a whole-region inversion of the
selected destination stencil. The area pattern is not a source operand for
that mode, so the portable adapter must not preflight `AreaPtSz` or read a
pattern word before committing the inversion. This keeps malformed or
provider-owned pattern storage behind the native/provider boundary while
leaving pattern decoding mandatory for non-complement modes. The contract is
anchored by the public [`BltPattern` autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/BltPattern)
and the direct/mapped regression named
`ComplementJam2DoesNotRequireAreaPatternStorageAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`.

### G08 AreaEnd mode-specific pen and pattern ownership

`AreaEnd` uses the same decoded area-fill operation as `RectFill` and
`BltPattern`, so its admission must use the same source ownership predicate.
For `COMPLEMENT|JAM2`, the selected polygon region is inverted without
consuming `BgPen`, `AreaPtSz`, or pattern words. Inverse-video JAM2 and
non-complement patterned JAM2 retain the BPen/source dependency. The direct
and mapped regression
`AreaEndComplementJam2DoesNotRequireBackgroundOrPatternStorageAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
keeps the area collector and void ABI on the same transaction boundary.

### G07 BltTemplate COMPLEMENT|JAM2 BPen ownership

`BltTemplate` stages the template source and then calls the planar pixel
writer for foreground and background cells. In `COMPLEMENT` mode that writer
toggles the destination bit and does not consume its colour argument, so the
combined `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` form must not preflight `RastPort.BgPen`. Ordinary
JAM2 templates retain the background-pen dependency for source-zero cells.
The direct and mapped regression
`BltTemplateComplementJam2DoesNotRequireBackgroundPenAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
keeps this field boundary aligned with the portable/native transaction.

### G04 Text COMPLEMENT|JAM2 BPen ownership

The planar `Text` renderer uses the complete font-cell envelope for JAM2 and
routes each cell through the same pixel writer as `BltTemplate`. In
`JAM2|COMPLEMENT`, the writer toggles the destination and ignores the colour
argument, so `BgPen` is not an operand and must remain outside the portable
admission read set. Non-complement JAM2 still paints source-zero cells from
`BgPen`; the direct/mapped regression
`TextComplementJam2DoesNotRequireBackgroundPenStorageAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
keeps both paths on that shared rule.

### G08 Flood COMPLEMENT|JAM2 BPen ownership

`Flood` shares the area-pattern decoder with `BltPattern` and `AreaEnd`, but
it also has a seed-region traversal and a caller-owned/allocator-backed
temporary raster. Its admission therefore reads `BgPen` only for a
non-complement JAM2 request with a real pattern, or for inverse-video JAM2
with the implicit all-one source. Null-pattern `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` skips both
`BgPen` and `AreaPtSz` while preserving connectivity, scratch ownership, and
the mapped void ABI.

### G06 Draw/PolyDraw COMPLEMENT|JAM2 BPen ownership

Line pattern zero samples normally select `BgPen` only in non-complement
JAM2. In the combined complement form, both pattern phases call the planar
inversion writer, so the background colour is not consumed. `Draw` and the
transactional `PolyDraw` preflight therefore share one predicate: ordinary
JAM2 and inverse-video JAM2 retain `BgPen`, while `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` keeps it
outside the guest admission envelope. The direct/mapped Draw regression
`DrawComplementJam2DoesNotRequireBackgroundPenAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
guards the shared rule.

### G06 Draw/PolyDraw COMPLEMENT foreground-pen ownership

The same source-field split applies to `FgPen`. `Draw`, `PolyDraw`,
`DrawEllipse`, and `WritePixel` read the foreground pen only when the selected
draw mode can consume colour; `COMPLEMENT` routes every selected destination
plane through the inversion writer and therefore ignores that argument. This
keeps a valid line/pixel operation available to native/provider ownership when
the caller's foreground byte is unreadable, while preserving the normal
foreground dependency for JAM1/JAM2 and inverse-video non-complement forms.

### G04 Text COMPLEMENT foreground-pen ownership

`Text` uses the same planar source contract as `BltTemplate`: in any
`COMPLEMENT` form, selected cells toggle the destination and the supplied
colour is ignored. The text admission path therefore reads `FgPen` only for
non-complement modes. A neutral colour is passed through the source decoder
for inversion-only calls so normal and ColorTextFont glyph-source validation
still occurs without making the caller's foreground byte part of the ownership
boundary. Direct and mapped text calls retain the cursor, extent, and void ABI
