transaction while leaving malformed/provider-owned `FgPen` storage available
to the native owner.

### G06/G07/G08/G11 COMPLEMENT foreground-pen ownership

The planar fill and template family shares the same admission predicate:
`BltPattern`, `AreaEnd`, `Flood`, and `BltTemplate` read `FgPen` only when a
non-complement source phase can consume the colour. `COMPLEMENT` is an
inversion-only destination operation, including source-zero cells, so its
foreground byte is not part of the portable ownership envelope. This keeps
area-pattern, temporary-raster, and template validation intact while allowing
native/provider ownership to claim a valid inversion whose pen storage is
unreadable.

### Validation supersession (2026-08-14)

The interim build-blocker notes in earlier ledger entries are superseded. The
repository's explicit DOS `freeMemory` callback is now supplied by the existing
console test fixture, and the mapped Text/Flood fixtures encode the real guest
ABI (decodable TextFont metadata; Flood mode in D2). The emulator and test
projects build with zero warnings/errors. The focused complement-ownership set
passes 7/7, and the complete `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests` class
passes 1033/1033.

### G19 V36 pixel-line requested-count closeout (2026-08-14)

The V36 `ReadPixelLine8` and `WritePixelLine8` paths now preserve the
Kickstart line-helper result contract: for a valid nonzero-width request they
return the requested `pixel_count`, even when the unsigned coordinate clips
the complete line or only part of it. The byte-array envelope is still fully
preflighted for normal masked work, reads publish deterministic zeroes for
out-of-raster samples, and writes retain transactional planar rollback. The
existing effective-zero-mask fast path remains a bounded successful no-op but
now returns the requested line width as the documented line result. Rectangle
`ReadPixelArray8`/`WritePixelArray8` and V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` retain their
clipped plotted/read counts. Direct, CopperStart register, and native-overlay
parity tests cover partial and fully clipped UWORD lines while preserving the
CPU cycle counter. This corrects the earlier clipped-count ledger entry for
line helpers without changing array-helper ownership or the CyberGraphX
provider boundary ([ReadPixelLine8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/ReadPixelLine8.html),
[WritePixelLine8 autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/WritePixelLine8.html)).

### G20 AddVSprite system-flag admission

The guest/native boundary treats VSprite status bits as system-owned state.
`AddVSprite` therefore snapshots the complete flag word, preserves only the
low user byte on successful list insertion, and restores the original word if
any reciprocal-link or flag publication fails. This keeps the standard
CopperSharp68k layout intact while making re-admission deterministic for
host-side GELS providers. The low/system split is defined by
[`graphics/gels.h`](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node00C3.html).

### G20 generic extended-node association

`GfxAssociate(pointer,node)` is modeled as an opaque pointer-to-extended-node
lookup independent of the concrete node payload. `ViewExtra` and
`ViewPortExtra` continue to mirror their documented backwards links in guest
memory. `SpecialMonitor` and `MonitorSpec` have no such public field, so the
portable registry stores their association only in its lookup map and removes
all aliases during reassociation or `GfxFree`. This keeps the guest layout
CopperSharp68k-compatible without fabricating private structure fields; a
native resident implementation may replace the registry with its own hash
table and Alert policy.

### G21 InitGels sentinel state

The portable `InitGels` path publishes the complete classic dummy-node state:
head and tail `OldY/OldX` and `Y/X` use signed minimum/maximum coordinates, and
the head's `ClearPath` points at the tail. The operation remains transactional
over the guest VSprite/GelsInfo envelopes, so CopperSharp68k memory and a host
adapter observe the same list and rollback state.

### G22 Bob/VSprite flag domains

Bob lifecycle code must not reuse equal-valued fields across the two adjacent
guest structures. `VSprite.Flags` owns `VSPRITE`, `SAVEBACK`, `OVERLAY`,
`MUSTDRAW`, and its background/draw status bits; `Bob.Flags` owns `SAVEBOB`,
`BOBISCOMP`, `BWAITING`, `BDRAWN`, `BOBSAWAY`, `BOBNIX`, and double-buffer
status. `AddBob` and `RemIBob` therefore publish each status in its own
envelope while preserving the CopperSharp68k 68k layout and allowing host
adapters to project the same state.

### G23 Compact collision-handler tables

The classic GELS API permits `GelsInfo.CollisionHandler` to reference a table
shorter than the sixteen-entry maximum. The portable `DoCollision` admission
contract therefore requires only entry zero to be readable up front (the
boundary callback and the smallest valid table); callback longwords for higher
`MeMask`/`HitMask` selections are read on demand and may be absent without
invalidating the list walk. This preserves the standard guest layout for
CopperSharp68k while avoiding an unnecessary host-side allocation requirement.

The GELS admission envelope additionally requires the head sentinel's
`PrevVSprite` field to be NULL. Traversed nodes must retain reciprocal links,
the tail must terminate with `NextVSprite == NULL`, and a stale head back-link
is rejected before any provider callback can observe the list.

### G08 Zero-capacity AreaInfo collectors

`InitArea` keeps the classic five-byte-per-vector address layout, but the
constructor does not dereference that caller-owned span. It validates the
even, fully addressable `AreaInfo` descriptor and checked 32-bit arithmetic,
then atomically publishes the vector/flag table and count fields for positive,
zero, odd, or currently unmapped buffers. The area consumers perform the
complete readable-span checks before writing records, preserving the
CopperSharp68k address boundary and the host transactional rollback path.

### G08 Zero-capacity temporary rasters

The temporary-raster constructor admits the analogous empty
`InitTmpRas(tmpRas, NULL, 0)` form. Kickstart/AROS only writes the descriptor's
`RasPtr` and `Size`; it does not touch backing bytes during initialization.
The portable path therefore publishes the descriptor after validating only its
own even/full envelope. Positive, zero, odd, or currently unmapped backing
pointers are not dereferenced by this vector; AreaEnd, Flood, and Text retain
their own operation-specific capacity/readability checks before consuming the
descriptor. This preserves the provider/native ownership boundary while
keeping the CopperSharp68k field layout ([AROS InitTmpRas](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/inittmpras.c)).

### G08 Empty AreaInfo closure

`InitArea(areaInfo, NULL, 0)` and `AreaEnd` form one guest-visible empty
collector contract. When `Count == MaxCount == 0`, all four AreaInfo storage
and cursor pointers may be NULL and `AreaEnd` returns success without reading a
bitmap, temporary raster, or vector byte. The portable reader admits only that
complete all-null zero-capacity tuple; any non-empty or partially-null tuple is
left for native/provider ownership. This preserves the CopperSharp68k layout
while keeping the host path from inventing backing storage for an empty
collector.

### G08 AreaInfo exact-end address envelope

The `InitArea` vector/flag buffer uses an exclusive end address. The portable
boundary therefore permits `buffer + 5 * maxVectors == 2^32`, which means the
last guest byte is exactly `$FFFFFFFF`; only a greater exclusive end is a
wrap. The actual flag-table pointer remains an inclusive 32-bit address, and
the existing even-buffer and readable-span checks still gate every positive
capacity collector. This keeps high-address guest objects representable for a
native CopperSharp68k implementation without manufacturing a host-side span.

### G08 InitArea descriptor-only ownership

The constructor is intentionally a descriptor boundary, not a storage probe.
After validating the `AreaInfo` envelope and the representable vector/flag
address arithmetic, it snapshots and atomically writes the four table/cursor
pointers plus `Count` and `MaxCount`. `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`,
and `AreaEnd` own the strict storage checks at consumption time. This mirrors
the resident field sequence ([AROS `InitArea`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initarea.c)) and keeps CopperSharp68k/native ownership possible for sparse buffers.

### G19 Zero-width pixel-line envelope

The line helpers treat `width == 0` as a claimed empty operation once the
RastPort has been shown to be non-layered. This is intentionally a narrower
exception than accepting a malformed non-empty raster: no bitmap, write-mask,
chunky array, or temporary RastPort cell can be consumed by an empty line, so
the core returns zero without reading those fields. The register adapter keeps
the UWORD width and cycle state untouched. Layered/RTG calls still route to
their provider boundary, and negative or positive widths still use the full
portable bitmap transaction. The guest layout remains suitable for a native
CopperSharp68k implementation.

### G05 SetMaxPen zero-request envelope

`SetMaxPen` has a field-free zero request: the Kickstart implementation
returns before dereferencing the `RastPort` when `maxpen == 0`. The portable
operation therefore claims that form without probing `RastPort->Mask`, while
nonzero requests retain the aligned guest-field check and publish the
contiguous mask derived from the requested pen range. This keeps the
CopperSharp68k guest layout unchanged and leaves malformed/provider-owned
state available for all requests that would actually consume it. The behavior
is grounded in the [AROS SetMaxPen source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setmaxpen.c).

### G05 SetMaxPen nonzero write-only envelope

For a nonzero maximum pen, the resident implementation computes the
contiguous mask entirely from the argument and stores the resulting byte. It
does not consume the previous `RastPort->Mask`. The portable operation follows
that boundary: `TryWriteRastPortByte` is the only guest-field access after the
zero-request branch. A writable mask whose read path is faulted therefore
still belongs to this operation, while an unwritable or misaligned field is
left for native/provider ownership. The guest layout remains unchanged and
the rule is grounded in the [AROS SetMaxPen source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setmaxpen.c).

### G15 FreeVPortCopLists link-only ownership envelope

`FreeVPortCopLists` owns four guest `ViewPort` links: `DspIns`, `SprIns`,
`ClrIns`, and `UCopIns`. Its portable transaction snapshots those four LONGs,
then clears them in order and restores the same four values if a later write
fails. It must not snapshot the entire `ViewPort`; unrelated display fields
are not consumed by the native teardown and may be sparse or provider-owned.
This keeps the CopperSharp68k guest layout and native/provider fallback
boundary aligned with the [AROS FreeVPortCopLists source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c).

### G01 SetOutlinePen exact-field ownership envelope

`SetOutlinePen` consumes the previous `AOlPen` byte and the `Flags` word. The
portable transaction therefore probes and snapshots those exact fields,
writes the requested byte and `AREAOUTLINE`, and restores only those fields on
a late write failure. It does not read the intervening `DrawMode`, `AreaPtSz`,
or `linpatcnt` bytes, preserving the CopperSharp68k/native-provider boundary
described by the [AROS SetOutlinePen source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setoutlinepen.c).

### G04 SetFont exact-cache ownership envelope

The SetFont transaction consumes the guest font pointer, `AlgoStyle`, and
`TxHeight`/`TxWidth`/`TxBaseline`; it preserves `TxSpacing` and does not read
the intervening `TextFlags` byte. Probe and rollback are therefore limited to
those exact fields. The soft-style reset remains part of the portable
compatibility behavior documented by the [SetFont autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/SetFont.html), while the
field access layout follows the [AROS SetFont source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setfont.c).

### G05 RastPort setter minterm-cache ownership envelope

The individual pen/mode setters and `SetABPenDrMd` consume the old scalar
pen/mode fields, the line-pattern phase, and the public `Flags` word. Their
eight minterm bytes are derived output, not input: native Kickstart regenerates
them from the scalar fields. The portable transaction therefore checks the
minterm address span and each write, but does not use a readable probe as an
ownership precondition. If a provider permits writes while faulting minterm
reads, the old cache used for rollback is rebuilt with the same deterministic
minterm function. This preserves the CopperSharp68k guest layout and leaves
read-faulting provider-owned caches claimable by the portable/native boundary.
The field contract is grounded in the [AROS SetAPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c),
[SetBPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setbpen.c),
[SetDrMd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setdrmd.c),
and [SetABPenDrMd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setabpendrmd.c)
implementations.

### G06 Move write-envelope ownership

`Move` publishes four guest fields: the two current-coordinate WORDs,
`linpatcnt = 15`, and `Flags |= FRST_DOT`. Only the old `Flags` word is an
operation input because the flag update is read/modify/write; the old cursor
and pattern-phase bytes are not consumed by the native routine. The portable
boundary therefore checks their address spans and writes them without a
readability precondition. It keeps a best-effort old-value journal for normal
rollback, but a provider-owned cursor or phase that faults reads remains
available to the portable/native owner. The guest layout and mapped A0/A1/D0
register seam remain unchanged. This follows the [AROS Move source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/move.c).

### G06 WritePixel `RPF_NO_PENS` envelope

The native WritePixel path branches on `RPF_NO_PENS` and consumes a private
graphics-context colour sidecar instead of `RastPort->FgPen`. The portable
planar implementation does not own that sidecar, so its preflight reads the
public `Flags` word and declines immediately when the bit is set. This keeps
the public pen and bitmap untouched and leaves CyberGraphX, Layers, or a
future CopperSharp68k body responsible for provider-owned colour state. The
branch is grounded in the [AROS WritePixel source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/writepixel.c).

### G06 Draw/PolyDraw `RPF_NO_PENS` envelope

`Draw` and `PolyDraw` are pen-dependent line operations even when their
current draw mode is `COMPLEMENT`: the native driver receives foreground and
background colours from the private GC, not necessarily from the public
RastPort pen bytes. The portable path therefore reads `Flags` and declines on
`RPF_NO_PENS` before its APen/BPen preflight. `PolyDraw` applies the same guard
before its connected-line pen checks and delegates only public-pen state to the
planar implementation. The source ownership is defined by the [AROS Draw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c),
[PolyDraw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c),
and [private GC macros](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G07 RectFill/BltPattern `RPF_NO_PENS` envelope

`RectFill` delegates to the portable BltPattern path, so one private-colour
guard covers both solid and patterned fills. When a readable `Flags` word has
`RPF_NO_PENS`, the portable path declines before APen/BPen reads or destination
plane writes. A failed `Flags` read is not itself a native BltPattern failure:
the resident routine does not consume that internal hint, and sparse guest
layouts must remain eligible for the ordinary public-pen path. Inverted bounds
still complete as the native empty no-op before the delegated fill. The source
contract follows [RectFill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/rectfill.c),
[BltPattern](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bltpattern.c),
and [gfxfuncsupport.h](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G03 Metric-query versus strike ownership

The resident metric vectors and the text renderer have different guest read
sets. `TextLength`/`TextExtent`/`TextFit`/`FontExtent` consume the TextFont
scalar fields and the metric tables needed for movement and bounds; they do
not require a nonzero `tf_YSize`, `tf_CharData`, or `tf_Modulo` strike
envelope merely to measure a fixed-cell font. `Text` and `SetFont` retain the
stricter strike admission because they can dereference glyph rows or publish a
renderable cache. The portable interface therefore exposes separate metric
query methods, with default provider fallbacks preserving the existing
strict contract. This matches the resident field use in
[AROS `TextLength`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textlength.c),
[AROS `TextExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c),
and [AROS `FontExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/fontextent.c).

### G11 BltTemplate private-colour ownership

The portable template writer checks the readable `RastPort.Flags` word before
public pen selection. `RPF_NO_PENS` means the resident/provider renderer owns
the foreground/background colours through its private graphics context; the
portable planar implementation therefore declines without decoding the
template or touching destination planes. A failed optional `Flags` read is
not itself a BltTemplate input failure, so sparse guest layouts continue with
the normal public-pen path. The source boundary follows [AROS BltTemplate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/blttemplate.c)
and [gfxfuncsupport.h](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G07 Clear/scroll minterm-cache ownership

The clear and scroll family treats `RastPort.Minterms[8]` as a derived cache,
not an operation input. The portable transaction first keeps a readable cache
as its exact rollback image; if a provider-backed guest faults those reads, it
recomputes the old image from the scalar foreground/background pens and draw
mode. The subsequent `SetAPen`/`RectFill` or `EraseRect` path can therefore
publish and restore the same guest-visible state without claiming a private
cache that the owner has intentionally made unreadable. This boundary covers
`ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `EraseRect`, `ScrollRaster`, and `ScrollRasterBF`,
and leaves layered damage and native private contexts with their providers.
The source field order follows [ScrollRaster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollraster.c),
[ScrollRasterBF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollrasterbf.c),
and [SetAPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c).

### G08 DrawEllipse `RPF_NO_PENS` envelope

The portable midpoint ellipse writer reads the internal `Flags` word only as
an optional provider hint. When the readable word carries `RPF_NO_PENS`, it
declines before APen or destination-plane work; when that optional word is
unavailable, it retains the native DrawEllipse field envelope and continues
with the public APen path. This keeps sparse guest fixtures valid while
leaving private-GC colour ownership to native/provider implementations. The
source basis is [AROS DrawEllipse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/drawellipse.c)
and [gfxfuncsupport.h](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G04 Text `RPF_NO_PENS` envelope

Resident Text selects a template, colour-font, or provider-backed renderer
from the selected TextFont. The portable renderer only owns public planar
`FgPen`/`BgPen` colours, so a readable `RastPort.Flags` word carrying
`RPF_NO_PENS` is an ownership handoff: decline before reading those public
bytes, decoding the glyph strike, or touching destination planes. Unlike the
optional flag checks on operations whose resident field envelope does not
consume `Flags`, Text already reads `Flags` for its transactional line-state
rollback, so the private-colour decision is exact and does not add a second
probe. This follows [AROS Text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c)
and [gfxfuncsupport.h](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G15/G16 MrgCop hidden-viewport envelope

The portable copper-merge boundary follows the resident `MrgCop` dispatch
order: it probes the View header and each linked ViewPort's public `Modes` and
`Next` fields, then skips all display/RasInfo validation for nodes marked
`VP_HIDE`. If no visible node remains, the vector claims `MCOP_NOP` without
calling a copper/display backend. Visible nodes still pass the strict
single-playfield or exactly-two-node `DUALPF` envelope before a provider can
publish a merged stream. The AmigaBoot compatibility projector applies the
same early hidden-node skip so malformed hidden payloads cannot steal a native
or provider call. Source: [AROS MrgCop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/mrgcop.c).

### G15/G17 LoadView hidden-viewport envelope

`LoadView` has three compatibility-side consumers: the publication validator,
the native ColorMap ownership admission, and the idempotence fingerprint. All
three now follow the resident display ownership order. The View header is read
first; each ViewPort then exposes `Modes` and `Next`. A `VP_HIDE` node is
hashed and advanced using only those fields, while visible nodes retain the
complete ViewPort/RasInfo/BitMap validation, instance-owned ColorMap check, and
topology hash. This keeps malformed or unmapped hidden payloads from blocking
the native/provider owner and prevents hidden private edits from forcing a
duplicate publication. The direct portable core, CopperStart mapped adapter,
and AmigaBoot signature cache implement the same rule. Source: [AROS display
traversal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/graphics_display.c).

`GetVPModeID` keeps its own field-access split from the display-construction
validators. A non-null, instance-owned `vp_ColorMap` is the authoritative
source for mode identity, so sparse or provider-backed `ViewPort` geometry and
`RasInfo` storage are not probed before the mode is returned. A null map still
uses the complete assembling-state validator before deriving the native mode
from `vp_Modes`; foreign maps remain outside the portable owner. This mirrors
the resident ColorMap-first access sequence while keeping CopperStart and a
future CopperSharp68k body on the same guest layout contract ([AROS
`GetVPModeID`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/getvpmodeid.c)).

### G08 InitTmpRas descriptor-only ownership

`InitTmpRas` is a descriptor publication vector, not a backing-storage probe.
The portable transaction snapshots the even, fully addressable `TmpRas`
envelope, then atomically writes `RasPtr` and `Size`; it does not dereference
the caller's buffer or impose a positive-capacity span limit. This mirrors the
resident `InitTmpRas` field writes and keeps sparse or temporarily unmapped
scratch storage available to native/provider ownership. AreaEnd, Flood, and
Text remain the consumers that validate capacity and readability for their
specific operation. Direct and mapped regressions cover positive, zero, and
unmapped backing pointers plus descriptor-write rollback.

### G15/G17 ViewPort default-layout ownership

`ViewPort.SpritePriorities` is a byte at the resident offset `$22`; its
`InitVPort` default `$24` is a layout constant, not a host-display policy.
Both the portable constructor and the synthetic Screen projector must source
that value from `GraphicsLayouts`. This keeps guest-memory initialization
identical across direct CopperScreen dispatch, mapped ROM overlay dispatch,
and a future native CopperSharp68k body. The lifecycle boundary still clears
the full `$28`-byte public envelope before publishing this one default byte.

### G18 native display-database sidecar initialization

`TryCreateNativeDatabase` treats the private native display-database block as
guest-visible state even though its format is CopperMod-owned. It first proves
the complete allocator span is readable, clears every byte, then writes the
header and ModeID table. Any failed write frees the unpublished allocation, so
`GfxBase.DisplayInfoDataBase` is never pointed at a partially initialized or
recycled image. Public ModeID queries and CyberGraphX ownership are unchanged.

### G15/G18 ColorMap default DisplayInfo handle ownership

The `ColorMap` `NormalDisplayInfo` and `CoerceDisplayInfo` fields carry a
DisplayInfo handle. Portable native records use their ModeID as that handle,
except for the real zero-monitor lores record, whose private nonzero handle
avoids the public NULL collision. `VideoControl` now validates that handle
class, and `GetVPModeID` resolves the default handle back to ModeID zero before
publishing the viewport mode. This keeps screen assembly compatible with the
guest ABI without claiming malformed or provider-owned handles.

### G15/G18 native display-database rebind ownership

`GraphicsLibraryCore.RebindGraphicsLibraryBase` treats its private display
database as part of the native-base binding. Before changing bases, it reads
the old GfxBase field and either clears/frees the owned sidecar, reclaims an
externally cleared owned block, or relinquishes ownership when a provider has
replaced the pointer. A failed read or clear aborts the rebind, so the
registries never move while their owned publication is still attached to the
old base. The public GfxBase pointer remains the only publication seam; no
private display-database record layout is exposed.

### G15/G17 CurrentMonitor publication

The shared `View` layout includes `Modes` at `0x10`; `EXTEND_VSTRUCT` selects
the associated `ViewExtra` path. The extended-node registry resolves only a
node allocated by this graphics-library instance and verifies its public
back-link before reading `ViewExtra.Monitor`. For a full native GfxBase,
`LoadView` prepares both `ActiView` and `CurrentMonitor`, probes writability,
commits them before the display handoff, and rolls both fields back if the
status-aware owner declines. The active-view signature hashes the selected
monitor pointer, so a same-address View with a changed monitor is republished.
No monitor object is decoded or freed by this path; provider-owned pointers
remain opaque. Layout reference: [graphics/view.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/view.h).

### G15/G17 ViewExtra TopLine publication

`ViewExtra.TopLine` is the word-sized companion to `ViewExtra.Monitor` in the
Kickstart extended-View layout. The portable owner resolves it only when the
View has `EXTEND_VSTRUCT` and the associated node is registry-owned with a
matching public backlink. On a full native GfxBase, `LoadView` probes and
journals `GfxBase.TopLine`, then commits it after `ActiView` and
`CurrentMonitor` are prepared. A failed write or a status-aware display
decline restores the complete sidecar set. The active-view signature hashes
the two-byte ViewExtra field, making vertical-start changes observable without
hashing foreign monitor objects. Compact host images, foreign ViewExtra
objects, and CyberGraphX/RTG providers remain unclaimed. Layout references:
[classic GfxBase](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node0612.html)
and [graphics/view.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/view.h).

### G15/G17 RethinkDisplay native ViewExtra sidecar refresh

The CopperStart Intuition rethink path is an alternate entry to the same
logical View activation as `LoadView`: resident Intuition rebuilds its
ViewLord copper chain and then calls `LoadView` ([AROS `RethinkDisplay`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/intuition/rethinkdisplay.c)).
The host projector keeps its existing copper scheduling and `ActiView`
publication, then invokes a sidecar-only portable-core seam. That seam uses
the same owned `ViewExtra` backlink, `EXTEND_VSTRUCT`, MonitorSpec alignment,
and transactional `CurrentMonitor`/`TopLine` writes as `LoadView`, but never
re-enters the display backend. Compact images, foreign/provider nodes, and
RTG views remain outside the optional native-tail claim.

### G15/G17 LoadView(NULL) native ViewExtra sidecar teardown

`LoadView(NULL)` is the inverse of the portable native ViewExtra publication
boundary. The core remembers the exact `GfxBase.CurrentMonitor` and `TopLine`
fields it last wrote, including their values and current native-base binding.
On a blank request it probes those fields and clears only matching values; if a
native/provider caller has replaced either value, that field is not touched.
The clear is part of the same `ActiView` transaction and is restored when a
status-aware display owner declines the blank handoff. Successful blanking
forgets the claims, and a native GfxBase rebind forgets claims tied to the old
base. This keeps teardown reversible for CopperSharp68k-compatible guest
layouts while leaving provider and CyberGraphX/RTG ownership intact.

### G15/G17 AmigaBoot LoadView native ViewExtra seam

The scheduler-owned AmigaBoot `LoadView` callback does not enter the portable
display backend, so it uses two sidecar-only GraphicsServices calls around its
existing copper publication. Non-null activation refreshes an associated,
instance-owned extended `ViewExtra`; the idempotent branch performs the same
refresh so monitor or TopLine edits are visible without re-queueing copper.
NULL activation clears matching fields and forgets their ownership without a
second display request. The host's compact `0xF0` image remains intentionally
unmapped at the native tail, while a full `0x220` native GfxBase receives the
same direct/core transaction. RTG/CyberGraphX and provider-owned fields stay
outside the claim.

### G15/G17 Native overlay envelope retry

ROM gateway installation and native resident initialization are separate
events. If the gateway table is installed while the positive GfxBase image is
still zero-filled, an idempotent install after Exec publishes its MonitorList
sentinels rebinds the portable registries to that same native base and retries
the display-database sidecar publication. This keeps later `GfxNew`, monitor,
and ViewExtra calls on the native 68k address envelope without widening the
compact CopperScreen image or taking ownership from RTG/CyberGraphX.

### G26 Native-base rebind refusal rollback

The native overlay installer treats `RebindGraphicsLibraryBase` as a guarded
transition rather than assuming its returned previous base implies success.
The register adapter exposes an explicit bound-base check; a refused transition
does not set `_reboundGraphicsBase`, and any font-list rebind performed before
the transition is restored. This keeps sidecar disposal and a later native
retry aligned with the actual portable registry owner.

### G15/G26 Existing native-node backlink migration

Native cutover can happen after host-side `GfxNew` or `OpenMonitor` has already
published guest objects. `GraphicsLibraryCore.RebindGraphicsLibraryBase` now
stages the shared `ExtendedNode.xln_Lib` field for every instance-owned
`ViewExtra`, `ViewPortExtra`, and resident `MonitorSpec`, then commits the
registry base only after all writes succeed. A late refusal restores every
previous backlink and leaves the old base authoritative. Monitor-list and
copper publication remain separate ownership seams; this unit changes only
the documented library-owner backlink, preserving native/provider and
CyberGraphX/RTG control of their own records.

### G15/G26 Resident MonitorList cutover

The native-base transition also handles resident monitor nodes that were
created before the transition. If the old list is readable and contains
exactly this registry's nodes, the nodes are detached from that list and
appended to an empty native `GfxBase.MonitorList`; an unmapped compact old
list is accepted only when every owned node still has null list links. A
non-empty or foreign native list is never rewritten. List headers, node
successor/predecessor fields, and `xln_Lib` backlinks are staged as one guest
transaction and restored on any refusal, so native/provider monitor-list
ownership remains explicit.

### G18 Resident MonitorSpec names

For an unnamed mode-ID open, the portable monitor registry allocates one
canonical public C string per native monitor family (`pal.monitor` or
`ntsc.monitor`) and publishes its address in `MonitorSpec.xln_Name`. The
string is instance-owned and remains resident with the monitor node; repeated
opens reuse the same address. Named opens retain the caller-provided pointer
for compatibility. Name allocation is deliberately post-commit and
best-effort: the monitor/list transaction may succeed with a null name when a
sparse provider-backed envelope refuses the optional field, and any newly
allocated name is freed on its own write failure. This is a documented
guest-layout aid for CopperSharp68k, not an attempt to expose the private
Kickstart display-record list.

### G04/G06 Zero-effective-mask admission

`Text` and `Draw` compute `EffectiveWriteMask` immediately after validating the
bitmap. When it is zero, the portable path skips public pen reads while still
decoding the text stream or walking the line to publish the documented cursor,
`FRST_DOT`, and line-pattern phase state. The destination preflight and pixel
writer remain untouched. This preserves a narrow field-level ownership seam:
the no-write operation is claimable even when a provider/native envelope does
not expose `FgPen`/`BgPen`, while any selected plane restores the ordinary
public-pen dependency.

### G06/G07 Zero-effective-mask BltPattern admission

`BltPattern` is the shared pure-planar body for `RectFill`. After validating
the RastPort layer boundary, bitmap header, and public mask, it computes
`EffectiveWriteMask`. A zero result returns success before consuming
`DrawMode`, `AreaPtrn`, stencil storage, or `FgPen`/`BgPen`; this keeps the
zero-write field ownership seam consistent with `Text`, `Draw`, and `SetRast`.
The readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker is still honored before this fast path, so
private-colour provider/native ownership is never claimed by the no-op.
The selected-plane path is unchanged and still owns its complete source,
pen, clipping, preflight, and rollback envelope. Layers, RTG, and CyberGraphX
continue to own provider clipping/damage and private backing stores.

### G06 PolyDraw zero-effective-mask pen ownership (2026-08-15)

`PolyDraw` is a connected `Draw` sequence, so its admission envelope must
match `Draw` when the declared bitmap depth collapses the write mask to zero.
The portable preflight now computes that effective mask before probing public
foreground/background pens. It still validates the RastPort, bitmap, point
stream, flags, pattern phase, and bounded line-state publication; it simply
does not claim unrelated pen bytes when no destination plane can be changed.
The readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker remains a provider/native boundary. Direct
and mapped gateway coverage proves the cursor/phase transition and preserves
D0/cycles and destination bytes.

### G06 WritePixel zero-effective-mask pen ownership (2026-08-15)

`WritePixel` uses the same field-level admission rule as the connected line
path. After validating the RastPort, bitmap, draw mode, and declared mask, the
portable body computes the effective mask before selecting `FgPen`; it also
skips the inverse-video/JAM2 `BPen` read when no declared plane can be written.
The operation still claims its bounded success result and leaves the raster
unchanged. `RPF_NO_PENS` is checked first and remains transparent to a private
colour provider. Direct and mapped gateways therefore expose the same
CopperSharp68k-compatible ownership boundary without taking over layer, RTG,
or CyberGraphX storage.

### G06/G08 zero-effective-mask pen admission for DrawEllipse and AreaEnd (2026-08-15)

The portable ellipse and area-fill paths now compute the effective destination
mask immediately after the validated bitmap/mask envelope. `DrawEllipse` skips
`FgPen` when no declared plane can be changed; `AreaEnd` skips both foreground
and mode-dependent background selection while still consuming and resetting a
valid recorded area stream. This keeps their bounded no-write contracts
consistent with Text, Draw, PolyDraw, and WritePixel. `RPF_NO_PENS`, layer
visibility, RTG, and CyberGraphX remain explicit provider/native boundaries.

### G11 Zero-effective-mask BltTemplate ownership

`BltTemplate` validates the standard RastPort/BitMap envelope, then checks a
readable `RPF_NO_PENS` flag before collapsing the destination mask. This keeps
private graphics-context colour ownership authoritative even for a no-write
request. If the marker is clear or unavailable, a zero effective mask returns
success without decoding the source template or reading public pens; a
nonzero mask follows the existing complete source/destination transaction.

### G03/G04 SetFont AlgoStyle ownership correction (2026-08-15)

`SetFont` publishes the selected guest `TextFont` pointer and the cached
`TxWidth`, `TxHeight`, and `TxBaseline` words, clears
`RastPort.AlgoStyle`, and preserves caller-owned `TxSpacing`. A later
metric write failure restores the complete prior font/style/cache state. The
reset rule is grounded in the public
[`SetFont` autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0479.html).

### G08 AreaEnd/Flood private-colour ownership envelope

`AreaEnd` and `Flood` share the public planar pen path, so a readable
`RastPort.Flags` word carrying `RPF_NO_PENS` is an explicit provider/native
decline before public colour fields are touched. `AreaEnd` leaves the recorded
`AreaInfo` stream available for the owner; `Flood` leaves its seed and scratch
state untouched. If the optional Flags word cannot be read, the portable
implementation retains its ordinary public-pen claim, matching the sparse
guest-layout rule used by the other drawing primitives. The CopperStart
register adapter preserves the caller frame on decline; layer damage, RTG,
and CyberGraphX remain outside this pure planar contract.

### G07/G08 Clear, erase, and scroll public-pen envelope

The clear, erase, and scroll family temporarily routes the RastPort through
public colour state (`BPen` and, for rollback, `FgPen`). A readable
`RPF_NO_PENS` flag therefore declines the complete operation before that
state is consumed. The helper is deliberately opportunistic: an unreadable
optional `Flags` word does not invent a new failure, while a readable private
marker transfers ownership to the native/provider path. Reversed or
out-of-surface empty geometry keeps its existing no-op boundary; layers, RTG,
and CyberGraphX remain explicit providers.

### G15/G18 OpenWindow reconstruction transaction

The Intuition host bridge keeps `OpenWindow` atomic through display
reconstruction. A successful guest window claim is returned only after
`RethinkDisplay` accepts the containing screen; a failed rethink closes the
new claim and returns NULL. This prevents a failed, invisible window from
holding the public `Screen.FirstWindow` ownership chain while preserving any
pre-existing screen or provider-owned display state.

### G15/G18 OpenWindow screen-admission transaction

`OpenWindow` must not commit a guest Window unless the associated Screen
handoff also produced a non-NULL guest Screen. The host bridge therefore
closes the just-created Window and returns NULL before calling `RethinkDisplay`
when `EnsureScreen` declines. This preserves the CopperSharp68k-visible
ownership boundary without claiming foreign display providers.

### G15/G18 OpenScreen NULL-handoff admission

The two screen-open vectors call their completion hook for request-scoped
error/palette handling, but they commit only a non-NULL Screen. If the hook is
permissive for a NULL result, the bridge returns NULL without finalization or
`RethinkDisplay`; the concrete synthetic owner still performs its own rollback
inside `CompleteScreenOpen`. This keeps host and future CopperSharp68k paths
from publishing an empty Screen lifecycle session.
## G15/G18 OpenWindow post-rethink admission

`OpenWindow` now performs a second Screen admission check after a successful
`RethinkDisplay` and requires the same Screen identity.  A provider or display
owner may replace/retire the active Screen while rebuilding the View; the
compatibility bridge therefore closes the newly claimed Window and returns
NULL when the post-rethink handoff is empty or changed.  The check is
intentionally outside graphics raster ownership and keeps the
CopperSharp68k/host lifecycle transaction equivalent.
## G15/G18 OpenScreen post-rethink identity admission

Both screen-open vectors now revalidate the exact Screen identity after a
successful `RethinkDisplay`.  A replaced or retired staged Screen is rolled
back through `CloseScreen`, and `FinalizeScreenOpen(false)` is published only
when that rollback accepts the owned object.  This keeps the CopperStart and
future CopperSharp68k paths transactional without claiming provider-owned
views.

### G15/G26 native display-database clear ownership

The private native display-database sidecar has three ownership outcomes at
release: an unchanged APTR is cleared and freed, an already-zero APTR is
unreachable and its instance-owned allocation is still freed, and a different
nonzero APTR is a provider/native replacement that is left untouched while
the bridge relinquishes its claim.  An unreadable field keeps the claim for a
later retry.  This prevents reset leaks without making the bridge a native
database owner.

### G15/G18 NewWindow target/type admission

`OpenWindow` decodes the standard `NewWindow` `nw_Screen` and `nw_Type`
fields through the guest layout shared by CopperStart and a future
CopperSharp68k ROM. The compatibility path accepts a null target and the
private custom screen encodings, but declines public/workbench types and
explicit foreign Screen pointers before `EnsureSyntheticWindow` can publish
a claim. The decoded target is retained only for the current call and is
checked again at the final publication boundary, so a provider replacement
cannot turn a foreign request into a synthetic window. Provider/native and
CyberGraphX window ownership remains outside this portable bridge.

### G15/G18 NewWindow alignment admission

The guest `NewWindow` envelope contains WORD/LONG fields, so the portable
CopperStart admission checks an even base before span, type, or target
decoding. This mirrors 68000 address-error ownership and keeps
byte-addressable host memory from swallowing a native/provider request.

### G15/G18 ScreenToFront alignment admission

The Intuition bridge checks the `Screen *` base before invoking either the
state-aware activation seam, the cycle-only display callback, or the legacy
`Screen + offsetof(Screen, ViewPort)` selector. An odd byte-readable pointer
is not a valid 68000 structure envelope, so the bridge leaves D0, cycles, and
provider dispatch untouched.

### G15/G18 OpenScreen structure alignment admission

The generic Intuition bridge applies the 68000 word-alignment rule at the
entry boundary: `OpenScreen` checks its optional `NewScreen *`, and
`OpenScreenTagList` checks both the optional legacy structure and the TagItem
chain. This keeps a byte-readable odd envelope from reaching screen staging or
display publication, without changing the null-default compatibility path.

### G15/G18 OpenWindow structure alignment admission

`OpenWindow` applies the same word-addressed guest rule as screen-open
vectors. The optional `NewWindow *` pointer is checked before
`ConfigureWindow`, so no host callback can reinterpret byte-addressable odd
storage as a valid 68k envelope. Null continues to select the compatibility
defaults.

### G15/G18 CloseScreen structure alignment admission

`CloseScreen` checks the live `Screen *` in the caller frame before invoking
the stateful teardown callback. An odd nonzero base is left for native/provider
address-error ownership, with D0 and cycles preserved; the null compatibility
form continues through the existing callback boundary.

### G15/G18 CloseWindow structure alignment admission

`CloseWindow` performs the same even-base admission for `Window *` before
calling the portable teardown seam. A mapped odd pointer is not reinterpreted
as a guest `Window` envelope, and the null no-op remains compatible with the
existing provider/native handoff.

### G15/G18 Intuition query/title structure alignment admission

The remaining screen/view-facing Intuition vectors apply alignment only to
structure pointers: `ShowTitle` checks `Screen *`, `SetWindowTitles` checks
`Window *`, `GetScreenData` checks its optional `Screen *`, and `QueryOverscan`
checks `Rectangle *`. Their byte-oriented title and copy buffers are not
artificially aligned, and declined odd structures preserve the caller frame
for native/provider ownership.

### G15/G18 ModifyIDCMP/AddGList structure alignment admission

The input and gadget-list vectors use the manifest's A-register structure
contract: `ModifyIDCMP` checks `Window *`, while `AddGList` checks `Window *`,
`Gadget *`, and `Requester *` in A0-A2. The adapter rejects odd nonzero bases
before callbacks and preserves D0/cycles for the native/provider path.

### G15/G18 ViewPortAddress structure alignment admission

`ViewPortAddress` consumes a `Screen *` in A0. The adapter checks that base
before reading the current viewport seam, preserving the null lookup and
leaving an odd envelope unclaimed for native/provider handling.

### G24 layer-ROM structure alignment admission

`LockLayerRom`, `AttemptLockLayerRom`, and `UnlockLayerRom` consume a `Layer *`
in A5; `SyncSBitMap` and `CopySBitMap` consume one in A0. The portable/core
boundary requires an even base before invoking the compatibility layer
registry or callback. The classic null lock form remains a successful
compatibility no-op; odd envelopes remain available to the Layers/native
owner, and the direct register frame is preserved on decline.

### G14/G15 palette ViewPort alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The viewport palette lock boundary now checks the `ViewPort *` base before
reading `vp_ColorMap`. A nonzero odd base cannot discover an instance-owned
`ColorMap`, acquire its host semaphore, call the palette backend, or publish
RGB words through the byte-addressable compatibility memory adapter. The
native-overlay ownership probe uses the same even-base rule, while `NULL`
continues through the established no-map compatibility callback path.

### G14 palette semaphore impossible-state admission (2026-08-15)

`PaletteExtra` exposes an Exec `SignalSemaphore`; its owner and nest fields
are therefore an admission boundary, not host-only bookkeeping. The portable
lock helper now rejects the impossible combination `ss_Owner != NULL` with
`ss_NestCount == 0` instead of incrementing the count as if it were a valid
re-entry. This preserves the guest envelope for a resident/provider repair or
teardown path. Direct and mapped register coverage proves that the RGB table,
register frame, and cycle count remain unchanged on the decline; valid foreign
contention and same-task nesting retain their existing behavior.

### G14 `PaletteExtra` semaphore-prefix corruption admission (2026-08-15)

`TryValidatePaletteExtra` now treats the embedded `SignalSemaphore` prefix as
part of the guest ownership contract. Pen-sharing operations require
`ln_Type == NT_SIGNALSEM` and the local Exec invariant that owner and nest are
both zero or both nonzero; queue links remain scheduler-owned and are not
interpreted by the portable host. A corrupted node type or owner/nest pair is
declined before list traversal or pen allocation. Direct and mapped
`ObtainPen` coverage proves the ColorMap, sidecar, D0, and cycles remain
unchanged for native/provider recovery.

### G14 ObtainBestPenA tag-item wrap admission (2026-08-15)

The `OBP_Precision`/`OBP_FailIfBad` parser consumes an Exec `TagItem` as two
guest LONGs. Its admission now checks the complete eight-byte envelope before
either field is read. A tag pointer at `$FFFF_FFFE` is therefore declined even
when a host mapping exposes wrapped bytes at address zero; no palette lock,
pen-list traversal, or allocation occurs. The check is shared by direct and
future CopperSharp68k register paths and keeps the native/provider owner of
the malformed request intact.

### G15/G17 BestModeIDA guest-boundary tag admission (2026-08-15)

The portable display-database tag walker applies the same complete-envelope
rule to `BestModeIDA`: `$FFFF_FFF8` is the last aligned address for an intact
eight-byte `TagItem`, while `$FFFF_FFFE` is malformed even if a permissive host
map wraps the second LONG through address zero. A valid terminal item is scored
through the shared mode database in both direct and CopperStart overlay paths;
the malformed form declines before any mode result or register state is
published, leaving the resident/native or provider vector available.

### G15/G18 default-zero viewport ModeID ownership (2026-08-15)

The viewport mode override needs a presence bit in the portable ColorMap
sidecar. The guest-facing `ColorMap` word is zero both after
`VTAG_VPMODEID_CLR` and after `VTAG_VPMODEID_SET(DEFAULT_MONITOR_ID)`, but only
the latter must make `GetVPModeID` return zero and rewrite a GET tag as
`VTAG_VPMODEID_SET(0)`. Keep the sidecar bit transactional with the guest tag
list, validate zero against the reserved default-monitor record, and leave
invalid/foreign modes to the native or provider boundary. The same rule must
be used by direct and CopperStart overlay entry points.

### G15/G18 OpenScreenTagList guest-boundary TagItem admission (2026-08-15)

`OpenScreenTagList` walks Exec `TagItem` records as two guest LONGs. Its
preflight must therefore accept a head at `$FFFF_FFF8` (bytes
`$FFFF_FFF8..$FFFF_FFFF`) and reject only starts above that inclusive limit.
The valid terminal item may complete a list at the address-space end; a
crossing cursor must decline before any tag override, error-code write, or
screen publication, leaving native/provider ownership intact.

### G15/G17 BestModeIDA continuation-wrap admission (2026-08-15)

`BestModeIDA` and the shared display-database decoder consume eight-byte Exec
`TagItem`s. After reading one item, compute the next cursor before handling
`TAG_SKIP`; reject a wrapped implicit cursor for ordinary, ignored, or skipped
items. `TAG_END` remains a valid terminal item at `$FFFF_FFF8`, and
`TAG_MORE` remains an explicit continuation. The direct core and mapped
CopperStart overlay must make the same ownership decision.

After a complete item is read, compute the next cursor before applying
`TAG_SKIP`. A wrapped next cursor is invalid for ordinary/ignored/skipped
items; only `TAG_END` may terminate at the final envelope and `TAG_MORE` may
replace the cursor with its explicit continuation pointer. This prevents a
permissive host map from converting a malformed high-address list into a
valid low-memory continuation.

### G01/G05 RastPort attribute TagItem boundary admission

`SetRPAttrsA` and `GetRPAttrsA` share an Exec `TagItem` collector. The
collector admits the final aligned eight-byte envelope at `$FFFF_FFF8` and
rejects only starts above `$FFFF_FFF7`. It computes the implicit next cursor
before applying ordinary, ignored, or skipped items, so a cursor wrap is
rejected before a setter mutates the RastPort or a getter journals a result.
`TAG_END` may terminate at the address-space end and `TAG_MORE` may explicitly
redirect to another aligned list. This keeps direct and CopperStart register
ownership identical for future CopperSharp68k dispatch.

### G02/G03 tagged-font TagItem boundary admission

The shared guest font paths contain two bounded walkers: `WeighTAMatch` reads
the optional `TA_DeviceDPI` suffix, while `ExtendFont` clones the caller's
extension tags. Both walkers treat bytes `$FFFF_FFF8..$FFFF_FFFF` as one
complete TagItem envelope. They compute `cursor + 8` before ordinary,
ignored, or skipped records are applied, reject an implicit wrap, and permit
only an explicit aligned `TAG_MORE` continuation at that boundary. This keeps
malformed DPI input from changing a score and malformed extension input from
publishing a partial owned extension.

### G20 extended-sprite TagItem boundary admission (2026-08-15)

`AllocSpriteDataA` uses the same guest-envelope rule as the other graphics
TagItem decoders. A complete aligned item at `$FFFF_FFF8` is readable, but an
ordinary, ignored, or skipped item whose implicit `cursor + 8` wraps is
rejected before sprite options are interpreted or allocator ownership is
published. Explicit `TAG_MORE` remains an explicit continuation. The direct
and CopperStart register paths therefore keep malformed high-address lists on
the native/provider boundary without claiming CyberGraphX.

### G14/G15 VideoControl TagItem boundary admission (2026-08-15)

The VideoControl collector now applies the complete eight-byte guest envelope
rule before reading or staging a tag. `$FFFF_FFF8` is a valid terminal start;
ordinary, ignored, and skipped records whose implicit `cursor + 8` wraps are
rejected before palette/view state or batch links are changed. Explicit
`TAG_MORE` and `VTAG_NEXTBUF_CM` redirects retain their existing semantics.
The register adapter reports the portable decline while preserving the frame
and leaves malformed lists available to the native/provider path.

### G18 GetDisplayInfoData guest-end output admission (2026-08-15)

Display-info chunks are byte-addressed, so the portable writer accepts an
output span whose inclusive final byte is `$FFFF_FFFF`, even when the buffer
base is odd. It rejects a span whose final byte would wrap before reading the
original buffer or publishing any chunk bytes. Direct calls retain the normal
byte-count result; the CopperStart adapter declines the crossing form without
rewriting D0, auxiliary registers, cycles, or the caller's sentinel bytes.

### G18 unavailable ECS display-record monitor discovery (2026-08-15)

Chipset availability is a property of the display record, not of whether its
monitor timing can be described. On an OCS host, an ECS SuperHires `DTAG_DISP`
query therefore remains a claimed native record and publishes
`DI_AVAIL_NO_CHIPS`; the adjacent `DTAG_MNTR` query still lazily resolves the
resident PAL/NTSC `MonitorSpec` with its physical timing fields and zero open
count. This preserves the monitor-list/native-provider handoff without
pretending that the portable display owner can execute the ECS scanout.

### G12 queued bltnode linkage publication (2026-08-15)

`QBlit` and `QBSBlit` keep the public packed 68k `bltnode` layout while
separating queue ownership from provider execution. The optional
`IGraphicsQueuedBlitterLinkBackend` sidecar is selected before the legacy
address-only and timed queue interfaces. Its portable FIFO transaction first
reads the new node's original `n`, terminates it with zero, and then links the
previous pending tail to the new node. A failed tail probe/write restores the
new node's original bytes and never enqueues the operation; capacity and
duplicate-address checks happen before any guest mutation. Dequeue preserves
the published successor link for the callback boundary and advances the host
tail only when no pending node remains.

CopperStart forwards the same sidecar to its scheduler-owned FIFO, so a
future CopperSharp68k body can observe the normal system-linked node chain.
Adapters without the sidecar—including provider and CyberGraphX paths—retain
their existing address-only submission and do not receive portable guest-link
writes.

### G12 profile-aware QBS frame catch-up

`CopperStartGraphicsBlitterScheduler` applies the beam predicate before the
portable FIFO dequeue so it can retain each node's submission frame. The
`bn_beamsync` word is interpreted as the 9-bit vertical value used by the
classic `VBeamPos` contract, not as a host display timestamp. For a target that
exists in the active profile, the scheduler returns the corresponding
`GetLineStartCycle` candidate. For a target beyond the profile's raster-line
count, it returns the next frame start after submission and then permits the
queued callback to catch up. The FIFO receives an affirmative post-check only
after this scheduler-owned decision; a null provider predicate therefore
cannot accidentally release a QBS node. Exact Kickstart interrupt fairness and
provider/native queue arbitration remain separate gates ([QBSBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/QBSBlit), [VBeamPos autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/VBeamPos)).

### G05/G26 unknown zero-data RastPort tags

The portable `GetRPAttrsA` parser now treats an unknown/private tag with a
zero data word as an ignored forward-compatible item. The null-output guard is
limited to recognized output tags, preserving the `RPTAG_MaxPen` no-op while
leaving native/provider ownership available for extensions. A focused direct
boundary test covers both the ignored unknown tag and the rejected null
`RPTAG_APen` destination.

### G09 `FreeBitMap` header alignment

The teardown reader treats the registered public `BitMap` as an untrusted
68000 structure envelope. It now requires a nonzero even header before any
WORD/LONG field probe, plane-span validation, or allocator release. This is a
separate guard from plane alignment and `BMF_DISPLAYABLE`: odd chip-plane
bases may remain ordinary non-displayable storage, while an odd structure
base is always left for native/provider address-error handling. A failed
alignment check consumes neither the instance ownership token nor allocator
state; `FreeBitMap(NULL)` remains the successful empty teardown.

### G06/G08 AreaInfo RastPort alignment

Area construction reaches the collector through `RastPort::AreaInfo`, then
uses word/long accesses for the descriptor and vector pointers. The portable
admission layer therefore requires an even nonzero RastPort base before
reading that link. This guard is intentionally in the shared AreaInfo reader
so `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, and `AreaEnd` share the same native
address-error behavior; it does not alter the provider-owned layered path or
the macro-only `AreaCircle` entry.

### G14 `ObtainBestPenA` TAG_SKIP cursor semantics

The best-pen tag walker keeps the current TagItem start, its data LONG
address, and the next complete TagItem as separate guest addresses. After a
`TAG_SKIP`, the data value is a count of following eight-byte TagItems, so the
new cursor is `nextCursor + data * 8`; it is not an offset from the data LONG.
The arithmetic is checked before the next read, while a terminal item at the
top of the guest address space and an explicit `TAG_MORE` continuation retain
their existing boundary behavior. This keeps portable palette selection
aligned with the 68000 TagItem ABI and leaves malformed/provider-owned lists
unclaimed at the register boundary.

### G14 `ObtainBestPenA` null `TAG_MORE` termination

The palette tag parser follows the same termination rule as the shared
`utility.library` `NextTagItem` implementation: a `TAG_MORE` whose continuation
pointer is zero ends the chain successfully. This is distinct from an odd,
unmapped, wrapped, or cyclic non-null continuation, which remains a checked
failure before `PaletteExtra` or ColorMap state is touched. Direct and
CopperStart coverage verifies that a null continuation still claims the valid
empty tag suffix and reaches ordinary pen acquisition.

### G14 `VideoControl` `TAG_SKIP` cursor semantics

Both VideoControl tag consumers keep the current TagItem, its data LONG, and
the next complete TagItem as distinct addresses. `TAG_SKIP` advances from that
next item by `data * 8` bytes, with checked guest-boundary arithmetic. The
collector therefore applies the intended later state command, and the batch
append path finds and rewrites the actual terminal item rather than a data
word. Null `TAG_MORE`/`VTAG_NEXTBUF_CM` continuations retain their clean-end
behavior; malformed chains still fail before any palette or guest-link write.

### G20 ExtendedSprite tag-list null continuation

The shared sprite option walker follows the Exec `TagItem` termination rule:
`TAG_MORE` with a zero continuation pointer ends the list successfully. This
keeps `AllocSpriteDataA`, `ChangeExtSpriteA`, and `GetExtSpriteA` consistent
with the other portable tag consumers without weakening the checked envelope:
odd heads/continuations, address-space wrap, cycles, unreadable records, and
the item budget still decline before sprite allocation or guest publication.
The direct and CopperStart adapter paths exercise the same null-suffix list.

### G15/G18 `OpenScreenTagList` large `TAG_SKIP` arithmetic

The synthetic screen-tag decoder treats the `TAG_SKIP` data word as a ULONG
count of complete eight-byte TagItems, matching the shared Exec/utility tag
ABI and the other portable graphics walkers. It computes the displacement in
`ulong`, rejects only a displacement or final cursor that cannot be represented
in the guest 32-bit address space, and then resumes at the next complete item.
The bounded visited-set and mapped-envelope checks remain in force, so a large
but valid skip can reach a later screen attribute while wrapped, cyclic, or
unreadable chains still decline before any Screen/ViewPort state is published.
This preserves the CopperSharp68k guest layout while leaving native display and
CyberGraphX provider arbitration at the register boundary.

### G02/G05 large `TAG_SKIP` cursor arithmetic

The remaining font and RastPort tag consumers use the same cursor rule as the
screen, palette, sprite, and VideoControl paths: the current item is eight
bytes, and `TAG_SKIP(data)` resumes at `nextCursor + data * 8`. The jump is
computed in `ulong` and rejected if the current item already wrapped or the
result leaves the 32-bit guest interval. Skipped records are not decoded or
counted against the bounded ordinary-item budget; the resumed item still goes
through the normal alignment, mapping, cycle, and terminal checks. This keeps
`ExtendFont`, tagged `WeighTAMatch`, and RastPort attribute lists consistent
with Exec `NextTagItem` semantics while preserving native/provider fallback for
malformed lists and keeping CyberGraphX outside the portable implementation.

### G05 `RPTAG_MaxPen` exclusive-limit readback

The portable `GetRPAttrsA` implementation now mirrors the resident mask walk
for `RPTAG_MaxPen`. It returns the number of pen values represented by the
current mask, rather than the highest index: an empty mask returns `0x100`,
and a mask whose highest bit is bit two returns `8`. The setter remains the
documented contiguous-mask operation, and the null-output no-op plus unknown
tag/provider boundary are unchanged. This keeps direct, CopperStart, and
future CopperSharp68k bodies on one guest-visible RastPort contract.

### G05 `SetMaxPen` range admission

`SetMaxPen` receives a ULONG but the classic planar contract defines the pen
value as `0..255`. The portable path keeps the zero request field-free, writes
the contiguous mask for `1..255`, and declines larger values before touching
`RastPort->Mask`. This avoids host-side narrowing that could steal a malformed
request from native or provider ownership.

### G09 AllocRaster UWORD gateway normalization

`AllocRaster` and `FreeRaster` use UWORD width/height fields in the public
68k vector frame. CopperStart therefore narrows D0/D1 at the register seam,
while the portable allocator helper retains a wider internal signature for
host-side geometry and overflow tests. This preserves the guest ABI without
changing the CopperSharp68k-compatible layout.

### G09 AllocBitMap UWORD gateway normalization

Superseded by the 2026-08-30 ULONG dimension unit. The earlier analogy to
AllocRaster was incorrect: [AllocBitMap's original declaration](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocBitMap)
uses ULONG width/height/depth/flags. Preserve complete dimensions at the register
seam and reject unrepresentable classic layouts without truncation. This does
not change AllocRaster's separate UWORD contract or provider ownership.

### G19 pixel-array UWORD gateway correction

The classic V36 pixel-array vectors carry UWORD coordinates/counts in D0-D3.
CopperStart therefore consumes each low word as an unsigned value before the
portable core or a layer provider sees it; `$FFFFxxxx` is a large non-negative
guest coordinate/count, not a negative clip coordinate. The provider
interface mirrors those UWORD types, and the portable core widens them to
checked host integers for bounded staging. V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` retains its
separate signed-LONG rectangle/stride contract. This keeps the
CopperSharp68k guest frame authoritative while leaving RTG/CyberGraphX
surface ownership in its separate seam.

### G11 BltPattern signed-WORD byte-count gateway normalization

`BltPattern` uses signed WORD rectangle coordinates and a signed WORD `byteCnt`
stride. The CopperStart adapter narrows D4 to that low register word before
entering the portable core or `IGraphicsLayerRasterBackend`; high-word residue
cannot alter stencil addressing. The portable core retains its bounded
contiguous-row preflight, so a non-positive or unstageable stencil request is
declined for native/provider ownership rather than partially read. A future
CopperSharp68k body can retain the same guest register layout, while
CopperScreen/provider paths can consume the explicit typed boundary.

### G10/G11 UBYTE minterm and mask gateway normalization

The Kickstart 3.1 blit vectors carry UBYTE values in the low bytes of D6
(`Minterm`) and, for `BltBitMap`, D7 (`Mask`). The register adapter explicitly
narrows those fields before entering the portable core or layered-provider
contract. This preserves the CopperSharp68k guest frame while ensuring upper
register residue cannot change the standard planar operation; RTG/CyberGraphX
surface ownership remains explicit.

### G03/G04 text-vector WORD/UWORD gateway normalization

The public text-vector register frame is now decoded at its documented field
widths. `Text`, `TextLength`, and `TextExtent` take a signed WORD character
count. `TextFit` takes UWORD `strLen`, width, and height fields plus a signed
WORD `strDirection`; negative signed counts are rejected before guest-string
or font traversal, and high-word residue is ignored. The mapped adapter and
`IGraphicsLayerRasterBackend` use the same narrowed values, while the
portable metric/rendering core retains widened host counts only for guarded
internal arithmetic and direct host tests. `TextLength` still publishes a
sign-extended WORD result. This is the CopperSharp68k-compatible guest
boundary; CyberGraphX/RTG remains provider-owned.

The contract is anchored by the official [Text](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/Text.html), [TextLength](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextLength.html), [TextExtent](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextExtent.html), and [TextFit](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit.html) autodocs.

### G02/G14 malformed shared-pen read ownership

`ObtainBestPenA` treats a shared ColorMap entry as observable guest state.
The nearest-color walk therefore fails closed when a shared entry's color
word is unreadable instead of silently skipping it and allocating another
pen. The public direct helper reports `-1`; the mapped adapter uses the
separate claim status to preserve D0 and cycles for native/provider fallback.
An actually empty shared list remains valid and calls the common
`ObtainPen(-1)` path, keeping allocation order, PaletteExtra links, and
viewport RGB publication in one implementation. This is a guest-memory
ownership rule, not a new color-distance metric; the documented palette
matching and precision behavior remains unchanged ([`ObtainBestPenA`](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/ObtainBestPenA.html)).

### G08 `NOCROSSFILL` area-filler boundary

The public `RastPort.Flags` bit `NOCROSSFILL` is part of the guest layout at
`$0020`. The portable AreaEnd renderer carries this state explicitly and
builds one temporary mask per recorded polygon or ellipse before applying the
pattern. That per-shape transaction is the no-crossover boundary and also
preserves the resident complement rule for overlapping shapes (one toggle per
shape, not one toggle for a merged union). A future CopperSharp68k-native
areafiller may specialize crossover handling behind the same flag and
function seam; CyberGraphX/RTG and layered damage remain provider-owned.

### G06 macro-level line-pattern setup

`SetDrPt` is a macro rather than a negative-vector entry, but its three guest
field writes are part of the RastPort line contract consumed by `Draw`,
`PolyDraw`, and area outlines. The portable implementation therefore exposes
one shared helper that writes `LinePtrn`, sets `FRST_DOT`, and stores a
15 preshift. The helper uses the same rollback boundary as the LVO setters so
host code cannot publish a half-updated RastPort, while native CopperSharp68k
code can use the identical offsets. No new ROM vector is claimed, and no
CyberGraphX/layer damage semantics are introduced.

### G05 `RPTAG_Font` exact `SetFont` transaction envelope

`SetRPAttrsA` snapshots each tag's native access envelope before publishing
the staged RastPort state. For `RPTAG_Font`, that envelope is deliberately
the font pointer, `AlgoStyle`, and `TextHeight`, `TextWidth`, and
`TextBaseline`, matching the fields read and written by `SetFont`. The
adjacent `TextFlags` and `TxSpacing` fields remain untouched caller state;
`AlgoStyle` is included because selecting a font clears the prior soft-style
effect and must be restored if a later tag fails. This keeps rollback
protection precise: a sparse or
provider-owned trailing field cannot block an otherwise valid font update,
while the same guest layout remains usable by a future CopperSharp68k body.
The regression injects a read fault only at `TxSpacing` and verifies that the
font and three cached metrics still publish atomically. Other G05 attribute
tags, layer damage, and CyberGraphX/RTG remain separate work units.

### G07 `SetRast` private-colour ownership envelope

`SetRast` receives its requested pen in the vector frame, but it still claims
the RastPort's standard-planar destination and therefore must respect a
readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker. The portable path admits that marker before
probing `BitMap` or `Mask`; a private-colour owner can keep those fields
unmapped while its native/provider renderer handles the operation. An
unreadable optional `Flags` word retains the sparse compatibility path, and
zero-mask/layer-provider behavior remains governed by its existing boundaries.
This keeps the guest field order identical for CopperStart and a future
CopperSharp68k-native body without adding CyberGraphX or custom-chip timing
dependencies.

### G11 Kickstart 3.1 interleaved masked-blit width compatibility

V39/V40 `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` constructs its temporary mask bitmap from an
interleaved source's aggregate guest `BytesPerRow`. Consequently the source
width presented to the mask walk is eight pixels per aggregate byte, not eight
pixels per linked plane row. The portable standard-planar path keeps this
quirk local to the masked blit: it widens the source geometry and external-mask
stride only when `BMF_INTERLEAVED` is set, while ordinary planar sources and
the later RTG/CyberGraphX provider retain their own contracts. The guest
BitMap layout remains aggregate-stride based for CopperSharp68k compatibility;
the host `BitmapInfo` exposes a temporary width view rather than mutating
caller-owned fields. This unit changes no custom-chip timing or layer damage
policy.

### G03 `FontExtent` result-envelope admission

`FontExtent` publishes the same packed 12-byte `TextExtent` result as the
other metric vectors. The portable path therefore validates the non-null,
word-aligned, fully addressable destination before asking the font backend for
metrics or walking the declared glyph range. A malformed output buffer stays
available to native/provider ownership without provider work for a result that
cannot be committed. The mapped CopperStart adapter applies the same odd and
address-envelope checks; valid metric and guest-write behavior is unchanged.

The same admission now applies to `TextExtent` and `TextFit`: direct portable
calls and the CopperStart adapter validate the output envelope before font
metrics or glyph-stream work. This keeps the three metric vectors on one
CopperSharp68k-compatible result boundary.

### G07 `ScrollRasterBF` two-dimensional backfill union

`ScrollRasterBF` moves the overlapping source snapshot first and then delegates
the vacated strips to `EraseRect`. For a nonzero `dx` and `dy`, the horizontal
and vertical strips overlap at a corner; that corner must be backfilled once,
not twice. The portable path narrows the second strip to the source-preserving
X span, preserving the classic union semantics for `COMPLEMENT` draw mode
where a second fill would toggle the corner back. The change is local to the
standard-planar BF path, keeps the public signed-WORD coordinates intact, and
does not introduce layer damage or CyberGraphX behavior.

### G07 `ScrollRasterBF` all-quadrant backfill union

The union rule applies symmetrically to leftward and rightward scrolls and to
both top and bottom vacated strips. When `dx < 0`, the second strip begins
after the left vacated edge; when `dx > 0`, it ends before the right vacated
edge. Applying those bounds in either `dy` branch prevents both diagonal
corners from receiving a second `EraseRect` under `COMPLEMENT`. The unit is
still standard-planar and provider-neutral, with no change to the guest
RastPort/BitMap layout or custom-chip timing boundary.

### G05 `DrawBounds` signed-word result envelope (2026-08-15)

`RPTAG_DrawBounds` publishes a classic eight-byte `Rectangle` whose four
coordinates are signed guest WORDs. The portable non-layered path now rejects
bitmap widths or heights whose final coordinate cannot fit that envelope
before writing any result field. This prevents an oversized malformed bitmap
from being narrowed into a wrapped negative bound and leaves the request
available to a native/provider owner. Layer-owned bounds remain behind the
explicit Layers boundary.

### G07 ClearEOL/ClearScreen signed-coordinate admission (2026-08-16)

`ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` delegate their nonzero-mask spans to the classic
`RectFill` coordinate contract, whose guest arguments are signed WORDs. The
portable path now validates every right/bottom endpoint before staging public
pens, line state, or plane storage. Oversized malformed bitmap geometry thus
declines to the native/provider owner instead of narrowing an endpoint into a
wrapped negative coordinate and silently turning a real clear into an
inverted no-op. The existing zero-effective-mask bounded success path remains
unchanged. Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage preserves the line-pattern
phase, D0, and cycle frame on decline; layer damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and
custom-chip timing remain separate boundaries.

### G07 `ScrollRasterBF` clipped negative-edge union

The BF backfill union is derived from the clipped source envelope rather than
the raw logical origin. A left/up scroll whose requested rectangle starts
outside the bitmap therefore clears the visible destination edge whose source
coordinate is still off-raster. The horizontal strip is computed first; the
vertical strip excludes that visible range, retaining exactly-once
`EraseRect` coverage for diagonal `COMPLEMENT` operations. The change keeps
the standard planar layout and provider/layer boundary unchanged.
### G15/G16 `FreeVPortCopLists` address-wrap admission (2026-08-16)

The four public copper-link fields cleared by `FreeVPortCopLists` are
68000-longword guest fields. The portable teardown now rejects a `ViewPort`
base whose final link would cross the 32-bit guest address envelope before it
performs any link read or write. This prevents unchecked host arithmetic from
wrapping a malformed high-memory base into unrelated low memory, while
preserving the existing link-only rollback and provider handoff behavior.

### G15/G16 `FreeVPortCopLists` sparse-link rollback envelope (2026-08-16)

The core teardown snapshot and restore now use the same four-link address
envelope as the portable clear operation instead of requiring the unrelated
`ViewPortSize` tail. A sparse/provider-owned viewport whose link fields fit
but whose full header crosses `$FFFFFFFF` can therefore be declined without
losing its links during the no-owner rollback path. Direct and CopperStart
mapped coverage exercises the failure and preserves D0/cycles; normal copper
resource handoff remains unchanged.

### G15/G16 palette viewport inclusive-longword envelope (2026-08-16)

Viewport palette admission now treats `vp_ColorMap` as an inclusive four-byte
guest envelope. The sole even base whose field ends at `$FFFFFFFF` is valid,
so owned ColorMaps remain claimable by direct and CopperStart native-overlay
palette paths instead of being declined one byte early. No CyberGraphX/RTG,
layer-damage, or custom-chip timing policy is changed.
### G09/G19 `BitMapScale` inclusive final plane-link envelope (2026-08-16)

Bitmap utility readers treat each declared `BitMap.Planes[]` entry as an
inclusive guest LONG envelope. A compact depth-one header whose final plane
pointer byte is `$FFFFFFFF` is therefore accepted; only a field that crosses
the 32-bit boundary declines to the native/provider owner. The mapped
`BitScaleArgs` pointer check uses the same inclusive arithmetic, preserving
the CopperSharp68k guest layout without changing RTG/CyberGraphX ownership.

### G04/G06 `DrawEllipse` optional Flags admission (2026-08-16)

`DrawEllipse` consumes `RastPort.Flags` only as a compatibility-provider hint
for `RPF_NO_PENS`; it does not publish or update that word. The portable
standard-planar path therefore honors the marker when the word is readable,
