but treats an absent or faulted optional word as a sparse-port condition and
continues with the ordinary ellipse geometry/bitmap contract. This keeps a
future CopperSharp68k body and the CopperStart adapter on the same ownership
boundary without turning a provider hint into a required field. Direct and
mapped coverage verifies identical pixels, D0, and cycles; layer damage,
CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing remain separate boundaries.

### G19 V36 pixel-array temporary RastPort inclusive-longword envelope (2026-08-16)

The explicit temporary `RastPort` supplied to the V36 `ReadPixelLine8`,
`WritePixelLine8`, `ReadPixelArray8`, and `WritePixelArray8` helpers is a
native guest structure, not host metadata. Its `rp_BitMap` link is consumed as
one 68000 longword, so portable admission now treats the field end
inclusively: the aligned base `$FFFF_FFF8` is valid because the link occupies
`$FFFF_FFFC..$FFFF_FFFF`, while a base whose link crosses the boundary remains
available to a native/provider owner. Direct and CopperStart mapped paths use
the same guard; temporary planar workspace probing, layer ownership, RTG, and
custom-chip timing remain separate contracts.

### G15/G16 palette viewport inclusive-longword validation closure (2026-08-16)

The shared viewport palette admission is evidence-closed: the portable
ColorMap ownership/lock gate accepts the final even `ViewPort` base whose
`vp_ColorMap` longword ends at `$FFFFFFFF`, and the native-overlay register
path reaches the same owned map. Direct and mapped lifecycle tests pass with
unchanged D0/cycles and palette data; RTG/CyberGraphX and display timing remain
provider-owned.

### G09/G19 `BitMapScale` inclusive final plane-link validation closure (2026-08-16)

The compact depth-one `BitMap` envelope at `$FFFF_FFF4` is now validated
through both direct and CopperStart dispatch. Its `Planes[0]` longword ends
at `$FFFFFFFF` and scales normally; crossing headers remain available to the
native/provider owner. The full graphics scaffold remains green, with no
change to RTG/CyberGraphX or display-DMA ownership.

### G15/G16 `FreeVPortCopLists` sparse-link rollback validation closure (2026-08-16)

Viewport copper teardown is now evidence-closed for both high-address and
sparse-link envelopes. The eight-test family passes, preserving all four
public copper links and the D0/cycle frame when no display owner can claim a
wrapped full header; ordinary owner release and the null no-op remain intact.

### G15/G16 `MakeVPort` transactional copper-link handoff (2026-08-16)

`MakeVPort` now snapshots the four public `ViewPort` copper links before
replaying optional video-control state, allocating a temporary `ViewPortExtra`,
or calling the copper builder. If a status-aware builder publishes partial
links and then declines, the portable core restores the snapshot and releases
only its temporary association. Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage use a
mutating failing builder and preserve all links, the failure status, and the
caller cycle frame; successful copper construction and caller-owned extras
remain unchanged. Hardware copper timing, layer damage, and CyberGraphX/RTG
ownership remain provider/native boundaries.

### G15/G16 `MrgCop` transactional copper-link handoff (2026-08-16)

`MrgCop` now snapshots the four public copper links for every visible
`ViewPort` in the validated chain before calling a status-aware merge owner.
If that owner publishes partial links and returns a failure status, the core
restores every visible link; hidden ViewPorts remain outside the snapshot just
as the resident merge loop skips their payload. Direct and CopperStart mapped
coverage exercise a two-viewport mutating failure and preserve the status,
links, and cycle frame. Hardware copper stream timing and provider-owned
display publication remain separate boundaries.

### G15/G16 direct `WaitTOF` scheduler ownership (2026-08-16)

The direct compatibility entry now consults the same optional
`IGraphicsFrameWaitStatusBackend` used by the timed/register gateway. A
status-aware display adapter that declines a frame wait returns failure without
calling its legacy void callback, leaving the native/provider vector available;
legacy display backends retain the existing successful void wait. This keeps
screen synchronization ownership explicit without fabricating a frame boundary.

### G19 V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` signed-LONG register geometry (2026-08-16)

The V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` vector carries `xstart`, `ystart`, `xstop`, and
`ystop` as signed `LONG` values, independently of the V36 UWORD pixel-array
vectors. The CopperStart provider and portable-core register paths now decode
D0-D3 as full signed 32-bit coordinates before entering the common planar
writer; source stride D4 remains a signed `LONG`. Direct and mapped coverage
uses a 65,536-pixel row with coordinates above 32767, proving that the same
guest destination is selected without narrowing through a WORD. The native
provider boundary remains explicit for layered/RTG surfaces and oversized or
malformed spans ([WriteChunkyPixels autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WriteChunkyPixels)).

### G15/G18 `OpenScreen` failure-finalization rollback (2026-08-16)

`OpenScreen` and `OpenScreenTagList` keep request-scoped failure finalization
independent from the result of the attempted `CloseScreen` rollback. After a
display-rethink failure or a post-rethink Screen-identity replacement, the
optional finalizer is now called exactly once even when teardown succeeds;
staged palette/error state therefore cannot leak into the next request. A
declined close remains available to the native/provider teardown boundary, but
does not keep the failed request pending. The change is limited to the
portable CopperStart Intuition transaction and does not claim CyberGraphX,
layer damage, or hardware display ownership.

### G15/G18 `ScreenToFront` ViewPort address-wrap admission (2026-08-16)

The legacy `ScreenToFront` selector now validates the derived
`Screen.ViewPort` guest address before adding the public `0x2C` field offset.
An even Screen pointer whose ViewPort field would wrap past `$FFFF_FFFF` is
left unclaimed for native/provider address-error handling rather than being
turned into a low-memory viewport selection. State-aware activation callbacks
retain first ownership of valid provider requests; the change does not add
screen ordering or CyberGraphX behavior.

### G07 Clear-vector odd TextFont ownership (2026-08-16)

`ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` consume the selected `TextFont.tf_YSize` through
the guest `RastPort.Font` pointer. A nonzero odd font address is therefore a
malformed 68000 word-access envelope and must remain available to the native or
provider implementation; it must not silently fall through to the cached
`TxHeight` compatibility fallback. The portable helper now rejects only that
odd non-null form while retaining the even-but-unmapped fallback used by
synthetic host font backends. Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage preserve
the raster, line-pattern phase, D0, and cycles on decline; no layer, RTG,
CyberGraphX, or custom-chip timing policy changes.

### G07 Clear-vector text-row top admission (2026-08-16)

The clear vectors pass the derived text-row top to the signed-WORD `RectFill`
body along with the right and bottom endpoints. A top below `-32768` must
therefore remain available to the native/provider implementation; narrowing it
through an unchecked cast could wrap an entirely off-screen clear into a
visible rectangle. The portable preflight now validates the top endpoint for
both ClearEOL and ClearScreen before public pen, line-pattern, or plane
publication. Direct and mapped coverage preserves the raster, phase, D0, and
cycles on decline; no layer, RTG, CyberGraphX, or custom-chip timing policy
changes.

### G15/G18 `ViewPortAddress` Window-to-ViewPort ownership (2026-08-16)

The Intuition ABI takes a `Window *`, not a `Screen *`: the returned viewport
is the viewport of the screen referenced by that window. The compatibility
context therefore gains an optional Window*-aware provider. Non-null requests
use that provider when present; NULL retains the single-screen compatibility
fallback, and odd pointers are rejected before either callback. The synthetic
boot owner accepts only its own Window-shaped object, verifies its `WScreen`
link still names the synthetic Screen, and derives `Screen + 0x2C` only after
an overflow check. Foreign or malformed windows remain available to
native/provider ownership. Layer damage, CyberGraphX/RTG presentation, and
custom-chip timing remain outside this seam.

### G15/G16 `FreeCprList` odd-address admission (2026-08-16)

`FreeCprList` now rejects a nonzero odd `CprList *` before probing the public
structure envelope or invoking a display/resource owner. The list contains
native word/long fields and therefore cannot be legally dereferenced at an
odd 68000 address; NULL remains the successful empty-list no-op. Direct
coverage proves no release callback is reached, while the CopperStart mapped
path chains a readable odd address back to the resident vector with D0/cycles
and the host callback unchanged. Hardware copper teardown, CyberGraphX/RTG,
and provider allocation ownership remain separate boundaries.

### G14 `GetRGB32`/`LoadRGB32` odd-table admission (2026-08-16)

The RGB32 vectors now reject a nonzero odd table before reading or writing
guest ULONG records. `GetRGB32` keeps its zero-count no-op, while
`LoadRGB32(NULL)` remains ignored; non-null tables are word-aligned before
the portable color-map or display callback boundary is considered. Direct
register coverage preserves D0, cycles, and table bytes, and the mapped ROM
overlay chains both malformed vectors to their native targets. Palette
publication, CyberGraphX/RTG surfaces, and custom-chip timing remain outside
this standard ColorMap envelope ([GetRGB32 autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node02E9.html), [LoadRGB32 autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node02FB.html)).

### G14 `LoadRGB4` odd-table admission (2026-08-16)

`LoadRGB4` now rejects a nonzero odd `UWORD *` color table before reading
guest words, mutating ColorMap entries, or calling the palette backend. A
positive count still requires a non-null aligned table; zero/negative counts
retain the successful no-op behavior. Direct register coverage preserves the
caller frame and table bytes, while the CopperStart mapped path chains a
readable odd table to the resident vector. This follows the documented
UWORD-table ABI and leaves palette publication, CyberGraphX/RTG, and
custom-chip timing outside this unit ([LoadRGB4 autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0458.html)).

### G10/G11 `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` chip-mask admission (2026-08-16)

The portable masked bitmap blit now treats the external `bltmask` plane as a
chip-memory resource when the active CopperStart memory adapter exposes the
optional display-DMA classifier. The complete mask span (`BytesPerRow * Rows`)
is checked for 32-bit address wrap and display-DMA ownership before any mask
bytes, source planes, or destination pixels are probed. A memory-only
CopperSharp68k implementation without that sidecar retains its ordinary
guest-range/readability contract; RTG/CyberGraphX and provider-owned surfaces
remain outside the portable path.

Direct sidecar coverage declines a readable non-chip mask before guest mask
access or destination mutation. The mapped ROM-overlay fixture proves the
same request leaves the void D0/cycle frame untouched and tail-chains to the
resident vector. The source contract follows the Kickstart 3.1 note that the
mask plane must reside in chip memory ([BltMaskBitMapRastPort autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/BltMaskBitMapRastPort.html)).

### G10 `BltBitMap` overlapping TempA chip admission (2026-08-16)

An overlapping, non-null `BltBitMap` `TempA` is now checked as a complete
one-scanline workspace through the optional `IGraphicsDisplayMemory` sidecar,
after the existing word-alignment and guest-readability checks and before any
plane validation or pixel staging. Non-overlapping requests retain the
documented no-TempA access path, and a memory-only CopperSharp68k adapter keeps
its ordinary guest-range contract. Allocator-owned TempA receives the same
display-DMA classification when the sidecar is present; its existing Chip
allocator/free transaction remains authoritative otherwise.

Direct sidecar coverage declines a readable non-chip workspace without
changing the source/destination raster. The mapped ROM-overlay fixture proves
the same decline preserves D0/cycles and tail-chains to the resident vector.
This follows the [BltBitMap autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/BltBitMap.html), which requires an overlapping TempA to be chip-accessible.

### G10/G11 shared planar-plane chip admission (2026-08-16)

The common planar blit validator now checks each participating real source and
destination plane as a complete guest envelope through the optional
`IGraphicsDisplayMemory` classifier, after word alignment and readability
preflight and before pixel staging. V36 source constants (`NULL` and
`$FFFFFFFF`) remain synthetic and are not classified; destination constants
remain invalid. Because `ClipBlit`, `BltBitMapRastPort`, and
`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` converge on this validator, they inherit the same
CopperStart/native address-class boundary without imposing a policy on
memory-only CopperSharp68k adapters.

Direct coverage proves source and destination class declines preserve the
raster, while the mapped ROM-overlay fixture preserves D0/cycles and
tail-chains the declined source-plane request. The shared blitter behavior is
consistent with the [BltBitMap autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/BltBitMap.html), which identifies these operations as using the Amiga blitter.

### G11 `BltClear` chip-memory admission (2026-08-16)

The portable clear vector now checks the complete scalar or row-mode
`memBlock` span through the optional `IGraphicsDisplayMemory` classifier after
word alignment and 32-bit envelope validation, but before the first guest
probe, snapshot, or write. Empty scalar/row forms retain their documented
claimed no-op behavior, and memory-only CopperSharp68k adapters retain the
ordinary readable guest-range contract.

Direct sidecar coverage declines a readable non-chip buffer without changing
its bytes. The mapped ROM-overlay fixture proves the same void call preserves
D0/cycles and tail-chains to the resident vector. This follows the [BltClear autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/BltClear.html), which describes `memBlock` as local, blitter-accessible memory.

### G11 `BltTemplate` chip-source admission (2026-08-16)

The portable template vector now preflights the complete clipped source-byte
envelope for every affected template row through the optional
`IGraphicsDisplayMemory` classifier before reading the A-source bytes. The
source pointer remains word-aligned and the existing signed-even modulo and
guest-address checks remain in force; negative modulo rows are classified at
their actual checked addresses. Memory-only CopperSharp68k adapters retain
their ordinary readable guest-source contract, while layered/RTG ownership
stays at the provider boundary.

Direct sidecar coverage declines a readable non-chip template without changing
the destination. The mapped ROM-overlay fixture proves the same void call
preserves D0/cycles and tail-chains to the resident vector. This follows the
Kickstart template contract, which uses a blitter A-source template in chip
memory ([BltTemplate autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/BltTemplate.html)).

### G15/G18 `OpenScreen` NewScreen envelope admission (2026-08-16)

The portable Intuition bridge now has an optional `ValidateNewScreenAddress`
boundary before either `OpenScreen` or `OpenScreenTagList` invokes a host
configuration callback. The synthetic CopperStart owner wires this seam to
require the complete legacy/extended `NewScreen` envelope (through the
`ExtNewScreen.Extension` pointer) to remain inside the 32-bit guest address
space. This closes the unchecked `base + field-offset` path for high even
addresses while retaining odd-pointer admission, mapped-memory checks, and
tag ownership in the synthetic builder.

The seam is deliberately optional: a CopperSharp68k memory-only host or a
native/provider implementation can leave it unset and apply its own mapping
and address-error policy. A rejected pointer returns the normal NULL result
before screen staging, `RethinkDisplay`, finalization, or rollback callbacks.
This matches the Kickstart contract that `OpenScreen` consumes a `NewScreen`
or `ExtNewScreen`, builds and links the complete screen, and returns NULL on
failure ([OpenScreen autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenScreen.html)).

### G15/G18 `OpenWindow` NewWindow envelope admission (2026-08-16)

The portable Intuition bridge now has an optional `ValidateNewWindowAddress`
boundary before `OpenWindow` invokes the host window-configuration callback.
The synthetic CopperStart owner wires this seam through the complete legacy
`NewWindow` prefix ending at `nw_Type`, preventing unchecked field additions
from wrapping the 32-bit guest address space for high even bases. Existing
odd-pointer, mapped-prefix, screen-target, and window/display transaction
rules remain in their respective owners.

As with the screen seam, this validator is optional so CopperSharp68k
memory-only and native/provider implementations can retain their own
high-address mapping or address-error policy. A rejected pointer returns the
normal NULL result before window staging, screen admission, display rethink,
or cleanup callbacks. This follows the Kickstart contract that `OpenWindow`
consumes a `NewWindow` structure and allocates the complete window before
returning it ([OpenWindow autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenWindow.html)).

### G15/G18 Screen/Window teardown envelope admission (2026-08-16)

The Intuition bridge now exposes optional `ValidateScreenAddress` and
`ValidateWindowAddress` seams for synthetic Screen/Window owners. CopperStart
wires them to the complete public `Screen` and `Window` envelopes before
`CloseScreen`, `CloseWindow`, `ScreenToFront`, `ShowTitle`, `GetScreenData`,
`ModifyIDCMP`, `SetWindowTitles`, or the window-specific `ViewPortAddress`
lookup can call a host callback. A high even base whose structure would wrap
the 32-bit guest address space therefore remains unclaimed, with D0 and the
live cycle frame unchanged.

The validators are optional and do not impose a host address policy on
memory-only CopperSharp68k or native/provider implementations. NULL and odd
pointer rules remain at their existing entry-point boundaries, while the
synthetic owner retains its screen/window lock and display teardown policy.
The close result follows the V36+ `CloseScreen` success/failure contract
([CloseScreen autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/intuition.library/CloseScreen.html)).

### G03/G04/G05 RTG RastPort metric ownership (2026-08-16)

Metric queries are part of the RastPort text surface, but a CyberGraphX-owned
RastPort may carry a provider-specific font, spacing, or layout model. The
register adapter therefore tests explicit RTG ownership before reading the
signed count, selected guest font, or result `TextExtent` envelope for
`TextLength`, `TextExtent`, and `TextFit`. A decline leaves D0 and the cycle
frame untouched so the provider/native vector can observe the original call.

This is an ownership-only seam: standard-planar metric decoding remains in
the portable core, layered text rendering keeps its existing layers provider,
and memory-only CopperSharp68k adapters do not acquire a host RTG policy.

### G04 ColorTextFont foreground-map contract (2026-08-16)

The portable ColorTextFont compositor now treats the low `ctf_Flags` bit as
the `CTF_MAPCOLOR` selector. A source color is replaced by the RastPort APen
only when that selector is set, `ctf_FgColor` is not `$FF`, and the selected
color lies in the guest-declared `ctf_Low..ctf_High` range. Grey fonts and
out-of-range foreground values therefore retain their composed planar color;
the existing `PlanePick`/`PlaneOnOff` destination mapping is unchanged.

The rule is implemented inside `GraphicsColorFontInfo`, so the pure core and
CopperStart register gateway share one guest-memory interpretation. The
regression exercises the grey/no-map case, an out-of-range mapped candidate,
and a valid mapped color; provider-owned RTG text remains outside this
standard-planar compositor ([graphics.library text reference](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Graphics_Library_and_Text)).

### G04 ColorTextFont antialias provider ownership (2026-08-16)

`Text` now resolves a selected `FSF_COLORFONT` font's color metadata before it
reads draw mode, mask, bitmap, or public pens. The portable compositor accepts
only the exact `CT_COLORFONT` and `CT_GREYFONT` low-nibble forms. A
`CT_ANTIALIAS` bit, or any combined/unsupported low-nibble value, declines the
standard-planar path so the native/CyberGraphX provider can supply its chunky
renderer without a partial guest operation.

The check is repeated at the shared text boundary rather than being left only
to `GraphicsMemoryFontBackend`; custom host font backends therefore cannot
accidentally claim an unsupported representation. Pure and mapped calls share
the same no-read/no-mutation handoff, while ordinary color/grey planar strikes
retain the existing `PlanePick`/`PlaneOnOff` and `CTF_MAPCOLOR` rules. The
ownership split follows the [ColorTextFont flag definitions](https://d0.se/include/graphics/text.h)
and the classic [Text branch selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c).

### G03/G04 RTG empty `Text` ownership (2026-08-16)

The CopperStart register adapter checks explicit RTG RastPort ownership before
interpreting the signed character count. This ordering is intentional: the
portable core may still implement the documented count-zero `Text` no-op for a
standard-planar RastPort without reading guest state, but an RTG-owned
RastPort must reach CyberGraphX/native text first even when the count is zero.
The adapter therefore returns a provider decline with D0 and cycles untouched,
and does not require the RTG RastPort, font, bitmap, or draw-state fields to be
readable. Direct calls that explicitly target the portable core retain their
existing empty no-op; the ownership check belongs at the provider-aware
register boundary. This keeps the CopperSharp68k guest layout unchanged while
allowing CopperScreen/native providers to supply their own empty-text semantics.

### G04/G06 RTG `Move` ownership

`Move` is a RastPort state transition, but an RTG RastPort's cursor belongs to
the CyberGraphX/native provider alongside its other raster vectors. The
CopperStart adapter therefore checks the explicit RTG predicate before
decoding D0/D1 or touching `cp_x`, `cp_y`, `linpatcnt`, or `Flags`. A standard
planar RastPort continues through the portable `Move` implementation; a
provider decline preserves the complete register/cycle frame for the original
vector. The guest layout and CopperSharp68k-compatible core remain unchanged.

### G04/G06 RTG empty `PolyDraw` ownership (2026-08-16)

The provider-aware register adapter checks the selected RastPort for explicit
RTG ownership before applying the portable low-word count-zero `PolyDraw`
no-op. This preserves the classic no-read behavior for standard-planar calls,
but leaves an empty RTG call transparent to CyberGraphX/native ownership with
the incoming D0 and cycle frame unchanged. The direct CopperStart adapter and
the mapped ROM-overlay gateway share the same decision; the guest `PolyDraw`
ABI and CopperSharp68k layout remain unchanged. The low-word/no-read behavior
follows the [AROS PolyDraw implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c).

### G05 RTG RastPort state, font, style, and attribute ownership (2026-08-16)

The provider-aware register adapter now checks explicit RTG RastPort ownership
before all portable RastPort state and attribute vectors: pen and draw-mode
set/get operations, `SetABPenDrMd`, write/max/outline pen operations,
`SetFont`, soft-style accessors, and `SetRPAttrsA`/`GetRPAttrsA`. The check is
performed before default-font lookup, tag-list validation, or public state
reads, preserving the incoming registers and cycle frame for CyberGraphX or a
native owner. Standard-planar and memory-only CopperSharp68k paths retain the
existing state ABI and transactional behavior.

### G02/G04 RTG `AskFont` ownership (2026-08-16)

`AskFont` is a RastPort text query even though its public result is a caller
owned `TextAttr`. The register adapter therefore checks explicit RTG ownership
before reading `rp_Font` or probing/writing the output envelope. A decline
leaves D-registers and cycles unchanged, so CyberGraphX or a native 68k owner
can apply its own font model. Standard-planar queries continue through the
portable guest-memory implementation, and the existing CopperSharp68k layout
does not change. The direct and mapped state/font/style matrix covers this
provider-first ordering.

## Graphics gate audit (2026-08-16)

The standard-planar implementation remains validated by the 1182-test
graphics scaffold and warning-free isolated builds. A broader layered ledger
fixture still fails after `SetFont` is deliberately left to its RTG/provider
owner; the subsequent provider `ClearEOL` therefore has no portable
`TxHeight`. This is recorded as a separate CyberGraphX/layer font-state goal,
not as a reason to broaden standard-planar or CopperSharp68k ownership.

## G04/G06 empty layered `PolyDraw` ownership (2026-08-16)

The empty `PolyDraw` fast path has two explicit ownership outcomes. A
readable nonzero `rp_Layer` declines from the pure planar collector and is
forwarded by CopperStart to the layer provider, preserving the caller frame.
A null or unreadable RastPort remains the classic no-read standard-planar
success. RTG ownership is checked first and is unchanged. This keeps the
CopperSharp68k guest layout independent of layer damage/backing-store policy.
The isolated emulator and test-project builds pass with 0 warnings and 0
errors.

## G03/G04 empty layered `Text` ownership closeout (2026-08-16)

The portable `Text` path keeps its classic empty-request no-read behavior for
standard-planar callers, but a readable nonzero `rp_Layer` is an explicit
ownership marker. Without a layer visibility predicate the pure collector
declines, and CopperStart gives a layered empty request to the layer provider
before clearing the void-vector D0. Unreadable/null endpoints remain
claimable as the bounded no-read standard-planar form. RTG checks still run
first, so CyberGraphX remains a separate patch surface; no guest layout or
CopperSharp68k ABI changes are required.

The focused pure, direct/mapped, RTG, and layer-provider regressions pass 5/5;
the full graphics scaffold passes 1185/1185, and isolated emulator/test
project builds are warning-free.

## G19 `BitMapScale` zero-factor ownership closeout (2026-08-16)

The scaler's zero-factor guard is an ownership boundary, not a zero-sized
success. It runs before bitmap reads and before publishing destination extents,
so an invalid ratio preserves both the caller's `BitScaleArgs` and destination
storage. CopperStart consequently leaves the mapped frame available to a
native or provider implementation. This is the portable transaction around
the `ScalerDiv` extent rule in [AROS `BitMapScale`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c);
it does not broaden RTG/CyberGraphX or alter CopperSharp68k guest layouts.

The focused pure/mapped regression passes 2/2, the full graphics scaffold passes
1186/1186, and isolated emulator/test-project builds are warning-free.

## G09 OCS interleaved rollback ownership closeout (2026-08-16)

`AllocBitMap` now snapshots the effective published bitmap flags for all late
rollback paths. A requested `BMF_INTERLEAVED` bit is removed from that snapshot
on OCS, so the separate plane allocations are released one by one after a
faulted plane-pointer write. ECS/AGA continues to publish one contiguous block
and release it as one span. This keeps rollback ownership aligned with the
guest `BitMap` header and the classic [`AllocBitMap` contract](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocBitMap.html).

The focused OCS rollback matrix passes 3/3 and the complete graphics scaffold
passes 1187/1187; isolated emulator/test-project builds are warning-free. No
CopperSharp68k layout or RTG/CyberGraphX provider surface is changed.

## G14 `GetRGB32` zero-count table ownership closeout (2026-08-16)

The portable palette boundary now orders its checks as range validation,
zero-count no-op, then output-table alignment/readability. `GetRGB32(cm,
first, 0, NULL)` therefore succeeds without a guest-memory read or write,
while every non-empty request retains its aligned table envelope and rollback
behavior. CopperStart maps the same result and only publishes the void-vector
D0 value; unrelated data registers and the call cycle remain untouched. The
no-output-envelope rule is grounded in the
[graphics.library `GetRGB32` autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/GetRGB32.html),
which sizes the table as `ncolors * 3` longwords. This is a portable ABI edge,
not a CyberGraphX/provider or CopperSharp68k layout change.

The direct/mapped regression passes 1/1, the palette subset passes 31/31, the
full graphics scaffold passes 1188/1188, and isolated emulator/test-project
builds are warning-free.

## G03 empty TextFit ownership boundary

The register adapter treats a zero-character `TextFit` as a result-only
transaction. It rejects explicit RTG ownership before any portable probe,
validates the output `TextExtent`, and then lets the core publish the empty
extent without reading `rp_Font`, optional `constrainingExtent`, or text bytes.
This keeps direct CopperStart and native-overlay dispatch on one ABI path while
leaving non-empty metric requests fully guarded.

The boundary is justified by the official [`TextFit` autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit.html):
`strLen == 0` denotes no characters and the result is an empty `TextExtent`.
Layer damage and RTG/provider behavior remain outside this portable unit.

## G03 `FontExtent` declared-range envelope

The portable `FontExtent` implementation iterates the declared
`tf_LoChar..tf_HiChar` range only. A TextFont carries one extra metric-table
slot for the out-of-range fallback glyph; that slot is consumed by text
rendering and `TextLength`, but it is not part of the font's declared
font-wide bounding envelope. The implementation therefore retains the
fallback decoder while excluding `TryGetMetricDefaultGlyph` from
`FontExtent`.

The result keeps the classic split: `te_Width` selects the maximum movement in
the font's direction (negative only for `FPF_REVPATH`), bitmap bounds include
kerning and glyph width, and neither algorithmic RastPort style nor `TxSpacing`
participates. The rule is grounded in the
[graphics.library `FontExtent` autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/FontExtent.html)
and is shared by direct CopperStart calls and the 68k register gateway.

## G07 `RectFill` inverted-geometry admission

The portable `RectFill` path first classifies inverted inclusive bounds as an
empty void operation. It does not require a bitmap or layer envelope for a
partially mapped standard-planar RastPort, but a readable non-null layer still
blocks the pure core so a layer provider can own the call. The CopperStart
adapter probes RTG ownership first, preserves readable layered routing, and
otherwise applies the same no-read no-op at the register boundary. This keeps
the CopperSharp68k memory contract explicit without forcing host-layer policy
into the portable core.

The boundary is grounded in the
[graphics.library RectFill autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/RectFill.html)
and the classic [AROS RectFill source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/rectfill.c).
The direct/mapped and layered regressions pass 3/3; the full graphics scaffold
is 1190/1190 with warning-free isolated builds.

## G07 `ScrollRaster` inverted-geometry admission

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` classify reversed inclusive bounds as an
empty affected rectangle before requiring bitmap or line-state storage. A
readable non-null layer still blocks the pure core so the layer provider can
own the operation; an unreadable or partially mapped layer cannot steal the
standard-planar no-op. CopperStart checks RTG ownership first, preserves the
layer-provider path, and otherwise applies the same register-level short
circuit.

The direct/mapped and layered regressions pass 3/3, and the full graphics
scaffold is 1191/1191 with warning-free isolated builds. This keeps the
portable/CopperSharp68k memory contract separate from layer damage and native
display timing.

## G07 `EraseRect` inverted-geometry admission

The portable `EraseRect` path classifies reversed inclusive bounds before
requiring bitmap, pen, or minterm state. A readable non-null layer still blocks
the pure core so a layer provider can own the operation; an unreadable or
partially mapped standard-planar RastPort can complete the empty no-op.
CopperStart checks RTG ownership first, preserves readable layered routing, and
otherwise applies the same register-level short-circuit.

The direct/mapped and layered regressions pass 3/3, and the full graphics
scaffold is 1192/1192 with warning-free isolated builds. Layer damage,
CyberGraphX/RTG rendering, and custom-chip timing remain separate boundaries.

## G18 standard-planar `SA_BitMap` borrowing

`OpenScreenTagList` now admits a caller-owned standard-planar bitmap when its
even BitMap header, declared plane links, row span, and interleaved aliases are
fully readable. The synthetic Screen.RastPort and ViewPort RasInfo chain point
at that exact guest bitmap; the embedded Screen.BitMap is only a compatibility
header copy. The close and rollback paths clear synthetic links but never free
or rewrite the caller's header or plane bytes. A malformed or foreign custom
bitmap still declines before screen publication, preserving the native/provider
handoff. This follows the documented [`SA_BitMap` contract](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Intuition_Screens#SA_BitMap)
and keeps the guest layout ready for a future CopperSharp68k image.

### Compact `BMF_MINPLANES` headers

The borrowed bitmap validator also accepts the public compact allocation form:
when `BMF_MINPLANES` is set, only the header prefix and the declared
depth-sized plane-pointer tail need to be mapped. The embedded Screen bitmap
is still a full compatibility envelope, but its unused plane pointers are
cleared before the mapped source prefix is copied. Teardown compares the
declared geometry and used plane links without probing an unmapped unused tail,
so the caller retains ownership of the compact header and all plane storage.

### Non-standard bitmap handoff

The portable screen bridge claims only headers marked `BMF_STANDARD`. A
readable geometry/plane envelope without that flag is deliberately left
unclaimed, preserving the caller's header, planes, and `SA_ErrorCode` for a
native Intuition or CyberGraphX implementation. This keeps the standard
planar contract distinct from provider-owned bitmap representations.

## G05/G26 `RPTAG_Font` rollback native-overlay parity

`SetRPAttrsA` snapshots the font pointer, cached font metrics, and
`rp_AlgoStyle` before applying a tag list. `SetFont` publishes the selected
font and clears algorithmic style, so a later invalid `RPTAG_Font` must restore
that whole envelope; `TxSpacing` remains caller-owned state. The same
transaction is exercised through direct CopperStart dispatch and the reversible
Kickstart ROM overlay. A declined mapped call preserves D0/cycles and
tail-chains to the original resident vector, keeping the CopperSharp68k guest
layout and the host gateway on one ownership boundary.

The parity regression is
`NativeOverlayAndHostGatewayRestoreAlgoStyleWhenALaterFontTagFails`; native
font/provider rendering, CyberGraphX, and custom-chip timing are intentionally
outside this portable transaction unit.

## G01/G05/G26 RastPort attribute base alignment

`SetRPAttrsA` and `GetRPAttrsA` now reject a NULL or odd `RastPort` before
walking the guest `TagItem` chain or journaling any output. Although a host
adapter can expose byte-addressable storage at an odd address, the classic
68000 guest ABI cannot issue the WORD/LONG RastPort accesses required by these
vectors. Direct and CopperStart calls therefore preserve D0/cycles and state;
the reversible ROM overlay declines and tail-chains the original vector.

This guard is shared by the portable core and the native-overlay admission
boundary, preserving one CopperSharp68k-compatible guest layout while leaving
layer and CyberGraphX ownership explicit.

## G04/G05/G06/G26 host RastPort ownership alignment (2026-08-16)

The host gateway applies the same even, non-null RastPort rule before it asks
the layer or RTG provider to classify an object. `IsLayeredRastPort`,
`IsNonLayeredRastPort`, RTG bitmap resolution, and text-metric font probes all
reject odd bases without reading guest fields. A byte-addressable mapping can
therefore not turn a native 68000 address-error case into a provider claim.

Direct dispatch preserves D0/cycles. The reversible mapped overlay keeps the
captured native vector reachable and tail-chains its original target; no layer
ownership or damage policy is moved into graphics.library.

## G18 `OpenMonitor(NULL, INVALID_ID)` default selection

The portable monitor resolver treats a NULL monitor name with either display
ID zero or `GraphicsModeIds.Invalid` as a request for the active
jumper-selected monitor. The resident registry still owns one canonical
PAL/NTSC `MonitorSpec`, so repeated opens return the same guest object and
only increment `ms_OpenCount`; close-to-zero keeps the resident node
available for display-database discovery and later opens. Named monitors and
explicit native ModeIDs retain their existing case-insensitive and
provider-boundary rules.

The unit is implemented once in the shared guest-memory core and exercised
through the CopperStart register adapter, direct host service, and reversible
Kickstart overlay. This preserves a single CopperSharp68k-compatible
`MonitorSpec` layout while leaving RTG/CyberGraphX monitor families and
native timing ownership outside the portable path.

## G18/G22 `CloseMonitor` guest-envelope admission

`CloseMonitor` keeps the resident `MonitorSpec` open-count state, but its
non-NULL input is still a public word-aligned structure pointer. The portable
registry now rejects odd pointers and any pointer whose complete
`MonitorSpecSize` envelope would wrap the 32-bit guest address space before it
looks up the resident object or reads `ms_OpenCount`. This prevents a
byte-addressable host mapping from turning an address-error/provider request
into a claimed portable close. Valid resident handles retain the existing
zero-count residency and reopen behavior; CopperStart leaves malformed calls
unclaimed so a native CopperSharp68k body or provider can retry with the
original register and cycle frame.

The focused regression is
`CloseMonitorRejectsOddAndWrappingSpecsBeforePortableOwnership`. It exercises
the pure core and register adapter without changing the shared `MonitorSpec`
layout or the CyberGraphX/RTG ownership boundary.

## G11 multicolor `BltPattern` source-field boundary

`GraphicsRasterOperations.BltPattern` decodes negative `AreaPtSz` patterns as
declared source planes. In ordinary JAM2, the encoded color (including zero)
is the destination value, so the operation must not consume `FgPen` or
`BPen`. The portable path now classifies that form before reading either pen;
positive one-bit patterns retain their background phase, NULL inverse-video
JAM2 retains `BPen`, and JAM1/complement retain their foreground/inversion
rules. This keeps malformed or provider-owned public pen bytes from stealing
a valid multicolor blit while leaving the shared RastPort layout unchanged.

`BltPatternMulticolorJam2DepositsEncodedPlanesWithoutReadingPens` covers the
pure core and CopperStart register ABI with a two-plane, two-row pattern and
faulted pen bytes. Layered clipping/damage and CyberGraphX remain explicit
provider boundaries.

## G14 `GetRGB4` requested-field ownership

`GetRGB4` is a scalar legacy lookup over `ColorMap.Count` and the selected
`ColorTable` UWORD. The portable path therefore must not require the
`ColorMap.Type` byte or the optional V36 `LowColorBits` entry: those fields
belong to RGB32 and palette-update paths, not to the 12-bit result. Keeping
the read envelope narrow lets a future CopperSharp68k body and the host
gateway preserve native/provider ownership when an unrelated extension is
sparse, while retaining the existing instance-owned ColorMap boundary.

`GetRgb4ReadsOnlyTheRequestedColorTableWord` faults the low-nibble table and
proves the same value through the pure core and CopperStart register adapter;
RTG/CyberGraphX palette providers remain outside this portable query.

## G18 default screen ColorMap lifecycle

The standard-planar synthetic screen bridge now allocates and links a
`ColorMap` for every successful `OpenScreen` and `OpenScreenTagList`, even
when the request has no `SA_Colors`, `SA_Colors32`, `SA_ColorMapEntries`, or
`SA_VideoControl` tag. The default entry count is `max(32, 1 << depth)`, and
an explicit `SA_ColorMapEntries` value remains authoritative. The map is
attached to `ViewPort.ColorMap` and back-linked through `ColorMap.ViewPort`
before the screen is exposed to the display reconstruction boundary.

CloseScreen releases only the compatibility-owned map. Before returning its
Exec allocation, the bridge clears the public ColorMap header so a subsequent
un-cleared `AllocMem` request cannot inherit stale Type/Count/pointer fields
from the former map block. This is a host hygiene step after ownership has
already been proven; it does not clear provider-owned maps or alter the guest
layout. Failed allocation, RethinkDisplay, and provider-repointed teardown
paths retain the existing transactional rollback and decline semantics.

The rule is grounded in the classic [`OpenScreen` contract](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenScreen),
which describes the screen viewport's color map as initialized by
`graphics.library/GetColorMap()`. The mapped regression
`OpenScreenPublishesTheDefaultColorMapForEverySyntheticViewport`, the full
OpenScreen subset, and the boot-memory lifecycle class cover publication and
teardown. CyberGraphX/RTG color ownership, Layers damage, and native timing
remain explicit provider boundaries.
## G09 `GetBitMapAttr` requested-field boundary

`GetBitMapAttr` is a scalar query over the public bitmap header. The portable
implementation therefore decodes BMA_HEIGHT, BMA_DEPTH, and BMA_WIDTH from
their individual guest fields instead of requiring the complete bitmap
layout, Flags byte, and all plane links. This preserves a valid geometry query
when an unrelated tail is sparse or provider-owned. BMA_FLAGS remains a
capability query: public storage bits are returned directly when
`BMF_DISPLAYABLE` is absent, while a displayable result is retained only after
the standard-planar geometry and every plane envelope pass the existing
display-DMA checks.

`GetBitMapAttrReadsOnlyTheRequestedScalarField` proves the pure and
CopperStart register paths with faulted Flags and plane links. The guest
bitmap layout is unchanged, and RTG/CyberGraphX bitmap ownership still falls
through before this portable query.
## G15/G16 `WaitBOVP` timing-only viewport validation (2026-08-16)

`WaitBOVP` now uses a dedicated viewport validator instead of reusing the
`ScrollVPort` validator. It still requires an even, fully mapped public
`ViewPort` envelope, zero `vp_ExtendedModes`, and a readable bounded `RasInfo`
chain whenever one is present. A null `vp_RasInfo` remains valid while
Intuition/graphics is assembling a viewport because the wait boundary needs
only `vp_DHeight` and `vp_DyOffset` to schedule the vertical target. Direct
and CopperStart register calls share this rule and preserve the void D0/cycle
ABI; malformed present chains remain provider/native-owned. No guest layout,
bitmap ownership, layer clipping, or CyberGraphX/RTG policy changes.

## G15/G16 `CalcIVG` display-list field boundary (2026-08-16)

`CalcIVG(View, ViewPort)` now has a dedicated admission validator. It reads
only the aligned View link and the viewport's `vp_DspIns` longword, allowing
the display-list pointer to be NULL while a viewport is unmade or a screen is
behind another screen. It no longer reuses `ScrollVPort`'s RasInfo/geometry
validator, because the resident contract counts the display copper list and
ignores UCopIns, SprIns, and ClrIns. An odd `vp_DspIns` remains unclaimed
before a host callback, preserving the native/provider fallback boundary.

`CalcIvgAcceptsAnUnmadeViewportWithoutReadingRasInfoOrGeometry` uses sparse
guest memory to prove the narrow field access; the malformed display-list
regression, direct/register paths, and the complete 1208-test scaffold pass.
The rule is grounded in the classic
[CalcIVG autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/CalcIVG).

## G15/G16 `GetVPModeID` no-ColorMap field boundary (2026-08-16)

`GetVPModeID` now separates its no-ColorMap admission from the stricter
scroll/rebuild envelope. The portable validator reads the aligned `vp_Modes`
word, requires the standard `vp_ExtendedModes` byte, and reads `vp_RasInfo`
only to validate a chain that is actually present. It no longer requires
unrelated display geometry or a fully mapped ViewPort, so Intuition can query
an assembling ViewPort whose mode has already been published. Foreign
ColorMaps, non-standard extended modes, malformed present chains, and odd
pointers still fall through to the native/provider owner.

`GetVPModeIDAcceptsASparseModeOnlyViewportThroughDirectAndCopperStart` proves
direct and CopperStart parity with sparse guest memory; the existing map,
provider, NTSC, and malformed-envelope regressions remain green, and the full
scaffold is 1209/1209. Isolated emulator/test builds are warning-free. The
mode association contract is grounded in the classic
[GetVPModeID autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/GetVPModeID).

## G06 `Draw` source-pen ownership boundary (2026-08-16)

`Draw` now resolves `FgPen` and `BPen` lazily. The portable line walker first
classifies the patterned sample and the layer/bitmap visibility boundary; it
reads `FgPen` only for a visible source-one sample and `BPen` only for a
visible JAM2 source-zero sample. COMPLEMENT remains pen-free because the
destination minterm ignores the source colour. This lets a valid all-zero
JAM1 pattern, an entirely clipped line, or an inversion line with no public
pen dependency complete its cursor and `linpatcnt` transition without
claiming unrelated provider-owned bytes. If a required pen read fails after
the line preflight, the existing destination snapshot restores the complete
raster and guest line state.

`DrawJam1WithNoForegroundSamplesDoesNotRequireForegroundPenAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
proves the direct and CopperStart paths with a faulted `FgPen`, including the
void-vector D0/cycle contract. The source operation is the classic
[`Draw` vector](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0436.html);
the complete portable scaffold is 1210/1210, and isolated emulator/test
builds are warning-free. Layer damage/clipping and CyberGraphX/RTG remain
provider boundaries.

## G04 zero-effective-mask text ownership boundary (2026-08-17)

The portable `Text` seam now distinguishes cursor-only work from template
publication. After the RastPort mask and bitmap depth produce an effective
zero mask, the operation admits the metric-only glyph decoder and advances the
cursor without probing `tf_CharData` or ColorTextFont plane storage. The
register adapter mirrors that decision for any zero-effective-mask request.
Any selected destination plane retains the strict strike/color-font preflight and rollback
path, so this does not widen ordinary planar text or provider-owned color
rendering.

`ZeroEffectiveMaskTextUsesMetricGlyphsWithoutReadingTheStrike` proves the
pure and CopperStart paths with a guest TextFont whose scalar tables are
readable while its strike pointer is unmapped; the complete portable scaffold
is 1212/1212. The source operation is the
classic [`Text` vector](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Text); layer
damage/clipping and CyberGraphX/RTG remain explicit provider boundaries.

## G17 `ChangeVPBitMap` field ownership boundary (2026-08-17)

`ChangeVPBitMap` now preflights only the public fields needed by the bitmap
exchange: the aligned `ViewPort.RasInfo` link, its bounded RasInfo chain, the
standard-planar extended-mode byte, DBufInfo ownership, and compatible current
and replacement bitmap layouts. It no longer reuses the broader
`ScrollVPort` geometry validator, so unreadable `DWidth`, `DHeight`, offsets,
modes, and sprite-priority fields cannot steal a valid exchange from the
native/provider owner. The extended-mode byte remains an explicit standard
planar guard; RTG and scheduler callbacks retain their existing boundaries.

`ChangeViewPortBitMapReadsOnlyTheRasInfoAndBitmapExchangeFields` proves the
direct and CopperStart paths with the unrelated viewport scalar span faulted,
while the guest RasInfo association, D0/cycle frame, and display notification
remain correct; the complete portable scaffold passes 1214/1214. The field
set follows the classic
[`ChangeVPBitMap` vector](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ChangeVPBitMap).

## G17 `AllocDBufInfo` field ownership boundary (2026-08-17)

`AllocDBufInfo` now uses a focused viewport validator: it reads the aligned
`RasInfo` link, the bounded RasInfo chain, and the standard-planar
`vp_ExtendedModes` byte before capability or allocation callbacks. It no
longer requires unrelated width, height, offsets, mode, or sprite-priority
fields, while malformed chains and nonstandard extended modes remain
provider/native-owned. Direct and CopperStart allocation preserve the
allocator envelope and register ABI.

`AllocDBufInfoReadsOnlyTheRasInfoAndStandardModeFields` proves the focused
read set with the geometry span faulted; the complete portable scaffold
passes 1214/1214. The field contract follows the classic
[`AllocDBufInfo` vector](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocDBufInfo).

## G17 `ScrollVPort` offset-refresh field boundary (2026-08-17)

`ScrollVPort` now uses a dedicated admission rather than the broad viewport
geometry validator shared by mode/coercion paths. It reads the aligned
`ViewPort.RasInfo` link and standard-planar `vp_ExtendedModes`, validates the
bounded RasInfo chain (including bitmap and offset links), and then notifies
the display rebuild boundary. Width, height, viewport offsets, and mode words
remain outside this operation's ownership set because the resident vector
reinterprets RasInfo offsets after they are adjusted by the caller.

Validation: `ScrollVPortReadsOnlyTheRasInfoAndOffsetRefreshFields` passes
through direct and CopperStart dispatch; the ScrollVPort-focused subset is
11/11 and the complete portable scaffold is 1215/1215. Isolated emulator and
test-project builds remain warning-free. The field contract follows the
classic [`ScrollVPort` autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/ScrollVPort).

## G15/G16 `WaitBOVP` timing-field boundary (2026-08-17)

`WaitBOVP` now has a timing-specific admission envelope. The portable path
reads only aligned `vp_DHeight`, `vp_DyOffset`, the standard
`vp_ExtendedModes` byte, and the `vp_RasInfo` link. A null RasInfo remains a
valid assembling-viewport state; a present chain is still bounded and
structurally validated before the display wait callback is allowed to claim
the call. Unrelated ViewPort display/copper fields are no longer probed, so a
faulted `DWidth` or similar field cannot divert a valid timing wait to the
native/provider path. Direct and CopperStart register calls retain the void
D0/cycle contract. Layer damage, RTG/CyberGraphX presentation, and exact
custom-chip beam timing remain outside this portable boundary.

`WaitBovpReadsOnlyTimingFieldsBeforeItsDisplayBoundary` proves the direct and
mapped paths with `DWidth` unreadable; the WaitBOVP-focused set passes 8/8 and
the complete portable scaffold passes 1216/1216. The operation shape follows
the classic [`WaitBOVP` autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/WaitBOVP).

## G07 clear no-op field boundary (2026-08-17)

`ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` now decide zero-effective-mask ownership directly
after reading the aligned `RastPort.Mask` and the minimal bitmap header needed
to apply `bm_Depth`. When the normalized mask is zero, the portable path only
publishes the documented line-pattern reset. It does not consume text-font
geometry, `CurrentX`/`CurrentY`, public pen, draw-mode, or destination-plane
state that cannot influence a write. Nonzero masks retain the existing complete
font, signed-coordinate, work-budget, snapshot, and rollback admission.

`ClearVectorsWithZeroEffectiveMaskDoNotReadPublicPensOrGeometryAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
faults public pens and both cursor/text geometry words and passes through direct
and CopperStart dispatch; the clear-focused set is 15/15 and the complete
portable scaffold remains 1216/1216. This is a planar ownership boundary only;
layer damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and exact custom-chip timing remain provider or
native concerns.

## G12 timed blitter FIFO schedule-peek boundary (2026-08-17)

`GraphicsBlitterFifoBackend.TryPeekForSchedule` now admits a candidate only
when the queue is nonempty, no operation is already in flight, and the guest
submission cycle has arrived. If the scheduler supplies a beam predicate, a
QBS head must satisfy it; when the predicate is null, the CopperStart owner
may apply its profile-aware line/frame rule after peeking and then pass an
affirmative adapter to dequeue. FIFO order therefore keeps a blocked QBS head
in front of later ordinary requests without fabricating a beam state.

`TimedBlitterFifoSchedulePeekHonorsDueCycleBeamPredicateAndInFlightBoundary`
proves the three admission edges. This is a scheduler-owned queue boundary,
not a CyberGraphX/RTG implementation; custom-chip callback timing and display
provider ownership remain outside the portable FIFO.

## G24/G26 `GfxNew` extended-node transaction (2026-08-17)

`GfxNew` now treats the allocated public node as a guest-visible transaction.
After the allocator returns an aligned, representable span, the portable
implementation snapshots the full node envelope before clearing it and
publishing `NT_GRAPHICS`, `SS_GRAPHICS`, the subtype, and the shared
graphics-library backlink. Any failed clear or metadata write restores the
snapshot, releases the provisional public span, and leaves the registry
without a node that could be found by `GfxLookUp` or freed by `GfxFree`.

The transaction is independent of host object addresses and preserves the
shared layout required by a future CopperSharp68k implementation. Native
monitor internals, layers, and CyberGraphX/RTG associations remain outside
this guest-node ownership boundary.

## G24/G25 `NewRegion` header transaction (2026-08-17)

`NewRegion` now snapshots the complete public Region header after receiving an
aligned, representable allocation and before writing the empty bounds and
`RegionRectangle` link. If either header write sequence fails, the snapshot is
restored and the allocation is released; the graphics-instance Region registry
is still untouched because registration occurs only after successful
publication. This keeps the guest Region layout recoverable for a native 68k
owner or retry and does not claim foreign layer/provider Regions.

## G24/G26 `GfxFree` backlink teardown transaction (2026-08-17)

`GfxFree` now snapshots the owned public association LONG before clearing it.
If the guest memory adapter rejects a later byte of that clear, the complete
original backlink is restored and the registry/allocation remain live. Only a
successful clear removes the node and all stale lookup entries before freeing
the public span. This keeps partial guest publication from crossing the
native/provider boundary and preserves the shared extended-node layout for a
future CopperSharp68k implementation.

`GfxFreeRestoresTheGuestBacklinkWhenItsLateClearFails` passes the injected
third-byte failure and retry path; the focused `GfxFree` filter passes 1/1,
and the complete portable scaffold passes 1220/1220. The isolated emulator
and test-project builds remain warning-free.

## G24/G26 `GfxAssociate` backlink publication transaction (2026-08-17)

`GfxAssociate` now snapshots the target node's public backlink and, when a
pointer is already associated, the displaced node's backlink before writing
either field. A late byte failure restores every changed LONG and leaves the
registry unchanged; only a complete pair of guest publications updates the
lookup map. This keeps the guest association layout atomic for direct,
CopperStart, and future CopperSharp68k owners while foreign/provider nodes
remain unclaimed.

`GraphicsExtendedNodeAssociationRestoresPartialBacklinkWrites` covers both
the new-node partial write and displaced-node partial clear. The focused
association set passes 2/2, and the complete portable scaffold passes
1221/1221.

## G16 `FreeVPortCopLists` byte-rollback transaction (2026-08-17)

`FreeVPortCopLists` now snapshots each public copper link as a complete byte
span while retaining the native LONG-read admission. If clearing any link
fails after partial publication, rollback writes the saved bytes directly,
rather than retrying a failing LONG operation. This preserves all four guest
links for a native/provider teardown retry, including sparse ViewPort tails;
display-resource ownership and hardware deallocation remain explicit backend
responsibilities.

`FreeVPortCopListsRestoresLinksAfterAPartialLongWrite` covers partial
publication and successful retry; the focused FreeVPortCopLists set passes
9/9.

## G14 `AttachPalExtra` allocation/publication transaction (2026-08-17)

`AttachPalExtra` now snapshots the ColorMap PaletteExtra backlink and the
complete newly allocated PaletteExtra, reference-count, and allocation-list
spans before clearing or publishing metadata. Any late semaphore/list/link
failure restores those guest bytes, leaves the ColorMap registry allocation
unattached, and releases the provisional public spans. A later attach can
retry cleanly without changing the palette lock or RTG/CyberGraphX boundary.

`AttachPalExtraRestoresAllocatedEnvelopesWhenTheFinalLinkWriteIsPartial`
covers the partial final-link publication and successful retry; the focused
AttachPalExtra set passes 4/4.

## G14 `GetColorMap` allocation/publication transaction (2026-08-17)

`GetColorMap` now captures the public ColorMap, ColorTable, and LowColorBits
spans before clearing or publishing their links. A late initialization failure
restores all guest bytes, frees every provisional allocation, and leaves the
registry without a partially visible map. Fresh sparse spans retain the
write-first admission used by the host allocator, while readable reused spans
are restored exactly for a native/provider retry.

`GetColorMapRestoresAllGuestEnvelopesWhenMapPublicationFails` covers partial
publication and successful retry; the focused GetColorMap set passes 2/2.

## G14 `SyncPaletteExtra` sidecar publication transaction (2026-08-17)

`SyncPaletteExtra` now snapshots the complete guest PaletteExtra header plus
its reference-count and allocation-list spans before publishing derived list
heads and WORD entries. A partial write restores all three spans and returns a
failure without losing the host shadow state, so a later pen operation can
retry. The AttachPalExtra call opts into deterministic zero rollback for
freshly allocated write-first spans; established sidecars must remain readable
before this portable path claims them. Exec semaphore scheduling, resident
provider behavior, and CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remain outside the envelope.

`ObtainPenRestoresPaletteSidecarsAfterAPartialSyncWrite` covers partial
publication and successful retry; the focused ObtainPen set passes 5/5.

## G22/G26 native graphics-base rebind transaction (2026-08-17)

Native-base cutover now journals the byte spans for every extended-node
`xln_Lib` backlink and resident MonitorList field before moving publication.
If a `LONG` write fails after partial publication, the currently failing field
and all earlier fields are restored byte-wise; the registry keeps the previous
base and can retry the cutover. The shared guest layout remains suitable for a
future CopperSharp68k resident body, while provider-owned monitor lists and
CyberGraphX/RTG state remain outside the portable transaction.

`NativeGraphicsBaseRebindRestoresBacklinksAfterAPartialLongWrite` covers the
failure and retry paths; the focused rebind set passes 8/8.

## G18/G22 `OpenMonitor` native-list publication transaction (2026-08-17)

`OpenMonitor` now journals every public MonitorList LONG touched by resident
publication before linking a new MonitorSpec. If a list write is partially
accepted, all list fields—including the currently failing field—and the
provisional MonitorSpec are restored byte-wise before the allocation is
released. Compact images retain their host-only path, and foreign/provider
monitor lists remain unclaimed.

`OpenMonitorRestoresNativeListAfterAPartialLongPublication` covers the failed
publication and successful retry.

## G22/G26 native display-database sidecar transaction (2026-08-17)

`TryCreateNativeDatabase` now snapshots the complete allocated public sidecar
before clearing and writing its header and mode records. If a sparse/native
adapter partially accepts a `LONG`, the original bytes are restored before
freeing the provisional block, so a subsequent CopperSharp68k or CopperScreen
publication sees the same guest envelope and the GfxBase APTR remains null.
Provider-owned display databases and CyberGraphX/RTG records remain outside
this portable sidecar transaction.

`NativeDisplayDatabaseRestoresItsGuestEnvelopeAfterPartialInitialization`
covers the failed write and retry path.

## G17/G25 `ChangeVPBitMap` publication transaction (2026-08-17)

The portable bitmap-exchange path now snapshots the four-byte
`RasInfo.BitMap` association after the existing RasInfo/DBufInfo/layout
admission and before the guest replacement write. A partial or failed LONG is
rolled back byte-wise, leaving the original bitmap link available for a later
display-boundary retry. The transaction does not claim DBufInfo message
ordering, presentation timing, layer state, or CyberGraphX/RTG surfaces.

`ChangeVPBitMapRestoresTheOldRasInfoPointerAfterPartialLongPublication`
covers the failure and clean retry path.

## G15/G25 native LoadView sidecar transaction (2026-08-17)

Native LoadView sidecars now use byte snapshots for same-value writability
probes and byte-wise restoration for ActiView, CurrentMonitor, and TopLine.
If a later active-view or monitor-tail publication partially commits, the
complete prior guest values are restored before the display owner can observe
an inconsistent View. A declined status-aware handoff follows the same
byte-restore path; portable view topology, presentation scheduling, and
CyberGraphX/RTG remain separate ownership domains.

`LoadViewRestoresNativeActiveViewAfterPartialCommitPublication` covers the
partial commit and retry path.

## G14/G25 ColorMap WORD update transaction (2026-08-17)

`TryApplyColorMapUpdates` now restores ColorTable and LowColorBits entries
byte-wise after a failed high/low WORD sequence. This handles adapters that
partially publish a WORD and then reject the same WORD during rollback, while
preserving reserved high nibbles and the existing pen/palette ownership
boundary. RGB4/RGB32 setters remain transactional without claiming provider
palette callbacks or CyberGraphX/RTG surfaces.

`SetRgb32CmRestoresTheLowWordAfterARejectedPartialWordWrite` covers the
partial low-word failure and clean retry.

## G20/G21/G25 `AddBob` publication transaction (2026-08-17)

`GraphicsAnimationOperations.AddBob` now restores Bob flags, VSprite flags,
and the `VSprite.VSBob` owner backlink with independent byte writes when
initial admission or GELS insertion fails. A partial guest WORD/LONG cannot
leave a Bob linked with mixed system state; SAVEBOB raster restoration,

separate boundaries.

`AddBobRestoresBobFlagsAfterARejectedPartialWordPublication` covers the

## G20/G21/G25 `RemIBob` teardown transaction (2026-08-17)

`GraphicsAnimationOperations.RemIBob` now restores Bob flags, the VSprite
owner backlink, and every reciprocal GELS link with byte writes when a late
teardown publication fails. This keeps a removed Bob fully retryable even when

`RemIBobRestoresLinksAfterARejectedPartialBobFlagWrite` covers the partial
teardown and retry path.

## AddAnimOb chain rollback

`GraphicsAnimationOperations.RestorePointers` now restores its journaled
AnimOb chain LONGs one byte at a time. A guest bridge that partially publishes
an AnimOb link and then rejects repeated LONG writes therefore returns the

fails. Component timer/head publication and provider animation ownership stay
outside this pointer-rollback helper.

## AdvanceAnimOb rollback

`GraphicsAnimationOperations.AdvanceAnimOb` now restores OldX, OldY, X, Y,

accepts the first WORD publication but rejects a repeated WORD rollback;

`AnimateRestoresAdvanceWordsAfterARejectedRepeatedWordRollback` covers the
failed frame and retry path.

## UpdateComponent rollback

`GraphicsAnimationOperations.UpdateComponent` now restores the active

`GraphicsGelsOperations.RestoreLongs` now restores each journaled reciprocal

## SetCollision rollback

`GraphicsGelsOperations.SetCollision` now restores a failed collision-table

unchanged.

`SetCollisionRestoresTheRoutinePointerAfterARejectedRepeatedLongRollback`

## AddVSprite flags rollback

`GraphicsGelsOperations.AddVSprite` now restores the VSprite flags WORD with

system/user-flag update cannot survive a repeated WORD rejection, while the

`AddVSpriteRestoresFlagsAfterARejectedRepeatedWordRollback` covers the failed
flags publication and retry path.

The bob-less branch of `GraphicsAnimationOperations.UpdateComponent` now
restores its active Timer WORD byte-wise when the timer publication fails. A

`AnimateRestoresAStaticComponentTimerAfterARejectedRepeatedWordRollback`

`GraphicsSpriteOperations.ChangeSprite` now restores the SimpleSprite
POS/CTL image pointer byte-wise after a failed image publication. The

`SimpleSpriteChangeRestoresTheImagePointerAfterARejectedRepeatedLongRollback`
covers the failed pointer publication and retry path.

## Queued blitter link rollback

`GraphicsBlitterFifoBackend.TryEnqueueLinked` now restores the original
system-owned `BltNode.bn_Next` bytes when the first node termination fails, as
well as when a later tail link fails. Queue admission remains atomic with
guest-link publication; FIFO/beam scheduling and callback execution stay at
the scheduler/native boundary.

`PortableQueuedBlitterRestoresTheFirstNodeLinkAfterARejectedPartialLongWrite`
covers the failed first-node publication and retry path.

## BitMapScale extent rollback

`GraphicsBitmapUtilityOperations.BitMapScale` now restores staged destination
width and height WORDs byte-wise before restoring the destination bitmap
snapshot. A later extent or pixel-stage failure cannot leave one extent field
half-published, while planar sampling and provider/RTG admission remain
unchanged.

`BitMapScaleRestoresExtentAfterARejectedRepeatedWordRollback` covers the
failed extent publication and retry path.

## PaletteExtra semaphore rollback

PaletteExtra acquisition now restores the newly published semaphore owner
LONG byte-wise when nest-count publication fails. This prevents a task ID
with a nonzero low byte from surviving a failed acquisition while preserving
contention, re-entry, and native Exec/provider ownership behavior.

`PaletteSemaphoreRestoresOwnerAfterARejectedNestPublicationRollback` covers
the failed acquisition and retry path.

## ViewPort copper-link rollback

`GraphicsLibraryCore.RestoreViewPortCopperLinks` now restores each of the four
public ViewPort copper links byte-wise after MakeVPort, MrgCop, or
FreeVPortCopLists crosses a status-aware display boundary and is declined.
The handoff keeps visible/hidden viewport filtering and native/provider screen
ownership unchanged.

`FreeVPortCopListsRestoresLinksAfterAStatusDeclineRejectsRepeatedLongRollback`
covers the status decline and retry path.

## Temporary ViewPortExtra transfer rollback

`GraphicsLibraryCore.GfxAssociate` now snapshots a temporary ViewPortExtra's
VPXF_FREE_ME marker before clearing it for caller ownership. A failed or
partially accepted clear restores both marker bytes before the association can
be retried; MakeVPort allocation and ViewPortExtra ownership rules remain
unchanged.

`GfxAssociateRestoresTemporaryFreeMeFlagAfterARejectedPartialWordWrite`
covers the failed transfer and retry path.

## PaletteExtra semaphore release rollback

`ExitPaletteSemaphore` now restores the original nest count when a decrement
fails and restores both owner and nest bytes when the final owner clear is
rejected. Release-side failures therefore leave a consistent re-enterable
semaphore instead of an owner-with-zero-nest state.

`PaletteSemaphoreRestoresOwnerAndNestAfterARejectedReleaseLong` covers the
failed release and retry path.

## ExtSprite unassigned-pair rollback

`GraphicsSpriteOperations.GetExtSpriteA` now journals the public SimpleSprite
number fields when an automatic attached-pair allocation fails. Both sentinel
WORDs are published together; if the second write is partially accepted or
rejected, both caller-owned numbers are restored byte-wise so the pair remains
consistent and retryable. Hardware reservation, attached-pair control bits,
and the optional display/provider sprite boundary remain unchanged.

`ExtendedSpriteGetRestoresBothUnassignedNumbersAfterARejectedPairWrite`
covers the exhausted-pool failure and retry path.

## SimpleSprite unassigned-number rollback

The single-sprite `GetSprite` failure marker now uses the same byte-wise
publication journal as attached ExtSprite pairs. A partially accepted or
rejected sentinel WORD restores the caller-owned `SimpleSprite.num`; a normal
successful failure still publishes `0xFFFF`, and pool ownership/retry behavior
is unchanged.

`SimpleSpriteGetRestoresTheUnassignedNumberAfterARejectedWordWrite` covers the
failed marker publication and retry path.

## Native display-database APTR rollback

`GraphicsLibraryCore.TryPublishNativeDisplayDatabase` now restores the
`GfxBase.DisplayInfoDataBase` APTR byte-wise when a sidecar pointer `LONG` is
partially accepted or rejected. The newly initialized sidecar is released only
after the public field returns to its original value, keeping native 68k
rebind/retry behavior coherent while provider-owned nonzero APTRs remain
untouched.

`NativeDisplayDatabaseRestoresTheGfxBasePointerAfterPartialPublication`
covers the failed pointer publication and retry path.

## ExtSprite allocation envelope rollback

`GraphicsSpriteOperations.AllocSpriteDataA` now captures the complete
caller-visible ExtSprite envelope and generated CHIP image before clearing or
publishing them. Any late clear, data write, or registry failure restores both
byte-wise before releasing the allocations. This keeps recycled guest spans
retryable while leaving display-DMA admission and provider/native ownership
boundaries unchanged.

`ExtendedSpriteAllocationRestoresRecycledEnvelopesAfterLatePublicationFailure`
covers the partial image-pointer publication and clean retry path.

## UCopperList internal-buffer rollback

`GraphicsCopperOperations.TryAllocateBlock` now captures the complete public
CopList and instruction-buffer spans before clearing or initializing them. A
partial CopList pointer or metadata write restores both buffers byte-wise
before release, keeping UCopperListInit and lazy CBump growth retryable without
changing copper scheduling or native merge ownership.

`UCopperListInitRestoresInternalBuffersAfterRejectedInitializationPointer`
covers the failed internal publication and clean retry path.

## UCopperList owner-publication rollback

The UCopperList transaction now retains each newly initialized block's
pre-call bytes until the caller-owned `UCopList` links are committed. If a
late owner-link write fails, the user envelope and both internal public
buffers are restored before release; successful registry admission discards
the journal. Lazy `CBump` growth follows the same commit/discard split.

`UCopperListInitRestoresInternalBuffersWhenOwnerPublicationFailsLate` covers
the failed owner publication and clean retry path.

## ExtendFont extension-envelope rollback

`GraphicsMemoryFontBackend.TryExtend` now snapshots the recycled
`TextFontExtension` allocation and the font's extension/style fields before
publishing a tagged extension. Any failed metadata, backlink, or style write
restores those guest bytes before freeing the extension, keeping the font
lifecycle retryable without changing the classic extension layout or native
font-list ownership.

`ExtendFontRestoresRecycledExtensionAfterPartialBacklinkPublication` covers
the partial backlink failure and clean retry path.

## StripFont backlink rollback

`GraphicsMemoryFontBackend.TryStrip` now snapshots the public extension and
style fields before detaching an owned extension. A partial or repeatedly
rejected backlink LONG restores both fields byte-wise, leaving ownership and
the extension allocation intact for a later retry; successful detachment
continues to release only the backend-owned extension.

`StripFontRestoresTheExtensionPointerAfterRejectedRepeatedLongRollback`
covers the failed detach and clean retry path.

## AddFont field rollback

`GraphicsMemoryFontBackend.TryAdd` now snapshots `tf_Accessors`, the font-node
type byte, and font flags before clearing/publishing registration state. A
partial WORD or later guest-list/provider rejection restores all three fields
byte-wise, preventing a half-registered resident font while preserving the
native font-list ownership boundary.

`FontRegistrationRestoresAccessorAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers
the failed registration and clean retry path.

## CloseFont accessor rollback

`GraphicsMemoryFontBackend.TryClose` now snapshots `tf_Accessors` before the
decrement and restores it byte-wise if the decrement, final removal, or
extension teardown fails. The accessor count therefore remains authoritative
through repeated-WORD bridges while native font-list and provider ownership
remain unchanged.

`CloseFontRestoresAccessorAfterRejectedRepeatedWordRollback` covers the failed
close and clean retry path.

## RemFont accessor publication journal

`RemFont` first snapshots the resident `tf_Accessors` bytes. If removal has to
fall back through `AddFont` because an owned extension cannot be stripped, the
fallback's accessor reset is followed by byte-wise restoration of the original
open count. This preserves a retryable public font state across adapters that
reject repeated WORD writes while leaving native and guest list ownership at
their existing boundaries.

`RemFontRestoresAccessorAfterRejectedRepeatedWordRollback` and
`RemFontRestoresAvailabilityWhenFallbackAddFontDeclines` cover partial
detach, repeated-WORD/fallback rejection, restoration, and retry sequences.

## OpenFont accessor increment journal

Before `OpenFont` publishes a new accessor count, the portable font lifecycle
backend captures the resident `tf_Accessors` bytes. If the increment WORD is
partially accepted or rejected, byte-wise restoration leaves the selected
font unchanged and available for a later retry; a successful increment keeps
the existing CloseFont lifecycle semantics.

`OpenFontRestoresAccessorAfterRejectedIncrementWord` covers the observable
`0x00ff → 0x0100` boundary, failed-open restoration, and retry/decrement.

## SetFont RastPort publication journal

`SetFont` treats the selected font pointer, `AlgoStyle`, and cached
`TxHeight`/`TxWidth`/`TxBaseline` fields as one guest-visible transaction. The
portable path snapshots each field before writing the new cache and restores
the captured bytes independently when a later write fails. This matters for
68000-compatible adapters that accept part of the font-pointer `LONG` and
then reject a repeated `LONG` during rollback; `TxSpacing` remains outside
the transaction as caller-owned state. A successful commit keeps the existing
CopperSharp68k-compatible layout and provider/native decline boundary.

`SetFontRestoresTheOldFontPointerAfterRejectedPartialLongPublication` covers
partial pointer publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes
1261/1261.

## Move fresh-line publication journal

`Move` treats the current X/Y cursor words, line-pattern count, and
`FRST_DOT` flags as one guest-visible fresh-line transaction. On a partial or
rejected cursor/phase/flag publication, each captured field is restored
byte-wise, so a bridge that rejects a repeated WORD cannot expose a half-moved
RastPort. The existing read-faulting cursor exception remains transparent to
native/provider ownership, while successful calls retain the classic
`linpatcnt = 15` and `FRST_DOT` state.

`MoveRestoresTheOldCursorAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial
cursor publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes
1262/1262.

## SetABPenDrMd Flags publication journal

`SetABPenDrMd` publishes three pen/mode bytes, the regenerated minterm cache,
the fresh line phase, and the `NoPens` Flags bit as one RastPort transaction.
If the final Flags WORD accepts only part of its value or is rejected, the
original Flags bytes are restored independently; the existing byte-wise
minterm and scalar rollback remains intact. This keeps the public state
retryable without changing the CopperSharp68k layout or taking ownership from
a native/provider implementation.

`SetABPenDrMdRestoresFlagsAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial
Flags publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1263/1263.

## SetOutlinePen Flags publication journal

`SetOutlinePen` publishes the outline pen and area-outline Flags bit as one
guest-visible operation. If the final Flags WORD is partially accepted or
rejected, the original Flags bytes are restored independently after restoring
the previous pen. This preserves the documented previous-pen result and the
native/provider ownership boundary without changing the shared RastPort
layout.

`SetOutlinePenRestoresFlagsAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial
Flags publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1264/1264.

## SetAfPt area-pattern publication journal

`SetAfPt` publishes the area-pattern APTR and signed pattern-size byte as one
