guest-visible macro transaction. A partial or rejected APTR LONG is restored
byte-wise before the size field is restored, preventing a recycled or
provider-backed bridge from exposing a mixed pointer/size pair. The shared
guest layout and native/provider ownership boundary remain unchanged.

`SetAfPtRestoresTheOldPointerAfterRejectedPartialLongPublication` covers
partial APTR publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes
1265/1265.

## SetDrPt line-pattern publication journal

`SetDrPt` publishes `LinePtrn`, `FRST_DOT` in `Flags`, and `linpatcnt` as one
guest-visible fresh-line transaction. If either WORD accepts only a prefix or
is rejected, the original pattern and Flags bytes are restored independently;
the phase byte then restores as before. This keeps line drawing retryable
without changing the shared RastPort layout or native/provider ownership.

`SetDrPtRestoresPatternAndFlagsAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers
partial line-pattern publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold
passes 1266/1266.

## SetOPen Flags publication journal

`SetOPen` publishes AOlPen followed by the area-outline Flags bit as one
guest-visible macro transaction. If the final Flags WORD is partially
accepted or rejected, the original Flags bytes are restored independently
after restoring the pen byte. The shared RastPort layout and native/provider
ownership boundary remain unchanged.

`SetOPenRestoresFlagsAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial Flags
publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1267/1267.

## BoundaryOff Flags publication journal

`BoundaryOff` publishes only the area-outline bit in the Flags WORD. If the
write accepts a prefix or is rejected, the original Flags bytes are restored
independently, preserving unrelated raster state and a retryable macro
boundary without changing the shared layout or provider ownership.

`BoundaryOffRestoresFlagsAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial
Flags publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1268/1268.

## Text cursor publication journal

`Text` publishes its final CurrentX, `linpatcnt`, and `FRST_DOT` Flags state as
one guest-visible operation. If the cursor or Flags WORD accepts only a
prefix or is rejected, the original fields are restored byte-wise before the
captured planar pixels are restored. This preserves cursor clipping and the
native/provider boundary while keeping Text retryable.

`TextRestoresCursorAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial cursor
publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1269/1269.

## Shared pen/mode Flags publication journal

`SetByteAndRestartPattern` publishes the requested pen or draw-mode byte,
derived minterms, `linpatcnt`, and Flags as one RastPort transition. If the
final Flags WORD accepts only a prefix or is rejected, the original Flags
bytes are restored independently along with the scalar and minterm fields.
This keeps all three classic setters retryable without changing provider
ownership or the shared guest layout.

`SetAPenRestoresFlagsAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial Flags
publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1270/1270.

## Draw cursor publication journal

`Draw` snapshots the raster destination and the current line state before
publishing its final cursor. If CurrentX, CurrentY, or Flags accepts only a
prefix or is rejected, the state fields are restored byte-wise before the
pixel snapshot is unwound. This keeps connected lines retryable without
changing the native/provider boundary.

`DrawRestoresCursorAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial cursor
publication, pixel rollback, and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes
1271/1271.

## PolyDraw cursor publication journal

`PolyDraw` nests the Draw transaction for each connected segment and keeps a
second aggregate snapshot for the whole point stream. If a nested or final
cursor/Flags WORD is partially accepted or rejected, the outer journal restores
CurrentX, CurrentY, and Flags byte-wise before restoring the aggregate pixels.
This preserves classic connected-line retry behavior and the native/provider
boundary.

`PolyDrawRestoresCursorAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers partial
cursor publication, pixel rollback, and retry; the complete graphics scaffold
passes 1272/1272.

## AreaEnd outline-state publication journal

AreaEnd keeps an outer journal around the fill and optional outline pass. If a
nested outline operation partially publishes or rejects CurrentX, CurrentY, or
Flags, the outer rollback restores those fields byte-wise before releasing
temporary raster state. This preserves area collector retryability and the
native/provider boundary.

`AreaEndRestoresOutlineCursorAfterRejectedPartialWordPublication` covers
partial cursor publication and retry; the complete graphics scaffold passes
1273/1273.

## InitView default-origin publication journal

`InitView` clears the caller-owned View and then publishes the classic default
vertical and horizontal display origins. The clear and both WORD writes form
one initialization transaction: if a guest-memory bridge publishes a prefix
of the second origin and rejects the call, the original View envelope is
restored byte-wise. No half-default origin is exposed to a future
CopperSharp68k body or native/provider owner, and the same guest object can be
retried after the bridge recovers.

`InitViewRestoresGuestBytesAfterPartialDefaultOriginPublication` covers the
partial publication, byte-for-byte rollback, and clean retry; the complete
graphics scaffold passes 1274/1274.

## OpenMonitor shared-count publication journal

The resident PAL/NTSC MonitorSpec is shared across OpenMonitor calls. Its
`ms_OpenCount` increment is now journaled as a guest WORD: the original bytes
are captured before publication, and a rejected or prefix-accepted increment is
restored byte-wise. This keeps the monitor registry's logical reference count
aligned with the guest envelope and leaves the same resident object retryable
for a native/provider bridge that recovers.

`OpenMonitorRestoresOpenCountAfterPartialWordPublication` covers partial count
publication, byte-for-byte rollback, clean retry, and balanced close; the
complete graphics scaffold passes 1275/1275.

## CloseMonitor shared-count publication journal

CloseMonitor now journals the resident MonitorSpec `ms_OpenCount` WORD before
decrementing it (including the final transition to zero). A partial or rejected
WORD is restored byte-wise, preserving the logical reference and resident-list
object for a retry. Successful zeroing still leaves the resident MonitorSpec
available to DTAG_MNTR and later OpenMonitor calls.

`CloseMonitorRestoresOpenCountAfterPartialWordPublication` covers partial count
publication, byte-for-byte rollback, clean retry, and balanced close; the
complete graphics scaffold passes 1276/1276.

## Native display-database teardown ownership journal

The portable provider keeps a private native display-database sidecar and
publishes its address through `GfxBase.DisplayInfoDataBase`. Release and
native-base rebind now use one byte-wise clear helper: snapshot the owned APTR,
attempt the guest LONG clear, and restore the original bytes if the bridge
rejects or prefix-accepts the operation. The sidecar is freed only after the
clear commits, so a half-cleared field cannot leave a dangling guest pointer.

`NativeDisplayDatabaseReleaseRestoresThePointerAfterPartialClear` covers the
failure/retry boundary; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1277/1277.

## Optional MonitorSpec name publication journal

ModeID-based OpenMonitor creates a shared canonical name string as a
best-effort extension. Before publishing its APTR into `MonitorSpec.NodeName`,
the portable registry snapshots the four guest bytes. A rejected or
prefix-accepted LONG restores that field byte-wise and then releases only a
newly allocated name, leaving a valid resident MonitorSpec with a null name.

`OpenMonitorRestoresNodeNameAfterPartialOptionalNamePublication` covers the
failure boundary; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1278/1278.

## Displaced temporary ViewPortExtra cleanup journal

`MakeVPort` may own a temporary `ViewPortExtra` until a caller explicitly
associates another node. If the old node's immediate `GfxFree` crosses a
guest-memory bridge that accepts a prefix and declines, the temporary marker
remains pending instead of being discarded. `FreeVPortCopLists` searches
pending temporary ownership by viewport, retries the displaced node, and only
removes the marker after `GfxFree` commits; the active caller-owned association
is never replaced during cleanup.

`GfxAssociateRetriesDisplacedTemporaryViewPortExtraCleanup` covers the
failure/retry boundary; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1279/1279.

## Temporary ViewPortExtra marker read boundary

Before transferring a temporary `ViewPortExtra`, `GfxAssociate` must read the
private `VPXF_FREE_ME` word. A failed read is now a pure decline: no zero is
published and the temporary association remains eligible for a later retry.
Only after a successful read does the existing zero-and-rollback transfer
transaction run.

`GfxAssociateLeavesTemporaryFreeMeFlagUntouchedWhenItCannotReadIt` covers the
read-failure boundary; the complete graphics scaffold passes 1280/1280.

## G17/G26 Native GfxBase field-address overflow closure

The AmigaBoot screen/view bridge now routes optional native `GfxBase` fields
through one checked address helper backed by `CanAddressField`. A discovered
base remains word-aligned before probing, and the complete field span must fit
inside the 32-bit guest address space before `ActiView` or `ChipRevBits0` is
read or published. This keeps the CopperSharp68k/native path authoritative for
malformed high bases and prevents a wrapped host calculation from reaching an
unrelated low-memory overlay. The same boundary is used when CloseScreen
reconciles guest ownership and when OpenScreen checks whether the synthetic
screen is already active.

`LoadViewNullRejectsWrappedNativeActiViewFieldBeforeLowAliasProbe` is the
regression contract: a base of `0xFFFF_FFE0` would otherwise map
`GfxBase->ActiView` at address `2`; the host must preserve that sentinel and
queue the actual blank handoff. `CloseScreenRefusesWrappedNativeActiViewReconciliationBeforeTeardown`
proves the same envelope refuses synthetic
screen teardown while the malformed owner is still unresolved. This is a
lifecycle envelope guard, not a CyberGraphX/RTG policy; provider/native owners
remain responsible for their own malformed structures.

## Synthetic Screen ViewPort query boundary

`GetSyntheticScreenViewPortAddress` is a guest-facing query, not a generic
host-object accessor. `EnsureSyntheticScreen` can return its reset-scoped
host-only sentinel when a public Screen envelope is unavailable. The query now
requires the real `_syntheticScreenAddress` to be live and checks the complete
embedded `ViewPort` span with `CanAddressField` before adding `Screen.ViewPort`.
Rejected or wrapped envelopes return NULL, so a CopperSharp68k/native caller
can retain ownership and no odd low-memory alias is exposed. CyberGraphX keeps
its independent RTG surface/provider path.

`SyntheticScreenViewportQueryDoesNotTurnHostOnlyScreenFailureIntoLowAlias`
locks the failure contract by forcing the staged configuration rejection and
checking that the query declines instead of returning sentinel + `$2c`.

## NewScreen optional-field envelope

The mandatory NewScreen prefix is word-aligned and address-checked before the
legacy configuration path reads it. Optional `Font` and `DefaultTitle` fields
sit beyond that prefix, so each is now admitted only when its complete LONG
span fits the 32-bit guest address space. `OpenScreenTagList` applies the same
rule to `ExtNewScreen` and legacy-title inspection. A high but otherwise
readable prefix can therefore remain available to native Intuition without
letting a wrapped address consume unrelated low memory; this is independent of
the CyberGraphX provider boundary.

`OpenScreenDoesNotReadWrappedNewScreenOptionalFieldsThroughLowAliases` uses a
`0xfffffff0` prefix and a valid low-alias title to prove the optional field is
not staged by the compatibility owner.

## Screen-data and QueryOverscan destination envelope

`GetSyntheticScreenData` now checks the complete source and destination spans
with `CanAddressField` before copying the requested Screen prefix.
`QuerySyntheticOverscan` requires an even Rectangle pointer and a complete
eight-byte envelope before publishing its four WORDs. This keeps the
CopperSharp68k/native screen bridge inside the guest address space; malformed
buffers remain available to native Intuition/provider code, and CyberGraphX
ownership is unchanged.

`GetScreenDataRejectsWrappedDestinationBeforeCopyingThroughLowMemory` and
`QueryOverscanRejectsOddAndWrappedRectangleEnvelopes` lock the D0/auxiliary
register and low-alias preservation contract.

## Native OpenWindow mandatory-prefix envelope

The synthetic Intuition bridge now applies `CanAddressField` to the complete
mandatory `NewWindow` prefix before reading any public field. A mapped high
base is therefore not enough to claim the compatibility owner when the Type
WORD or preceding fields would wrap through address zero. The request declines
with its caller state and window chain intact, leaving native Intuition or a
provider to handle the structure. This is a lifecycle ownership guard and does
not alter CyberGraphX/RTG policy.

`OpenWindowDeclinesWrappedNewWindowEnvelopeBeforeLowAliasReads` proves that a
wrapped Type address cannot consume a low-memory alias and that a later null
request still retries the compatibility window. The focused OpenWindow
lifecycle family is the regression boundary for this host/native seam.

## AddGList Window/Gadget admission

`AddGList` now uses the same optional full-Window validator as teardown and
query vectors before forwarding a caller-owned Window to the compatibility
owner. The AmigaBoot callback also checks the complete Window and Gadget spans
before publishing its private gadget link or writing `Window.FirstGadget`.
Malformed high pointers therefore remain native/provider-owned and cannot
partially update the host session. The optional validator remains unset for
memory-only/native providers that own their own structure policy.

`AddGListRejectsWrappedWindowBeforeCallbackPublication` locks the D0/cycle and
callback-decline boundary through the Intuition gateway.

## SetWindowTitles byte-string admission

`SetWindowTitles` keeps its classic byte-addressed title arguments, but the
compatibility reader treats the bounded C-string scan as a guest-memory
transaction. NULL and `NoTitleChange` remain valid sentinels. Every other byte
is checked for a non-wrapping address and mapped visibility before it is read;
a non-terminated string that would cross `$FFFF_FFFF` declines without
changing the Screen title or repainting the synthetic title bar. This leaves
malformed strings to the native/provider owner while retaining the existing
CopperSharp68k-compatible public layout.

## ShowTitle nested-title admission

`ShowTitle` is a Screen lifecycle mutation, so the synthetic owner now reads
and validates the public `Screen.Title` APTR before it changes `Screen.Flags`
or redraws the title bar. The same bounded byte-string rule used by
`SetWindowTitles` applies: NULL and `NoTitleChange` are legal, while a
non-terminated pointer that would cross `$FFFF_FFFF` declines before any
publication. This keeps nested title storage outside the host claim when it is
malformed and leaves the CopperSharp68k/native owner available.

## CloseScreen visible-write admission

CloseScreen owns a compatibility ViewPort only while its public copper-link
fields can be inspected and cleared by the guest bus. The write-admission
query therefore follows visible mapping order: a newest read-only image/ROM
overlay masks an older writable chip/fast range. The ViewPort DspIns/SprIns/
ClrIns/UCopIns slots and the compatibility View LOF/SHF CPR slots must all be
writable before the active View is blanked or the CPR wrapper is released.

If any slot is readable but not writable, the synthetic owner declines without
mutating the Screen, GfxBase->ActiView, public copper links, or compatibility
registry. A native Intuition/provider owner can remove the overlay or detach
the link and retry; CyberGraphX remains a separate provider boundary.

`CloseScreenRefusesWhenViewportCopperSlotIsReadOnlyBeforeOwnershipRelease`
locks this failure/rollback edge and verifies that a second OpenScreen request
still observes the original compatibility claim.

## MakeVPort publication admission

`TryBuildViewPortCopperList` is a replacement transaction for a ViewPort's
display copper stream. Before it allocates a raw list or retires an existing
CPR wrapper, it now checks the visible writable spans of `View.ViewPort`,
`View.LOFCPRlist`, `View.SHFCprList`, and `ViewPort.DspIns`. This follows the
guest bus's newest-overlay precedence, so a readable ROM/image overlay cannot
be mistaken for writable standard-planar ownership.

A declined admission leaves the prior CPR registry, DspIns, and View links
untouched. A native Intuition/provider owner can remove the overlay and retry;
the CopperSharp68k-compatible structure layout and CyberGraphX boundary do not
change.

`MakeVPortDeclinesReadOnlyViewPublicationBeforeRetiringCopper` verifies that a
read-only `View.LOFCPRlist` overlay declines before the old copper wrapper is
retired or a replacement DspIns is published.

## SetWindowTitles visible-publication admission

The title-string envelope is only the first half of `SetWindowTitles`. For a
non-`NoTitleChange` Screen title, the synthetic owner now admits the complete
public `Screen.Title` LONG as a visible writable guest span before logging,
repainting, or advancing the host display boundary. A readable ROM/image
overlay therefore leaves the existing title pointer and caller frame intact.

NULL and `NoTitleChange` retain their classic sentinel behavior, including the
window-title-only repaint path. A native Intuition/provider owner can remove a
read-only overlay and retry; CyberGraphX remains outside this standard-planar
compatibility contract.

`SetWindowTitlesRefusesReadOnlyScreenTitleBeforeRepaint` locks the decline
boundary and verifies that the stable title, D0, and cycles survive.

## ShowTitle visible-flag admission

`ShowTitle` mutates the public `Screen.Flags` WORD before the optional title
bar repaint. The synthetic bridge now requires that complete WORD to be a
visible writable guest span after the Screen.Title envelope and nested string
have been admitted. A read-only image/provider overlay therefore leaves both
the guest flag and host title state untouched.

`ShowTitleRefusesReadOnlyFlagsBeforeRepaint` covers the unchanged flags, D0,
and cycle boundary. NULL/`NoTitleChange` title semantics and CyberGraphX
ownership remain unchanged.

## CloseWindow visible-chain admission

Closing the synthetic Window is a two-sided ownership transition: host
`WindowOpenCount` must agree with the public `Screen.FirstWindow` chain. The
bridge now reads that chain before decrementing the host count and requires a
visible writable LONG when the compatibility Window is its head. A read-only
overlay therefore declines without leaving a stale public Window pointer
behind a retired host claim.

`CloseWindowRefusesReadOnlyScreenChainBeforeRetiringOwnership` proves that a
subsequent CloseScreen still declines while the guest chain remains attached.
Foreign/native Window links and CyberGraphX ownership stay outside this path.

## ModifyIDCMP writable-field admission

`ModifyIDCMP` publishes `Window.IdcmpFlags` and, when absent, a synthetic
`Window.UserPort`. The compatibility bridge now exposes a status-aware callback
seam and admits both public LONG writes before changing `_syntheticIdcmpFlags`
or allocating a UserPort. A readable read-only overlay returns the original
request result to the native/provider path instead of claiming success.

The legacy `Action<M68kCpuState>` callback remains available for providers that
cannot report status. `ModifyIdcmpRefusesReadOnlyWindowFlagsBeforePublication`
locks the compatibility-owner failure boundary.

## OpenWindow visible-chain admission

`OpenWindow` inserts the compatibility Window at `Screen.FirstWindow` and may
write its previous head into `Window.Next`. The synthetic owner now reads both
links and requires visible writable spans before incrementing
`WindowOpenCount`. A read-only overlay therefore returns NULL without
publishing a host claim or leaving a chain that CloseScreen cannot reconcile.

`OpenWindowRefusesReadOnlyScreenChainBeforePublishingOwnership` covers the
empty-chain insertion case; provider/native tails and CyberGraphX ownership
remain independent.

## GetScreenData writable-destination admission

`GetScreenData` already validates the source and destination address envelopes,
but a mapped read-only destination is still readable. The compatibility bridge
now requires the complete requested destination prefix to be visibly writable
before taking the source snapshot or returning success. This keeps ScreenData
queries atomic across standard/custom screen forms and leaves read-only
provider-owned buffers to their owner.

`GetScreenDataRejectsReadOnlyDestinationBeforeCopying` verifies D0 and every
destination byte remain unchanged.

## QueryOverscan writable-rectangle admission

`QueryOverscan` publishes four WORDs into the caller's Rectangle. The
synthetic OCS/ECS owner now requires the complete eight-byte span to be both
mapped and visibly writable before resolving profile-aware geometry or issuing
the first write. A readable provider/image overlay therefore declines without
changing D0, auxiliary registers, or the prior rectangle, leaving the native
and CyberGraphX provider boundaries available for retry.

`QueryOverscanRejectsReadOnlyRectangleBeforePublication` locks this atomic
publication boundary while the existing odd/wrapped and foreign-display
vectors retain their ownership behavior.

## AddGList visible-chain admission

`AddGList` publishes the compatibility gadget head through
`Window.FirstGadget`. The synthetic owner now requires that complete LONG to
be visibly writable after validating the Window/Gadget envelopes and before
updating host gadget state. A readable provider/image overlay therefore
declines with the caller's D0 and existing link unchanged, leaving native
Intuition/provider ownership available for retry; CyberGraphX remains outside
this standard-planar path.

`AddGListRefusesReadOnlyWindowFirstGadgetBeforePublication` locks the
no-partial-publication boundary.

## RastPort host-overlay write admission

The CopperStart `IGraphicsMemory` adapter previously treated every mapped
guest byte as writable, so a read-only bus overlay could still let the
portable Draw/Text core update the cursor and then fall through to the
AmigaBoot host renderer. The adapter now checks `Bus.IsWritableMemoryRange`
for every byte/WORD/LONG write. The fallback Draw path additionally admits
both cursor WORDs, while Text admits its final CurrentX WORD, before emitting
pixels. This keeps mapped and direct ownership aligned without moving
CyberGraphX/RTG surfaces into the standard-planar implementation.

The two focused regressions prove D0, cursor, and first-plane bytes remain
unchanged when a provider/image overlay masks the cursor publication.

## MrgCop View-publication admission

`MrgCop` may temporarily expose the first visible ViewPort when a hidden chain
head precedes it, then republishes the View's LOF/SHF CPR links. The synthetic
owner now requires all three public View LONGs to be mapped and visibly
writable before any replacement CPR is allocated or any temporary link is
written. A read-only provider/image overlay therefore returns MCOP_NO_MEM with
the prior ViewPort chain, CPR links, and per-viewport DspIns intact.

`MrgCopRefusesReadOnlyViewPublicationBeforeRebuildingCopper` locks this
screen/view handoff boundary while native/provider ownership remains separate.

## MrgCop merged-destination admission

The linked-ViewPort merge appends waits, source words, and a copper terminator
into the first raw compatibility stream in place. Before taking the source
snapshot, `TryMergeCompatibilityCopperLists` now requires that complete
destination span to be mapped and visibly writable. A readable ROM/image
overlay therefore declines without any partial stream mutation, leaving the
existing CPR registry available to the native/provider owner.

`MrgCopRefusesReadOnlyMergedCopperDestinationBeforeAppendingLinkedStream`
locks this write boundary separately from the public View-link admission.

## ActiView publication admission

LoadView and active RethinkDisplay both publish the public
`GfxBase->ActiView` LONG as part of their display handoff. The compatibility
owner now admits a mapped sidecar only when the bus-visible four-byte span is
writable. A read-only native/provider image therefore declines before copper
queueing, host active-view mutation, or a partial display rethink. Odd, high,
or unmapped native bases remain the existing non-claiming boundary and do not
get interpreted through wrapped arithmetic.

`LoadViewRefusesReadOnlyNativeActiViewBeforeCopperHandoff` and
`RethinkDisplayRefusesReadOnlyNativeActiViewBeforeRebuildingCopper` lock the
native sidecar write boundary while CyberGraphX/RTG remains provider-owned.

## SetChipRev publication admission

`SetChipRev` has two ownership layers. The portable capability backend still
decides which OCS/ECS/AGA bits are available, while the host shim may mirror
the result into the native `GfxBase->ChipRevBits0` byte. A compact native image
without a full rebound GfxBase tail retains that compatibility callback. Once a
full native base is bound, the mapped byte is an ownership record: a read-only
provider/image overlay declines the native-overlay vector before the callback
can mutate host capability state. The direct AmigaBoot shim also checks visible
writability before mirroring the byte. Odd, wrapped, or unmapped optional fields
remain the existing provider/native boundary.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyChipRevisionPublicationBeforeHostCallback`
proves the callback, D0, cycle, program counter, and sentinel byte remain
unchanged under a read-only overlay. CyberGraphX/RTG capability policy remains
outside this OCS/ECS boundary.

## SA_ErrorCode output admission

`SA_ErrorCode` is an output pointer in the caller-owned OpenScreen request,
not an optional readable hint. The synthetic tag-list path now requires its
four-byte span to be bus-visible writable before allocating or publishing a
Screen. The staged success/failure paths repeat the writable check before
writing, so a provider/image overlay cannot consume a request and silently
lose its result word.

`OpenScreenTagListDeclinesAReadOnlySaErrorCodeDestination` locks this screen
ownership boundary without entering CyberGraphX/RTG handling.

## `GetDisplayInfoData` output admission

`GetDisplayInfoData` writes caller-owned `DTAG_DISP`, `DTAG_DIMS`, `DTAG_MNTR`,
and `DTAG_NAME` payloads. The portable display database stages each recognized
chunk and requires the complete destination envelope to be mapped and
bus-visible writable before any byte is published. The native overlay returns
zero before its original-vector tail chain when a read-only provider/image
mapping masks that output, so the caller's sentinel and D0/cycle/program-counter
handoff remain intact. Unsupported chunks, malformed spans, and CyberGraphX/RTG
records remain provider-owned rather than being coerced into the standard
OCS/ECS database.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyDisplayInfoDataOutputBeforePublication` locks this
transactional output boundary independently of the existing direct-vs-mapped
display-data parity tests.

## `InitRastPort` output admission

`InitRastPort` owns a complete caller-provided RastPort envelope: it clears the
classic structure, publishes the default pen/mode/minterm state, and may then
publish the selected default font and cached metrics. The native-overlay
register seam now checks the entire visible RastPort span for writability before
resolving the compatibility default-font owner. A read-only provider/image
overlay therefore declines without clearing bytes, consuming host font state,
or changing the caller's register frame. Odd, NULL, wrapped, and malformed
structures continue to the existing native/provider boundary; ordinary direct
portable calls retain the transactional clear-and-restore implementation.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyRastPortBeforeDefaultStatePublication` locks this
ordering separately from the existing initializer rollback and direct/mapped
structure-parity tests.

## `InitView`/`InitVPort` output admission

`InitView` and `InitVPort` are void lifecycle initializers, but both publish a
complete guest structure before the CopperScreen projection seam is allowed to
observe a ViewPort. The native-overlay adapter now checks each full visible
envelope for writability before entering the portable clear/default-state
transaction. A read-only provider/image mapping therefore tail-chains without
clearing guest lifecycle bytes or invoking `InitializeCompatibilityViewPort`;
the caller's D0, cycles, and PC remain untouched. Direct calls retain the
portable snapshot/restore behavior for late write failures, while odd, NULL,
wrapped, and malformed structures remain native/provider-owned.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyViewInitializersBeforePublication` locks this
ordering and the no-projection guarantee for both initializers.

## Text-metric output admission

`AskFont` writes a caller-owned TextAttr, while `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and
`FontExtent` write the packed 12-byte TextExtent envelope. Their portable cores
already validate alignment and readable shape transactionally; the native
overlay now adds the bus-visible writable-span check before selected-font or
metric decoding. A read-only provider/image result buffer therefore declines
without consuming the text/font query or publishing partial fields, preserving
the caller's D0/cycles/PC for native retry. The check does not alter TextFit's
zero-length no-font path, signed TextExtent fields, or UWORD register inputs;
CyberGraphX/RTG metric ownership remains outside the standard-planar seam.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyTextMetricOutputsBeforePublication` locks this
output-ordering boundary for all four vectors.

## `InitBitMap` output admission

`InitBitMap` publishes only the fixed eight-byte `BitMap` geometry/header
prefix. The eight public `Planes[]` links are caller-owned and are not read or
validated by the initializer. The native-overlay register seam now requires
that prefix to be bus-visible and writable before the portable transaction
starts, so a read-only provider/image mapping cannot consume the vector or
partially change geometry. Direct portable calls retain the existing
snapshot/restore behavior and compact/truncated plane-table semantics.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBitMapGeometryBeforePublication` locks the
prefix-only write boundary and preserves the caller's D0/cycles/PC and plane
links for native/provider retry.

## `InitArea`/`InitTmpRas` output admission

`InitArea` and `InitTmpRas` publish public descriptor state, but neither
initializer owns the caller's area vector/flag storage or temporary-raster
backing span. The native-overlay seam now checks the complete `AreaInfo` or
`TmpRas` descriptor for bus-visible writability before entering the portable
snapshot/write transaction. A read-only provider/image mapping therefore
tail-chains without consuming caller storage or partially publishing
collector/temporary-raster state; direct calls retain their existing
transactional and zero-capacity semantics.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyAreaInitializersBeforePublication` locks this
descriptor-only ordering for both drawing initializers.

## `GetRGB32` output admission

`GetRGB32` publishes three guest ULONGs per requested color. Zero-count calls
remain successful no-ops without reading the output table; nonzero calls retain
the portable checks for NULL, odd, wrapping, and truncated tables. For a valid
native-overlay result, the adapter now checks the complete `12*nColors` table
through the bus-visible writable-range predicate before decoding ColorMap
entries or entering the portable rollback writer. A read-only provider/image
mapping therefore tail-chains with the caller's table, ColorMap, D0, cycles, and
PC unchanged. Direct portable calls retain palette snapshot/restore semantics,
while CyberGraphX/RTG providers remain a separate owner.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyRgb32OutputBeforePaletteRead` locks this ordering
and verifies that palette allocation succeeds but the read-only output table is
never touched.

## `ReadPixelLine8`/`ReadPixelArray8` output admission

The V36 pixel-read vectors publish byte-per-pen rows whose guest stride is
rounded to a 16-pixel boundary. The native-overlay adapter now computes the
positive line or rectangle geometry and preflights the complete padded output
span through the bus-visible writable-range predicate before entering planar
sampling. These are byte arrays rather than public word-aligned structures, so
odd starts remain valid and are checked rather than automatically deferred.
NULL, zero/negative/inverted, oversized, and wrapping requests retain the
portable/provider validation boundary. A read-only provider/image mapping
therefore leaves the output, planar bytes, D0, cycles, and PC untouched for the
native retry; `WritePixelLine8` and `WritePixelArray8` retain their source-array
read contract, and CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remains separate.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyPixelArrayOutputsBeforePlanarRead` locks both
line and rectangle spans with odd guest array addresses.

## `BitMapScale` argument admission

`BitMapScale` derives and publishes destination width and height in the
caller-owned `BitScaleArgs` record. The native-overlay adapter now requires the
complete public 0x30-byte argument envelope to be bus-visible and writable
before reading source/destination bitmap links, checking ownership, or staging
the scaled planar transaction. A read-only provider/image record therefore
tail-chains without endpoint decoding, extent publication, or pixel mutation;
the caller's D0, cycles, and PC remain available for native retry. Odd and
malformed records, foreign/RTG endpoints, and invalid scale factors retain their
existing portable/provider boundaries.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBitScaleArgsBeforeEndpointDecode` locks this
ordering with a readable but non-writable argument record.

## `SetFont` output admission

`SetFont` publishes the selected `TextFont` pointer plus cached TextHeight,
TextWidth, TextBaseline, and algorithmic-style state into the caller's
RastPort. The native-overlay adapter now preflights the complete RastPort
envelope before resolving guest font metrics. A read-only provider/image
RastPort therefore tail-chains without consuming font state or partially
publishing cache fields; the original RastPort bytes, D0, cycles, and PC remain
available to native retry. NULL default-font selection, malformed fonts, RTG
RastPorts, and direct portable rollback retain their existing boundaries.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlySetFontRastPortBeforeMetricDecode` locks this
ordering for a readable font and a read-only RastPort.

## `SetSoftStyle`/`SetRPAttrsA` field admission

`SetSoftStyle` publishes only the RastPort algorithmic-style byte. Native
overlay admission now probes that exact byte before entering font-style
resolution. `SetRPAttrsA` has a wider but still sparse contract: the adapter
collects its native-safe tag list and checks the exact fields each setter can
mutate, including regenerated line-pattern/minterm/flag bytes for pen and draw
mode tags, the cached font fields for `RPTAG_Font`, and the mask byte for write
mask/max-pen tags. Unrelated trailing RastPort bytes remain outside the
admission envelope. Read-only provider/image fields therefore tail-chain
without partial style or tag publication, preserving guest bytes, D0, cycles,
and PC; unknown tags, malformed lists, RTG surfaces, and direct transactional
rollback remain on their existing boundaries.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyRastPortAttributeWritersBeforePublication` locks
the soft-style and pen-tag cases against the mapped native overlay.

## `GetRPAttrsA` result admission

The native-safe `GetRPAttrsA` subset now exposes its exact guest result spans
before the portable query reads RastPort state. Scalar tags publish four-byte
ULONGs and `RPTAG_DrawBounds` publishes a Rectangle envelope; odd, NULL, and
wrapping destinations retain the existing native/provider validation boundary,
except for the documented NULL `RPTAG_MaxPen` no-op. The adapter checks each
destination's bus-visible writability before font/style/pen decoding, so a
read-only provider/image result remains byte-for-byte unchanged with D0, cycles,
and PC preserved for native retry. Unknown tags, RTG RastPorts, and direct
transactional rollback remain separate ownership paths.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyGetRpAttrsOutputsBeforeRastPortRead` locks the
scalar result ordering.

## Direct RastPort setter admission

The native-safe drawing-state setters now use sparse, exact writable spans at
the overlay boundary. Pen and draw-mode setters admit their primary byte plus
the regenerated line-pattern, minterm, and flag bytes; `SetWriteMask` and the
non-zero `SetMaxPen` path admit only the mask byte; `SetOutlinePen` admits its
outline byte and flags; and `Move` admits the two cursor words, line-pattern
count, and flags. The zero-`SetMaxPen` form remains a no-op and needs no
RastPort publication. This avoids requiring unrelated trailing RastPort bytes,
preserves direct 68k register/return semantics, and leaves read-only or RTG
provider mappings to their existing retry boundary.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyDirectRastPortSettersBeforePublication` locks the
whole setter family against a mapped read-only RastPort.

## `SetRast` selected-plane admission

`SetRast` is an unconditional planar initialization vector: it publishes the
requested pen to every selected bitplane, while the RastPort mask limits the
planes it may touch. The native overlay now reads the validated bitmap header,
derives the effective mask, resolves each selected plane pointer, and checks
the complete physical plane span (including interleaved row stride) for host
writability before claiming the vector. Zero effective masks remain bounded
no-ops; unselected plane pointers are not admitted; malformed or provider
ownership cases continue to the portable/native boundary. A read-only selected
plane therefore leaves all bitmap/RastPort bytes and the original register
frame available for retry.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlySetRastPlanesBeforeBitmapWrite` locks the
selected-plane ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `WritePixel` selected-plane admission

`WritePixel` updates one byte in each bitplane selected by the RastPort mask,
using the current pen/draw mode to choose the target bit. The native overlay
now resolves the validated bitmap geometry and exact per-plane byte addresses
for the requested pixel, then checks those bytes for host writability before
claiming the vector. Out-of-bounds coordinates and zero effective masks remain
bounded successful no-ops; malformed, layered, and RTG/provider cases retain
their existing ownership boundaries. A read-only selected byte therefore
leaves the pixel and the original 68k register/cycle frame untouched for
native/provider retry.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyWritePixelPlaneBeforePixelWrite` locks this
single-pixel ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `RectFill` selected-row admission

`RectFill` delegates its standard-planar fill to the patterned destination
writer, so the native overlay now derives the inclusive rectangle after
clipping it to bitmap bounds and checks the complete byte span of every
selected plane row. The check uses the bitmap's physical row stride, including
interleaved layouts, while leaving inverted geometry, fully off-raster regions,
and zero effective masks as bounded no-ops. Layered, RTG, malformed, and
provider-owned ports retain their existing boundaries; a read-only selected
row tail-chains before any patterned state or pixel publication.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyRectFillPlaneBeforePlanarPublication` locks the
row-span ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `Draw` line-state and destination admission

The native overlay now checks the complete RastPort state that `Draw`
publishes—current X/Y, line-pattern phase, and Flags—before walking the
destination. It then mirrors the integer Bresenham traversal and checks the
exact byte of every selected planar destination sample, while off-raster
samples remain line-state-only. This keeps connected-segment and zero-mask
semantics in the portable core but prevents a read-only bitmap or truncated
RastPort from being claimed by the host overlay. Layered, RTG, malformed, and
provider-owned ports retain their existing boundaries.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyDrawPlaneBeforeLinePublication` locks the line
preflight ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `PolyDraw` connected-line admission

`PolyDraw` is a connected sequence of `Draw` operations, so the native overlay
now validates the cursor/line-state publication once and walks every guest
point in order, checking each segment through the shared integer Bresenham
destination preflight. The low-UWORD zero-count no-read behavior remains
unchanged, and malformed point streams remain available to the native/provider
owner. A read-only destination in any later segment therefore prevents the
chain from partially mutating the bitmap or RastPort.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyPolyDrawPlaneBeforeChainPublication` locks the
multi-segment ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `DrawEllipse` destination admission

`DrawEllipse` computes a midpoint outline without mutating RastPort line state.
The native overlay now derives its signed center/radius bounds, clips those
bounds only for the writable-span check, and preflights every selected plane's
physical row span before entering the portable midpoint collector. The core's
documented no-clipping behavior and zero-mask no-op remain unchanged; malformed,
layered, RTG, and provider-owned ports retain their prior boundaries.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyDrawEllipsePlaneBeforeOutlinePublication` locks
the outline ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `EraseRect` backfill admission

`EraseRect` temporarily selects `BPen` through `SetAPen`, delegates its
selected planar region to `RectFill`, then restores the caller's foreground
pen, minterms, and line-pattern phase. The native overlay now admits both
envelopes: exact clipped physical row spans for selected planes and the
multi-field pen/mode publication fields. Reversed geometry remains a no-op;
layered, RTG, malformed, and provider-owned ports retain their existing
boundaries. A read-only backfill therefore cannot partially clear the raster or
leak temporary style state.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyEraseRectPlaneBeforeBackfillPublication` locks
the ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `ClearEOL`/`ClearScreen` admission

Both clear vectors can reset the line-pattern phase even when their effective
write mask is zero, and otherwise temporarily select a clear pen through
`SetAPen` before filling planar storage. The native overlay now preflights the
line-pattern byte unconditionally, then checks the complete selected-plane
storage and the pen/minterm/Flags fields only when pixels can be published.
This preserves the zero-mask ordering while preventing a read-only bitmap from
being claimed before text geometry or font state is decoded. Layered, RTG,
malformed, and provider-owned ports remain separate boundaries.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyClearPlanesBeforeTextDecode` locks both clear
vectors against a mapped native overlay.

## `ScrollRaster`/`ScrollRasterBF` admission

The scroll vectors have several observable no-op boundaries: reversed bounds,
zero displacement, ordinary full displacement, and a zero effective write
mask. The native overlay now preserves those boundaries before asking the
portable core to stage a source rectangle. When a move can publish pixels, it
preflights every selected destination row using the physical bitmap stride and
the line-pattern byte. `ScrollRasterBF` additionally delegates vacated strips
to `EraseRect`, so its admission includes the temporary FgPen/minterm/Flags
publication that is restored before return. Layered, RTG, malformed, and
provider-owned ports remain separate boundaries.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyScrollPlanesBeforeMovePublication` locks both
scroll variants against a mapped native overlay.

## `Flood` connected-region admission

`Flood` discovers a connected region incrementally and may write any selected
pixel in the bitmap, while an attached `TmpRas` is cleared and used as the
visited-bit map. The native overlay therefore admits the complete selected
plane span before beginning discovery and checks an attached TmpRas buffer for
the required byte count. A null TmpRas remains the managed/allocator path;
invalid seeds, zero masks, malformed objects, layers, RTG, and provider-owned
ports keep their existing boundaries. A read-only selected plane now
tail-chains before the first connected-region publication.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyFloodPlaneBeforeConnectedPublication` locks this
ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `BltPattern` selected-row admission

`BltPattern` reads an optional external mask and AreaPtrn source, then writes
selected destination planes through the same patterned writer used by
`RectFill`. The native overlay now derives the clipped inclusive rectangle and
preflights every selected row span before source traversal, leaving source
buffers read-only and preserving inverted, off-raster, zero-mask, malformed,
layered, RTG, and provider boundaries. A read-only selected plane therefore
tail-chains before the patterned operation can partially publish.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBltPatternPlaneBeforePatternPublication` locks
this ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## `BltTemplate` clipped destination admission

`BltTemplate` reads a word-addressed chip-memory source and publishes pixels in
the clipped destination rectangle selected by the RastPort mask. The native
overlay now mirrors the core's negative-coordinate clipping and preflights all
selected destination rows before decoding the template. Zero-mask and
off-raster paths remain bounded no-ops; malformed, layered, RTG/provider, and
source display-DMA ownership boundaries remain explicit.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBltTemplatePlaneBeforeTemplatePublication` locks
this destination ordering against a mapped native overlay.

## Pixel-array writer destination admission

The V36/V40 pixel-array writers consume caller-owned chunky bytes and publish
only selected planar destination pixels. The native overlay now mirrors their
inclusive destination geometry, including the line writer's exclusive width,
and checks the clipped selected-plane rows before source staging. Zero-mask and
empty requests remain bounded, while source arrays, temporary RastPorts,
malformed endpoints, layers, RTG, and providers retain their existing
ownership boundaries.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyPixelWriterPlanesBeforeArrayPublication` locks
`WritePixelLine8`, `WritePixelArray8`, and `WriteChunkyPixels` against a mapped
native overlay.

## AreaInfo collector and `AreaEnd` admission

Area recording vectors publish AreaInfo state, coordinate vectors, and flag
bytes; `AreaEnd` reads those records, may clear/mark TmpRas, fills selected
planes, optionally restores outline cursor/style state, and resets the
collector. The native overlay now preflights the appropriate output envelope:
recording calls check the descriptor plus full vector/flag capacity, while
`AreaEnd` checks the descriptor reset, selected planar storage, outline fields,
and a full-sized attached TmpRas when its descriptor can cover that envelope.
Empty collectors and zero-mask forms retain their no-write boundaries; malformed,
layered, RTG, and provider ownership remains separate.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyAreaCollectorBeforeVectorPublication` and
`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyAreaEndPlanesBeforeFillPublication` lock these
collector/fill boundaries against a mapped native overlay.

## RastPort destination blit admission

`BltBitMapRastPort` publishes through the destination RastPort mask, while
`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` deliberately ignores that field and participates across
the common source/destination depth under its external one-bit mask. The
native overlay now checks the clipped destination rows with the corresponding
plane mask before source staging or minterm publication. Source bitmaps and
external masks remain read-only inputs; layered, RTG, malformed, and provider
ownership boundaries remain explicit.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBlitRastPortPlanesBeforeBlitPublication` locks
both destination blit variants against a mapped native overlay.

## Pure `BltBitMap` destination admission

`BltBitMap` receives direct `BitMap` pointers, unlike the RastPort variants.
The native-overlay boundary therefore uses a direct word/byte header decoder,
derives the physical per-plane row stride (including interleaved bitmap flags),
clips D2/D3 plus D4/D5 to the destination bitmap, and checks the D7
participating plane mask before the portable core can publish. A zero effective
mask remains a no-write claim. Source and TempA validation remains in the core
display-DMA boundary; malformed or provider-owned endpoints still tail-chain.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBltBitMapDestinationBeforePublication` locks the
direct-header and D7 destination admission against a mapped native overlay.

## `ClipBlit` destination admission

`ClipBlit` has two RastPort endpoints and publishes only through the
destination port. After the existing non-layered/RTG classification, the
native overlay now clips D2/D3 plus D4/D5 against the destination bitmap and
checks the destination RastPort mask before entering the portable operation.
Source decoding and any provider/layer ownership remain unchanged, so an
unreadable or foreign source still reaches its existing native boundary.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyClipBlitDestinationBeforePublication` locks the
destination-only admission and preserves the call frame for native retry.

## `BltClear` destination-span admission

`BltClear` publishes a contiguous byte span in scalar mode and a
bytes-per-row-by-row-count span in row mode. The overlay now decodes that
geometry, preserves bounded no-op and malformed forms for the existing core,
and checks the complete writable span before claiming the native slot. The
portable core still owns display-DMA classification, aggregate staging limits,
and transactional rollback.

`NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBltClearDestinationBeforePublication` locks the
complete-span admission against a mapped native overlay.

## Palette mutation write admission

Palette setters and bulk loaders are graphics-owned only after the ColorMap
ownership check succeeds. The native overlay now decodes the owned map's
ColorTable span and, for V36/V39 maps, the matching LowColorBits span before
entering the portable mutation transaction. A readonly span therefore
tail-chains without taking the portable lock or allowing a partial WORD
publication. Bulk loaders use the complete declared table envelope because
their source records may select any entry; malformed or provider-owned maps
remain with the resident/provider vector. CyberGraphX is still outside this
boundary and retains its own surface/palette patching policy.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyPaletteMutationBeforeColorMapWrite`
and `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBulkPaletteMutationBeforeColorMapWrite`.

## Region mutation write admission

Region booleans publish a guest Region header and linked RegionRectangle nodes.
The native overlay now checks the owned destination header before all boolean
mutations and additionally checks every existing node for allocation-free
`AndRectRegion`. Other operations allocate replacement nodes through the
portable allocator and retain that transaction's rollback boundary. Readonly
headers or nodes therefore tail-chain before the portable engine mutates or
reclaims guest state; foreign, malformed, and provider-owned chains remain
outside this graphics-owned admission.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyRegionOutputsBeforeBooleanPublication`.

## BitMapScale destination admission

BitMapScale publishes both scaled planar pixels and the destination width and
height in `BitScaleArgs`. The native overlay now derives those extents with the
same `ScalerDiv` arithmetic as the portable core, decodes the direct destination
BitMap, and checks the common source/destination plane mask before staging
samples. A readonly destination therefore tail-chains before either pixels or
extent fields change; the existing argument-record, ownership, aliasing, and
RTG/provider checks remain authoritative.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBitScaleDestinationBeforePublication`.

## ChangeVPBitMap association write admission

`ChangeVPBitMap` publishes one guest LONG: the viewport's
`RasInfo.BitMap` association. The native overlay now follows the viewport
pointer to RasInfo and checks that exact four-byte field before entering the
portable validation and display-publication transaction. The replacement
bitmap, DBufInfo, RTG/provider classification, malformed envelope, and
display callback remain existing input/ownership boundaries. A readable but
readonly association therefore tail-chains without changing the pointer or
consuming the callback, preserving the full register frame for native retry.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyChangeVPBitMapAssociationBeforePublication`.

## UCopperListInit record write admission

`UCopperListInit` first clears and republishes the caller-owned `UCopList`
record, then allocates and links its internal `CopList` and instruction
buffers. The native overlay now checks the complete public record span before
entering that transaction. A readonly record therefore leaves allocator and
registry state untouched and tail-chains to resident Kickstart/provider
ownership; writable records retain the portable allocator's existing
transaction and rollback boundary.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyUserCopperListBeforeInternalAllocation`.

## CMove/CWait instruction write admission

`CMove` and `CWait` publish exactly one current `CopIns` record. They do not
advance the caller's `UCopList`; that publication belongs to `CBump`. The
portable copper registry now exposes the validated current instruction
address, and the native overlay checks only that record's writable span before
entering the word-level transactional writer. A readonly instruction record
therefore tail-chains without changing metadata, registers, or allocator
state, while malformed and foreign lists remain outside the graphics-owned
boundary.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyCopperInstructionBeforeCMoveAndCWaitPublication`.

## CBump branch-specific write admission

`CBump` has two distinct guest publication branches. While the current block
has capacity, it writes only `CopList.CopPtr` and `CopList.Count`. Once the
block is full, it republishes `UCopList.CopList`; when no next block exists it
also writes `CopList.Next` after allocation. The portable registry now exposes
that validated branch state, and the native overlay checks exactly the spans
the selected branch will publish. This keeps block allocation and link
rollback out of readonly requests without over-preflighting metadata that the
current branch does not touch.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyCopperBumpStateBeforeInBlockAdvance`
and `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyCopperBumpLinksBeforeFullBlockAllocation`.
### G18/G26 native monitor lifecycle parity

`OpenMonitor` and `CloseMonitor` share the same typed guest-memory registry
through direct CopperStart dispatch and the mapped native overlay. A full
native `GfxBase` may cause the overlay to allocate its own private display
database sidecar before opening the monitor; therefore the parity contract
compares the resident `MonitorSpec` fields and list topology relative to each
instance, not raw allocator addresses. Repeated opens increment the one guest
`ms_OpenCount` WORD, closes decrement it without reclaiming the resident node,
and the final close leaves the node linked with count zero. The host and future
68k paths consequently agree on ownership and ABI while preserving provider
sidecars and allocator provenance.
### G18/G25 `CloseMonitor` writable ownership admission

`CloseMonitor` has a narrow native-overlay write boundary: only the resident
instance-owned `ms_OpenCount` WORD is mutated. The adapter verifies ownership,
alignment/range, and writable guest storage before invoking the portable
decrement transaction. Null remains an idempotent close; foreign, malformed,
or read-only specs remain available to native/provider monitor ownership.

## G02/G27 native font lifecycle parity

The font-list lifecycle uses the same reversible ownership rule as monitor
objects. A mapped `OpenFont`/`CloseFont` call is claimed only after the
rebound guest `TextFonts` list is readable and the selected font is resident
in the active graphics-library instance. Accessor-count publication remains
guest-owned, while a foreign or malformed font is left to the captured
native/provider vector with the original register and cycle frame.

## G02/G25 native `CloseFont` ownership admission

The mapped close boundary is narrower than the portable guest-list reader:
resident membership alone does not authorize the compatibility bridge to
decrement a native font's accessor word. The overlay tracks each successful
`OpenFont` handle in the active instance, preflights that handle's writable
accessor WORD, and otherwise leaves the request to the captured
Kickstart/provider vector. Direct host dispatch retains the classic portable
guest-list behavior; only the reversible native overlay applies this
instance-ownership guard.

## G24/G25 native layer-lock ownership admission

The mapped native overlay treats the Layers lock trio as an explicit
capability boundary. A configured Layers backend or a complete
`LockLayerRom`/`AttemptLockLayerRom`/`UnlockLayerRom` callback bundle admits
the portable bridge; a provider-less adapter declines all three vectors so
the captured Kickstart implementation remains reachable with the original
register and cycle frame. Direct host dispatch retains its existing
provider-less compatibility behavior, because only the reversible native
overlay needs to avoid swallowing a vector that it cannot implement.
The capability is propagated through `GraphicsServices` as well, so a plain
`IGraphicsLayerBackend` and a scheduler-aware gateway follow the same native
admission rule.

## G02/G25 rebound TextFonts alignment boundary

The guest `GfxBase.TextFonts` list is an Exec-style word-linked list. The
portable rebound backend therefore treats the selected `GfxBase`, list head and
tail predecessor, each `TextFont` node, both node links, and the `DefaultFont`
pointer as 68000 word addresses. A zero optional pointer remains legal where the
Kickstart contract permits it; every non-zero pointer must be even. Validation
occurs before list traversal or any `AddFont`/`RemFont`/default publication,
which is important because host memory itself is byte-addressable and would
otherwise accept an ABI-invalid odd pointer.

The native overlay uses the same admission boundary after rebinding to the
discovered native `GfxBase`. A malformed odd node is not claimed by the
compatibility bridge: the captured Kickstart/provider vector receives the
request with the original CPU frame, while the malformed links remain intact.
The direct host and mapped native tests intentionally exercise both paths so
CopperSharp68k guest layouts and CopperScreen host dispatch share the same
alignment rule.

## G26/G27 per-vector native HUNK entry routing

The relocatable native image builder has two paths. The compatibility overload
keeps its historical one-entry stream: every public and reserved slot points
at the beginning of the supplied code, which is useful for a minimal headless
JMP fixture. The native cutover overload receives a complete map from each
public `GraphicsLvo` to an even, in-range byte offset within the native code
stream plus an explicit fallback offset for the private/reserved slots (the
V40 `-648` gap included).

The builder derives one slot map and feeds it to both the negative-vector
`JMP.L` table and the AUTOINIT function array. HUNK relocation groups remain
segment-relative, so loader relocation changes the code-segment base without
changing the per-vector deltas. Missing public entries, odd offsets, and
offsets that cannot fetch a 68000 word are rejected before any image bytes are
published. This keeps the CopperSharp68k native path independently selectable
while preserving the existing CopperScreen/host compatibility path.

## G20/G21/G27 guest GELS direct/mapped parity

GELS maintenance is a guest-memory state machine, so the host and native
overlay paths share one comparison boundary rather than maintaining separate
expected-value tests. The fixture starts from identical `GelsInfo`, sentinel,
RastPort, VSprite, image, and mask memory on two buses. It then invokes
`InitGels`, `SetCollision`, two `AddVSprite` insertions, `SortGList`,
`RemVSprite`, and `InitMasks` through direct host dispatch on one bus and the
mapped overlay jump table on the other. After each call it compares the full
guest fixture span plus D0 and the CPU cycle frame.

The same fixture also installs an original Kickstart `JMP.L` for `InitGels`
and sends a malformed null-pointer call through the mapped entry. The adapter
must preserve D0 and cycles and set the PC to that original native target. No
CyberGraphX, hardware DMA, or provider callback behavior is included in this
unit; those remain separate capability boundaries.

## G21/G27 animation lifecycle direct/mapped parity

Animation state is layered on the GELS guest lists, so its native cutover
boundary compares the complete lifecycle on identical memory images. The
fixture creates one AnimOb, one component, one Bob/VSprite pair, and the
RastPort/GelsInfo links required by the guest algorithms. It then runs
`InitGels`, `AddAnimOb`, `Animate`, `InitGMasks`, and `RemIBob` through direct
host dispatch on one bus and the mapped overlay on the other. Each operation
compares the whole guest fixture, not just the headline field, along with D0
and the preserved CPU cycle frame.

`AddAnimOb` also has an installed original Kickstart `JMP.L`. A null malformed
request is sent through the mapped vector after the valid lifecycle and must
tail-chain with the original D0, cycles, and PC frame. `DrawGList`, collision
callbacks, and allocator-backed `GetGBuffers` remain separate provider and
ownership units rather than being conflated with this guest-only transition.

## G22/G27 extended-node lifecycle direct/mapped parity

Extended graphics nodes are public guest allocations whose library backlink
and association fields are part of the native cutover contract. The
differential fixture binds both host services to the same native `GfxBase`
address and deterministic public allocator stream. It creates a
`ViewPortExtra`, associates it with one owner pointer, looks it up, and frees
it through direct host dispatch and the mapped overlay. The complete allocated
node span, D0/cycles, and allocator free count are compared after each step.

The mapped `GfxNew` vector retains an original Kickstart `JMP.L`; an
unsupported node subtype must preserve the incoming register/cycle frame and
tail-chain rather than being mistaken for a portable allocation. Monitor
driver-private payloads and native display-database sidecars remain outside
this guest-node parity unit.

## G14/G27 ColorMap/RGB lifecycle direct/mapped parity

Palette state is public guest storage, not a host-only color cache. The
differential fixture therefore gives direct and mapped services identical
allocator streams, creates a four-entry ColorMap, and compares the complete
allocated palette envelope after each `SetRGB4CM`, `GetRGB4`, `SetRGB32CM`,
`GetRGB32`, and `FreeColorMap` call. The RGB32 output table is also compared,
along with D0, cycle preservation, and the number of public releases.

The mapped `GetColorMap` vector retains an original Kickstart `JMP.L` for a
zero-size malformed request. This keeps invalid or foreign palette ownership
transparent while the standard ColorMap path remains portable-owned. Color
publication to copper hardware and Exec semaphore scheduling remain separate
provider/timing boundaries.

## G14/G27 palette-pen lifecycle direct/mapped parity

Palette sharing adds a second ownership layer over ColorMap storage. The
fixture starts from identical maps and viewports, attaches the palette extra,
obtains a shared pen, repeats the selection through `ObtainBestPenA`, resolves
it with `FindColor`, releases it, and finally frees the ColorMap. Direct host
dispatch and the mapped overlay compare the complete allocation sidecar,
viewport ColorMap publication, register results, CPU cycles, and allocator
release count after each operation.

The mapped `ObtainPen` vector retains an original Kickstart `JMP.L`; a foreign
ColorMap must preserve the caller frame and tail-chain. Host semaphore
projection and copper palette timing remain explicit provider boundaries.

## G13/G27 Region lifecycle direct/mapped parity

Regions are allocator-owned guest structures with linked rectangle nodes, so
their native cutover proof compares the entire deterministic allocation span.
The fixture creates a Region, unions and intersects a caller rectangle,
clears the resulting node chain, and disposes the Region through direct host
dispatch and the mapped overlay. D0/cycles, boolean results, and allocator
release counts are compared after each transition.

The mapped `DisposeRegion` vector retains an original Kickstart `JMP.L`; a
foreign Region is never interpreted as a portable allocation. Provider-owned
clipping and layer damage remain outside this Region utility boundary.

## G10/G27 fixed-cell Text style and JAM2 parity

The fixed-cell text seam is now exercised through the same two dispatch paths
that a future CopperSharp68k resident vector will use. A guest `TextFont` with
no proportional tables is decoded from its `tf_XSize` cell width and one-byte
row modulo. The differential then runs a two-character JAM2 operation with
bold and underline algorithmic styles, checking the complete planar output,
cursor advance, FRST_DOT/line-pattern state, D0, and cycles. This keeps the
native-safe text contract grounded in the classic RastPort layout without
claiming CyberGraphX color-font or provider clipping semantics.

## G04/G25 native-overlay `Text` state write admission

The native overlay admits `Text` through a deliberately smaller write set than
the line primitives. `Text` publishes the final `CurrentX`, resets
`linpatcnt`, and sets `FRST_DOT`; it does not rewrite `CurrentY`. The adapter
therefore checks those three guest spans against the bus-visible writable
mapping before entering `GraphicsTextOperations.Text`. If any span is
read-only, the mapped vector remains unclaimed with its incoming D0/cycle/PC
frame intact, allowing the captured Kickstart/provider entry to handle the
request. The portable core retains its own transactional rollback for direct
CopperSharp68k-compatible calls and does not claim layer or RTG ownership.

## G19 pixel-line result-count boundary

`ReadPixelLine8` and `WritePixelLine8` use the V36 line ABI's plotted/read
count, not the requested width, as their D0 result. The portable conversion
stages the full padded row and consumes every logical source cell, but increments
the result only for coordinates inside the destination bitmap. A fully
out-of-raster line therefore returns zero without becoming malformed. The
writer's effective-zero mask is the same successful no-op and also returns
zero because no destination pixel was plotted. `ReadPixelArray8`,
`WritePixelArray8`, and `WriteChunkyPixels` continue to return their clipped
rectangle count. Direct host dispatch and the native overlay share this pure
operation; mapped RTG/layer endpoints remain provider-owned.

## G19 clipped pixel-array status admission

The register-facing status seam must not perform a stronger bitmap ownership
probe than the portable operation it is admitting. `GraphicsLibraryCore` now
computes the requested line/rectangle intersection in widened, saturating
arithmetic. It probes the clipped top-left pixel only when that intersection
is non-empty; a fully out-of-raster request skips bitmap-plane reads and lets
the pure body consume/zero its valid padded guest array as usual. This keeps
direct CopperSharp68k calls, mapped host calls, and the native HUNK overlay on
the same zero-count clipped result.

For writers, the probe is additionally gated by
`EffectiveWriteMask(bitmap, rp_Mask)`, so a zero or high-only mask remains a
bounded successful no-op even if the untouched bitmap endpoint is malformed.
Readers still validate the source planes when their clipped region is real;
the write mask is not a read-source ownership signal. Intersecting malformed
planar storage remains unclaimed, preserving the native/Kickstart fallback,
while CyberGraphX, RTG, and layer providers stay outside this portable rule.
## G17/G25 native-overlay copper-link admission

`MakeVPort` and `MrgCop` publish public copper-list link fields even though
their actual instruction storage belongs to the display/copper backend. The
native overlay must make that guest ownership decision before entering the
portable builder. `MakeVPort` checks the target ViewPort's `DspIns`, `SprIns`,
`ClrIns`, and `UCopIns` LONGs. `MrgCop` walks the visible ViewPort chain and
checks the same four fields on each visible node; hidden nodes are not part of
the resident merge loop and are not probed. An explicitly read-only mapped
field tail-chains to the resident/native vector without allocating a temporary
ViewPortExtra, invoking the backend, changing D0, or advancing cycles.

### G17/G25 `AllocDBufInfo` RTG ownership boundary (2026-08-17)

`AllocDBufInfo` is now admitted only for a standard OCS/ECS viewport. The
native-overlay adapter resolves the viewport's bounded `RasInfo` chain through
the existing bitmap ownership classifier before asking the portable core to
allocate a guest `DBufInfo`. If any linked bitmap is CyberGraphX/RTG-owned,
the call is declined with the caller's D0, cycle, and program-counter frame
unchanged; mapped ROM dispatch therefore tail-chains to the captured native
vector. Standard-planar double buffering keeps its existing transactional
message-envelope and scheduler boundaries, while RTG message ownership stays
with the separate CyberGraphX patch.

### G17/G25 `FreeVPortCopLists` teardown admission

`FreeVPortCopLists` clears the same four public `ViewPort` copper-link LONGs
that the portable `MakeVPort`/`MrgCop` builders publish. The native overlay
therefore reuses `CanPublishNativeViewPortCopperLinks` before entering the
transactional teardown. A read-only link is a provider/native ownership
signal, not a reason to attempt a host write and then claim a partial cleanup;
the mapped vector tail-chains with D0, cycles, and PC untouched. Direct
CopperSharp68k-compatible dispatch retains the core's sparse-link snapshot and
rollback behavior, and writable standard-planar teardown remains unchanged.

### G20/G25 `MoveSprite` publication admission

`MoveSprite` mutates the guest `SimpleSprite.X` and `SimpleSprite.Y` words and,
when `PosCtlData` is nonzero, the referenced two-word OCS/ECS position/control
envelope. The native overlay checks only those output spans before entering the
portable movement transaction. Explicitly read-only spans therefore
tail-chain to the resident/provider vector without partial coordinate writes,
while odd, unreadable, or otherwise malformed pointers remain the portable
validator's boundary. Writable standard sprites retain the existing rollback
and optional display-backend projection; CyberGraphX/RTG sprite ownership is
not claimed here.

### G20/G25 `ChangeSprite` association admission

`ChangeSprite` has one guest-visible output at the portable boundary: the
`SimpleSprite.PosCtlData` LONG that selects the new image stream. The native
overlay checks that association field before validating and publishing the
source image, so a read-only resident/provider sprite is left for the captured
native vector without a partial rebinding. Odd, unreadable, or malformed
envelopes remain with the core validator; writable standard sprites retain
their existing source-span checks, rollback, and optional display projection.

### G20/G25 `ChangeExtSpriteA` output admission

Standard `ChangeExtSpriteA` republishes the old `ExtSprite`'s
`PosCtlData`, height, coordinates, number, word width, and flags from a
validated replacement. The native overlay checks those seven exact output
spans before entering the transactional core, leaving soft-sprite,
scan-doubled, malformed, and read-only provider envelopes available to their
native/provider owner. The source image remains an input; writable standard
extended sprites retain the existing rollback and display/DMA boundaries.

### G20/G25 `AllocSpriteDataA` RTG source admission

`AllocSpriteDataA` consumes a source `BitMap` and allocates both the public
`ExtSprite` envelope and its CHIP-memory image. A bitmap classified by the
registered CyberGraphX/RTG ownership predicate is therefore rejected before
tag decoding, source reads, or either allocation. Standard planar sources
retain their existing guarded conversion and rollback; RTG sprite conversion
remains the separate provider's responsibility.

### G20/G25 `GetSprite` output admission

`GetSprite` has one guest-visible output in the portable path: the caller's
`SimpleSprite.num` WORD. Before a native-overlay call can select a resident
or portable-pool sprite, the adapter checks that exact mapped span is
writable. A read-only resident/provider mapping therefore tail-chains to the
captured native vector without consuming a pool entry, changing D0/cycles, or
touching the guest number. The direct portable path retains the normal
Kickstart-compatible `-1` result when its transactional WORD publication is
rejected. Odd, unmapped, and malformed envelopes remain the core/native
validation boundary; CyberGraphX sprite ownership is still supplied by its
separate patch.

### G20/G25 `GetGBuffers` output admission

`GetGBuffers` allocates private SAVEBOB, collision, border, shadow, and
optional double-buffer storage, then publishes five guest LONG pointers per
Bob/VSprite. The native overlay now performs a read-only structural walk of
the same animation/component chain and probes those caller-owned pointer
fields before invoking the allocator. A read-only provider envelope therefore
tail-chains without temporary allocation, pointer writes, or registry changes;
malformed chains remain with the core/native validator. Writable standard GELS
requests retain the existing complete allocation, packet initialization, and
rollback transaction.

### G20/G25 `InitGMasks` output admission

`InitGMasks` first republishes each component Bob through `VSprite.VSBob`, then
builds border and collision masks in caller-provided buffers. The native
overlay performs the same bounded animation/component walk as the portable
validator and returns the exact `VSBob` LONG plus border/collision byte spans.
Those spans are checked through the mapped-memory writability boundary before
the mask transaction is claimed. A read-only provider/image destination thus
falls through with the original register frame and native PC; direct portable
calls keep their existing owner-pointer journal and mask-write rollback.
CyberGraphX mask ownership remains outside this portable admission rule.

### G20/G25 `FreeGBuffers` teardown admission

`FreeGBuffers` is a visible teardown transaction, not only an allocator call:
when a Bob is marked back-saved it restores SAVEBOB rows into the RastPort,
clears the Bob/VSprite drawn state, then clears only pointer fields whose values
still match the registry-owned allocations before releasing storage. The native
overlay asks the live BufferSet for those exact raster-row, flag-word, and
matching-pointer spans and checks them through the mapped writability boundary.
A read-only raster or provider envelope therefore falls through before any
restore or free; direct portable teardown retains its existing retryable pointer
journal. CyberGraphX display and raster ownership remains separate.

### G20/G21/G25 `DrawGList` raster admission

`DrawGList` is a mixed guest/provider transaction. Before the host GELS
callback, the portable path may restore previous SAVEBOB rows, capture current
rows into save storage, and publish Bob/VSprite flags and old coordinates. The
native overlay now walks the validated Bob regions and checks those exact
restore/save rows and state words through the mapped writability boundary. A
read-only provider raster therefore falls through before any callback or guest
mutation; writable standard-planar state keeps the classic restore-then-capture
ordering and explicit provider callback boundary.

### G20/G25 `InitGels` publication admission

`InitGels` clears both system sentinel `VSprite` envelopes, publishes the
`GelsInfo.Head`, `GelsInfo.Tail`, and `GelsInfo.Flags` fields, and clears the
optional boundary collision-handler LONG. The native overlay derives those
exact destinations from the same structural validation used by the portable
transaction and checks their mapped writability before claiming the vector. A
read-only resident/provider envelope therefore tail-chains without clearing,
relinking, or changing the register frame; writable standard GELS retains the
existing clear-and-rollback transaction. The collision routine is an output
destination only when the guest `GelsInfo` points to one, so null handlers do
not create a synthetic host write.

### G20/G25 `SetCollision` publication admission

`SetCollision` publishes one LONG in the collision-handler table selected by
the guest collision number. The native overlay resolves the handler pointer,
validates the bounded table entry, and checks that exact four-byte destination
through the mapped writability boundary before claiming the vector. A
read-only resident/provider table therefore falls through without changing the
routine entry or register frame; the direct portable path keeps its existing
single-write transaction and rollback behavior. Invalid numbers, absent
handlers, and malformed tables remain with the core/native validator rather
than producing a host-only success.

### G20/G25 `InitMasks` output admission

`InitMasks` reads a VSprite image (or a Bob's `ImageShadow`) and publishes two
caller-owned planar word spans: the border line and collision mask. The native
overlay repeats the bounded geometry/source validation and checks both output
spans through the mapped writability boundary before claiming the vector. A
read-only resident/provider mask therefore tail-chains without a partial
border/mask write or register-frame change; writable standard VSprites retain
