the direct source walk and rollback transaction. CyberGraphX sprite conversion
and non-planar mask forms remain provider-owned.

### G20/G25 GELS list-maintenance admission

`AddVSprite` publishes four reciprocal links and a filtered flag WORD after a
bounded y/x insertion walk. `RemVSprite` publishes two neighbor links and
clears the removed node's two links. `SortGList` validates the complete
reciprocal chain, performs the stable y/x ordering, and rewrites the derived
head, node, and tail links. The native overlay now repeats those read-only
walks and returns the exact LONG/WORD destinations before claiming a vector.
Read-only resident/provider lists therefore tail-chain before any partial
relink; writable standard GELS retains the existing transactional list owner,
and malformed chains remain with the core/native validation boundary.

### G20/G22/G25 `AddBob` ownership admission

`AddBob` is a compound guest transaction: it marks the Bob waiting, clears the
VSprite hardware-sprite bit, publishes `VSBob`, and then delegates to the
ordered VSprite insertion. The native overlay now resolves the Bob/VSprite
flag and owner fields together with the delegated reciprocal-link spans before
claiming the vector. A read-only resident/provider Bob therefore tail-chains
before any partial ownership or list publication; writable standard Bob state
retains the existing rollback transaction and provider GELS callbacks remain
outside this admission rule.

### G20/G22/G25 `RemIBob` teardown admission

`RemIBob` may first restore a SAVEBOB background into the RastPort, then unlink
the VSprite, clear Bob system flags, and clear `VSBob`. The native overlay now
repeats the bounded Bob/bitmap/raster validation and derives those exact
restore rows plus reciprocal-link and ownership spans before claiming a
guest-only teardown. Read-only resident/provider state therefore tail-chains
before raster or list mutation; provider-backed GELS remains rejected at the
adapter boundary, and writable standard teardown keeps its retryable rollback
and idempotent removed-Bob behavior.

### G20/G23/G25 `Animate` publication admission

`Animate` advances every linked AnimOb, updates active and sequence component
state, and can remove an old Bob, switch component links, add a replacement
Bob, or restore a SAVEBOB raster. The native overlay now performs the same
bounded AnimOb/component traversal and resolves the participating public
envelopes, current GELS links, and any required restore rows before claiming
the frame. Read-only resident/provider animation therefore tail-chains before
partial frame publication; writable standard animation retains its existing
rollback and integer fixed-point update semantics.

### G20/G23/G25 `AddAnimOb` publication admission

`AddAnimOb` links the object into the animation-key chain, initializes every
active component, and may admit multiple distinct Bobs through the GELS list.
The native overlay now validates the active component walk and resolves the
AnimOb, key, component, Bob/VSprite, and current-list link envelopes before
claiming the compound transaction. Because delegated insertion destinations
depend on earlier Bobs in the same call, the admission covers the complete
validated public envelopes while the portable path retains its existing
rollback journal and provider/native boundary.

### G15/G17/G25 `LoadView` publication admission

`LoadView` publishes the active View through the optional native `GfxBase`
tail before handing the request to the display owner. The native overlay now
recognizes a validated full `GfxBase` envelope as one bounded publication span,
covering `ActiView` and the extended `CurrentMonitor`/`TopLine` sidecars. A
read-only resident/provider base therefore tail-chains before the display
callback or sidecar transaction; compact compatibility images with no
validated native tail retain the portable status-aware LoadView path and its
rollback/idempotence rules. CyberGraphX continues to own RTG View handoff.

### G20/G23/G25 RTG RastPort ownership boundary for GELS

GELS and animation calls that carry a RastPort now classify the endpoint with
the same RTG/CyberGraphX ownership predicate used by planar drawing and text.
`AddVSprite`, `SortGList`, `AddBob`, `DoCollision`, `DrawGList`, `RemIBob`,
`AddAnimOb`, `Animate`, `GetGBuffers`, and `FreeGBuffers` decline before their
portable structural walks or provider callbacks when the RastPort is RTG-owned.
Standard planar GELS remains unchanged; CyberGraphX/native patches retain the
declined register frame and own the RTG path.

### G22/G24/G25 native-overlay `GfxLookUp` association ownership

`GfxLookUp` claims a null key or an association present in the active portable
registry. For a non-null key with no portable association, the native overlay
returns false before publishing D0, leaving the captured Kickstart/provider
vector responsible for any resident association. The host compatibility path
continues to publish the classic zero no-match result.

### G15/G17/G25 RTG active-view blanking ownership

The `LoadView(NULL)` blanking form also classifies the currently published
native `GfxBase->ActiView`. If its validated View/ViewPort/RasInfo chain reaches
an RTG bitmap, the portable adapter declines before clearing `ActiView` or
calling the planar display owner. Standard planar and compatibility images
without an RTG active view retain the existing blanking transaction.

### G20/G25 native-overlay `FreeSprite` ownership admission

`FreeSprite` has no guest pointer from which a mapped overlay can infer the
resident owner of a hardware slot. The portable registry therefore records
which slots this graphics instance acquired through `GetSprite`; a native
overlay claims release only for one of those recorded slots. An untracked
valid number is left to Kickstart or a provider with the incoming D0, cycles,
and native PC unchanged. The direct compatibility path keeps its established
range-only behavior, while the ownership check is limited to native-overlay
dispatch and does not alter sprite image or display-DMA ownership.

### G16/G25 native-overlay `FreeCprList` ownership admission

`FreeCprList` receives a pointer to a hardware-facing `cprlist` whose private
allocation size and custom-chip ownership are outside the portable guest
layout. A legacy void display callback therefore cannot prove that a valid
non-null list belongs to the compatibility graphics instance. The CopperStart
display bridge exposes an explicit result-bearing ownership sidecar when the
host supplies `TryFreeCprList`; mapped native-overlay dispatch claims a
non-null list only when that sidecar is present, then lets the callback make
the address-specific decision. Legacy direct dispatch remains unchanged, and
the NULL no-op plus word-aligned public-envelope validation remain portable.
This keeps resident/provider copper resources available to their captured
Kickstart or CyberGraphX owner without broadening the graphics overlay.

### G16/G25 native-overlay `FreeVPortCopLists` ownership admission

`FreeVPortCopLists` has the same private-resource ambiguity for a non-null
ViewPort: its four public copper links may be writable even when the linked
resources belong to a resident or provider implementation. The CopperStart
display bridge therefore exposes a separate result-bearing
`TryFreeVPortCopLists` sidecar. A mapped native overlay requires that explicit
owner before clearing the links or invoking teardown; a legacy void callback
continues to serve direct compatibility dispatch. NULL remains the native
no-op, and the existing link-envelope transaction still handles malformed or
late-write failures. This preserves the CopperSharp68k-facing ViewPort layout
while keeping private copper ownership outside the portable overlay.

### G13/G25 native-overlay `FreeCopList` publication admission

`FreeCopList` releases only intermediate `CopList` blocks recorded by the
portable copper registry, but its teardown first clears both links in the
caller-owned `UCopList`. The native-overlay adapter now resolves that owning
record and requires the complete `UCopList` envelope to be visibly writable
before entering the teardown transaction. A read-only provider/image mapping
therefore tail-chains without attempting either link write or allocator
release; NULL remains the native no-op, and unknown lists remain with the
resident/provider owner. Direct compatibility dispatch keeps its existing
registry and rollback behavior.

### G02/G25 native-overlay `OpenFont` accessor admission

`OpenFont` selects a resident `TextFont` from the rebound `GfxBase.TextFonts`
list and increments exactly one public `tf_Accessors` WORD. The memory font
backend now exposes a side-effect-free candidate-resolution pass; the mapped
native overlay uses it to preflight the selected accessor field before the
portable lifecycle increments it. A valid request with no matching font has
no guest publication and remains claimable, while a read-only/provider-owned
resident font tail-chains with the original D0, cycles, and native PC. Direct
compatibility opens and the existing resident-list lifecycle remain unchanged.

### G12/G25 native-overlay queued-blitter link admission

The CopperStart scheduler is the guest-linked owner for `QBlit` and
`QBSBlit`: it publishes the classic `bltnode.n` link before queueing a node.
The queue contract now advertises that capability explicitly, while the
address-only/provider callback path remains unchanged. Mapped native overlay
dispatch preflights the node's own `bn_Next` word when the linked scheduler is
active, so a read-only node tail-chains before publication with D0, cycles,
and the native PC intact. The FIFO/core transaction still provides rollback
for later tail-link failures; direct compatibility queue behavior and
CyberGraphX ownership remain outside this portable admission boundary.

### G02/G25 native-overlay `RemFont` list-publication admission

`RemFont` is a compound guest-list teardown: it rewrites the predecessor and
successor links, may republish the `GfxBase.TextFonts` head/tail-predecessor,
detaches the removed node, and sets `tf_Flags.FPF_REMOVED`. The memory-backed
font-list owner now exposes a side-effect-free publication plan for those
exact fields. Native-overlay dispatch checks each planned span through the
guest writable-range boundary before entering the lifecycle transaction, so a
read-only resident/provider font remains with the captured Kickstart vector
without partial list writes. Direct compatibility dispatch retains its
existing rollback and extension teardown behavior; CyberGraphX remains outside
this standard TextFonts boundary.

### G02/G25 native-overlay `AddFont` list-publication admission

`AddFont` is the insertion counterpart to `RemFont`: it publishes the new
`TextFont` successor/predecessor pair, updates the previous tail and rebound
`GfxBase.TextFonts` tail-predecessor, optionally publishes the empty-list head,
and clears `FPF_REMOVED`. The memory-backed guest-list owner now resolves those
exact spans without writing. Native-overlay dispatch checks the complete plan
through the mapped writable-range boundary before claiming insertion, so a
read-only resident/provider list remains available to its original owner with
the incoming register frame and list bytes unchanged. Direct compatibility
insertion retains its existing transaction and duplicate/malformed checks.

### G02/G25 native-overlay `ExtendFont` publication admission

`ExtendFont` materializes a system-owned `TextFontExtension`, then publishes
its pointer in `TextFont.tf_Extension` and the tagged-style bit in the
caller-owned `tf_Style` byte. The native-overlay adapter now preflights those
two exact fields before the font backend clones tags or asks the allocator for
the extension envelope. A read-only/provider-owned font therefore tail-chains
without allocation, guest writes, or register-frame changes; direct
compatibility extension and its transactional rollback remain unchanged.

### G02/G25 native-overlay `StripFont` publication admission

`StripFont` detaches only a `TextFontExtension` previously allocated by the
portable font backend; foreign/provider extensions remain untouched. For an
owned extension, the native-overlay adapter now verifies the font's
`tf_Extension` LONG and `tf_Style` byte before clearing either field or
releasing the allocation. A read-only/provider-owned font therefore
tail-chains without partial publication or `Free`, while NULL, foreign
extensions, and direct compatibility rollback keep their existing semantics.

### G02/G25 native-overlay `CloseFont` chained-strip admission

The final accessor `CloseFont` can enter `RemFont` and then `StripFont` for a
non-ROM resident font. The font backend now exposes a side-effect-free check
for that exact owned-extension path; native-overlay admission preflights the
extension pointer and tagged-style byte before the accessor transaction can
reach the chained free. Ordinary accessor closes, foreign extensions, NULL,
and direct compatibility rollback retain their existing lifecycle behavior.

### G02/G25 native-overlay `RemFont` chained-strip admission

`RemFont` first unlinks a resident `TextFont` and then invokes `StripFont` for
an owned extension. The native-overlay planner now admits the complete
transaction: the existing list link/flag spans plus the owned font's
`tf_Extension` LONG and `tf_Style` byte. A read-only extension envelope is
therefore declined before list teardown or allocator release; foreign and
no-remove extensions keep their existing list-only ownership rules.

### G02/G25 native-overlay `CloseFont` chained-list admission

The final accessor `CloseFont` can unlink a resident `TextFont` from the
rebound guest `TextFonts` list before reaching an owned extension strip. The
native-overlay admission now resolves and preflights those exact removal spans
when this chained path is active, alongside the accessor WORD and extension
fields. A read-only list therefore declines before any close mutation or
`Free`; ordinary closes, foreign extensions, and direct compatibility rollback
retain their existing lifecycle behavior.

### G15/G18 native-overlay `FreeVPortCopLists` chained-node admission

`FreeVPortCopLists` has two guest-visible teardown stages: it clears the four
classic copper links in the `ViewPort`, then releases a temporary
`ViewPortExtra` when `VPXF_FREE_ME` is set. Releasing that extended node first
revalidates its graphics metadata and then clears the public `ve_ViewPort`
backlink. The native-overlay planner now resolves that optional chained
backlink without writing and preflights it before any copper link is cleared.
A read-only or sparse temporary node therefore tail-chains with its links,
lookup association, allocator state, and register frame untouched. Direct
compatibility teardown retains its existing link rollback and fail-closed
extended-node free behavior; CyberGraphX ownership remains outside this
standard ViewPort boundary.

### G15/G22/G25 native-overlay `GfxFree` association admission

`GfxFree` revalidates the owned extended-node metadata and, for associated
`ViewExtra`/`ViewPortExtra` nodes, clears the guest backlink before releasing
the allocation. The native-overlay gateway now resolves that exact public
teardown span without writing and checks it through the mapped writable-range
boundary before entering the registry transaction. A partial or read-only
backlink therefore tail-chains with the association, allocation, register
frame, and guest bytes intact. `SpecialMonitor` and `MonitorSpec` nodes retain
metadata-only teardown because they have no public association backlink;
direct compatibility behavior and CyberGraphX ownership remain unchanged.

### G15/G22/G25 native-overlay `GfxAssociate` publication admission

`GfxAssociate` can publish a temporary `ViewPortExtra`'s `VPXF_FREE_ME` WORD,
the incoming node's association backlink, and, when the pointer already names
another associated node, the displaced node's backlink clear. The
native-overlay adapter now asks the extended-node registry for a
side-effect-free plan covering the temporary marker, both metadata envelopes,
and both current backlink values, then checks every planned span through the
mapped writable-range boundary before invoking the transaction. A read-only
or sparse temporary/displaced node therefore tail-chains before any public
state can be published. Direct compatibility keeps its existing
write/rollback behavior, nodes without public backlinks remain
opaque-association compatible, and CyberGraphX/provider ownership is still
outside this standard boundary.

### G15/G25 native-overlay MakeVPort batch-state admission

MakeVPort replays an owned ColorMap's static `VideoControl` batch before it
enters the copper builder. The replay is transactional, but successful replay
publishes ColorMap scalar fields and can update associated guest state. The
native-overlay planner now resolves the owned batch map without replaying it
and preflights the complete `ColorMap` envelope alongside the four ViewPort
copper links. It also checks static command-buffer rewrites and immediate/
query output LONGs; association setters/getters remain provider-owned. A
read-only batch map or command buffer therefore tail-chains before allocation,
temporary `ViewPortExtra` publication, or display-provider entry; null,
foreign, and non-batch maps retain their existing compatibility/provider
boundaries.

### G14/G25 native-overlay VideoControl output admission

Direct `VideoControl` has two guest-visible output classes beyond ColorMap
state: classic GET tags are rewritten in place, and immediate/V40 query tags
write caller-supplied LONGs. Native-overlay admission now preflights the
ColorMap envelope plus those exact tag/output spans before the transaction.
Read-only outputs therefore tail-chain without changing tag bytes, palette
state, or the register frame; pointer-bearing association tags remain on the
native/provider boundary.

### G15/G18/G25 native-overlay display-query output admission

`GetDisplayInfoData` now has a side-effect-free output-length probe. The
native-overlay adapter resolves the public mode/handle and fixed chunk size
(`DTAG_DISP`, `DTAG_DIMS`, `DTAG_MNTR`, or `DTAG_NAME`) before entering the
database writer, then checks only the bounded bytes the caller's buffer can
actually receive. This keeps monitor-spec discovery out of a read-only
provider/image mapping and preserves the original register frame for the
resident/native vector. Unknown public tags, empty buffers, and the
`NULL`/`INVALID_ID` sentinel remain valid zero-byte results; `DTAG_VEC` stays
with the monitor-driver/provider boundary.

### G15/G18/G25 native-overlay monitor-query side-effect admission

`DTAG_MNTR` may lazily create a resident `MonitorSpec` and link it into the
native `GfxBase.MonitorList`. Native-overlay admission therefore checks the
full native GfxBase envelope before entering that query when a non-empty
monitor chunk is requested. A read-only native base tail-chains before
allocation or list publication. Zero-sized/NULL destination queries now stop
before building the monitor chunk, so they cannot create a resident monitor
for a no-write request; direct compatibility and already-resident monitor
queries retain their existing semantics.

### G15/G18/G25 native-overlay malformed MonitorList admission

`OpenMonitor` now distinguishes a compact compatibility image from a mapped
but malformed native `GfxBase.MonitorList`. The native-overlay adapter records
the discovered native base even when its list sentinels are invalid, probes the
mapped list fields before allocation, and tail-chains malformed resident state
without creating a temporary compatibility `MonitorSpec`. This preserves the
native/provider ownership boundary for CopperSharp68k-shaped images while
retaining the compatibility allocation path for zero-filled compact images.

### G06 line clipping/provider visibility admission

`Draw` checks the planar bitmap bounds before asking an optional layer-raster
visibility predicate to classify a sample. Off-raster Bresenham traversal still
advances the guest endpoint and line-pattern phase, but never probes or
delegates an impossible destination. Connected `COMPLEMENT` endpoint undo now
reuses the visibility result already admitted for the shared sample, keeping
provider clipping deterministic without moving layer ownership into
graphics.library.

### G04/G05 Text clipping/provider visibility admission

`Text` now follows the same bitmap-first admission boundary for glyph,
background, bold-smear, and underline samples. Off-raster text continues its
cursor and metric traversal, while preflight and publication skip provider
visibility classification and planar probes for cells outside the projected
bitmap. This keeps layer clipping/damage with the explicit provider and leaves
CyberGraphX as a separate patch surface.

### G08 layered ellipse clipping/provider visibility admission

`DrawEllipse` applies the planar bitmap envelope before consulting an explicit
layer-raster visibility predicate. A provider-backed outline skips midpoint
samples outside the backing bitmap, while in-bitmap samples retain the normal
visibility, plane-probe, snapshot, and rollback sequence. A direct non-layered
call still rejects an outline that leaves the bitmap, preserving the portable
no-clipping boundary. Layer damage and CyberGraphX ownership remain outside
graphics.library.

### G08 layered AreaEnd complement-outline provider admission

The closed-polygon `AreaEnd` outline path uses a single-cell `COMPLEMENT`
undo after the final connected `Draw`. That undo now accepts an explicit layer
visibility predicate, checks the planar bitmap envelope before invoking it, and
then uses the existing transactional planar writer. Ordinary public
`WritePixel` calls still require an unlayered RastPort; only the provider-backed
AreaEnd path can claim the extended boundary. This preserves provider damage
ownership and keeps CyberGraphX separate.

### G08 layered AreaEnd bitmap clipping/provider admission

The provider-backed `AreaEnd` path clips the decoded polygon/ellipse envelope
to the planar bitmap before destination preflight, temporary-mask publication,
and provider visibility admission. A shape may therefore cross the bitmap
edge while only in-bitmap cells reach the planar writer or layer predicate.
The direct path keeps its strict all-or-nothing bounds contract, and the
collector reset, snapshot rollback, and outline transaction remain shared.

### G06/G08 layered WritePixel clipping/provider pen admission

The explicit provider form of WritePixel now establishes the planar bitmap
boundary before loading public pen bytes. An off-raster cell is a valid -1
no-op, so a sparse/provider-owned FgPen or BPen field cannot steal the call and
the provider visibility predicate is not asked to classify a destination that
cannot reach the backing bitmap. The direct/core path keeps its historical pen
admission order; this remains a clipping/ownership seam, not an implicit layer
or CyberGraphX implementation.

### G06/G08 layered DrawEllipse hidden-outline pen admission

The explicit provider form of DrawEllipse now records whether any outline
sample survives the planar bitmap and provider visibility gates before loading
FgPen. A fully hidden outline is a successful clipped no-op that does not
consume sparse/provider-owned pen storage. Visible samples retain normal
foreground/complement selection and transactional planar publication, while
the direct path keeps its strict no-clipping contract. Layer damage and
CyberGraphX remain provider-owned.

### G05/G11 layered RectFill/BltPattern hidden-rectangle pen admission

The shared BltPattern path now checks an explicit provider visibility predicate
before resolving public foreground/background pens or decoding per-cell
area-pattern colour. RectFill therefore treats a fully hidden provider
rectangle as a successful clipped no-op without claiming sparse/provider-owned
pen storage. Visible pattern cells retain the existing draw-mode, mask,
snapshot, and rollback behavior; direct planar and CyberGraphX ownership stay
on their existing boundaries.

### G05/G08 layered Flood hidden-region pen admission

Layered Flood keeps its source connectivity walk independent from destination
publication, but now applies provider visibility before area-pattern decoding
and public pen admission. A fully hidden connected region is a successful
clipped no-op that does not consume sparse/provider-owned `FgPen` or `BgPen`
storage. Visible cells retain the existing temporary-raster, planar snapshot,
rollback, and direct ownership boundaries; CyberGraphX remains separate.

### G05/G11 layered BltTemplate hidden-sample pen admission

The portable BltTemplate path now resolves public foreground/background pens
only after a clipped template sample survives the explicit provider visibility
gate. Fully hidden templates are successful clipped no-ops without consuming
sparse/provider-owned colour storage. Visible JAM1/JAM2 and COMPLEMENT paths
retain their existing source decoding, planar preflight, snapshot, rollback,
and direct/CyberGraphX ownership boundaries.

### G07 layered ClearEOL/ClearScreen hidden-row pen admission

Provider-backed clear vectors now classify their full planar-visible envelope
before reading the clear pen, public FgPen/BPen, or reconstructing minterms. A
fully hidden text prefix and remaining-row set is a successful clipped no-op
that still publishes linpatcnt=15. Direct calls retain classic clear-pen
ordering and rollback; provider damage and CyberGraphX remain outside this
portable graphics contract.

### G07 layered ScrollRaster/ScrollRasterBF hidden-destination pen admission

Layered scroll vectors now establish their clipped destination visibility
before admitting BPen, FgPen, or minterm state. A hidden real move skips source
staging and planar writes but still resets linpatcnt; a zero-displacement
request remains a no-op. Visible source overlap, BF backfill, snapshots,
rollback, direct ownership, and CyberGraphX boundaries are unchanged.

### G06 layered PolyDraw hidden-destination pen admission

The connected PolyDraw preflight now uses its provider-visible destination
journal to decide whether public pen fields are needed. A fully hidden stream
still advances the guest cursor and line phase but does not read provider-owned
FgPen/BPen; direct/core eager admission, visible Draw publication, rollback, and
the separate CyberGraphX boundary remain intact.

### G08 layered AreaEnd hidden-shape pattern/pen admission

AreaEnd now decodes provider-backed geometry before admitting AreaPtrn/AreaPtSz
or public pen fields. If the shape envelope has no provider-visible
destination, it consumes the collector and returns clipped success without
temporary-raster ownership or planar publication. Visible pattern/outline
transactions, direct ordering, rollback, and CyberGraphX separation remain
unchanged.

### G05/G07 layered EraseRect hidden-rectangle pen admission

The layered EraseRect path now establishes the provider-visible destination
set before admitting public FgPen/BPen or reconstructing minterms. When that
set is empty, the operation is a successful clipped no-op that still publishes
the native line-pattern reset (linpatcnt=15). Visible and direct calls retain
the BPen-to-SetAPen/RectFill transaction, bitmap snapshots, rollback, and
separate CyberGraphX ownership boundary.

### G10/G11 layered bitmap-blit hidden-destination admission

The portable bitmap-blit family accepts an optional provider visibility
predicate. Fully hidden `BltBitMap`/`BltBitMapRastPort` requests complete with
their plane-count/BOOL result before source or destination plane admission;
fully hidden `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` requests similarly skip the external mask.
Partial visibility filters pixel staging, snapshots, and writes to visible
destination samples. Direct planar validation, overlap/TempA behavior, and
CyberGraphX/layer ownership remain separate.

### G19 layered pixel-array hidden-destination admission

The V36/V40 planar array writers accept an optional provider visibility
predicate. Fully hidden destinations complete with zero plotted samples before
array or planar admission. Partial visibility keeps complete source-array
staging for alias safety, while destination preflight, snapshots, and writes
are restricted to visible samples. The ordinary register ABI and explicit
CyberGraphX/layer provider boundary are unchanged.

### G11 layered `BltPattern` hidden-source admission

The portable `BltPattern` path treats provider visibility as the first source
ownership gate after the bitmap envelope. A fully hidden destination returns a
successful no-op before `AreaPtrn`, `AreaPtSz`, public pens, or external
stencil storage are admitted. A partially visible destination skips hidden
samples during stencil probing, planar preflight, snapshot, and publication,
while preserving the direct signed-WORD ABI and rollback behavior.

### G04/G05 layered hidden ColorTextFont admission

Layered `Text` has a second, source-neutral admission pass for ColorTextFont
requests. It walks metric glyph geometry and the styled destination envelope,
applies the bitmap bounds before invoking the provider visibility predicate,
and records whether any destination cell is visible. If none is visible, the
operation still decodes metric glyphs to advance `CurrentX` and publishes the
usual line-pattern/first-dot state, but it leaves color-font plane metadata,
strike storage, public pens, and planar writes to the provider boundary. A
visible or direct request follows the existing ColorTextFont validation,
strike preflight, rollback, and publication path; direct requests retain the
native/provider decision before unrelated draw-state reads.

### G04/G05 partial layered ColorTextFont source admission

For a partially visible layered ColorTextFont run, destination visibility is
also applied before each source-cell decode. The preflight and publication
passes skip hidden glyph rows, so a malformed or unmapped provider-owned color
plane outside the visible fragment cannot make an otherwise visible row fail.
Visible cells still require their complete `TryGetPixel`/planar probe contract;
direct calls retain whole-strike validation and the native/provider ordering.

### G17/G18 OCS/ECS double-buffer capability admission

`AllocDBufInfo` capability selection must share the display database's active
chipset availability rule. The portable database therefore accepts the active
PAL/NTSC profile and ECS-display capability as explicit inputs when deciding
whether a native mode's `DIPF_IS_DBUFFER` record is executable. OCS keeps ECS
SuperHires records queryable but declines double-buffer allocation for them;
ECS-capable hosts retain the standard DBufInfo path. CyberGraphX and foreign
monitor ownership remain outside this boundary.

### G17/G18 default DisplayInfo-handle capability admission

The zero-monitor default display record is exposed through a reserved
non-zero `FindDisplayInfo` handle because raw ModeID zero is also the public
NULL sentinel. Capability probes must normalize that handle before checking
`DIPF_IS_DBUFFER`; otherwise a valid default PAL/NTSC viewport can be denied
double buffering solely because its display state came through the
DisplayInfo handle path. The normalization shares the existing profile and
OCS/ECS availability checks, and does not claim unknown native/provider or
CyberGraphX handles.

### G04/G06 `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` complete-template text admission

`Text` treats `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` as a whole-template operation. The metric
pass computes the same styled `TextExtent` envelope used by JAM2, then the
portable planar writer applies `DrawModeComplement` once to every in-envelope
cell, including inter-character spacing and rows with no strike bits. It does
not resolve APen/BPen or read glyph strike bytes for this mode; metric glyphs
are sufficient for cursor movement and malformed/provider-owned strike storage
remains outside the portable ownership boundary. Direct calls and the
CopperStart register adapter share the same cursor/first-dot and transactional
publication contract, while CyberGraphX and foreign layer ownership remain
explicitly separate.

Evidence: `TextComplementJam2ComplementsTemplateWithoutReadingStrikeAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`;
the focused text family passes 53/53 and the complete scaffold passes 1415/1415.

### G11 `BltTemplate` source-free clipped no-op admission

`BltTemplate` resolves the RastPort layer before geometry so a validated
nonzero layer remains a provider boundary. For a zero or negative `SizeX` or
`SizeY`, the portable void path returns success immediately after that layer
check, without reading the template pointer, source offset, modulo, bitmap,
or pens. For a positive request it computes the clipped destination envelope
before admitting those source fields; a rectangle wholly outside the bitmap is
therefore also a source-free success. Requests with visible destination cells
retain the existing even-pointer/even-modulo source contract, `RPF_NO_PENS`
ownership check, complete source and destination preflight, and rollback.
The direct and CopperStart register paths share this ordering, while layered
providers and CyberGraphX remain outside the portable planar claim.

Evidence: `BltTemplateTreatsEmptyAndFullyClippedDestinationsAsSourceFreeNoOps`;
the focused `BltTemplate` family passes 21/21 and the complete scaffold passes
1416/1416.

### G11 `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` source-free empty admission

`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` is a documented void vector. Its portable admission
now resolves the RastPort layer first, then treats a non-positive requested
rectangle as a successful no-op before reading the source bitmap, destination
bitmap, external mask, or participating plane storage. A validated nonzero
layer remains a provider boundary; non-empty standard-planar calls retain the
existing external-mask, clipping, address-class, preflight, snapshot, and
rollback rules. The direct and CopperStart register paths share this ordering,
while CyberGraphX remains a separate ownership surface.

Evidence: `BltMaskBitMapRastPortTreatsEmptyRequestsAsSourceFreeNoOps`; the
focused masked-blit family passes 10/10.

### G09 null bitmap admission

`TryReadBitmapLayout` now rejects a zero guest address before probing its
geometry fields. This matters for CopperSharp68k-compatible memory adapters
that may map page zero: address `$0` is still the classic null BitMap
association, not a compact header that can be attached by `ChangeVPBitMap` or
used as a friend bitmap. The guard is deliberately local to the shared layout
reader, so valid standard and declared-depth compact headers retain their
existing field-level admission and CyberGraphX remains a separate provider
surface. `ChangeVPBitMap` therefore leaves the existing RasInfo link and the
native register frame untouched when passed a null replacement.

Evidence: `ChangeVPBitMapRejectsNullBitmapEvenWhenAddressZeroLooksLikeAHeader`.

### G15/G17 null ViewPort admission

`TryReadViewportRasInfo` now rejects a zero guest ViewPort before probing its
RasInfo and extended-mode fields. Address `$0` remains the native null display
object even when a CopperSharp68k-compatible or test memory adapter maps page
zero. The guard is intentionally local to the `ChangeVPBitMap` mutation
envelope, so legal `LoadView(NULL)` calls and assembling viewports retain their
existing lifecycle behavior. A rejected null ViewPort leaves the RasInfo
bitmap association and the native register frame untouched; CyberGraphX and
foreign monitor/provider ownership remain separate.

Evidence: `ChangeVPBitMapRejectsNullViewPortEvenWhenAddressZeroLooksLikeAnEnvelope`.

### G17 null ViewPort admission for timing and mode queries

The display-object null sentinel is enforced at every validator that requires
a concrete ViewPort, not only at the bitmap-swap mutation seam. `ScrollVPort`,
`WaitBOVP`, and direct/native `GetVPModeID` admission now reject address `$0`
before reading a page-zero envelope. This keeps a CopperSharp68k-compatible
memory adapter from turning a mapped zero page into a display callback or a
portable mode result, while null `RasInfo` during assembly and `LoadView(NULL)`
remain legal lifecycle states.

Evidence: `WaitBovpRejectsNullViewPortEvenWhenAddressZeroLooksLikeAnEnvelope`.

### G15/G16 `MrgCop` malformed-status admission

`MrgCop` has a result-bearing portable boundary even though its classic ABI is
void-shaped to callers. A structurally malformed `View` produces the internal
`GraphicsRasterOperations.Failure` sentinel; the CopperStart adapter must not
claim that result or overwrite D0. Returning `false` preserves the original
register frame and lets a captured native Kickstart vector or explicit
provider decide ownership. Valid `MCOP_NOP`, `MCOP_OK`, and other non-negative
status-aware results remain claimed and are published in D0. This keeps the
CopperSharp68k guest layout and the CopperScreen host overlay on one admission
contract without conflating malformed portable input with a completed merge.

Evidence: `MrgCopRejectsNullViewBeforeAZeroPageEnvelopeCanReachCopper`,
`MrgCopRejectsAnExtraRasInfoPlayfieldBeforeCopperMerge`, and
`RomOverlayDeclinesTheMrgCopFailureForAnExtraRasInfoPlayfield`; the complete
scaffold passes 1,421/1,421, the `CopperStartIntuitionLifecycleTests` slice
passes 28/28, the `AmigaBootMemoryTests` slice passes 313/313, both affected
projects build with 0 warnings and 0 errors, and `git diff --check` exits 0
apart from existing line-ending notices.

### G03/G04 `TextFit` alternate-constraint selection

`TextFit` now follows the Kickstart 3.1 contract that the explicit
`constrainingExtent` pointer and the D2/D3 rendering-box dimensions are
alternative forms. When A3 is nonzero, the portable metric walk uses only the
explicit origin-relative rectangle; D2/D3 are ignored, even when their UWORD
values are outside 0..32767. The documented range and minimum-font-height
shortcut remain active for the alternate (A3 == NULL) form. This keeps the
CopperSharp68k guest ABI, direct register adapter, and CopperScreen ROM overlay
on one result/ownership boundary without imposing a host-only dual constraint.

Evidence: `TextExtentFontExtentAndTextFitWriteGuestTextExtentStructures` and
`NativeOverlayAndHostGatewayPreserveProportionalMetricParity`; the complete
graphics scaffold passes 1,421/1,421.

### G15/G17 hidden-node chain traversal layout parity (2026-08-18)

The host `RethinkDisplay` and publication-fingerprint walks now use the shared
`GraphicsModeIds.ViewPortHidden` contract instead of duplicating the numeric
`VP_HIDE` literal. The hidden-payload regression includes a later visible
ViewPort, proving that the `Modes`/`Next` filter skips only hidden payload and
still reaches the visible node's normal admission path. CopperSharp68k guest
layout and CopperScreen host lifecycle therefore share one constant and walk.

Evidence: `LoadViewSkipsMalformedPayloadBehindHiddenViewPortAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`;
focused lifecycle tests pass 21/21 and the complete graphics scaffold passes
1,430/1,430.

### G15/G17 ViewPort envelope uses the shared guest layout size (2026-08-18)

The host `RethinkDisplay`/`MrgCop` admission and copper-list builder now use
`GraphicsLayouts.ViewPortSize` for mapped ViewPort envelopes instead of a
duplicated byte count. This keeps the host lifecycle and the future
CopperSharp68k guest layout on the same structure-size contract while leaving
hidden-node payload ownership and CyberGraphX/provider handoff unchanged.

Evidence: the hidden-head/visible-tail `MrgCop` regression and the hidden-node
`LoadView` regression pass through direct and mapped paths; the focused
lifecycle subset passes 3/3 and the compiled graphics scaffold remains
1,430/1,430. The normal emulator build is still blocked only by the unrelated
`IIntuitionPlatform.NextObject(APTR)` mismatch.

### G07/G27 layered `ScrollRaster` visibility transaction consistency (2026-08-18)

The shared `ScrollRaster`/`ScrollRasterBF` implementation now memoizes each
in-bitmap provider visibility decision across destination admission, source
staging, destination probes, rollback snapshot, publication, and BF backfill
`EraseRect` calls. Source reads remain independent of layer clipping; direct
scroll phase and BPen semantics, CopperScreen damage ownership, and
CyberGraphX/RTG boundaries remain unchanged.

Evidence: `LayeredScrollRasterReusesVisibilityAcrossStagingProbeSnapshotAndPublication`;
the focused ScrollRaster family passes 22/22 and the complete graphics
scaffold passes 1,440/1,440. The source build used the existing temporary

`IIntuitionPlatform.NextObject(APTR)` mismatch.

### G07 layered `ClearScreen` visibility transaction consistency (2026-08-18)

Layered `ClearScreen` now shares one provider visibility cache across its text
prefix and remaining-row admission regions, outer rollback snapshot, and both
nested `RectFill` publications. This preserves the all-or-nothing clear and
line-state transition while keeping off-raster cells and provider-owned
damage/RTG behavior outside the portable graphics path.

Evidence: `LayeredClearScreenReusesVisibilityAcrossBothRegionsAndPublication`;
the focused layered ClearScreen family passes 3/3 and the complete graphics
scaffold passes 1,439/1,439. The source build used the existing temporary
compile-only Intuition interface shim, removed before verification; a normal
emulator build remains blocked by the unrelated
`IIntuitionPlatform.NextObject(APTR)` mismatch.

### G07 layered `ClearEOL` visibility transaction consistency (2026-08-18)

Layered `ClearEOL` now caches each in-bitmap provider visibility result across
its visible admission, outer rollback snapshot, and nested `RectFill`
publication. The clear's line-state transition and pen/minterm rollback stay
unchanged, while off-raster cells remain outside the provider boundary and
CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remains explicit.

Evidence: `LayeredClearEolReusesVisibilityAcrossAdmissionSnapshotAndPublication`;
the focused layered ClearEOL family passes 3/3 and the complete graphics
scaffold passes 1,438/1,438. The source build used the existing temporary
compile-only Intuition interface shim, removed before verification; a normal

`IIntuitionPlatform.NextObject(APTR)` mismatch.

### G05/G07 layered `SetRast` visibility transaction consistency (2026-08-18)

Layered `SetRast` now reuses each in-bitmap provider visibility decision
between its visible snapshot and publication walk. A stateful clip therefore

### G17/G25 active RTG blank-display handoff (2026-08-18)

`LoadView(NULL)` remains a portable blank-display operation when the active

filter passes 1,471/1,471 and the portable scaffold passes 1,450/1,450.

The active-view `MrgCop` host handoff now reclassifies the public

### G12 timed `OwnBlitter`/`WaitBlit` software ownership boundary (2026-08-18)

The timed CopperStart blitter scheduler now treats `OwnBlitter` as the
software ownership gate, not as a BBUSY poll. A caller may acquire ownership
while a previous owner's custom-chip blit is still draining and must then use
`WaitBlit` before touching blitter registers, matching the Kickstart contract
documented by the [OwnBlitter autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0466.html).
`WaitBlit` uses the bus's canonical DMA drain through the predicted completion
boundary and fails closed if BBUSY remains asserted, instead of claiming a
completion from the scalar synchronization shortcut that can stop before a
live-slot transition.

Evidence: `CopperStartBlitterSchedulerOwnBlitterAcquiresBeforePreviousBlitFinishes`
starts a real A-only custom-chip blit, acquires the software gate before BBUSY
clears, waits, verifies completion and destination memory, and disowns at the
reported cycle. The complete `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests` class
passes 1,451/1,451; the focused CopperStart scheduler family passes 8/8.
The complete `FullyQualifiedName~Graphics` filter passes 1,472/1,472.
Exact native 68k wait-loop timing, queued QBlit arbitration, and full
CopperSharp68k differential parity remain open gates.

### G26 native 68k RastPort state-body slice (2026-08-18)

The native-ROM path now has a small, relocatable body packer for the public
RastPort pen and draw-mode state vectors: `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`,
`SetABPenDrMd`, `GetAPen`, `GetBPen`, and `GetDrMd`. Each body uses only the
documented guest `RastPort` offsets, returns the same zero-extended getter or
void-setter register shape as the portable adapter, and leaves all other
public/reserved vectors pointed at a shared `RTS` fallback. The code stream is
therefore usable by the existing relocatable HUNK builder without host object
addresses or a second layout definition.

Evidence: `NativeGraphicsRasterBodiesExecutePenAndModeStateVectors` loads the
relocatable HUNK, enters each vector through its generated `JMP.L`, executes
the emitted M68000 instructions, and verifies guest bytes and D0. Full native
raster drawing, validation before entry, and native/provider timing remain
later G26/G27 gates.

### G26 native `Move` body extension (2026-08-18)

The native state-body slice now also emits `Move`. Its M68000 body writes the
new signed cursor coordinates, restarts `linpatcnt` at 15, preserves unrelated
`RastPort.Flags` bits while setting `FRST_DOT`, and returns a void-shaped zero
in D0. This keeps the native body aligned with the portable `Move` transaction
and the shared guest layout rather than introducing a host-only cursor path.

Evidence: the extended `NativeGraphicsRasterBodiesExecutePenAndModeStateVectors`
fixture enters `Move` through its generated vector, verifies cursor/phase/flag
publication, and checks that unrelated flag bits survive. Full native Draw,
line-pattern execution, pre-entry validation, and provider timing remain open.

### G26 native pen/mask extension (2026-08-18)

The same native body packer now emits `SetWriteMask`, `GetOutlinePen`, and
`SetOutlinePen`. `SetWriteMask` narrows the ULONG input to the public Mask byte
and returns the void-vector zero shape. `GetOutlinePen` zero-extends AOlPen.
`SetOutlinePen` preserves the new pen in a scratch register, returns the old
pen in D0, publishes the new byte, and sets `AREAOUTLINE` without disturbing
the other Flags bits. All three entries remain relocatable guest code and all
unimplemented vectors still use the explicit RTS fallback.

Evidence: the extended accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture verifies mask publication,
outline-pen replacement, previous-pen return, `AREAOUTLINE` publication, and
the getter. Native Draw/line-pattern execution, pre-entry validation, provider
handoff, and exact ROM timing remain open.

### G26 native `SetMaxPen` body extension (2026-08-18)

`SetMaxPen` is now emitted as a compact 68000 loop. A zero request takes the
field-free no-op path; nonzero input is reduced to a contiguous low-bit mask by
shifting a scratch copy and publishing the result to `RastPort.Mask`. The body
clears D0 on both paths and remains a relocatable vector entry. The portable
adapter's range and provider validation still run at the host/native boundary;
the body itself follows the validated native call contract.

Evidence: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture covers zero/no-write, one, three,
and 0xFF mask requests. Native Draw/line-pattern execution, pre-entry
validation, provider handoff, and exact ROM timing remain open.

### G26 native `InitRastPort` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native body packer now emits `InitRastPort`. It validates a non-null, even,
non-wrapping `RastPortMinimumSize` envelope before clearing the complete public
`0xB4`-byte RastPort prefix with 45 longword stores driven by a 68000 `DBRA`
loop. It then publishes the classic no-font
mask, pen, draw-mode, line-pattern, and minterm defaults, and reads
`GfxBase->DefaultFont` through A6 when present. A valid default font's public
YSize, XSize, and Baseline are copied into the cached RastPort metrics and
`AlgoStyle` is reset; a zero default follows the no-font path. Malformed
descriptors preserve D0 through the explicit RTS fallback.

Evidence: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture exercises both the populated and
zero `DefaultFont` branches, verifies cleared tail bytes through offset `0xB3`,
and covers null/odd/wrapped descriptor declines. Native
font-list validation, provider handoff, and exact ROM timing remain open.

### G17/G26 native `InitView`/`InitVPort` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native body packer now emits the pure guest-memory lifecycle constructors
`InitView` and `InitVPort`. Each validates a non-null, even, non-wrapping public
descriptor envelope before clearing it. `InitView` then publishes the standard
DY/DX origin words; `InitVPort` publishes the documented sprite-priority byte.
Both return the classic void-vector D0 shape and leave copper/display scheduling
to the later native lifecycle gates.

Evidence: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture executes both generated vector
entries, verifies cleared links/origin/default fields and D0, and proves
null/odd/wrapped descriptor declines. Native display publication, copper
timing, provider handoff, and exact ROM timing remain open.

### G09/G26 native `InitBitMap`/`InitTmpRas` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native constructor cluster now includes `InitBitMap` and `InitTmpRas`.
`InitBitMap` validates a non-null, even, non-wrapping eight-byte descriptor,
accepts only the standard OCS/ECS depth range 1..8 and a width safe for its
native WORD arithmetic, then computes the documented word-rounded BytesPerRow,
publishes rows, standard flags, depth, and the zero pad without touching
caller-owned plane links. `InitTmpRas` validates a non-null, even,
non-wrapping eight-byte descriptor envelope before storing only the descriptor's
backing pointer and byte count; it does not dereference the caller-owned scratch
span. Both bodies preserve the void-vector D0 result shape and remain
independent of host allocation.

Evidence: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture verifies 320-pixel geometry,
untouched plane links, temporary-raster descriptor publication, null/odd/
wrapped descriptor declines, and InitBitMap depth/width declines. Native
provider validation, allocator ownership, and exact ROM timing remain open.

### G09/G26 native `InitArea` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native constructor cluster now includes `InitArea`. Its M68000 body clears
the public AreaInfo descriptor, derives the flag-table address as
`buffer + maxVectors * 4`, publishes both table/pointer pairs, resets the
count and first point, and retains the caller-owned coordinate/flag storage
untouched. A signed-negative `MAXVECTORS` word declines before the first
descriptor write and preserves D0 through the shared RTS fallback. The body
follows the classic void-vector D0 result shape and keeps all remaining vectors
on the explicit RTS fallback.

Evidence: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture verifies a four-vector descriptor,
the derived flag-table pointer, zeroed counters/first point, unchanged backing
storage, and the negative-capacity no-write decline. Provider handoff and exact
ROM timing remain open.

### G03/G04/G26 native fixed-metric `TextLength` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native body packer now emits a guarded `TextLength` entry for fixed metrics.

implementation.

Evidence: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture covers positive and negative
spacing, selected fixed-cell XSize arithmetic, proportional-font fallback, and
odd/wrapping font declines through
`NativeGraphicsTextMetricsGuardSelectedTextFontEnvelopeOnAccurateM68000`. Full
native variable-width metrics, glyph rendering, provider handoff, and exact ROM
timing remain open.

### G09/G26 native guarded `ReadPixel` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native body packer now emits a guarded `ReadPixel` implementation for the

### G07/G26 native guarded `SetRast` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native body packer now emits a standard-planar `SetRast` implementation

### G05/G07/G26 native guarded `Draw` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native body packer now emits a conservative fresh-line `Draw` body for
forward or reverse horizontal and vertical lines on a one-plane standard
bitmap. It requires `FRST_DOT` and one of the implicit-source modes 0/1/2/3/4/5.
All-ones patterns and non-inverse JAM1 patterns are sampled in the native

current cursor. Sloped Bresenham lines, connected endpoints,
`COMPLEMENT|INVERSVID` modes 6/7, patterned JAM2/inverse lines, and
provider/layer surfaces remain on the shared fallback. `ONE_DOT`/`SING` is
also deliberately declined at native admission so row-suppression and
single-dot phase semantics remain owned by the portable implementation.

Evidence: the accurate-M68000 HUNK fixture covers forward and reverse
horizontal and vertical publication, pattern-phase/cursor/flag updates,
inverse JAM1 no-op, JAM2 background publication, and forward/reverse
`COMPLEMENT` toggles; the combined inverse/complement fallback remains
covered, including an explicit `ONE_DOT` admission/fallback regression.
Clipping, connected-line ownership, remaining patterned JAM2/inverse
and minterm semantics, provider handoff, and exact ROM timing remain open.

### G03/G05/G07/G26 native guarded `Text` body extension (2026-08-19)

The native body packer now emits a deliberately narrow fixed-cell text path.
It first requires a non-NULL, even, non-wrapping TextFont public prefix, then

forms (including the complete JAM2 cell), and verifies combined inverse/

### G19/G26 native `ScalerDiv` arithmetic body (2026-08-19)

## G15/G17 native Exec-backed display-resource teardown ownership unit (2026-08-25)

The native screen/view allocator now has a paired private teardown body. The
allocator tags its public `CopList.System` with the allocated `Screen` and

shared raw stream, and the marker before any write or `FreeMem` call.

On success it clears the public links and releases SHF CprList, LOF CprList,
CopList, raw copper, plane, RasInfo, View, and Screen in reverse acquisition
order, returning `D0=1`. Wrong markers, foreign/provider objects, malformed
or split topology, odd/wrapped pointers, and size failures discard the private
frame and return `D0=0` without freeing anything. The body is a private
non-LVO seam for a future native `OpenScreen`/`CloseScreen` owner; public
Intuition activation, hardware display-DMA publication, general copper merge,
provider/RTG ownership, and CyberGraphX remain separate boundaries.

## G16/G26 native one-slot `UCopperListInit`/`FreeCopList` ownership unit

publishes the standard `CopIns`, `CopPtr`, `Count=0`, and `MaxCount=1` fields.
It records the user-list link and a private native ownership marker in the
paired `CopList` envelope. The two allocations are transactional: a failed
second allocation frees the first block and every declined path keeps the
caller's original D0.

`FreeCopList` claims only the marker/link/resource envelope emitted by that
native arm (plus the classic NULL no-op). It frees `CopIns` first, clears the
three public `UCopList` links, then frees `CopList`, and returns zero. Foreign,
already-linked, malformed, larger-count, provider-owned, and CyberGraphX
forms remain with the portable/provider owner; this prevents the native arm
from freeing memory it did not allocate. The code uses only guest-relative
68000 moves, relative branches, and the Exec vector ABI, so the bounded form
has the same CopperSharp68k ROM and CopperScreen native-overlay layout.

## G03/G04 native exact `WeighTAMatch` metric admission

The native `WeighTAMatch` vector now owns one allocation-free metric form:
`A0` and `A1` point at complete, even eight-byte `TextAttr` records, `A2` is
NULL, and YSize, Style, and Flags match bit-for-bit. The exact untagged pair
returns Kickstart's maximum match weight (`32767`) without reading either
name pointer or walking a tag list. This keeps the body a small guest-relative
68000 unit suitable for both a CopperSharp68k ROM image and the CopperScreen
native overlay.

Tagged DPI attributes, non-NULL target tags, metric mismatches, null/odd/
wrapping envelopes, provider-owned fonts, and CyberGraphX forms restore the
incoming D0 and remain owned by the portable/provider matcher. The native arm
therefore publishes no partial score and does not claim the richer
size/style/source ordering implemented by the host lifecycle.

## G03/G04 native resident-default `OpenFont` admission

The native `OpenFont` vector now owns an allocation-free resident form for
future native text initialization. It validates an ordinary eight-byte
`TextAttr`, a valid graphics base, and a complete resident `TextFont` envelope;
then it matches the name pointer identity plus `ta_YSize`, `ta_Style`, and
`ta_Flags`. On an exact match it increments `tf_Accessors` without wrapping and
returns the resident font pointer.

This deliberately does not walk name strings or tagged `TTextAttr`/DPI lists.
Those forms, non-default resident fonts, malformed envelopes, missing defaults,
allocation, and provider-owned fonts preserve D0 and remain with the portable
font lifecycle owner. The body uses only guest-relative 68000 operations and
therefore has the same CopperSharp68k ROM and CopperScreen overlay layout.

## G03/G04 native resident-default `CloseFont` admission

The native `CloseFont` companion claims the resident-default pointer already
validated by the graphics base. `CloseFont(NULL)` remains an idempotent success;
for a non-null exact default font, a complete envelope is checked, an accessor
count above zero is decremented, and a zero count is left unchanged. No list
unlink or extension teardown is attempted.

Foreign pointers, missing/odd/wrapping graphics bases or default fonts, and
provider-owned or removable fonts preserve D0 and fall through to the portable
owner. This keeps native text teardown safe while retaining the classic
CopperSharp68k guest layout and the host overlay's richer lifecycle path.

This is deliberately a scalar query slice: multi-tag traversal, other pen or
mode queries, DrawBounds, font/style lookup, and exact CopperSharp68k timing
remain separate units.

and the complete graphics scaffold passes 1499/1499 in
`TestResults/getrpattrs-scaffold/getrpattrs-scaffold.trx`.

`SetFont(NULL)` form. After the tag-list, RastPort, and selected A6 library-base

### G01/G26 native guarded `Text` fixed-cell default glyph slot (2026-08-20)

The native `Text` body now follows the classic fixed-cell fallback slot for
bytes outside the declared `LoChar..HiChar` range. The existing admitted form
is deliberately eight pixels wide in one standard planar bitmap, with NULL
`CharLoc`, `CharSpace`, and `CharKern` tables; the native renderer synthesizes
the bit offset from `tf_XSize` and the row stride from `tf_Modulo`. The new
dispatch validates `LoChar <= HiChar` before touching the destination, then
maps either below-range or above-range source bytes to table index
`(HiChar-LoChar)+1`, the extra default cell. In-range bytes retain their
existing direct index. JAM, inverse, complement, cursor, and line-pattern
publication are unchanged, and malformed, styled, variable-width, clipped,
layered, RTG, and provider-owned forms remain on their prior owner boundary.

This keeps the native path compatible with CopperSharp68k's guest `TextFont`
layout without introducing host-side font metadata or CyberGraphX behavior.

passes 1/1 in

`TestResults/text-native-regression/text-native-regression.trx`;

### G07/G11/G26 native guarded `BltPattern` aligned multi-row form (2026-08-20)

The native `BltPattern` body now extends its source-free aligned arm from the
single row `x=0..7, y=0` case to the bounded standard-planar rectangle
`x=0..7, y=0..yMax`. The dispatch reads the declared `Rows` field and rejects
`yMax >= Rows` before loading the plane pointer for publication. After the
existing no-mask, no-AreaPtrn, ordinary-JAM1, non-layered, depth-one, even
BytesPerRow, and bounded-plane checks, APen bit zero selects either `0xFF` or
`0x00`; a zero-extended BytesPerRow advances the plane pointer between rows.
The void D0 ABI remains unchanged: native success returns zero and all guarded
failures restore the incoming D0 to the existing provider/fallback tail.

This deliberately does not decode AreaPtrn or external masks, clip, traverse
layers, claim interleaved or RTG storage, or alter CyberGraphX ownership.

Evidence: `NativeGraphicsBltPatternPublishesAlignedAllOnRowsWithinBitmapOnAccurateM68000`
and the existing native source-free cases pass 3/3 in
`TestResults/bltpattern-multirow-final4/bltpattern-multirow-final4.trx`;

### G03/G26 native guarded proportional `TextExtent` reverse one-glyph movement envelope (2026-08-20)

The native `TextExtent` selector now has a bounded reverse proportional arm for
one source byte. It requires `FPF_PROPORTIONAL|FPF_REVPATH`, zero text and
algorithmic styles, complete even table spans, and a negative selected
`CharSpace + CharKern + TxSpacing` cell. The body publishes the signed movement
in Width and MinX, sets MaxX to `-1`, and retains the selected font's ordinary
baseline-relative vertical rectangle.

The extent pointer is saved before any late table or metric check, so every
decline restores the caller's D0 and leaves the twelve-byte result untouched.
Counts above one, nonnegative movement, reverse glyph geometry, styled fonts,
provider/RTG/CyberGraphX ownership, and exact CopperSharp68k timing remain on
their existing owners.

### G03/G26 native guarded proportional `TextExtent` bounded movement envelope (2026-08-20)

The native `TextExtent` body now has a relocatable proportional metric arm for
forward counts of one through eight. It preflights the source bytes, the
twelve-byte destination, and the complete even/non-wrapping `CharLoc`,
`CharSpace`, and `CharKern` table spans, including the extra default slot.

The admitted form excludes reverse-path and algorithmic-style fonts, negative
spacing or table movement, zero/reverse accumulated movement, malformed
objects, and provider/RTG/CyberGraphX ownership. It sums the selected
declared/default table entries with `TxSpacing`, then publishes a movement-cell
width and the selected font's height/baseline rectangle only after the entire
walk succeeds. Every decline restores the incoming D0 and leaves the result
envelope untouched.

This unit does not claim glyph-ink bounds, leading-negative-kern compatibility,
reverse-path behavior, larger strings, or exact ROM timing; those remain

### G03/G26 native guarded fixed-cell `FontExtent` bounded declared range (2026-08-20)

### G03/G26 native guarded proportional `TextLength` bounded forward walk (2026-08-20)

The native body now has a small, independently guarded multi-character arm.
Counts 2 through 8 are admitted only after checking that the text pointer and
the complete declared range plus one default WORD slot are addressable. Each
byte selects `2*(character-LoChar)` when declared and
`2*(HiChar-LoChar+1)` otherwise. CharSpace and CharKern are read as signed
WORDS; `TxSpacing` is sign-extended and added for every character. A negative
kern is omitted only for the first glyph, matching the portable forward metric
contract; subsequent signed kern values are retained.

The arm keeps its scratch state in relocatable 68k registers, returns the
accumulated movement in D0, and declines to the existing D0-preserving owner
for all malformed envelopes, counts outside the bound, reverse-path/richer
font forms, provider/RTG ownership, and CyberGraphX. This makes the unit
compatible with a future native CopperSharp68k ROM without forcing host-only
state into the guest ABI.

### G03/G26 native guarded proportional `TextLength` declared/default glyph slot (2026-08-20)

The one-glyph proportional native arm now selects the metric slot from the
guest character. After validating `LoChar <= HiChar`, it treats bytes inside
the declared range as index `character-LoChar`, and bytes below or above the
range as the documented extra default index `(HiChar-LoChar)+1`. The index is
converted to a WORD offset and added to both `CharSpace` and `CharKern` only
after each pointer passes the non-NULL/even test.

Each table addition rejects address carry and any resulting base above
`$FFFFFFFE`, so the selected signed WORD remains wholly addressable. The
existing D0 shadow still restores the complete incoming value for reversed
ranges, unsupported counts, richer proportional strings, malformed tables,
and provider/RTG/CyberGraphX ownership. The successful result remains the
signed table sum plus `RastPort.TxSpacing`; full walks, reverse-path movement,
rendering, and proportional extent/fit/font metrics remain outside this native
slice.

### G10/G26 native guarded `ReadPixelLine8` second-row span (2026-08-20)

The native line-reader arm now covers the smallest non-origin planar span that
can be proved without taking ownership from the portable/provider path. It
accepts an even, bounded RastPort and one-plane BitMap with `BytesPerRow=2`,
`Rows=1 or 2`, `x=0`, and a width from one through eight. Y is copied into a
zero-extended scratch value before D1 is reused for the width. Y zero permits
the existing one-row `ReadPixelArray8` form; Y one requires two rows and adds
one byte stride word to the plane base through a separate address scratch.

relocatable range guard: an out-of-range branch to the shared offset-zero RTS
gets a local RTS copy at the construction frontier. This preserves the
fallback's exact terminal behavior without adding an absolute code relocation;
nonzero targets still fail fast if they cannot be represented by Bcc.W.

### G05/G07 native guarded fixed-cell `Text` spacing-eight JAM1 extension (2026-08-20)

The native fixed-cell `Text` body now admits one additional spacing cell:
`RastPort.TxSpacing=8` with JAM1. Because the glyph width is eight pixels,
the extra spacing keeps the strike byte-aligned. The native loop therefore
adds one byte to its destination walk and sixteen pixels to the cursor for
each glyph, while the zero-spacing form retains its existing eight-pixel
advance. A JAM2 spacing cell would require publishing the intervening BPen
template byte, so non-JAM1 spacing remains on the portable/provider owner.

The admission does not widen any font, bitmap, layer, clipping, proportional,
complement/inverse, RTG, or CyberGraphX claims. It remains a compact
CopperSharp68k-compatible guest-memory body with the same D0, line-pattern,
and first-dot publication rules as the prior fixed-cell path.

representable-storage, draw-mode, mask, and clipping gates. `(1,13)` and all

forms remain on their prior owners. Each point now forms the candidate plane
address in a data register, compares it against the original plane base, and
only then copies it to A3, because 68000 `ADD.L` to an address register does
not update CCR. This keeps the native pointer guard cycle-accurate while
preserving the wrapped-pointer fallback boundary. At the 2026-08-20
checkpoint, the next generated Y cell was deliberately deferred until a
stream-wide 68000 trampoline/relocation map existed; the local DrawEllipse
islands were not enough once downstream `PolyDraw` branches were also moved
by the larger stream.

## Native branch relaxation and the `(1,13)` continuation (2026-08-21)

The deferred `(1,13)` cell is now admitted through marker 20. Its generated
point body emits the fifty-two-point `(0,13)` through `(1,0)` midpoint walk,
while the existing one-plane, non-layered, representable-storage, JAM1/
COMPLEMENT/zero-mask contract remains unchanged. `(1,14)` and richer forms
still restore the incoming void-vector D0 and remain on the shared owner.

The stream now has a reusable `AppendBranchIsland` primitive for short,
relocatable `BRA.W` hops. The current long-edge topology is deliberately
positioned rather than absolute:

- a target-side island sits beside the native `Draw` entry;
- DrawEllipse has dispatch-side and tail-side relays for the `PolyDraw` BSR;
- a point-sequence-done island receives the early radius-one completion arms;
- a success island receives early zero-mask exits; and
- midpoint and tail fallback islands preserve D0 restoration before the
  shared offset-zero RTS.

Every hop is a signed-word displacement from the extension word, so copied
HUNK code remains relocatable. The `PolyDraw` call remains a real BSR: the
relay chain uses BRA.W only after the return address has been pushed, and the
native Draw wrapper still returns through the caller's stack frame. No host
address, absolute JMP, or CyberGraphX dependency is introduced.

This is the first stream-wide branch-relaxation seam. Future large native
units should route their cross-fragment edges through the same stream-level
allocator; the next expansion gate is to add explicit fragment-boundary
placement to its range-audited reservations so a unit cannot accidentally
create an unrelaxed Bcc.W edge in another body.

Current-source AccurateM68000 execution proves `(1,13)`, the existing `(4,1)`
ellipse path, and the long `PolyDraw` one-step diagonal path all return with
the expected planar bytes. The formal xUnit/native/scaffold rerun remains
pending the unrelated Layers/CopperSharp project-reference conflict in the
full emulator build.

## Construction-time branch range audit (2026-08-21)

The native builder now has a non-ABI diagnostics overload. It records every
patched branch displacement and counts uses of the reusable relay helper while
the stream is being constructed. The normal `BuildCode` overload discards the
audit, so the HUNK image and its entry offsets are unchanged. Focused tests can
request the audit and assert that every signed-word edge stays inside the
68000 `Bcc.W`/`BRA.W` range. Each record retains the extension offset, resolved
target offset, and final displacement, which is the input needed by the future
fragment-boundary allocator.

The current-source build reports 4,456 patched branches, nine helper-created
relays, nine word-aligned fragment boundaries, a minimum displacement of
-28,268, a maximum of 32,514, and a maximum absolute displacement of 32,514
for the 60,844-byte stream. The Draw target
and DrawEllipse relays are now emitted through one fixed-width reservation
helper; their targets are patched after the surrounding point template has
been laid out, and they are covered by the same `PatchBranch` audit. A
stream-level linker rejects duplicate or missing links, audits each named
boundary, and owns the checked
`(4,1)` multi-hop chain. This keeps range validation construction-local and
leaves a clear seam for the allocator's next fragment-placement slice rather
than relying on a hand-maintained distance table.

The linker also supports a checked multi-hop chain: every hop is preflighted
against the signed-word range, every reserved relay is verified before any
reservation is consumed, each intermediate `BRA.W` is patched to the next
island, and the final hop is patched to the target label. The existing `(4,1)`
path now uses this chain API, making intermediate fragment islands an explicit
future extension point without leaving a partially linked route on failure.

A controlled `(1,14)` expansion was not retained: the audit stopped it at the
first unrelaxed point-dispatch edge (`7740 -> 41142`, displacement `33402`) and
the early fallback edge (`6244 -> 39174`, displacement `32930`). The native
contract therefore remains explicitly bounded at `(1,13)` until the allocator
can reserve relays at intermediate fragment boundaries.

and absent resources restore D0 and remain available to the complete

synthesize DIW/DDF/bitplane registers, activate display DMA, or claim

raw-list, and display publication; a future native allocator ABI can replace

NULL. Kickstart's portable validator reports `MVP_NO_VPE` (`2`) before any
temporary `ViewPortExtra` or copper allocation in this assembling state, so
the native body can publish the same status without mutating guest memory.

The body still declines detached View/ViewPort pairs, odd or wrapped bases,
nonzero extended-mode state, and every resource-bearing form (`vp_RasInfo !=
NULL`). Those cases preserve the caller's D0 and remain with the existing
portable/provider owner, which keeps native CopperSharp68k layout separate
from host allocation and CopperScreen display projection. CyberGraphX is not
referenced.

AccurateM68000 coverage is provided by
`NativeGraphicsMakeVPortUnassembledViewportReturnsNoViewPortExtraOnAccurateM68000`;
the focused MakeVPort group passes `2/2`, and the complete graphics scaffold

the generated body remains relative-only and host-pointer-free.

## G15/G17 native resident-default `OpenMonitor` admission

The native public vector now owns one deliberately small lifecycle form:
`A1=0` (no monitor name), `D0=GraphicsModeIds.Invalid` (the default selector),
and `A6` addressing a valid graphics-library base whose resident
`GfxBase.defaultMonitor` points at a complete, even `MonitorSpec` envelope.
The body validates both address spans, rejects a saturated open count, increments
the resident count in place, and returns the resident pointer in D0. It performs
no allocation, list publication, or provider lookup, so the layout is directly
usable in a CopperSharp68k ROM image and remains relocatable in the CopperScreen
native overlay.

Named monitors, explicit PAL/NTSC or foreign display IDs, absent or malformed
library/monitor envelopes, and open-count saturation preserve the original D0
and fall through to the portable lifecycle owner. That boundary leaves full
allocation/name/provider and future CyberGraphX admission outside this native
unit while making the resident default usable by a future native `OpenScreen`
owner.

## G15/G17 native Exec-backed `AllocRaster`/`FreeRaster` ownership unit

The native raster lifecycle now has a paired, relocatable 68000 arm for the
classic UWORD/UWORD `AllocRaster` and `FreeRaster` vectors. `AllocRaster`
rounds width to complete words, multiplies by height, adds a private ten-byte
ownership header, and calls Exec `AllocMem` with `PUBLIC | CHIP | CLEAR`.
The returned PLANEPTR is the first payload byte after that header, so callers
see the normal word-addressed raster layout. The header stores a private
marker, the original dimensions, and the exact allocation span.

`FreeRaster` subtracts the private header only after rejecting null, odd,
short, zero-dimension, and mismatched requests. It checks the marker and

## G16 native generic `FreeVPortCopLists` teardown design (2026-08-28)

The native teardown counterpart uses a bounded two-pass 68k walker for a
canonical post-`MrgCop` visible chain. Pass one preserves incoming D0 and the
head pointer, validates every terminal standard-planar ViewPort/RasInfo/CopList
envelope, counts nodes, and records the first merged raw stream and CopList. A
nonterminal thirty-third node (including a repeated pointer) is declined before
the commit pass. It then checks that the first Count is `12 * N`, first
MaxCount is at least `12 * N - 1`, its final terminator is at `48 * N - 4`,
and every retained source has Count 12, MaxCount at least 12, and its 44-byte
terminator. No public field is changed in this pass.

Pass two rewinds to the original ViewPort and clears `DspIns`, `SprIns`,
`ClrIns`, and `UCopIns` on each validated node. It returns D0=0 only after the
last store. Any NULL, hidden, richer, malformed, cyclic, over-limit, or
provider-owned form restores A0/D0 and transfers to the existing compatibility
owner with no partial teardown. A bounded 32-node admission is adequate for
the initial ROM-compatible native owner; longer chains remain provider-owned
until a documented resource limit supersedes it. CyberGraphX is outside this
native ownership claim.

## G16 generic `MrgCop` dispatch handoff (2026-08-29)

The generic three-pass merger now owns every canonical terminal standard-planar
chain from two through thirty-two ViewPorts. Its validation, separation, and
commit rules are identical regardless of cardinality: each unmerged source has
twelve instructions and a canonical terminator; the first CopList and both CPR
wrappers have capacity for `12 * N`; every retained source lies beyond the
caller-owned destination envelope; and Count is written last. The older fixed
two-through-ten publisher bodies remain generated but unreached from the
public dispatch until their removal can be reviewed as a code-size-only change.
All hidden, malformed, cyclic, over-limit, provider, RTG, and CyberGraphX forms
continue to fall through without native mutation.

## G16 generic `FreeVPortCopLists` dispatch handoff (2026-08-29)

The generic teardown walker now owns canonical post-`MrgCop` chains of three
through thirty-two ViewPorts. It requires the complete standard-planar
RasInfo/CopList/raw-stream envelope before the first commit store. A distinct
two-ViewPort generated-output form is retained as a compatibility tail because
it may omit RasInfo while still carrying a valid merged destination and source
CopList pair. Empty forms retain their existing no-op owner. Everything else
falls through to the host owner with the incoming D0 and all public links
unchanged. The fixed three-through-thirteen teardown arms are no longer emitted
into the native body.

## G04 native fixed-cell text boundary `CurrentX=1344` (2026-08-29)

The byte-aligned three-glyph native `Text` family now admits `CurrentX=1344`
on a two-plane standard planar one-row raster. The exact arm requires a
171-byte row envelope, preflights all source glyphs and both selected planes,
preserves the first 168 destination bytes, publishes bytes 168–170, and
advances `CurrentX` to 1368. A late odd second-plane pointer leaves the whole
transaction available to the fallback owner; the next byte-aligned position
(`CurrentX=1352`) remains outside this bounded native contract. Styled,
proportional, layered, RTG, and CyberGraphX forms remain provider-owned.

## G04 native fixed-cell text boundary `CurrentX=1352` (2026-08-29)
