Its 172-byte row envelope preserves the first 169 bytes of each selected
plane, publishes bytes 169–171 only after complete source/plane preflight, and
advances the cursor to 1376. `CurrentX=1360` remains fallback-owned; all style,
layer, provider, RTG, and CyberGraphX boundaries are unchanged.

## G04 runtime byte-aligned fixed-cell text envelope (2026-08-29)

The public native `Text` entry now begins with bounded runtime arms for one,
two, and three 8x1 fixed-cell glyphs. They accept only unlayered, base-JAM1,
standard-planar, byte-aligned `CurrentX`; their terminal positions are 2040,
2032, and 2024 respectively, so each complete strike fits the same
conservative 256-byte non-wrapping plane envelope. The computed byte offset is
retained in D0, and `BytesPerRow` must include the complete one-, two-, or
three-byte strike before publication. This covers positions beyond the former
generated selector ceiling without making layer clipping, styled or
proportional text, RTG, CyberGraphX, or malformed caller-owned data native.

The source preflight retains glyph zero in D4 while subsequent glyph validation
uses D3. This prevents later-character validation from corrupting the first
strike before the all-plane transaction begins. Existing fixed arms remain the
fallback chain for every count, bit offset, and richer text form that is not
admitted by this narrow runtime envelope.

Because the runtime arm covers every formerly generated byte-aligned
three-glyph position, the corresponding fixed 8..1352 selector ladder is kept
as disabled generator source but is not emitted into the default native image.
The fixed two-glyph `CurrentX=8` and `CurrentX=16` bodies are likewise removed
from emission and alias directly to the non-byte-aligned fallback chain.
This is a code-size-only retirement: it does not broaden layer, provider, RTG,
or CyberGraphX ownership.

## G22 native empty `GfxLookUp` query (2026-08-29)

`GfxLookUp(NULL)` now has a short guest-native terminal body: it returns zero
in D0 without inspecting the extended-node registry or guest memory. Every
non-null key restores the incoming D0 and uses the existing association-owner
fallback, since a resident library or provider may own an association that the
portable registry cannot see. This preserves the V40 empty-query contract
without claiming extended-node allocation, free, or provider-owned lookup
state. It is independent of display timing, layer clipping/damage, RTG, and
CyberGraphX ownership.

## G06 native shallow `Draw(224,1)` terminal (2026-08-29)

The direct `Draw` vector now recognizes the exact fresh `(0,0)` to `(224,1)`
standard-planar shallow segment. It uses the existing one-plane, unlayered,
base-JAM1 17-byte-by-two-row transaction, including full plane preflight,
first-dot consumption, endpoint publication, and line-pattern advance. The
terminal is deliberately direct-Draw-only for now; one-segment `PolyDraw`
continues through its existing bounded selector/fallback until its own vector
entry is extended. Arbitrary slopes, connected paths, clipping/damage, RTG,
CyberGraphX, and provider-owned surfaces remain outside this native form.

## G06 runtime shallow `Draw(x,1)` envelope (2026-08-29)

The direct `Draw` entry now first tries runtime Bresenham bodies for fresh
origin-rooted `(x,1)` segments on four strict one-plane, two-row envelopes:
`192 <= x <= 223` with a 14-byte row, `200 <= x <= 231` with a 15-byte row,
`208 <= x <= 239` with a 16-byte row, and `216 <= x <= 255` with a 17-byte
row.
Each computes the `ceil(x/2)` row-zero run and clipped row-one suffix at
runtime; samples after the relevant visible width never wrap the plane yet
still publish the complete endpoint and line phase. AccurateM68000 fixtures
prove three non-generated endpoints: `(231,1)` produces the 116-pixel
first-row prefix plus the four-pixel row-one suffix, `(239,1)` produces the
120-pixel prefix plus the eight-pixel suffix, and `(255,1)` produces the
128-pixel first-row run plus its final eight-pixel suffix. The runtime also
owns FgPen-zero clear through the same low-bit selection used by the exact
arms. Independent portable-reference fixtures prove the complete clipped
raster, cursor, first-dot, and pattern-phase contract for every BPR=14
endpoint `(192,1)`–`(199,1)`; this replaces the historical sparse samples in
the 192–196 generated arms. All richer draw modes, layers, geometry, RTG,
CyberGraphX, and provider-owned forms retain the preceding exact/native or
portable fallback owner. With both pen outcomes covered, generated terminals
192–212 and 216–224 are retained only as disabled builder reference and are
no longer emitted. A declined BPR=14–BPR=16 state re-enters the existing
generic Draw fallback without mutating the plane or RastPort state; the prior
215-terminal chain remains the runtime fallback gateway for all other
declined forms.

The preceding BPR=13 `(184,1)`–`(191,1)` generated ladder is superseded by a
strict runtime envelope for `184 <= x <= 207`. Ordinary planar raster
operations accept a nonzero byte stride; only display/blitter-specific forms
retain their word-alignment restrictions. The portable and native forms now
publish the same full clipped raster, cursor, first-dot, and line-pattern
state for the historical selectors, while the old sparse arms remain only as
disabled builder reference.

## Validated Layers raster projection and damage ownership (2026-08-29)

Layered graphics operations do not infer visibility from a RastPort. The
Layers owner supplies the validated public ClipRect and SuperClipRect heads
once for each endpoint, and graphics then rasterizes only the resulting
display, compact-backing, and SuperBitMap fragments. A two-endpoint ClipBlit
receives independently validated source and destination projections.

This is intentionally not a graphics-side damage API. Successful painting and
rolled-back failures leave Layer.Flags, DamageList, and the damage-region
bytes unchanged. layers.library retains the sole responsibility for topology,
refresh scheduling, BeginUpdate/EndUpdate, and damage publication. The
CopperStart layer-raster regression covers all 29 supported graphics vectors,
occluded backing writes, SuperBitMap complements, and late-fragment rollback
under that rule. RTG/CyberGraphX remains a separate provider boundary.

An incomplete `EndUpdate(FALSE)` restores the ordinary ClipRect topology but
retains the Layers-owned damage region for a later refresh. A caller can then
replace its caller-owned ClipRegion before resuming with `BeginUpdate`; the
temporary update projection is the intersection of the retained damage and
every ClipRegion rectangle, rather than a collapsed bounding box. Consequently
disjoint Region islands remain independently drawable and their intervening
gap remains hidden. Graphics still treats that projection as a raster-only
constraint: it never changes `Layer.Flags`, the DamageList pointer, or region
bytes. Only the successful outer `EndUpdate(TRUE)` consumes the damage.
The owned-damage block release is that final transaction's commit point: a
failed release leaves its descriptor ownership and public DamageList intact,
so a later `EndUpdate(TRUE)` retry can retire both together.

## G06 clipped shallow-runtime empty suffix (2026-08-29)

The BPR=11 and BPR=13–17 native (x,1) runtime forms explicitly skip their row-one walk
when ceil(x / 2) begins beyond the visible row. This keeps the clipped raster
fully in bounds and prevents the zero suffix count from wrapping to a
65,536-iteration DBRA walk. The complete endpoint, first-dot, and
line-pattern publication remains independent of whether the clipped row-one
suffix has pixels. AccurateM68000 coverage now exercises every BPR=13
admitted target through (207,1); the portable reference includes that upper
endpoint too. Richer geometry, layers, RTG, and CyberGraphX retain their
existing ownership boundaries.

## G06 runtime shallow Draw BPR=11 envelope (2026-08-29)

The bounded native Draw chain now admits fresh origin-rooted (171,1) through
(175,1) segments on the standard one-plane, two-row, 11-byte bitmap form.
It replaces the previous sparse generated terminal pixels with the complete
visible two-row clipped Bresenham raster, while preserving JAM1 pen selection,
first-dot consumption, endpoint publication, and the full line-pattern phase.
One-segment PolyDraw reaches the same body. Noncanonical geometry, layers,
rich draw modes, RTG, and CyberGraphX still fall through to their prior owner.

## G06 runtime shallow Draw BPR=12 envelope (2026-08-29)

The next bounded runtime body covers fresh origin-rooted (176,1) through
(191,1) segments on the standard one-plane, two-row, 12-byte bitmap form.
It supersedes the historical sparse terminal samples with the complete
24-byte clipped two-row Bresenham raster, including the empty row-one suffix
at the high endpoint. Direct Draw and one-segment PolyDraw share the same
body and publish the full cursor, first-dot, and line-pattern state. All
noncanonical geometry, layers, rich draw modes, RTG, and CyberGraphX retain
their existing fallback boundaries.

## G06 runtime shallow Draw BPR=10 boundary (2026-08-29)

The native chain now admits the exact fresh (160,1) endpoint for a
one-plane, two-row, 10-byte bitmap. Its 80-pixel row-zero run exactly fills
the visible first row and leaves the clipped row-one suffix empty. Direct
Draw and one-segment PolyDraw share the body and publish first-dot, endpoint,
and full phase advancement. Wider BPR=10 shallow segments are deliberately
not admitted here because their first-row run must itself be clipped; that is
a distinct runtime form. Layers, rich draw modes, RTG, and CyberGraphX remain
outside this native boundary.

## G06 direct Draw BPR=9 boundary (2026-08-29)

Direct Draw now admits fresh (144,1) through (159,1) segments for a
one-plane, two-row, 9-byte bitmap. The shared first-row clamp fills only the
72-pixel visible row-zero span and skips the empty clipped suffix, including
at the upper endpoint. This body is direct-Draw-only: low-range one-segment
PolyDraw still follows its established selector/fallback and does not claim
the new Draw body. Layers, rich modes, RTG, and CyberGraphX remain outside
the form.

## G06 clipped-first-row shallow runtime (2026-08-29)

The shared native shallow runtime now clamps its row-zero store count to the
visible byte stride before entering DBRA, while retaining the full D0 target
for the later row-one phase and cursor publication. This permits direct Draw
to cover BPR=8 (128,1) through (143,1): the upper endpoint has row-zero
samples beyond the 64-pixel visible width, but writes only the visible first
row and never spills into row one. The BPR=8 form remains direct-only until
the lower-range PolyDraw selector is extended separately.

## G15/G17 native `ChangeVPBitMap` exact-end address contract (2026-08-29)

The geometry-only native `ChangeVPBitMap` arm treats `RasInfo` as its complete
12-byte public envelope: the greatest valid aligned guest start is
`$FFFF_FFF4`, not `$FFFF_FFF3`. The `CompareImmediateLong` guard therefore
admits that exact endpoint and still rejects starts whose required final byte
would wrap. AccurateM68000 verifies the corresponding `$00FF_FFF4` physical
alias, and publication remains limited to the empty head's `BitMap` field.
All richer lifecycle and provider-owned forms remain outside this arm.

The same exact-end rule is shared by native `ScrollVPort`, the bounded
`LoadView` RasInfo readers, and `MakeVPort`'s CPR wrapper guards. A public
12-byte header beginning at `$FFFF_FFF4` is valid because its final byte is
`$FFFFFFFF`; `$FFFF_FFF3` was a conservative off-by-one rejection, not a
wrap-safety requirement. The guards do not relax the other structural tests:
alignment, termination, full public layout, and provider ownership remain
unchanged.

`AskFont` applies the same final-byte rule to its caller-owned `TextAttr`
destination. Its four output fields occupy exactly eight bytes, so an aligned
destination beginning at `$FFFF_FFF8` is valid and is written through the
ordinary 24-bit alias. The native body still preflights the complete output
envelope before its first store and leaves malformed or provider-owned font
state to the portable/native owner.

The bounded two-visible `MrgCop` arm uses both `vp_Modes`/`vp_ExtendedModes`
and `vp_RasInfo`; its ViewPort pointer guard therefore spans the complete
0x28-byte public envelope, not merely the early mode fields. This prevents a
high aligned pointer from making the later RasInfo long access wrap into low
memory before ownership has declined. The guard is read-only and preserves
the normal provider handoff for any noncanonical ViewPort.

## G24 active-update ClipRegion boundary (2026-08-29)

`BeginUpdate` temporarily replaces a Layer's ordinary ClipRect head with the
damage projection and saves the ordinary head for `EndUpdate`. `InstallClipRegion`
does not rebuild topology while that ownership pair is live: it returns the
incoming caller-owned Region unchanged and makes no public or private mutation,
including to a nonempty foreign DamageList.
The caller must first issue `EndUpdate(FALSE)` to restore the ordinary tiling
while retaining damage, then install the Region and start the next update.
This keeps Region clipping, temporary damage projection, and retry-safe
ClipRect retirement separate.

The preallocated singleton `MrgCop` admission has the same ViewPort envelope
rule as the two-visible arm. Although it decides visibility from the early
mode fields, it subsequently reads `vp_RasInfo` and `vp_DspIns`; the initial
pointer guard covers the entire 0x28-byte public ViewPort. A shallow mode-only
check would permit a high aligned address to wrap the later RasInfo access.

Hidden ViewPort walkers intentionally read only `vp_Modes` and `vp_Next`, but
`vp_Modes` is a two-byte field at `+0x20`. Their highest valid guest base is
therefore `$FFFF_FFDE`; `$FFFF_FFDF` lets the second byte wrap. Native
`MrgCop` and `LoadView` reject that value before rebinding their read register,
preserving their read-only hidden-chain lifecycle ownership boundary.

## G15/G17 native `ScrollVPort` exact ViewPort envelope (2026-08-29)

The native empty-list `ScrollVPort` form reads `vp_ExtendedModes`, `vp_DspIns`,
and `vp_RasInfo`; the final read begins at `+0x24` and consumes through `+0x27`.
It consequently preflights exactly the 0x28-byte public ViewPort, whose final
valid aligned base is `$FFFF_FFD8`. The former `$FFFF_FFD7` guard described a
nonexistent extra byte and incorrectly handed this valid structural no-op to
the provider. RasInfo, CopList, alignment, and ownership tests are unchanged.

## G15/G17 native `CalcIVG` DspIns field envelope (2026-08-29)

`CalcIVG`'s empty-display-list form does not need the full ViewPort, but it
does read the four-byte `vp_DspIns` field at `+0x08`. Its precise maximum base
is thus `$FFFF_FFF4`, not `$FFFF_FFF7`: the latter permits `$FFFF_FFF6`, for
which the field's final bytes wrap into low memory. The guarded native body
accepts the exact endpoint and transfers malformed or populated-list forms to
the existing provider path without altering D0.

## G05/G26 native `AreaEllipse` vector-cursor envelope (2026-08-29)

The empty collector form writes two four-byte vectors and then commits the
advanced `AreaInfo.VectorPointer`. Although `$FFFF_FFF8` contains a complete
eight-byte write span, its resulting one-past cursor is zero and cannot be
published as a valid continuation. The native guard deliberately admits the
last aligned base `$FFFF_FFF6`, which commits `$FFFF_FFFE`, and declines the
next address before any data or public cursor mutation. This is a transaction
publication boundary, rather than a raw write-span boundary.

## G24 outer `EndUpdate` retry boundary (2026-08-29)

An outer `EndUpdate(TRUE)` restores the ordinary ClipRect head before retiring
the Layer-owned DamageList. If that opaque release fails, the restored head is
also retained in `SaveClipRects`, `Updating` stays set, and the caller keeps
the update lock. This is an intentional retry state: a subsequent outer end
does not reconstruct or redisplay damage; it merely repeats final retirement
and then clears the public update markers. The order avoids either losing the
normal tiling or forgetting the private owner of a still-published DamageList.

## G25 native Region boolean staging (in progress)

`NewRegion`, `DisposeRegion`, and `ClearRegion` establish a native
private-prefix ownership marker while retaining the public Kickstart Region
layout. Native `AndRectRegion` now claims only marker-owned, canonical chains:
it validates the complete Region/Rectangle envelopes, predecessor links, each
relative node rectangle, and its bounded termination before changing public
memory. It then calculates the absolute result bounds, proves every surviving
relative result is representable, compacts survivors into the existing node
prefix, publishes the header, and frees only the obsolete suffix through Exec.
Foreign, malformed, evil-rectangle, and provider-owned forms remain on the
portable/provider path. The first allocation-bearing `OrRectRegion` case
is a marker-owned empty Region with a valid Rectangle.
It allocates one `PUBLIC|CLEAR` 16-byte RegionRectangle through Exec, writes
its relative rectangle and predecessor link before exposing the node, then
publishes the Region bounds and head pointer. Allocation failure returns FALSE
without mutating the empty header; an odd or wrapping allocation result is
released through Exec and likewise returns FALSE. A nonempty marker-owned
Region is also claimed when it is exactly one canonical node. An input inside
its header bounds is a verified no-growth no-op; an input containing every
header bound rewrites the same node's relative extents and then publishes the
new header, with no allocation. Equal-span horizontal or vertical overlaps
and pixel adjacency coalesce to one rectangle and reuse that node without
Exec. Only a maximum proven smaller than the opposing minimum is incremented
for the adjacency check; it is restored on both accepted and gap paths. Real
gaps remain separate and relative extent overflow declines before mutation. The first native
topology-changing form is a fully disjoint one-node-plus-rectangle union: it
preflights both relative encodings, allocates and validates two fresh PUBLIC
nodes, initializes their sorted (`minY`, then `minX`) links and bounds before
publishing the replacement head, then frees the obsolete node through Exec.
If either replacement allocation fails or is odd/wrapping, every provisional
node is released and the old header/chain remains published. The first
overlapping native form is the upper-left L union `[8,18..19,30]` plus
`[15,25..21,32]`: it preflights every relative word, validates three fresh
PUBLIC nodes, initializes the complete three-band chain `[8,18..19,24]`,
`[8,25..21,30]`, `[15,31..21,32]`, publishes it, and only then retires the
old node. A third-allocation failure releases the second then first
provisional node with the original header still published. All four strict
L mirrors use the same transaction. The strict horizontal crossing bar
`[10,10..20,20]` plus `[5,14..25,16]` is also native: it emits top, expanded
middle, and lower bands under header `[5,10..25,20]`. Other shapes require
their own canonical admission and transaction coverage. Its vertical
counterpart `[10,10..20,20]` plus `[14,5..16,25]` likewise publishes top,
full-width middle, and bottom bands under `[10,5..20,25]` through the same
private three-node allocation/rollback transaction. The strict left-extending
horizontal T `[10,10..20,20]` plus `[5,14..15,16]` is native as well: it
retains the old top/right/bottom edges, publishes the three bands under
`[5,10..20,20]`, and admits only a strict interior-Y, left-extending,
right-contained input. Its right-extending mirror `[10,10..20,20]` plus
`[15,14..25,16]` is likewise native, retaining the old left/top/bottom edges
and updating only the header maximum X. Both horizontal Ts also admit pixel
adjacency, while an actual X gap remains two separate rectangles. Each
relative output coordinate is checked before allocation, including the input
maximum X used by the right T.

Both horizontal Ts also allow equality at the retained opposite X edge.
The left adjacency check temporarily decrements the old minimum X, whose
strict separation from input.minX prevents underflow; the right temporarily
increments old maximum X, whose strict separation from input.maxX prevents
overflow. Each restores the original coordinate before taking either its
success or gap route, including equality at signed WORD endpoints.

Reversed-source horizontal Ts keep the old Region as the narrow-height stem
and input as the taller bar. Under `input.minY < old.minY <= old.maxY <
input.maxY`, connected X intervals yield three canonical bands: the complete
input X span above the old stem, the union X span across its Y interval, and
the complete input X span below it. For old `[5,14..15,16]` plus input
`[10,10..20,20]`, output is `[10,10..20,13]`, `[5,14..20,16]`, and
`[10,17..20,20]`. The right mirror extends only the middle band's right edge.
Overlap, pixel adjacency, and retained-X equality use the same writer; true
gaps retain the separate two-node transaction. This repairs the previous
adjacency decomposition that incorrectly retained two whole rectangles.

The vertical crossing bar shares this input/union-X/input writer. Its middle
union X span is exactly the old X span, preserving its previous geometry.
Before allocation, the complete union envelope's relative width and height
must fit 0..32767. Strict Y containment makes the absolute +/-1 cuts safe,
and every output endpoint lies inside the checked envelope. The three-node
frame saves the input pointer and obsolete node; the writer reconstructs
the envelope without swapping owner/source roles, then publishes all bounds
and the head only after every node is initialized. Native execution tests
cover source reversal, signed limits, and null/odd/wrapping allocation in
each of the three slots with A0/A1/D1 overwritten by Exec.

That volatile-register coverage also caught an old emitted-ABI defect in the
shared allocator: d16(A7) requires one displacement word, not two. The corrected
`MOVE.L 4(A7),D1; MOVEA.L D1,A1` restores the saved input pointer; previously,
an extra zero made the following MOVEA decode as ORI.B immediate data. The
regression first reproduced failed native returns with clobbered A1 and now
passes for existing L/T unions as well as the shared vertical-bar writer.

The top-extending vertical T `[10,10..20,20]` plus `[14,5..16,15]` uses the
two-node transaction. Its exposed stem `[14,5..16,9]` precedes the complete
old rectangle `[10,10..20,20]`; the covered input bottom does not split
identical active X intervals. The three-node specification was incorrect.
Native and portable output must match in header, sorted bounds, links, and
allocation count, with null/odd/wrapping allocations retaining the old list.

The bottom-extending mirror `[10,10..20,20]` plus `[14,15..16,25]` also
uses the two-node transaction: the complete old rectangle comes first,
followed by `[14,21..16,25]`. Its post-allocation discriminator distinguishes
Y-overlap from adjacency and real gaps, reloads the original old maximum Y
before clipping the stem, and preserves the checked result envelope. The
strict extension proves that `old.maxY + 1` cannot wrap a signed word.
Both vertical T selectors also accept equality at the opposite Y edge:
top input MaxY may equal old MaxY and bottom input MinY may equal old MinY.
This includes one-row old rectangles without creating an empty third band.

Both vertical Ts now support reversed source roles: a narrow old Region stem
and a wider input Rectangle bar produce the same two canonical bands as the
opposite call order. Header-first dispatch clips the old top stem's MaxY at
`input.minY-1`; input-first dispatch clips the old bottom stem's MinY at
`input.maxY+1`. Each discriminator rechecks Y overlap and both inclusive X
containment edges so disjoint/adjacent inputs retain their full geometry.
Source identities never swap: A5 owns the Region, A2 the obsolete node, and
A1 remains the immutable input. D0..D3 retain the preflighted envelope across
both writers. Strict Y extension makes the endpoint adjustment safe, and the
adjusted endpoint remains inside the original checked source span. Differential
coverage checks both source orders, retained-edge equality, single-row bars,
single-column stems, signed limits, and rollback under volatile Exec clobbers.
The contained X interval may share either bar edge. Complete X-span equality
still coalesces earlier to one node, and a stem extending both Y edges remains
the existing three-band case. The shared-Y dispatcher runs before ordinary
source sorting, so equal MinY/MinX ties select the correct two-band geometry.

The same differential gate verifies all four L mirrors. Once one rectangle
ends in Y, the remaining band keeps the entire other rectangle's X span.
In particular, the upper-right and lower-right old-rectangle mirrors must
not subtract the previous overlap horizontally from their final band.
Pixel-adjacent X spans with crossing Y ranges also use this three-band writer:
the joined overlap band cannot be represented by two unchanged source nodes.
Each adjacency guard increments only the strictly bounded maximum and restores
it before both success and real-gap exits.

When sources share exactly one Y edge, connected X spans can instead form two
bands even without X containment. The shorter-Y source must protrude in X;
otherwise the result is the existing one-node containment form. After checking
both X directions for overlap or pixel adjacency, the two-node transaction
dispatches to the matching vertical-T geometry body and widens only its full
bar to the union X envelope. The remaining tail retains its source X bounds.
The checked envelope remains in D0..D3; allocation validation, publication,
input-pointer preservation, and reverse-order rollback are shared unchanged.
Real X gaps bypass this join and retain two whole source rectangles.

The differential matrix enumerates all 1,296 ordered rectangle pairs with
endpoints in 0/1/2. It first reproduced 128 shared-Y-edge two-band errors and
16 adjacent-L errors; those wrong native claims are now corrected. The verified
matrix initially had 1,264 exact native results and 32 honest declines. Inclusive
X containment in the four vertical-T selectors and matching writer discriminators
now admits those final 32; all 1,296 pairs match natively with zero mismatches.
Native results are compared against the portable canonical builder, including
ordered bounds, links, allocation counts, and obsolete-node retirement. Declines
must preserve the caller frame, Region/node/input bytes, and allocation logs.
Targeted tests additionally cover signed limits and every failing allocation
slot under volatile Exec clobbers. The matrix now requires all pairs to execute
natively so an honest fallback cannot hide a regression in this bounded domain.
An independent audit found legacy native graphics/test call sites using A0/D0
instead of Exec FreeMem's A1/D0 convention. The A1-accurate subtraction matrix
then reproduced wrong releases in every node-retiring case: the input pointer,
a volatile-register poison value, or even a fresh published node was passed
instead of the obsolete allocation. An adapter first applied to Region saves A1 on the
stack, copies A0 to A1, calls Exec, and restores A1 with `MOVEA.L (SP)+,A1`.
It covers all 43 Region-family source call sites without changing geometric
frames or borrowing callee-saved registers. Its execution verification is
recorded in the active checkpoint. The generic JSR emitter remains raw; the
two ColorMap sites now share this adapter, and the two Raster sites have a
separate D0/D1-to-A1/D0 adapter. Those units are described in their sections
below. The other 89 graphics cleanup sites retain D0-address/D1-size staging
and remain separately audited follow-up units.

Both 1,296-pair matrices now pass with real A1/D0 FreeMem gateways and volatile
register clobbers. A separate lifecycle fixture binds the production
`ExecMemoryServices` directly to the classic guest allocator: native NewRegion,
seed, two-node union replacement, optional repeated ClearRegion, and DisposeRegion
must retire the exact allocations and coalesce the heap back to its original
free chunk. Both disposal sequences pass, including immutable Rectangle bytes,
public/private layout, node links, and caller-stack checks. No CPU-core or
custom-chip behavior changed for these emitted-code corrections.

Remaining XOR, subtraction, and Region-to-Region forms retain the portable
builder until their allocation/rollback and native envelope rules have
equivalent 68k coverage.

`ClearRectRegion` now claims the corresponding marker-owned empty Region
form. It performs the same bounded Rectangle input read used by the portable
Boolean entrypoint, leaves the already-empty Region header untouched, and
returns TRUE without calling Exec. It also claims a canonical one-node native
Region only when a valid clear Rectangle is wholly disjoint from its absolute
header: complete link/relative-bound validation precedes the unchanged TRUE
return. When that Rectangle wholly covers the admitted canonical node, native
code first resolves Exec and then publishes the portable empty header
`[0,0,-1,-1]` and null head before retiring the sole public node. Missing Exec
declines before mutation. The previous free-before-publication order and zero
maximum bounds were both reproduced by the 1,296-pair subtraction matrix (225
empty results); allocation-free retained results and two/three/four-node
replacement results are checked independently. FreeMem-boundary snapshots
verify the published list, exact retired address, and unchanged private ownership
prefix. Input Rectangle bytes are checked across allocation/free calls and return.

The empty sentinel is this implementation's portable/native parity contract,
not a claim that undocumented Kickstart empty-bound bytes have been measured.
The [public Region documentation](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Graphics_Regions)
defines emptiness in terms of drawable area and keeps clipping/damage ownership
with Layers. Exact ROM-byte conformance for other empty Region producers remains
a separate compatibility check.

The first partial `ClearRectRegion` subtraction arm is deliberately limited to
a clear rectangle that spans the canonical Region's full vertical extent and
removes its left edge through an interior inclusive X. That leaves one right
rectangle, so the existing node and links remain owned: native code rewrites
the header, resets the relative origin, and recomputes its relative width.
All other partial subtraction shapes still require the portable builder.
The symmetric full-height right strip has the same retained-node contract and
rewrites the surviving left rectangle.

The corresponding full-width top strip is also allocation-free: once the
clear Rectangle covers both horizontal edges and begins at or above the
Region's top edge, an interior inclusive bottom Y leaves exactly one lower
rectangle. Native code keeps the node and links, raises the public minimum Y
to `clearMaxY + 1`, resets the relative origin, and recomputes the relative
height. Bottom strips and every partial subtraction that can create more than
one rectangle remain with the portable builder.

The symmetric full-width bottom strip follows the same retained-node rule.
After full-width admission, an interior clear minimum Y with coverage through
the Region's bottom edge leaves exactly one upper rectangle; native code
lowers the public maximum Y to `clearMinY - 1` and recomputes the relative
height. Split-producing shapes use the separately admitted transactions below.

An interior full-width clear is the first replacement-list subtraction form.
It yields two vertical bands, sorted upper then lower. Native code resolves
Exec, allocates and validates both public nodes while the previous header and
node remain live, initializes their links and relative bounds, publishes the
new head, and only then retires the old node. A failed or invalid provisional
allocation releases only provisional ownership and returns failure without a
public Region write.

The symmetric interior full-height clear uses a replacement chain ordered left
then right: `[header.minX .. clear.minX - 1]` followed
by `[clear.maxX + 1 .. header.maxX]`, with unchanged Y bounds. It uses the
same two-allocation, initialize-before-publish, retire-after-publish contract
as the horizontal split; corner and hole forms require their own geometry. In
particular, an upper-left corner clear is not a left-strip update: it uses the
separate upper-right/full-width-lower publisher below.

The upper-left publisher's native admission is intentionally narrower than a
general corner Boolean operation: the clear must cover the Region's left and
top edges and end strictly inside its right and bottom edges. It allocates the
upper-right node first and the full-width lower node second, validates each
public address before any Region write, links both nodes with the Region-head
`Previous` pointer, publishes the upper-right head, and only then frees
the old node. A missing, odd, or unaddressable allocation frees every
provisional node and retains the original public chain. The focused regression
must cover the full public envelope, both relative rectangles, ordered links, old-node
retirement, and the allocation-failure rollback boundary.

The lower-left counterpart admits only a clear that covers the Region's left
and bottom edges, starts strictly below the top edge, and ends strictly inside
the right edge. It is deliberately separate from the bottom-strip route: a
clear that stops above the bottom uses the separate three-node edge-interior
form below. Its two native replacements are ordered by relative
`MinY`/`MinX`: `[header.minX..header.maxX, header.minY..clear.minY-1]` then
`[clear.maxX+1..header.maxX, clear.minY..header.maxY]`. It shares the
validated two-allocation/publish-then-retire transaction with the split and
upper-left arms.

The upper-right counterpart admits only a clear that covers the Region's top
and right edges, starts strictly inside the left edge, and ends strictly above
the bottom edge. Its replacements are `[header.minX..clear.minX-1,
header.minY..clear.maxY]` followed by `[header.minX..header.maxX,
clear.maxY+1..header.maxY]`: upper-left first, then the full-width lower band.
The shared post-allocation selector explicitly distinguishes
this form from the upper-left form, while full-height clears continue to their
left/right split publisher.

The lower-right counterpart is admitted only when the clear starts inside the
Region's left and top edges and reaches its right and bottom edges. It retains
`[header.minX..header.maxX, header.minY..clear.minY-1]` followed by
`[header.minX..clear.minX-1, clear.minY..header.maxY]`. Any clear that fails
either edge predicate must not enter this two-node corner publisher.

All four corner outputs must use the portable builder's maximal horizontal
intervals per Y band. A full-height side strip plus a partial-width remainder
may preserve pixels but is not the same canonical Region. The differential
fixture checks exact ordered rectangles, not just area or outer bounds.

The native strictly interior clear form admits a rectangle whose four edges
are strictly inside the canonical Region. Its hole result needs FOUR nodes,
ordered by relative `MinY`/`MinX`: upper full
width `[header.minX..header.maxX, header.minY..clear.minY-1]`, middle-left
`[header.minX..clear.minX-1, clear.minY..clear.maxY]`, middle-right
`[clear.maxX+1..header.maxX, clear.minY..clear.maxY]`, and lower full width
`[header.minX..header.maxX, clear.maxY+1..header.maxY]`. Native code must
allocate and validate all four nodes before initializing or publishing any.
The former three-node implementation and its hand-written expectation wrongly
deleted the middle-right survivor; the portable differential fixture now
guards every band, including the one-pixel-hole and narrow-strip cases.

The strict-hole arm reuses the first three allocations, saves the old node
and geometry on the guest stack, and keeps the third pointer in callee-saved
D6 across the fourth Exec call because A1 is volatile. Once allocation four
is validated, it restores geometry, preserves clear MaxX through scratch use,
initializes the complete chain, publishes the new head, and frees the saved
old node. Null/odd/wrapping failures at any allocation retire every provisional
node in reverse order without changing the old header/list. The tests poison
Exec's volatile registers and check for early writes at each allocation.

The shared three-node prefix completes a lower-interior clear that starts
inside both X edges and reaches the Region bottom. Its sorted result is the
upper full-width band `[header.minX..header.maxX, header.minY..clear.minY-1]`,
then the lower-left band `[header.minX..clear.minX-1,
clear.minY..header.maxY]`, then the lower-right band
`[clear.maxX+1..header.maxX, clear.minY..header.maxY]`. The post-allocation
selector chooses this geometry only after all three addresses are valid, so
the existing third-allocation rollback remains the atomic failure boundary.

A right-interior clear that reaches the Region's right edge but stops above
its bottom needs upper/middle-left/lower-full-width nodes only: there is no
middle-right survivor. It retains the three-node geometry and transaction. An upper-interior
clear must not enter the two-node full-height splitter merely because it ends
inside both X edges; it joins the same three-node allocator and selects its
distinct three-band geometry after all provisional addresses are valid.

The upper-interior form is admitted only when the clear covers the
Region top, begins and ends strictly inside its X edges, and stops above the
bottom. Its canonical chain must be `[header.minX..clear.minX-1,
header.minY..clear.maxY]`, `[clear.maxX+1..header.maxX,
header.minY..clear.maxY]`, then `[header.minX..header.maxX,
clear.maxY+1..header.maxY]`, ordered by relative `MinY` then `MinX`. The
third-allocation rollback shared with hole/lower/right interior clears keeps
the old node and public envelope intact on any failed or invalid allocation.

A left-interior clear reaches the Region's left edge, starts below the top,
and stops above the bottom while ending inside the right edge. It uses the
same validated three-node allocator and publishes `[header.minX..header.maxX,
header.minY..clear.minY-1]`, `[clear.maxX+1..header.maxX,
clear.minY..clear.maxY]`, then `[header.minX..header.maxX,
clear.maxY+1..header.maxY]`. Its middle-right geometry remains distinct from
the right-interior middle-left form, while preserving relative-MinY/MinX
ordering and the shared atomic rollback boundary.

The horizontal mirror of the native upper-left `OrRectRegion` L union is
native too. Given an existing upper-right rectangle and an incoming lower-left
rectangle with overlapping spans, it publishes the existing upper-right band,
then the middle full-width overlap band, then the incoming lower-left band.
It dispatches into the same three-node private allocation/rollback transaction
as the upper-left form, selects the input minimum X as the new relative origin,
and publishes the changed header minimum X and maximum Y only after the list is
fully initialized. XOR and subtraction remain separate units because their
pixel topology is not union geometry.

The vertical mirror is also native: an existing lower-left rectangle plus an
incoming upper-right rectangle produces upper-right, middle-full-width, and
lower-left bands. It uses the existing minimum X and the input minimum Y as
the relative origin, then publishes the input-driven minimum Y and maximum X
only after all three replacements have been linked and initialized. The shared
transaction continues to preserve the pre-publication rollback boundary.

The fourth orientation (existing lower-right, incoming upper-left) is emitted
through the same transaction. It uses both input minima as the relative origin,
publishes upper-left, middle-full-width, and lower-right bands, and updates the
header's minimum X/minimum Y only after all replacements are private and linked.

For an empty marker-owned Region, `XorRectRegion` shares `OrRectRegion`'s
ordinary-Rectangle allocation transaction. The native XOR front end recognizes
an evil Rectangle itself and returns TRUE with no allocation, preserving the
empty header; this retains the portable Boolean contract without accidentally
turning the evil form into OR allocation.

For a nonempty Region, XOR reuses that OR transaction only after validating a
canonical one-node chain and proving the Rectangle is wholly disjoint from the
absolute header. This is the exact set identity `A xor B = A or B` for
disjoint inputs. Equal canonical rectangles are the other single-step native
identity: after the same admission, their node is retired through Exec and an
empty header is published. Every other overlap tail-chains to the portable XOR
builder instead of accidentally applying union semantics.

The Region-to-Region Boolean vectors also have a first native identity arm:
when both source and destination are empty marker-owned Regions,
`OrRegionRegion`, `AndRegionRegion`, and `XorRegionRegion` validate both
private-prefix and public-header envelopes and return TRUE without changing the
destination. Any nonempty source or destination remains with the portable
Region-to-Region Boolean builder until complete chain replacement is native.

`AndRegionRegion` additionally admits a canonical one-node marker-owned source
when the marker-owned destination is empty. Intersection cannot add pixels to
that destination, so the native body validates the source's complete one-node
chain and relative bounds, then returns TRUE without allocation or a public
write. Nonempty destinations, malformed sources, and larger chains remain
portable.

`OrRegionRegion` and `XorRegionRegion` likewise admit an empty marker-owned
source with either an empty or canonical one-node marker-owned destination.
For that exact identity the destination is unchanged, so the native body
validates its complete chain and returns TRUE without allocation or writes.
Any nonempty source still uses its operation-specific portable Boolean builder;
the OR identity must never be used to claim XOR overlap semantics.

For `AndRegionRegion`, an empty marker-owned source with a canonical one-node
marker-owned destination is the first native Region-to-Region mutation. The
body validates both ownership envelopes and the destination's full canonical
chain, resolves Exec before retirement, frees the public node, and publishes
the zero bounds/head header. Other source/destination combinations still
tail-chain to the existing portable Boolean builder.

For `OrRegionRegion` and `XorRegionRegion`, a canonical one-node source and
empty destination is the first native transfer transaction. The public Region
header's first eight bytes are the source's absolute Rectangle envelope; after
validating that the node is exactly canonical, the adapter reorders A0/A1 and
tail-enters `OrRectRegion`. This reuses its allocation, publication, and
rollback contract without pretending a multi-node Region is one rectangle.

The same reuse also applies when both marker-owned Regions are exact one-node
rectangles and their inclusive absolute bounds are strictly disjoint. Both
node links, relative envelopes, and public bounds are validated before the
source header is passed as `OrRectRegion`'s Rectangle-compatible input. The
destination is retained as the publisher Region, so the established two-node
replacement transaction initializes the sorted chain before publication and
retires only its prior node. Strict non-overlap is required because only then
does `A xor B` equal `A or B`; touching, overlapping, malformed, and multi-node
forms retain their operation-specific portable paths.

`OrRegionRegion` has a distinct emitted entry after that shared boundary. Once
both one-node native envelopes are canonical, union may always tail-enter the
existing `OrRectRegion` publisher: contained, same-span coalescing, supported
L-shaped replacement, and disjoint forms retain the publisher's own bounded
admission and portable fallback. `XorRegionRegion` continues to use the
strict-disjoint entry, because union is not XOR for touching or overlapping
rectangles. Equal canonical one-node source/destination rectangles are its
additional exact identity: after the same full admission, native code retires
only the destination node through Exec and publishes that destination's empty
header. Non-identical overlap remains with portable XOR subtraction.

`AndRegionRegion` now has a similarly narrow two-nonempty identity: after
both canonical one-node envelopes are fully validated, a source whose absolute
rectangle contains every destination edge returns TRUE without modifying the
destination. It is exactly `source ∩ destination = destination`. Reverse
containment, partial overlap, disjointness, malformed memory, and larger lists
retain the existing portable Boolean transaction.

When the destination instead contains the validated source, that same one-node
native AND body rewrites the destination header and its relative bounds to the
source rectangle. This remains allocation-free and preserves the existing
destination-node ownership; only the exact one-rectangle intersection is
claimed, while all non-containment shapes remain portable.

For the remaining overlapping one-node rectangle pairs, native AND selects the
maximum lower edges and minimum upper edges, verifies the resulting inclusive
rectangle is nonempty, and rewrites the existing destination node in place.
This completes the allocation-free nonempty rectangular intersection set. For
disjoint canonical one-node rectangles, the same preflight resolves Exec,
retires the admitted destination node, and then publishes zero bounds and a
null head. Multi-node Regions remain portable.

The public Region guard spans all twelve bytes while also reserving the four
private marker bytes before it. Thus the final valid aligned public pointer is
`$FFFF_FFF4`; `$FFFF_FFF6` declines before the final public header byte could
wrap through zero. The native rectangle guard is independently complete before
the first marker or header access. AccurateM68000 raw-memory regression covers
this exact-end envelope for both `AndRectRegion` and native `OrRectRegion`
arms.

## G14/G25/G26 native ColorMap allocator ABI and envelopes (2026-08-30)

The ColorMap lifecycle now uses the same explicit Exec boundary as Region.
Its odd-result rollback previously passed the allocator-clobbered A1 to
FreeMem, reproduced as `$A1A1A1A1` instead of the returned `$00D40001` for a
72-byte request. Both constructor rollback and ordinary disposal now stage
A1 through the balanced adapter; obsolete D1 flag setup is removed because
FreeMem has no flags argument. The rollback test requires unchanged allocation
bytes, original count on decline, and a balanced stack. Normal disposal was
already a passing control because A1 happened to retain the private base;
NULL and foreign maps still make no free call. A separate production Exec/
classic-allocator fixture proves private marker, exact size, public+12 layout,
cleared tables, and full heap restoration for counts 2 and 3. Count 3 frees
its requested 76 bytes, not the allocator-rounded 80.

ColorMap's complete address envelope is checked independently of that ABI.
The constructor validates the inclusive last byte `base + (size-1)` before
any marker/header write; an odd or wrapping result is retired through the
same exact-size cleanup. Disposal first proves the 52-byte public header fits
(maximum base `$FFFFFFCC`), then proves the complete count-derived allocation
extent before reading table pointers or calling Exec. Matching forged pointer
equalities cannot bypass these guards. A seven-case accurate-68000 fixture
first reproduced four wrong native claims, then verified both constructor
wraps and both forged frees decline with memory/SysBase and D0/SP preserved.
The three passing controls end exactly at `$FFFFFFFF`: counts 2, 3, and 65535,
with the latter requesting `$4003C` bytes. Computing size-minus-one before the
addition is essential to retain that legal endpoint. These are logical-address
tests using 24-bit physical aliases, not claims about installed memory.
The constructor guard uses volatile D1 to avoid adding D4 to its previous
scratch set; five constructor rows enforce that D4 canary after reproducing
the initial guard's clobber. This narrow guarantee is not full public-entry
register preservation. PaletteExtra sidecar ownership also remains separate.

## G09/G25/G26 native Raster FreeMem boundary (2026-08-30)

Raster's two cleanup sites use a different private staging convention from
Region/ColorMap: D0 holds the allocation address and D1 the complete span.
The new `AppendExecFreeMemFromD0D1PreservingA1` adapter saves A1, transfers
D0 to A1 and D1 to D0, calls Exec, and restores A1. It is applied only to
AllocRaster's odd-result rollback and FreeRaster's retirement. The generic
JSR emitter and the remaining 89 family cleanup sites remain unchanged.

The accurate-Exec fixture first reproduced six failures: normal disposal
passed its address as the size, and odd rollback also passed poisoned A1.
Seventeen independent rejected-input controls passed before the correction
and retain no-free/no-mutation behavior afterward. All 23 targeted cases now
pass, including the legacy loaded-HUNK lifecycle, isolated manually seeded
FreeRaster, odd rollback with full-width D0 restoration, and two production
ExecMemoryServices/classic-allocator round trips. A 17x3 raster has a 12-byte
payload after its ten-byte private prefix. Its 22-byte allocation occupies
24 bytes after classic rounding; FreeMem receives 22, not 24 or the address,
and the original free chunk is restored. CLEAR payload and untouched padding
are checked independently.

Both plain dimensions and stale high-word register values are covered. The
[AllocRaster Autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0412.html)
and [FreeRaster Autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node02DC.html)
specify low-word dimensions. Only a contradictory host-adapter comment needed
correction; its existing casts were already correct. Native large-width row
rounding and complete Raster envelope admission remain separate from this ABI
unit. No CPU-core or custom-chip behavior changed.

## G01/G26 native negative-vector physical layout (2026-08-30)

The physical negative table and the AUTOINIT function array have different
orders. A vector's byte offset within the negative table is
`VectorTableSize + signedLvo`: with a 1056-byte table, -6 lives at offset 1050,
GetColorMap (-570) at 486, and -1056 at zero. The function array instead lists
ordinal -6, -12, ... entries. Both native builders previously used the ordinal
index as the physical table offset; the old scaffold helper repeated the same
error, so jumping to a helper-selected stub did not prove real library routing.

Independent accurate-68000 fixtures now call every slot with `JSR d16(A6)`
using the actual GfxBase, and separately execute each resident AUTOINIT pointer.
Distinct tiny identity bodies isolate placement from graphics-body semantics.
Both fixed and production-loader-relocated HUNK images initially failed all
176 negative-vector calls while all 176 function-array controls passed. The
two physical-offset corrections and the scaffold helper correction now pass
all 352 vector calls and 352 controls, including 163 public and 13 reserved
slots per image. Reserved slots use their explicit fallback target. A6, caller
return, stack balance, physical JMP operands, and function-array termination
are checked independently. Synthetic mappings avoid the built-in Chip RAM
decode, which otherwise takes precedence over mapped fixture bytes.

AUTOINIT ordinal order, GfxBase/code placement, and the complete set of HUNK
JMP-operand relocations remain unchanged. Fourteen focused builder tests and
the rebuilt native suite pass (804/804); generated body bytes and branch
fingerprint are unchanged. This proves entry routing, not complete semantic
or public-register ABI parity for all vectors, and changes no CPU/custom-chip
behavior or CyberGraphX boundary.

## G14/G26 ColorMap public-entry register preservation (2026-08-30)

Local allocator adapters do not establish the enclosing library's complete
calling convention. The [Amiga library-call rules](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Libraries_Manual_guide/node0290.html)
allow D0/D1/A0/A1 scratch but require preservation of the other registers.
The native HUNK and fixed-image vector JMPs and AUTOINIT arrays expose body
starts directly, so the selected body's own entry must honor that convention.
Forty-eight real public-call cases first reproduced saved-register corruption
on every ColorMap path, including zero count and NULL disposal. D0, caller
PC/SP, fallback classification, allocation/free arguments, and memory checks
were already passing and remain independent controls.

GetColorMap now saves D5..D7/A6 with MOVEM masks 0702/40E0 (16-byte frame).
FreeColorMap saves D3..D7/A6 with masks 1F02/40F8 (24-byte frame). All three
exits in each body restore exactly once: ordinary success, zero/NULL success,
and common fallback. The fallback first moves the original argument from
working D7 into D0, then restores caller D7 and A6. Nested Exec/A1 adapter
frames are balanced before the outer frame is popped. Unused callee-saved
registers need no extra stack space; no generic wrapper or builder contract
has changed.

The fixture covers twelve paths through fixed and relocated-HUNK vectors
and independently recovered AUTOINIT pointers. D2..D7/A2..A5 canaries and
actual GfxBase A6 are checked after the real caller JSR returns, without host
restoration; Exec callbacks poison only their permitted volatile registers.
All 48 pass, alongside 101/101 focused Raster/ColorMap/branch, 465/465 Region/
branch, 852/852 full native, and 178/178 broader scaffold gates. Eight MOVEM
opcode/mask pairs add exactly 32 bytes, producing 1,434,972 generated bytes
with the previous branch topology unchanged. No CPU/custom-chip code changed.

Raster's public entry frame is a separate unit from its remaining large-width
rounding and complete-envelope work. Public callee-save proof does not establish
a future provider handoff's preservation of all volatile arguments or complete
native semantics for every declining input.

## G09/G26 Raster public-entry register preservation (2026-08-30)

The Raster family now uses the same opt-in in-body frame approach as ColorMap.
AllocRaster saves D2..D7/A6 (MOVEM masks 3F02/40FC, 28 bytes); FreeRaster saves
D2/D3/D7/A6 (3102/408C, 16 bytes). Their success RTS and common fallback each
restore exactly once. The fallback reconstructs the caller's full-width D0
from working D7 before restoring D7, including stale high-word input bits.
Allocation failure and odd rollback join that same restore; all ten FreeRaster
guards do likewise. Exec retains A6 until its nested call/cleanup has finished.

Fifty-two cases first reproduced saved-register failures with D0, caller
PC/SP, fallback, Exec arguments, and memory controls already passing. All now
pass: thirteen scenarios through fixed/relocated-HUNK negative vectors and
independent AUTOINIT entries. Plain and high-word-residue 17x3 allocations,
manually seeded frees, zero dimensions, missing Exec, NULL allocation, odd
rollback, and NULL/foreign/dimension-mismatched free paths are covered. The
existing twenty-case boundary suite still covers additional individual guards.
No caller-side register repair can mask a failed preservation assertion.

Six MOVEM opcode/mask pairs add exactly 24 bytes and no branches. Generated
code is 1,434,996 bytes with unchanged branch topology; 153/153 focused,
465/465 Region/branch, 904/904 full native, and 178/178 broader scaffold gates
pass. Row rounding, full allocation-envelope admission, and preservation of
volatile A0/D1 arguments for a future transparent provider handoff remain
separate contracts. No CPU/custom-chip behavior changed.

## G09/G26 native Raster wide row rounding (2026-08-30)

UWORD input dimensions do not make intermediate row rounding a WORD operation.
For widths 65521..65535, adding fifteen must retain bit 16 through the four
right shifts. AllocRaster now emits `ADDI.L #15,D6` and four `LSR.L #1,D6`
instructions. Its existing normalized inputs, doubling, unsigned WORD multiply,
ten-byte ownership prefix, public frame, and Exec boundary remain unchanged.
The maximum row stride is 8192, which fits the multiply's unsigned source word;
the maximum complete envelope is 536862730 (`$1FFFE00A`).

An independent eighteen-case accurate-M68000 fixture first produced ten real
size failures and eight passing controls. Upper-width lifecycle cases requested
and later freed ten instead of 8202/16394 bytes; maximum-height NULL probes
also requested ten instead of the full span. The fixture masks public words
explicitly before its checked widened arithmetic, avoiding a test-only checked
cast of high-register-half inputs. Real vector calls, literal expected sizes,
private headers, payload clearing, untouched padding, actual Exec A1/D0 frees,
callee-save canaries, caller return, and fallback are checked independently.
Free consumes the header Alloc actually produced, without repairing its size.

All eighteen cases now pass, including last-safe width65520, ordinary17x3,
high-word residues, zero dimensions, and maximum-height probes without giant
allocations. Generated code grows by two bytes to 1,434,998 with unchanged
branch topology. Rebuilt gates pass 171/171 focused, 465/465 Region/branch,
922/922 full native, and 178/178 broader scaffold. Complete inclusive-envelope
admission and coherent forged-free rejection remain a separate next unit.

## G09/G25/G26 Raster complete-envelope admission (2026-08-30)

Native Raster ownership now covers the complete inclusive allocation, not just
the ten-byte marker/dimension/size prefix. AllocRaster checks `base + (size-1)`

zero reproducer's width17/height119/span486 header leaves SysBase `$00770000`
intact by construction, rather than repairing and invalidating the evidence.

Full logical pointers are recorded at Exec boundaries while high addresses

All 21 cases now pass. Code grows by 46 bytes and two branch patches to

## G17/G26 DBufInfo public-entry register preservation (2026-08-30)

Correct public input registers and nested Exec arguments do not establish
callee-save parity. Seventy-two accurate-M68000 cases first failed solely on

## G17/G25/G26 DBufInfo complete-envelope admission (2026-08-30)

The native DBufInfo allocation is a fixed 88-byte envelope: four private bytes
and the 84-byte public object. Its last legal private base is `$FFFFFFA8`, with
public pointer `$FFFFFFAC` and final byte `$FFFFFFFF`. AllocDBufInfo now checks

higher results share the already-correct exact rollback. FreeDBufInfo retains
NULL success, rejects public pointers <=4, and checks the public upper bound
before subtracting the prefix or reading its marker. A constructor can never
own a private-zero allocation because AllocMem's zero result is failure.
